Title: A note on the distribution of the least squares estimator of a random walk with drift: Some analytical evidence
Abstract: In this paper we define the notion of a local drift in a unit root process. The theory provides a bridge between the apparent diverging asymptotic theories that apply when a drift is either present or absent in an integrated time-series. Our asymptotic results help to explain the Monte Carlo results of Hylleberg and Mizon (Economics Letters, 1989, 29, 225-230) and Schmidt (Advances in Econometrics, 1988, 8, 161-200). © 1995.

Title: Distributional constraints on the speed of privatization
Abstract: This paper argues that adverse distributional effects may prevent speedy privatization in former command economies. An imbalanced structure of the work force, combined with a politically motivated subsistence consumption constraint, may necessitate gradual privatization. This possibility is illustrated by a numerical example, and a model of gradual privatization is suggested. © 1995.

Title: The length of the effect of aggregate advertising on aggregate consumption
Abstract: We investigate the longevity of aggregate advertising effects on aggregate consumption over the period 1947-1988, using updated methods. The effects appear to linger for nine years, raising further questions. Perhaps a return to this near-dormant area of research could be productive. © 1995.

Title: Sharp regulatory performance with blunt instruments
Abstract: A regulatory environment is analyzed in which the regulator is uncertain about potential production costs and consumer preferences. A blunt instrument policy, consisting of either a price control or quantity restriction, is shown to perform well in maximizing expected surplus. © 1995.

Title: The interaction of explicit and implicit contracts
Abstract: We analyze explicit and implicit contracts in a repeated principal-agent model with observable but only partially contractable actions of the agent. It is shown that the set of implementable actions may increase or decrease if additional actions become contractable. © 1995.

Title: Internal labor markets and firm-specific determination of earnings in the presence of immigrant workers
Abstract: In this paper we study earnings determination at the firm level in Austria. We distinguish firms who employ immigrant workers and those who do not. By using a switching regressions model we find that native workers in firms with immigrant employees face rising earnings-tenure profiles whereas natives in other firms do not. © 1995.

Title: Common trends and common cycles in international labor productivity
Abstract: The objective of this paper is to present a trend-cycle decomposition of the industrial labor productivity series in six major industrialized countries, to study the relationship between trend and cycle innovations, and to highlight the role of monetary policy as a possible source of transitory and permanent variations in labor productivity. © 1995.

Title: Educated guesses and income distribution
Abstract: The matching of jobs and workers depends on the level of knowledge in the economy. In this paper, a natural ‘threshold’ arises and hence there are two possible steady states asymptotically.

Title: Euler equation tests of Ricardian equivalence
Abstract: Tests of Ricardian equivalence based on the Euler condition can be written in several mathematically equivalent ways. This paper shows that these alternative solutions may give rise to different empirical results when liquidity constraints are ignored. This may be due to misspecification, since a crucial assumption of the model is violated, or due to the different parameter restrictions imposed by the different solutions. The evidence suggests that misspecification is the most likely explanation. Previous evidence based on restricted specifications should be interpreted with caution. © 1995.

Title: ‘Time-to-build’ completion patterns for nonresidential structures, 1961–1991
Abstract: Using extensive government survey data, 'completion patterns' are derived for US nonresidential structures over the period 1961-1991. Value-weighted construction periods average five to six quarters, with enough variation over time to undermine somewhat the interpretation of 'time-to-build' parameters as 'structural' in nature. The rapid time path of completions raises some questions about lengthy investment-spending lags typically estimated in econometric studies. © 1995.

Title: The demand for money and non-GDP transactions
Abstract: This paper argues that transactions in non-GDP items have an important influence on the level of money demand. The paper provides empirical estimates of models of both M1 and M2 money demand that include variables proxying for the volume of transactions in real estate and financial assets. These variables have the theoretically-predicted positive sign, and are statistically significant. Their inclusion also improves out-of-sample forecasts. © 1995.

Title: Insurance and decision-taking
Abstract: In this paper we show how the holding of an insurance contract influences the choice variable of a decision-taker. We analyze two decision problems: optimal saving by consumers, and optimal production by firms. We find an unambiguous sign change in the decision variable under common assumptions about the utility of decision-takers. © 1995.

Title: Constraints in perfect-foresight models: The case of old-age savings and public pensions
Abstract: The solution of discrete-time perfect-foresight models with constrained state variables differs considerably from the solution of models without constraints. In this paper this is worked out for a simple model of decision making on public pensions. © 1995.

Title: A new approximate GLS estimator for the linear regression model with ARMA(p, q) disturbances
Abstract: This paper introduces a new approximate GLS estimator for the linear regression model with ARMA(p, q) disturbances, which involves a simple two-step transformation procedure and is readily implemented using any basic econometrics package. © 1995.

Title: Bartlett-corrected tests for heteroskedastic linear models
Abstract: This paper uses the results in Rothenberg (Econometrica, 1984, 52, 827-842) to derive Bartlett-corrected tests for heteroskedastic linear models. The corrections are applied to three commonly used test statistics, namely: the likelihood ratio, Wald and Lagrange multiplier statistics. © 1995.

Title: Bootstrapping J-type tests for non-nested regression models
Abstract: We propose a bootstrap procedure to approximate the finite sample distributions of the J and the JA test statistics. The proposed method also overcomes the problem of the substantial size distortion of the J test when the regressors are near orthogonal. © 1995.

Title: Health capital and cross-country variation in income per capita in the Mankiw-Romer-Weil model
Abstract: This paper examines the effects of incorporating a proxy for health capital in Mankiw, Romer and Weil's empirical growth model. Results suggest a stronger and more robust relationship between income per capita and health capital, than between income per capita and educational human capital. © 1995.

Title: The complete complementarity of consumption and real balances and the strong superneutrality of money
Abstract: In the representative agent model with money in the utility function, if consumption and real balances are perfect complements, steady-state capital intensity and real balance holdings are both invariant to monetary growth, regardless of the nature of time preferences. © 1995.

Title: On flexibility in oligopoly
Abstract: This paper demonstrates that, even when firms' initial moves are simultaneous, the mere opportunity to wait out the opponent's move may be as harmful as a second-mover disadvantage. © 1995.

Title: New-firm formation in Italy: A first report
Abstract: We find that greater profitability, lower wages, job dislocations, and the degree to which an entrepreneurial environment already exists, positively influence the extent of new-firm formation in Italian provinces. © 1995.

Title: Firm's information-sharing policy and strike incidence
Abstract: A model is build to study when the firm will share the information (open the books) regarding the true state of its profit with the workers. It is shown that when book-opening is allowed, strikes cannot be an equilibrium outcome. It is argued that the pure strategy of always opening the books is adopted only because the firm fails to credibly commit itself to a mixed strategy. © 1995.

Title: Wage-employment determination and a union tax on capital: Can theory and evidence be reconciled?
Abstract: If unions appropriate quasi-rents from relation-specific capital, observed factor prices no longer reflect effective costs. Unionism has effects akin to a partial factor tax on capital. Demand curve settlements need not imply higher K/L among union firms. © 1995.

Title: Integrated-GARCH and non-stationary variances: Evidence from European stock markets during the 1920s and 1930s
Abstract: This paper provides a study of the persistence of stock return volatility in five European markets during the 1920s and 1930s. The empirical investigation is conducted using the Integrated-GARCH model. Results show that for the bulk of the series shocks to volatility are permanent, implying a significant impact of volatility on stock prices. © 1995.

Title: Stock returns, inflation, and the ‘proxy hypothesis’: A new look at the data
Abstract: This paper reexamines the proxy hypothesis of Fama (American Economic Review, 1981, 71, 545–565) as the main explanation for the negative correlation between stock returns and inflation. We look at quarterly data on industrial-production growth, monetary-base growth, CPI inflation, three-month Treasury-bill rates, and returns on the equally-weighted NYSE portfolio, for the 1954–1976 and 1977–1990 periods. Using time-series techniques, we find that production growth induces only a weak negative correlation between inflation and stock returns, and explains less of the covariance between the two series than inflation and interest-rate innovations.

Title: Optimal wage indexation with exchange rate uncertainty in an oligopolistic and unionized economy
Abstract: The role of wage indexation as a policy instrument in a model of an oligopolistic and unionized economy is examined. There is uncertainty on the future exchange rate evolution when writing labour contracts. Optimal indexation is shown to depend on product market characteristics. © 1995.

Title: A note on the measurement of mobility
Abstract: This paper shows that the minimum discrimination information statistic suggested by Kullback can be regarded as a measure of mobility. We also show the use of the Kullback measure for testing certain statistical hypotheses concerning mobility. © 1995.

Title: Individual discounting and the purchase of durables with random lifetimes
Abstract: A number of papers have suggested that the returns consumers require on energy efficiency investments are much higher than the capital market rate of return. The earlier literature has typically assumed that the lifetime of the energy-using durables is fixed. I show that if risk-neutral consumers anticipate that the lifetime is random, ignoring the randomness results in an upward bias of estimated discount rates. The bias may be as large as 35%. © 1995.

Title: On Shephard's Lemma and the continuity of compensated demand functions
Abstract: In this paper Shephard's Lemma will be proved under very weak conditions. Neither the differentiability of the cost function nor the transitivity and completeness of the underlying preferences will be assumed. © 1995.

Title: A weak utility function for acyclic preferences
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to provide a continuous weak utility function for acyclic preferences which characterizes the maximal elements of the binary relation in terms of the maxima of this function. © 1995.

Title: Wage bargaining, imperfect competition and the markup: Optimizing microfoundations
Abstract: Combining the conjectural variations and Nash bargaining approaches it is shown that the demand-insensitive markup depends on the bargaining power of unions relative to owners of firms (in addition to more standard product market characteristics).

Title: Solving stochastic optimization models with learning and rational expectations
Authors: Hans M. Amman, David A. Kendrick, Sudhakar Achath
Abstract: In this paper we present a general single-agent stochastic dynamic optimization model that is capable of dealing with learning and with rational expectations. We obtain the solution by solving at every time step the rational expectations model and then applying existing optimization schemes to derive the optimal solution. © 1995.

Title: An exposition of the decomposition in a Controlled Autoregressive Integrated Segmented Moving Average (CARISMA) model
Abstract: This paper proposes a Controlled Autoregressive Integrated Segmented Moving Average (CARISMA) model with the segmentation of the signals which postulate the disturbances acting on a time-series process. It also shows the decomposition of a CARISMA process into its components. © 1995.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index of volume 47
Author index of volume 47
The correlation of productivity growth across regions and industries in the United States
Abstract: This paper shows that productivity growth is more strongly correlated across U.S. regions than across the G7 countries. Cross-region correlations of productivity growth within a given industry are typically stronger than cross-sector correlations of productivity growth within the same region. © 1995.

Title: Innovation incentives through third-degree price discrimination in a model of patent breadth
Abstract: In a model of patent breadth generating linear demand functions, it is shown that if a potential inventor has to be given an innovation incentive, this is better done by permitting him to price discriminate than requiring uniform prices. © 1995.

Title: Market foreclosure without vertical integration
Abstract: This paper challenges the assumption that vertical integration is the sole way for upstream and downstream firms to monopolize the downstream market. Future trade, switching costs, and reputation may constitute alternatives for vertical integration and lead to dominant outcomes. © 1995.

Title: On the robustness of the argument that price-matching is anti-competitive
Abstract: The existing literature suggests that price-matching leads to monopoly prices. I show that this argument relies on an arbitrary and unrealistic restriction of the firms' strategies. In particular, if firms may adopt price-beating policies the competitive outcome prevails. © 1995.

Title: Work quality and optimal pay structure: Piece vs. hourly rates in employee remuneration
Abstract: This paper constructs a model investigating the impact of pay structure on the quantity and quality of work and its welfare implications. We prove that a change in pay structure alone could increase the utility of employers given the employees' utility level, and hence, by appropriate income distribution, could increase social welfare. © 1995.

Title: Ethnicity, race, and earnings
Authors: William Darity, David Guilkey, William Winfrey
Abstract: Utilizing the 1980 and 1990 USA censuses and Blinder-Oaxaca decompositions, we examine the extent of discrimination across women and men by ancestry and race. The charge that Blinder-Oaxaca decompositions indicate cultural rather than discriminatory differentials is addressed with two futher experiments - one that controls for color and varies culture, and one that controls for culture and varies color. © 1995.

Title: Competitive investment in higher education: The need for policy coordination
Abstract: When aggregate advanced skills determine an economy's capacity to attract external capital they function as an 'impure' public good. Education subsidies are indicated, but Nash equilibrium in education policies yields excessive subsidies if the supply of capital is not elastic. © 1995.

Title: The suboptimality of efficiency
Abstract: It is standard practice for economists to make policy recommendations on the basis of efficiency, that is maximization of aggregate income at the prices that would prevail in a competitive equilibrium. The purpose of this article is to show that in the absence of lump-sum taxes and transfers, the use of some instruments to pursue efficiency and others to pursue equity is never justified. For any outcome attained using such a division, there is a Pareto superior feasible outcome. Unlike the hypothetical Pareto-improvements used to justify the efficiency approach, this Pareto-superior outcome can be attained using available policies. © 1995.

Title: On the optimal hedge under unbiased futures prices
Abstract: We derive both necessary and sufficient conditions for optimal hedge ratios to be a constant proportion of the physical position, independently of risk-averse agents' utility functions. Assumptions frequently employed in hedging studies are discussed in relation to the conditions derived. © 1995.

Title: Bootstrapping options: An application to recapture clauses
Abstract: We use bootstrapping to value the recapture clauses in three debt restructuring agreements. The bootstrapping values are between those of the Black, and the Black and Scholes formulas. The main benefit of using bootstrapping is less reliance on an arbitrarily chosen price process. © 1995.

Title: A new class of duration measures
Authors: Kelly T. Au, David C. Thurston
Abstract: This paper presents a definition of duration for continuous time term structure models based on proportional bond price changes for instantaneous changes in spot rates. We apply this definition to derive a duration measure for Heath et al.'s (Econometrica, 1992, 60, 77-105) dynamic term structure model. © 1995.

Title: A theory of overseas joint ventures
Authors: Sugata Marjit, Udo Broll, Indrajit Mallick
Abstract: It is shown that in a case where the host-country government and a multinational firm have different risk perceptions about the foreign investment project, a suitably designed joint venture can enhance the level of foreign investment in comparison with the level attainable without such an arrangement.

Title: Poverty trap and growth with public goods
Abstract: We examine an endogenous growth model with public goods. By generalizing the assumption of linearity, we have a steady state which is asymptotically stable. That is, multiple convergence occurs. Discretionary government policy is required to sustain economic growth. © 1995.

Title: Welfare-maximizing vs. growth-maximizing shares of government investment and consumption
Abstract: This paper examines the relationship between economic growth and the investment and consumption components of government spending by modifying a specification of Barro's (Journal of Political Economics, 1990, 98, S103-S125) model to prevent asymmetry in the production process. The predictions are consistent with existing empirical findings. © 1995.

Title: Adjustment costs and price and quantity adjustment
Abstract: The role of prices and quantities in the adjustment process changes qualitatively when both price and quantity adjustment are costly. Not only relative adjustment costs but also structural characteristics affect the adjustment process which is asymmetric and implies rationing. © 1995.

Title: Are market perceptions of corporate layoffs changing?
Authors: Arjun Chatrath, Sanjay Ramchander, Frank Song
Abstract: We examine the response of stock returns to corporate layoff announcements for the 12-year period from 1981 to 1992. The results indicate a dramatic shift in the investors' perception of initiatives to reduce the number of employees. While there were negative abnormal returns associated with the announcements during the recessionary and boom periods of the 1980s, there are positive abnormal returns associated with the announcements in the early 1990s. This evidence suggests that important structural changes in the U.S. labor market may be underway. © 1995.

Title: Disaggregate stochastic trends in industrial production
Abstract: Several industries appear cointegrated at a highly disaggregated level, but the cointegration is not sufficient to reduce the system to a single common trend. Instead the results indicate that ten common trends are present in the industrial production aggregate. © 1995.

Title: Time-additive representations of preferences when consumption grows without bound
Abstract: Koopmans' classic theorem on the representation of intertemporal preference orders by time-additively separable utility functions is inapplicable to economies where consumption streams grow without bound. This paper provides a 'Koopmans-like' theorem for the case of unbounded consumption growth. Feasible consumption streams obey an asymptotic growth condition, growing in the limit no faster than an arbitrary, fixed reference stream. © 1995.

Title: Incentive contracting with hidden choices of effort and risk
Abstract: We formalize an agency model where a firm's insiders choose both unobservable effort and risk, and identify conditions under which the insiders can commit to the first-best effort and risk levels while issuing securities under limited liability. © 1995.

Title: On an asymptotic property of expected utility
Abstract: Suppose S n = Σ i = 1 n X i where the X i are elements of a sequence of random variables. Letting U be a risk-averse utility function, we show that the asymptotic approximation E[U(S n )] ∼ U(E[S n ]) holds under generally applicable conditions. © 1995.

Title: Does sunspot monetary policy matter?
Abstract: In this note we examine the effectiveness of pure, random monetary policies (i.e. changes in the money supply with no direct redistributive effects, conditioned only on some extrinsic source of uncertainty) in the framework of a general, infinite horizon economy with uncertainty. We show that these policies affect the agents' insurance opportunities and hence have in general real effects when markets are incomplete and some nominal assets are traded. The result is shown to extend, though in a slightly weaker form, to the case in which monetary policy is conditioned only on the intrinsic uncertainty in the economy. © 1995.

Title: A distinction between continuous-time and discrete-time models of uncertain lifetime
Abstract: This paper shows that continuous-time models and discrete-time models of uncertain lifetime do not generate the same predictions on the consumption and savings trajectories. A fundamental feature of uncertain lifetime is lost when time is formulated as a discrete variable.

Title: On the relationship between the Frisch and Slutsky decompositions
Abstract: We present an alternative to the traditional Slutsky decomposition for parametric changes in constrained optimization problems called the Frisch decomposition. The Frisch decomposition is useful for the analysis of dynamic models and we establish the relationship between the two decompositions.

Title: Unilateral altruism may be beneficial: A game-theoretic illustration
Abstract: This paper examines when unilateral altruism may be beneficial. The example of two-person, 2 × 2 noncooperative games is used to develop an intuitive criterion, namely that a 'role reversal' would result in the two persons' behavior changing in a similar direction. © 1995.

Title: On the possibility of stable renegotiation
Abstract: This paper discusses the relation between the concepts of stability and renegotiation. They have been shown to be incompatible in their standard definitions. Here we propose a way to restore their compatibility. © 1995.

Title: Unbiased estimation as a solution to testing for random walks
Abstract: A new formula for the mean squared error of a unit root estimator is derived. Its minimization gives rise to an estimator which is almost unbiased, unlike the maximum likelihood estimator. For this reason, it is suggested that the problem of testing for unit roots may be solved more satisfactorily in the future by using estimation techniques that lead to smaller biases. © 1995.

Title: Response surface estimates of the KPSS stationarity test
Abstract: A series of Monte Carlo experiments provide the basis for response surface estimates of approximate critical 1%, 5%, and 10% values of the Kwiatkowski et al. test of stationarity. The methodological approach closely follows MacKinnon. © 1995.

Title: Semiparametric efficiency bounds for the binary choice and sample selection models under conditional symmetry
Abstract: We consider a binary choice model and a sample selection model in which the conditional distribution of the error term, given the explanatory variables, has a symmetric form. We show that the semiparametric efficiency bounds are infinity for both models under the symmetry restriction. Hence, it is not possible to obtain a √n consistent and asymptotic normal estimator for the two models under the restriction. © 1995.

Title: Aggregated heterogeneous dependent data and the logit model: A suggested approach
Abstract: We suggest an approach for estimating logit models that are based on aggregated cell data, which may be heterogeneous as well as dependent. A test for aggregation bias is a by-product of the procedure. © 1995.

Title: Testing for unit roots in flow data sampled at different frequencies
Abstract: Perron (1989) finds that increasing the span of the point sampled data always increases the power of unit root tests. We extend the analysis to analyze flow data which have a moving average error structure. We examine five unit root tests which correct for serial correlation and find the power of some tests not to be monotonic in the span of the data. © 1995.

Title: Restrictions in labor supply estimation: Is the MaCurdy critique correct?
Abstract: According to the MaCurdy critique the Hausman method implicitly imposes restrictions that generate a positive Slutsky effect. This paper shows that the Hausman method imposes no other restrictions than alternative methods do and that the MaCurdy critique is unfounded. © 1995.

Title: Corrigendum Increases in prudence and increases in risk aversion (Economics Letters, vol. 45, no. 1, 1994, pp. 51–53)
Human capital and economic growth Tests based on the international evaluation of educational achievement
Authors: Doo Won Lee, Tong Hun Lee
Abstract: Using the secondary school science achievement scores obtained by the International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement, this paper provides more direct tests than others on the effect of human capital on economic growth, bearing important implications for theory and olicy. © 1995.

Title: Domestic taxation and international portfolio choice
Abstract: Given uncertain domestic currency denominated tax payments, risk averse investors hold a portion of their wealth in a tax hedge portfolio, which empirical results show is comprised chiefly of the domestic bond. Tax hedging may, therefore, explain the observed preference for home country assets. © 1995.

Title: Subsidized buyer credits: Atypical results in strategic trade theory
Authors: G.J. Stoelinga, J.-M. Viaene, L.T. Visscher
Abstract: Using subsidized buyer credit as a policy tool, it is shown that the general result of strategic trade policy, namely that, by committing itself to an export subsidy, any government can favorably change the outcome of the Cournot oligopoly, does not necessarily hold. © 1995.

Title: Using capital mobility to enforce commitment
Abstract: In this paper I show that capital mobility helps to enforce commitment in an environment where there is no commitment mechanism. This is done by comparing the set of sustainable outcomes à la Chari and Kehoe Journal of Political Economy, 1990, 98, 783-802, in an open economy to those in a closed economy. I show that the set in an open economy is always larger. © 1995.

Title: Nonfarm employment and the arbitrage pricing theory
Abstract: Here we use a nonlinear seemingly unrelated regression technique to demonstrate that nonfarm employment (NFE) is a priced source of risk in financial markets. We also find that NFE affects primarily cyclical industries. © 1995.

Title: Do small menu costs explain large business cycles?
Abstract: The menu cost approach to business cycle theory is amended for the costs of adjusting factor demand. This modification drastically reduces the size of the social externality commonly associated with small menu costs. The existence of menu or other (small) adjustment costs is hence not likely to have explanatory power for large scale economic fluctuations. © 1995.

Title: A note on affine aggregation
Abstract: If a vector-valued function has convex range and one of its components is related to the others by a Pareto-like condition, that component must be affine w.r.t. the others; sign restrictions on the coefficients follow from suitably strengthening the unanimity condition. The theorem is applied to social choice and decision theories. © 1995.

Title: A note on the Malmquist productivity index
Abstract: In recent years the Malmquist index has gained in popularity as a measure of productivity change. We demonstrate that, in the presence of non-constant returns to scale, the Malmquist productivity index does not accurately measure productivity change. The bias is systematic, and depends on the magnitude of scale economies. © 1995.

Title: Stochastic choice with deterministic preferences: An experimental investigation
Abstract: Most theories of decision-making under risk imply deterministic choice, yet actual choice appears to be stochastic, the resulting discrepancy being attributed to 'error'. This paper explores an alternative explanation - in which preferences are deterministic but choice is stochastic. Whilst being more satisfying from a theoretical perspective, our results show that the empirical performance is far from satisfactory. © 1995.

Title: Lexicographic rationalizability and iterated admissibility
Abstract: Using lexicographic probability systems, we define the concept of 'lexicographic rationalizability' and show it to coincide with iterated admissibility (i.e. the iterated elimination of weakly-dominated strategies). © 1995.

Title: Markov perfect equilibria in an N-player war of attrition
Abstract: A symmetric finite-player war of attrition is studied in discrete time using the notion of Markov perfect equilibria. Considering the limit of the discrete time model as the decision interval becomes arbitrarily small allows a simple characterization of the mixed strategy equilibrium. © 1995.

Title: Renegotiation in a repeated Cournot duopoly
Abstract: We investigate a repeated Cournot duopoly with strictly convex cost functions. In an example the set of Weakly Renegotiation Proof Equilibrium payoffs shrinks towards the joint profit maximizing payoff point as marginal costs are made to rise more rapidly. © 1995.

Title: Using spatial contiguity as prior information in vector autoregressive models
Abstract: Spatial contiguity information is often available information to economists modeling cross-sections of counties, states, regions, etc. yet it is frequently ignored. We show that this information can be easily incorporated in vector autoregressive models with little or no effort, using existing software, to produce improvements in forecasting performance. © 1995.

Title: A comparison of Johansen and Phillips-Hansen cointegration tests of forward market efficiency Baillie and Bollerslev revisited
Authors: Michael J. Moore, Laurence S. Copeland
Abstract: This paper tries to clarify the issues involved in comparing the use of Johansen-Juselius and Phillips-Hansen cointegration estimators in testing forward market efficiency. We present results generated by the two techniques from the dataset used by Baillie and Bollerslev. © 1995.

Title: New small sample estimators for cointegration regression: Low-pass spectral filter method
Authors: Yikang Li, G.S. Maddala, Mark Rush
Abstract: In this paper we propose a low-pass spectral filter method to estimate cointegrating vectors. The simulation study shows that the small sample properties of the proposed estimators are quite appealing. For the low signal to noise ratio cases in which fully modified least squares (FMLS) is better than ordinary least squares (OLS), filtered least squares beats OLS and filtered FMLS is dominantly better than the FMLS. © 1995.

Title: Are exchange rate changes normally distributed?
Abstract: Although assumed to be normal, daily returns in reality are leptokurtic. Monthly returns, however, are shown to be more normally distributed. Evidence was found of dependence on consecutive daily price changes, which may be an explanation for the leptokurtosis. © 1995.

Title: Stock markets and growth: A brief caveat on precautionary savings
Abstract: By allowing portfolio diversification, the introduction of a stock market may reduce precautionary savings, thereby tending to lower economic growth. The analysis incorporates well-known results from the theory of precautionary savings into an endogenous growth model of 'family businesses'. © 1995.

Title: On the definition of favorableness
Abstract: Laffont and Tirole (1993, A theory of incentives in procurement and regulation, MIT Press, Cambridge, MA) introduced 'favorableness' to compare two distributions of technologies in principal-agent analysis. Although their definition of 'favorableness' included two conditions called first-order stochatic dominance and hazard rate dominance, we show that the latter implies the former. © 1995.

Title: Licensing a sequence of innovations
Abstract: It is common for a firm which receives a license for a technology also to obtain, as part of the contract, a license for future improvements on that technology. We derive market structure reasons why such a provision might be used in a two period setting. © 1995.

Title: Unions and strategic managerial incentives
Abstract: This paper shows how strategic managerial incentives weaken union power at Cournot-Nash duopoly equilibrium, although, because of a prisoner's dilemma, unions are not averse to those contracts. Thus, one should question whether oligopolists automatically maximize profits when bargaining with trade unions. © 1995.

Title: Income taxation vs. consumption taxation in terms of the effect on savings
Abstract: We examine an income tax with a consumption tax in terms of the effect on savings adopting the differential tax incidence approach. We clarify the source of ambiguity surrounding the subject and derive a simple formula for a comparison of the two axes. © 1995.

Title: Consumption path following a tax increase: Implications for the analysis of the welfare cost of taxation
Abstract: The consumption path following a capital income tax increase is analyzed to demonstrate that short-run increases in consumption dominate future declines in consumption for a considerable time. It takes 25 years before a tax increase resutls in a loss of welfare. © 1995.

Title: Price-reducing taxation
Authors: David de Meza, John Maloney, Gareth D. Myles
Abstract: We show that the imposition of an ad valorem tax on a free-entry Cournot-Nash industry may lower price. The conditions that the cost function must satisfy for this to occur are characterised and the issue of multiple equilibria is resolved. © 1995.

Title: Asymptotic shareholder unanimity with exogenous noise
Abstract: The effect of exogenous noise on the asymptotic unanimity property is analyzed. Asymptotic unanimity is defined as the coincidence of net market value maximization of a firm with the interests of its shareholders as the economy becomes very competitive via replication. © 1995.

Title: Capital gains and asset switching
Abstract: We consider an uncertain asset defined on a Wiener dividend process, which can be exited to a certain asset for low realizations of the dividend (and asset value). We characterize the value that triggers exit (and re-entry) and observe that pure capital gains in the asset define the switch point. We observe an option value of the possibility of exit and note some links between our set-up and an alternative measurement of risk aversion. © 1995.

Title: The optimal taxation of savings and investment in an open economy
Abstract: While the taxation of savings and of investment are equivalent in a closed economy, there is a real choice between the two in an open economy setting. A tax authority can, specifically, tax the return to domestic capital following the source principle, or it can tax the return to domestic savings following the residence principle. This paper examines the optimal joint taxation of savings and investment for a country that has access to the international capital market. Conditions under which such a country should tax only savings or investment are identified. Generally, however, countries optimally tax both savings and investment. Most countries' tax systems, indeed, are a mixture of the source and residence systems of taxation. © 1995.

Title: Explaining international differences in the share of services in real expenditure
Abstract: Recent empirical evidence suggests that the share of services in real expenditure not only varies considerably across countries, but is negatively correlated with real income per capita. This paper formulates and tests a framework aimed at explaining international differences in real service expenditure shares in terms of underlying differences in exogenous factor endowments, populations and trade balances. The implications for changes in the service share of a growing economy are also noted. © 1995.

Title: On dynamic real trade models
Abstract: This paper examines the steady-state implications of differences in tax policies in an overlapping generations, two-country, two-good, dynamic model of international trade. It is also shown that, in the overlapping generations framework, production diversity along with factor-price equalization obtains in the long run. © 1995.

Title: Labor productivity during the Great Depression
Authors: Michael D. Bordo, Charles L. Evans
Abstract: During the 1929-1933 contraction, labor productivity was countercyclical in several manufacturing sectors- evidence consistent with the view that large negative demand shocks pushed the economy down a static, neoclassical production function. This evidence does not readily square with explanations for the contraction emphasizing labor hoarding and increasing returns. © 1995.

Title: Incentive compatibility without compensation
Abstract: Standard public good mechanisms rely on a transferable medium of compensation to overcome incentive compatibility constraints (Groves, Laffont). If no such medium exists, and information is incomplete, the available rules with satisfactory welfare and incentice compatibility properties require a unidimensional set of alternatives. We define a dynamic procedure for two-dimensional economies that is Pareto optimal and individually rational, with incentives as those of rules exploiting compensatory transfers. © 1995.

Title: Monitoring, diversification and managerial incentive contracts
Authors: Yoon K. Choi, Larry J. Merville
Abstract: A principal-agent model is extended to examine the optimal incentive contract when the manager is motivated by both diversification in product lines and monitoring over subordinates. © 1995.

Title: Strategic R&D success announcements
Abstract: We consider a two-stage R&D racing game in which there are two types of uncertainty: uncertainty about firm type and basic uncertainty about the feasibility of the project itself. We show that R&D success in the initial stage will be announced if it occurs early enough in the race; otherwise it will be suppressed. © 1995.

Title: The weak axiom of revealed preference and homogeneity of demand functions
Abstract: We characterize (a weak version of) the Weak Axiom of Revealed Preference for demand functions which are not necessarily homogeneous. We relate this property to the validity of the Weak Axiom and to the negative semidefiniteness of the Slutsky substitution matrices. In particular, it is shown that the Weak Axiom implies homogeneity. © 1995.

Title: Multi-valued demand and rational choice in the two-commodity case
Authors: Charles Blackorby, Walter Bossert, David Donaldson
Abstract: We show that the weak and strong congruence axioms for consumer demand correspondences are equivalent if there are only two commodities. This result generalizes a well-known analogous equivalence theorem that applies to single-valued demands. © 1995.

Title: Subgame-perfect attainment of minimax punishments in discounted two-person games
Abstract: Necessary and sufficient conditions are given for minimax payoff levels to be attained in a subgame-perfect equilibrium of repeated two-person games for sufficiently low discounting. © 1995.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
A note on the diffusion of flexible manufacturing systems technology
Abstract: This paper examines the pattern of diffusion of flexible manufacturing systems (FMS) technology across firms in the U.S. tooling and machining industry. Evidence is presented regarding the importance of compatibility standards in determining the timing of adoptions of FMS technology. © 1994.

Title: Hidden unemployment a search-theoretic interpretation
Abstract: Labor force surveys show that in the United States a significant fraction of the jobless who do not search for work, and who are therefore not classified as unemployed by official statistics, state that they 'want a job now'. A model of job search is used to interpret this phenomenon. © 1994.

Title: Pollution, the cost of public funds and endogenous growth
Authors: Jenny E. Ligthart, Frederick van der Ploeg
Abstract: Theories of endogenous growth are used to investigate the effect of environmental policy on the rate of economic growth and the provision of public goods in a second-best market outcome. Pollution gives rise to a negative environmental externality and is modeled as an inevitable by-product of production. The government faces the dual task of, on the one hand, internalising environmental externalities, and, on the other hand, raising public funds to finance public spending. A tougher environmental policy reduces the rate of economic growth, improves environmental quality, raises the optimal tax rate, and changes the composition of public spending away from productive government spending towards public consumption and abatement. The marginal cost of public funds falls (rises) if productive government spending is negligible (substantial) relative to public consumption and abatement. © 1994.

Title: Electing monetary policymakers according to inflation performance
Abstract: In this paper a dynamic model of monetary policymaking in an environment of uncertainty about a policymaker's actions is presented. In a world where policymakers' preferences are not known, and the outcomes of policymakers' actions are observed only with noise, how do voters choose among different policymakers, and how do voters learn about policymakers' preferences? The model presented solves for the actions of voters in such a noisy environment. © 1994.

Title: Problems with identifying adjustment costs from regressions of investment on q
Abstract: Most econometricians evaluate investment-q regressions by using the coefficients to estimate adjustment costs. However, these coefficients do not uniquely identify average adjustment costs or speeds, nor do they appear in the expression for marginal adjustment costs in terms of observables. © 1994.

Title: The interest sensitivity of wealth in the life cycle model
Abstract: This paper examines Modigliani's (American Economic Review, 1986, 76, 297-313) conjecture that in the simple life cycle model with Leontief consumption preferences, an increase in the interest rate from zero will cause aggregate wealth to decline. I find that the conjecture does not hold in general, but depends on the age of retirement. © 1994.

Title: Imputing a continuous income variable from grouped and missing income observations
Abstract: Most cross-sectional data sets collect income in a discrete number of categories (that is, in grouped form) to simplify the respondent's task and to encourage a response. In spite of such grouped data collection, many respondents refuse to provide information on income. This paper develops a method to impute a continuous and reliable value for income from grouped and missing income data. © 1994.

Title: Autocorrelation specification in singular equation systems
Abstract: We propose a new parametric specification of the autocorrelation matrix for singular equation systems that satisfies the restrictions of adding-up and that entails only as many parameters as the number of equations. © 1994.

Title: Testing for the exogeneity of real income in models of the poverty process evidence from post-independence India
Abstract: This paper examines the issue of the exogeneity of real income in models of the poverty process. An empirical application of specification testing procedures to data from post-independence India suggests that the incidence of poverty was determined independently of factors influencing mean income. © 1994.

Title: Unequal numbers of observations and partial efficiency gain
Abstract: This paper investigates the efficiency gain from Aitken estimation in the seemingly unrelated regression equations with unequal numbers of observations and identical regressors. We find that there is efficiency gain for the equation with a smaller number of observations only. © 1994.

Title: The measurement unit problem in estimating demand systems
A generalization of an aggregate almost ideal demand system (Economics letters, vol. 41, no. 4, 1993, pp. 369–371)
Self-reinforcing mechanisms and interactive behaviour
Abstract: We consider the possibility of switching between two options when there are benefits from compatibility and imprecise information about the other agents' choices. We find that lock-in to one of multiple equilibria is just a temporary occurrence. The system lingers at prevalence of one option with intermittent transitions to prevalence of the other. © 1994.

Title: Black-white male earnings and employment prospects in the 1970s and 1980s evidence for Britain
Authors: D.H. Blackaby, K. Clark, D.G. Leslie, P.D. Murphy
Abstract: Using a sample of around 80,000 whites and 2500 blacks, the paper highlights not just the economic disadvantage of blacks but also that this disadvantage worsened in the 1980s in Britain. © 1994.

Title: Testing an hypothesis about differences in poverty estimated from grouped data
Abstract: This paper develops procedures for testing an hypothesis about differences in poverty estimated from grouped data. The methodology developed in the paper is applied to analyze changes in poverty in India between 1983 and 1986-1987. © 1994.

Title: Simple foreign exchange market efficiency revisited
Abstract: We present empirical evidence supporting the conjecture that rejections of the simple foreign exchange market efficiency hypothesis could result from the use of statistical tests that, while asymptotically valid, may have poor finite sample properties. © 1994.

Title: Mean reversion in real exchange rates
Abstract: A modified Dickey-Fuller test, which is approximately uniformly most power invariant, is employed to examine mean reversion in real exchange rates. Results from this test provide a wider and more significant support for mean reversion than the standard Dickey-Fuller test. © 1994.

Title: The nature of credit-market failure
Abstract: Hidden knowledge gives rise to over-lending if, as evidence suggests, the returns distributions preferred by borrowers are also favoured by lenders. Even the Stiglitz-Weiss model yields over-lending when entrepreneurs are sufficiently risk averse. © 1994.

Title: Renewal theory and natural resource regulatory policy under uncertainty
Authors: Amitrajeet A. Batabyal, Seung Jick Yoo
Abstract: In this paper we show how renewal theory can be used to model a large class of natural resource regulatory problems involving systemic and policy uncertainty. We stress the policy implications of our approach and then we suggest possible extensions. © 1994.

Title: Consistency, monotonicity, and the uniform rule
Abstract: We consider the problem of fairly allocating an infinitely divisible commodity among a group of agents whose preferences are single-peaked. We show that the uniform rule is the only solution to satisfy consistency, monotonicity and individual rationality from equal division. © 1994.

Title: Ricardian equivalence are the required assumptions defensible?
Abstract: Ricardian Equivalence (RE) requires universal provision of bequests for purely altruistic reasons. This paper argues that no defensible set of values for relevant parameters is consistent with this requirement; hence observed bequests must at least partly reflect motives inconsistent with RE. © 1994.

Title: A state space model for reducing the uncertainty associated with preliminary vintages of data with an application to aggregate consumption
Abstract: In order to forecast the financial vintage of data on U.K. aggregate consumption we construct a state space model incorporating bias adjustments, a model of the measurement error process and a dynamic model for the final vintage of data. © 1994.

Title: A stochastic variance model for absolute returns
Abstract: Empirical research has shown that the autocorrelation function of a stationary series is maximised when the latter is raised to a positive power δ, which rarely coincides with two. Thus, both the GARCH and stochastic variance (SV) models fail to capture all the non-linear dependence of the data. The proposed model, in which δ equals one, improves the specification for the SV models. © 1994.

Title: Risk comparison of the inequality constrained least squares and other related estimators under balanced loss
Abstract: This paper considers the risks of the inequality constrained least squares and pre-test estimators using the balanced loss function proposed by Zellner. It is found that some of the well-known results which hold under squared error loss do not necessarily hold under a balanced loss function. © 1994.

Title: Improved estimates and forecasts of error correction models in economics
Abstract: This paper is concerned with improved estimation and better forecasting of major economic activity within the context of error correction (EC) models as pioneered by Sargan in 1964, and extended by numerous economists over the past three decades. A new and general econometric methodology with superior average mean squared errors (MSE) for EC models is introduced and, for illustration, applied to the estimation and forecasting of private consumption and demand for money in Australia for the period 1960-1992. The improvement in terms of historical and ex post forecasting MSE of our new methodology over the conventional statistical approaches currently in use for EC models is found to be up to 15.43%. © 1994.

Title: Bayesian estimation and forecasting in non-linear models application to an LSTAR model
Abstract: This paper considers the Bayesian estimation and prediction in a non-linear model by means of Monte Carlo integration with importance sampling. The importance function is derived from a first-order Taylor series expansion of the non-linear conditional expectation of the endogenous variable. The method is applied to an LSTAR model with an artificial sample. © 1994.

Title: Seventh international symposium on applied stochastic models and data analysis
Periodic properties of interpolated time series (Economics Letters 44, no. 3, 1994, pp. 221–228)
A diagnostic test without numerical integration (Economics Letters 42, nos. 2–3, 1993, pp. 129–132)
Relaxed speed limits and highway safety new evidence from California
Abstract: Focusing upon higher speed limit effects, California accident data are used to estimate monthly time series and panel data models of highway safety. Although no model finds system-wide effects, the panel data results identify significant redistributive effects not strongly evident in the time series models. Attempts to account for the differences were only partially successful. © 1994.

Title: Manipulating Lindahl equilibrium via endowments
Abstract: Simple examples of two- and three-person economies with a single private and a single public good are presented to show that the Lindahl equilibrium is individually manipulable, by donation, by destruction and by hiding of one's endowment, as well as coalitionally manipulable by intra-coalitional reallocation of endowments. © 1994.

Title: Some estimates of the effects of unemployment insurance on re-employment duration
Abstract: This paper examines how re-employment spell durations are affected by the potential unemployment benefit period (an ex-ante notion) and benefit exhaustion (an ex-post notion). The extent to which benefit duration affects re-employment duration is found to depend on the nature of the separation. © 1994.

Title: Why do dividend yields forecast stock returns?
Abstract: This paper presents a continuous time version of Lucas' (Econometrica, 1978, 46, 1426-1445) asset pricing model which is capable of explaining the observed increase in the correlation between stock returns and dividend yields as a function of the length of the holding period provided that certain weak conditions on agents' utility are satisfied. © 1994.

Title: Adding bond funds to M2 in the P-Star model of inflation
Abstract: During the early 1990s, M2 growth has been unusually weak and the P-Star model has underpredicted inflation; at the same time, bond funds have grown rapidly. We find that the P-Star model performs well recently when M2 is adjusted for bond funds. © 1994.

Title: Cyclicality of real wages among young men
Abstract: This paper analyzes the cyclical behavior of real wages received by the young men in the National Longitudinal Surveys of labor market experience. It extends the studies by Bils (Journal of Political Economy, 1985, 93, 666-689) and Tremblay (Quarterly Review of Economics and Business, 1990, 30, 90-101) by using the full duration of the survey and by examining differences in wage cyclicality across industries and between workers that change employers and those that stay with the same employer. © 1994.

Title: Convergence of least squares learning to a non-stationary equilibrium
Abstract: Linear rational expectations models can have explosive equilibria. For a linear model with multiple AR(1) solutions we show that least squares learning can converge to an explosive AR(1) equilibrium if a stability condition is met. © 1994.

Title: Dynamic consistency, consequentialism and reduction of compound lotteries
Abstract: We use Karni and Schmeidler's (Journal of Economic Theory, 1991, 54, 401-408) formalization of the concepts of dynamic consistency, consequentialism and reduction of compound lotteries in atemporal sequential decisions to show that given dynamic consistency and any of the other two concepts, the third is equivalent to the independence axiom of choice under risk in one-stage decision problems. © 1994.

Title: Moral hazard, renegotiation and debt
Abstract: Renegotiation of financial contracts is frequently observed in practice. We show how contract renegotiation based on unverifiable information improves efficiency when both ex-ante (private action) and ex-post (costly state verification) moral hazard are present simultaneously. We find that the final contract is always debt, since renegotiation allows the parties to handle sequentially the two information problems. © 1994.

Title: Dynamic stability and learning processes in 2 × 2 coordination games
Abstract: Learning processes with bounded recall and fictitious play are studied in 2 × 2 coordination games. It is shown that such learning processes never converge to a risk-dominated equilibrium, and fictitious play always converges to the risk-dominant equilibrium. Memory could be a source of risk-aversion, and certain asymmetry of bounded rationality across players could be a source of stability. © 1994.

Title: Rational expectations in limited dependent variable models
Abstract: The appropriate characterizations of rational expectations solutions in one-limit and two-limit models are derived. We prove the existence and uniqueness of the rational expectations solution for each model. Our analysis is general without imposing serial independence and the parametric distributional assumption. © 1994.

Title: The determinants of dismissals tests of the shirking model with individual data
Abstract: This study tests the shirking model by estimating dismissal equations with data on individual workers. Fires were found to depend negatively on firm size and on the local and industry unemployment rates and to depend positively on the capital-labor ratio. © 1994.

Title: A new look at incentive effects and golf tournaments
Abstract: This paper uses data from the 1992 Professional Golf Association Tour to analyze the incentive effects offered by tournaments. The results suggest that the level of the total prize money has an insignificant effect on the total score (output) of the players (workers). This conclusion contradicts the findings of an earlier paper by Ehrenberg and Bognanno (Journal of Political Economy, 1990, 98, 1307-1324). © 1994.

Title: Neutrality and the private provision of public goods with incomplete information
Authors: Mark Gradstein, Shmuel Nitzan, Steven Slutsky
Abstract: In this paper we introduce incomplete information about income into a standard model of private provision of public goods. Generally, one obtains neutrality results similar in nature to those obtained in the complete information model. However, with incomplete information, several additional difficulties exist in attaining neutrality. For neutrality to hold, (i) positive contributions have to be made by all individual types, (ii) any redistribution of income must not convey information to the individuals, and (iii) any redistribution must not depreciate the private information individuals have. © 1994.

Title: Tax reform with sub-additive and nested-additive preferences
Abstract: This paper characterizes the direction of tax reform when preferences are sub-additive or nested-additive. This information should be useful for researchers doing empirical research on tax reform based on some form of additive functions for preferences. © 1994.

Title: Residual securities and personal taxes
Abstract: This paper suggests that a residual security should have a tax advantage in a model which includes personal taxes and admits the possibility of low income states. © 1994.

Title: Exchange rate variability and the flow of international trade
Abstract: This study uses a GARCH (Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity) model to test if real exchange rate volatility has an adverse effect on the value of U.S. imports from Canada. We find that exchange rate uncertainty has a negative and statistically significant affect on trade flows. © 1994.

Title: The optimal consumption-wealth relation and the permanent income-life cycle hypothesis under recursive preferences
Abstract: In preferences are of the Uzawa-Epstein recursive kind, an individual agent's optimal consumption-wealth relation can always be expressed in the form of c(t)=α(·)W(t), where the factor α(·) is determined by the future paths of consumption and real interest rate. The proportionality of this relation as contended by the permanent income-life cycle hypothesis requires that the instantaneous discounting function be constant and that the instantaneous utility function be iso-elastic, thereby implying that the underlying preferences are homothetic. The converse also holds. Thus, the preference homotheticity and the proportionality of the optimal consumption-wealth relation are equivalent. © 1994.

Title: Repeat purchases under quality uncertainty
Abstract: If the quality of a seller's products is uncertain and a single purchase cannot reveal the seller's expected quality, all sellers may benefit if their mean quality or type is not revealed. © 1994.

Title: A note on Pareto optimality in differential information economies
Abstract: A mechanism is posterior efficient if the agents' expected utilities, given the outcomes of this mechanism, can never be Pareto improved. A non-revealing (resp. completely revealing) mechanism is posterior efficient if and only if it is incentive interim (resp. ex post) efficient. © 1994.

Title: A fixed-point theorem for decreasing mappings
Abstract: A normal form game has a Nash equilibrium if all the strategy sets are one-dimensional, each player's utility only depends on his own strategy and the sum of the strategies of the partners, and the best replies are non-increasing. © 1994.

Title: The shapley value of resale-proof trades
Abstract: This paper studies the Shapley value, Ψ, of transferable utility games associated with resale-proof trades of information. Ψ is in the core iff there is exactly one minimal resale-proof set. A simple expression for Ψ is obtained for 'symmetric' games; and some bounds are given for ψ in non-symmetric cases. © 1994.

Title: Connections between GARCH and stochastic coefficients (SC) models
Abstract: GARCH and SC models are suggested as less restrictive alternatives to the conventional models in the econometric literature. Connections between them are made explicit in this paper. © 1994.

Title: Weighted generalized least squares estimation for complex survey data
Abstract: If data are stratified and clustered, the intra-cluster correlation can be used to improve the efficiency of weighted estimators. However, ‘weighted generalized least squares’ (WGLS) is potentially biased. Two specification tests are presented, along with an unbiased ‘conditional WGLS’ estimator.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Inequality aversion, resource depletion and sustainability
Abstract: A welfare function which incorporates aversion to inequality across generations is applied to the 'cake-eating' problem and it is shown that sustainability with positive welfare will be ensured provided that inequality aversion is sufficiently strong. © 1994.

Title: Knowledge-based growth with exogenous population evolution
Abstract: We investigate a centrally-planned, infinite-horizon, single-good economy in which the labour force grows exogenously and new knowledge is generated in a separate R&D sector. Various balanced growth scenarios are studied and characterized, using a general production technology and a broad class of social utility functions. © 1994.

Title: The turnover costs and the Solow condition in an efficiency wage model with intertemporal optimization
Abstract: This paper sets out an intertemporal optimizing model embodying the efficiency wage hypothesis, and examines whether the Solow condition is valid. It is shown that, unless the turnover costs are absent and the voluntary quitting rate is independent from wage offer, the effort-wage elasticity is less than unity. Our result thus can be regarded as a theoretical solution of the Akerlof and Yellen criticism on the efficiency wage theory. © 1994.

Title: A note on the substitution between wage and non-wage benefits in spot labour markets
Abstract: Recent empirical work suggests that spot labour market workers have a strong preference towards wages over fringe benefits. This paper provides a theoretical framework based on this finding. After a discussion of the utility function and equilibrium, the paper proceeds to a comparative statics analysis. An important result is that workers spend all extra compensation on wages only. This is shown to be true in the case that wage benefits are taxed. Furthermore, proportional taxes have no effect for workers' choice between wage and non-wage benefits. © 1994.

Title: Recent trends in white-black earnings differentials
Abstract: This paper tracks white-black earnings differentials between 1967 and 1986 using panel data. Separate estimates are computed for males and females. Corrections for selectivity bias have been made, and Neumark's modified version of the Oaxaca procedure is used to derive estimates of the earnings gap. The finding of secular decline in the white-black earnings gap is re-established. © 1994.

Title: Poverty rankings using noisy data on living standards
Abstract: A consistent and robust poverty ranking will be unaffected by the omission of random and identically distributed idiosyncratic determinants of individual welfare. However, ambiguities in ranking due to heterogeneity in error distributions are difficult to resolve on a priori grounds. © 1994.

Title: Budget shares, distributional characteristics and the direction of tax reform
Abstract: We present a distinction between budget shares and distributional characteristics in the framework of the marginal tax reform approach of Ahmad and Stern (Journal of Public Economics, 1984, 25, 259-298). In a simplified case we show that distributionally motivated tax changes based on budget shares will not be welfare improving. © 1994.

Title: Irrational behavior in the AT&T investment game
Abstract: We test for Nash equilibrium in the results of a nationwide investment game, and show that, at a very high confidence level, the hypothesis of Nash equilibrium can be rejected. Either players did not respond to the considerable incentives to win, or they failed to reach an equilibrium. © 1994.

Title: Growth and its disparity in rich and poor regions
Authors: James L. Seale, Henri Theil, Sri Devi Deepak
Abstract: We use international comparison data to relate the regional growth and the inequality across countries for four regions of the non-Communist world: The North, South-East Asia, South-Central Asia and Sub-Saharan Asia. The results are compared with findings by Kuznets and others. © 1994.

Title: The foreign exchange market efficiency hypothesis revisiting the puzzle
Abstract: The Engle-Granger bivariate (strong form) and the Johansen-Juselius multivariate (weak form) cointegration tests are performed between the spot and forward rate series over multiple horizons to test the market efficiency hypothesis (MEH). © 1994.

Title: Transfers or public good provision? A political allocation perspective
Abstract: Employing an extended rent-seeking model this paper focuses on the problem faced by an optimizing politician of allocating a given budget among monetary transfers to individuals, monetary transfers to groups and public-good transfers to groups. © 1994.

Title: Monotonicity, dominance and the Pareto principle
Abstract: We examine the implications of three similar criteria that are commonly used in welfare economics and the analysis of inequality and poverty - income dominance, monotonicity and the Pareto principle - within the context of income-distribution comparisons. We show that whilst there is a simple logical relationship between the first two criteria, the third is neither implied by nor implies the other two unless an assumption of individual indifference to income distribution is made. Similar problems arise with a fourth criterion - utility dominance - that is a natural counterpart to income dominance. © 1994.

Title: On the optimality of cost-plus non-uniform pricing in vertical control problems
Abstract: This paper argues that cost-plus non-linear contracts are the general solution of the vertical control problem where there are multiple upstream firms, one downstream firm and no uncertainty. Two-part tariffs are only optimal if upstream firms have linear costs. Cost-plus contracts are also shown to be a solution of the bilateral monopoly problem. © 1994.

Title: Capital constraints and optimal hedging in factor markets
Abstract: This paper examines the optimal hedging strategy of a capital-constrained firm which faces an uncertain price of one of its inputs. Risk-neutral firms take either a long or short position in the futures/forward market when capital constrained, despite the absence of a speculative motive. Key parameters which govern the firm's position include the elasticity of demand for the hedged factor with respect to output and the elasticity of supply. © 1994.

Title: Optimal vintage capital utilisation Supportability conditions
Abstract: This paper is aimed at showing that, if the extensive lifetime of vintage capital equipment is limited, there exists a time-truncation in the vintage capital utilisation programming span. It is shown that output allocations generated by vintage-truncated capital equipment are supported by both prices and vintage-weighted capital productivities and constitute a price quasi-equilibrium (PQE). © 1994.

Title: Time-of-use electricity pricing
Abstract: Seemingly unrelated regression (SURE) analysis is applied to data from a British time-of-use (TOU) pricing experiment. It is shown that consumption changes are statistically significant and important but vary by consumption strata. The results have implications for demand system analysis of TOU data. © 1994.

Title: Social rents, interest rates, and growth
Abstract: We present a simple OLG model with a convex technology in which physical capital exhibits a productive externality, and workers receive part of the social rents generated by that externality. This setup allows for sustained growth without incurring poverty traps. Moreover, every equilibrium path displays constant interest rates as suggested by some empirical evidence. © 1994.

Title: The Moebius strip and a social choice paradox
Abstract: A remarkable topological property of the Moebius strip is equivalent to the Chichilnisky impossibility theorem in social choice theory, which states the impossibility of finding a continuous, anonymous and unanimous aggregation rule for two agents, defined on the unit circle. © 1994.

Title: Buy-in through goldplating
Abstract: Bower and Osband (RAND Journal of Economics, 1991, 22, 107-119) recognized the role of the defense profit policy as a 'handicapping device' that induces low cost firms to aggressively buy in for future profits. When designs are variable and actively competed in the bidding stage, this paper finds that this handicapping role of the profit policy is weakened by the fact that firms can dilute bidding competition by inflating quality. © 1994.

Title: The impact of taxes on the privatization of municipal services
Authors: Robert A. McGuire, Robert L. Ohsfeldt
Abstract: Municipal governments incur a cost of privatization through taxes paid to other governments by private contractors producing municipal services. Empirical analysis finds lower tax costs do not increase privatization of school transportation. © 1994.

Title: A note on backward compatibility
Abstract: A system innovator with a monopoly over the production of both hardware and software chooses to make a new system not backward compatible with the software of the preceding generation when profits on sales of new software outweigh the development costs. © 1994.

Title: On the economic efficiency of liquidated damages
Abstract: Recently, Aghion and Bolton (American Economic Review, 1987, 77, 388-401) have shown that liquidated damages can serve as a barrier to entry and may therefore be socially harmful. In this paper I show that liquidated damages remain excessive and continue to serve as a barrier to entry even in the presence of relationship-specific investment, but may nevertheless have an overall positive effect on welfare. © 1994.

Title: The duration of unemployment as a signal
Abstract: A model is studied in which the unemployment duration of job applicants affects firms' hiring decisions. The equilibrium wage offered to applicants is decreasing in their unemployment duration. A fraction of the workers whose unemployment spell exceeds a critical length withdraws from the labor market. © 1994.

Title: Occupational segregation and wages in Australia
Abstract: The Australian labour market is characterised by a gender wage differential of about 13%. This paper investigates the claim that this is associated with the absence of appropriate evaluation ofthe work performed in female occupations. About 40% of the differential might be removed by the implementation of true comparable worth, a figure at the upper end of the range reported for the US labour market. © 1994.

Title: Temporal dependence in asset pricing models
Abstract: Estimating and testing conditional models in an unconditional statistical context often results in model disturbances that display temporal dependence. This paper presents an economic explanation for temporal dependence found in disturbances of financial returns in many studies. © 1994.

Title: Pareto ranking optimal tariffs under foreign monopoly
Abstract: This paper shows that whether or not optimal ad valorem and specific tariffs can be Pareto ranked for a country trading with a foreign monopoly firm depends on parameters of the economy. © 1994.

Title: Profit-sharing and welfare in an export subsidy game
Abstract: This paper studies an export subsidy game in a duopoly in which one firm engages in sharing profits with its union. In a non-cooperative equilibrium of an export subsidy game without any cost advantage of firms, the export subsidy to the profit-sharing firm is smaller than the export subsidy to the non-sharing firm, and the output of the profit-sharing firm is smaller than the output of the non-sharing firm. Thus, in an export subsidy game, a profit-sharing contract reduces the welfare in the country. © 1994.

Title: Product quality regulation in open economies
Abstract: The presence of quality and safety regulations provides an explanation for comparative advantage and the basis for trade in regulated open economies. This paper investigates these trade issues in a factors-specific model of quality regulation. © 1994.

Title: Is the UK treasury bill rate a good proxy for expected inflation in the United Kingdom?
Abstract: The conjecture that short-term interest rates reflect agents' changing perceptions of future inflation is known as the Fisher Effect. In this paper we test for both short- and long-run Fisher Effects using UK data. Using both Kalman filtering techniques and the Johansen procedure for inference on cointegrated time series we find no evidence of short- or long-run Fisher Effects in the United Kingdom. Since in testing, for example, the relationship between equity returns and expected inflation many researchers use a short government bill rate as a proxy for expected inflation, the main implication of our findings is that it would be inappropriate to use such a proxy for expected inflation in the United Kingdom. © 1994.

Title: Unemployment persistence under profit sharing
Abstract: In a simple dynamic model with an employment externality generated by union bargaining, an increase in a mandated rate of profit sharing reduces not only the steady-state unemployment rate but also the persistence of unemployment out of steady state. © 1994.

Title: Borrowing constraints, income expectations and the Euler equation
Abstract: Using the Euler Equation, I show that under borrowing constraints consumption growth will depend not only on contemporaneous expected income, as the model with 'rule-of-thumb' consumers predicts, but also on future expected income. Historical data confirm this insight. © 1994.

Title: Investment under uncertainty and the value of the firm
Abstract: The investment behavior of a monopolistic firm with a constant returns to scale production function facing a randomly shifting, elastic demand is examined. Uncertainty can have a negative effect on the value of the firm and on investment. © 1994.

Title: On the relation between Nash equilibria and undominated strategies for two person, finite games
Abstract: We show the equivalence between the existence of Nash equilibria for two-person finite games and sets of strategies being undominated relative to each other. An example shows that similar results will not be true for games with three or more players. © 1994.

Title: A range-CUSUM test with recursive residuals
Abstract: A range test for the constancy of regression coefficients based on cumulated sums of recursive residuals is proposed, and its asymptotic null distribution is derived. Simulation results suggest that the proposed test is useful for different alternatives. © 1994.

Title: A note on measurement error and Euler equations
Abstract: The paper describes how to avoid taking log-linear approximations of non linear decision rules when measurement errors are present. This is achieved by imposing some distributional assumptions on these errors. © 1994.

Title: Status variables in fixed-effect models
Abstract: A merely technical application of fixed-effects models without considering the unique meaning of each status variable can yield incomplete and biased results. This point is demonstrated by reestimating published results of the effect of marital status or earnings. © 1994.

Title: A note on calculating the autocovariances of the fractionally integrated ARMA models
Abstract: The autocovariances of the stationary fractionally integrated ARMA model derived by Sowell (Journal of Econometrics, 1992, 53, 165-188) are complicated functions of hypergeometric functions. We give an alternative expression for these autocovariances which can be easily and accurately computed by computers. © 1994.

Title: Fractional integration analysis of long-run behavior for US macroeconomic time series
Abstract: We apply a new ARFIMA approach to distinguish between the trend and difference stationary models of long-run dynamics for a well-known representative macroeconomic dataset. Our results strengthen the case for the difference stationary model for these series. © 1994.

Title: Long-range dependence in the conditional variance of stock returns
Authors: Nuno Crato, Pedro J.F de Lima
Abstract: We examine persistence in the conditional variance of U.S. stock returns indexes. Our results show evidence of long memory in high-frequency data, suggesting that models of conditional heteroskedasticity should be made flexible enough to accommodate these empirical findings. © 1994.

Title: Testing for unit roots in seasonally adjusted data
Abstract: The power of the Dickey-Fuller test is known to be low if seasonal data are adjusted via a moving average filter. I extend this result by considering alternatives to moving average filtering; a preliminary regression on dummy variables, and a frequency domain, band-pass filter. © 1994.

Title: Efficiency of least-squares-estimation of polynomial trend when residuals are autocorrelated
Authors: Ralf Busse, Roland Jeske, Walter Krämer
Abstract: We derive lower bounds for the efficiency of OLS relative to GLS in the polynomial trend model where disturbances are stationary AR(1). © 1994.

Title: Portfolio characterization of risk aversion
Abstract: Investment behavior in a portfolio choice situation with one risky and one riskless asset reflects investors' attitude toward risk. A higher fraction of wealth invested in a risky asset indicates smaller risk aversion.
