We examine the equivalence of this way of measuring risk aversion with the standard way based on the Arrow-Pratt measure in several cases distinguished by specification of short-sales restrictions for both assets. © 1994.

Title: Why are extended warranties so expensive?
Abstract: Intense users place greater demands than other users on repair services during the period covered by the manufacturer's basic warranty. An extended warranty with a price exceeding expected cost permits the recovery of the extra costs of servicing more intense users. © 1994.

Title: Nash equilibrium with mark-up-pricing oligopolists
Abstract: If business managers formulate strategies in terms of mark-ups, then it is natural to think they will think of their rivals' actions in these terms. For a market characterized by constant elasticity of demand and supply, the mark-up equilibrium is derived and compared with the traditional monopoly, Cournot and perfectly competitive equilibria. We also compute the 'revenue as strategy' equilibria. © 1994.

Title: A theorem of voting rules and budget deficits
Abstract: A theorem showing that deficits under a procedure requiring expenditures to accompany revenues as they are enacted, followed by a vote on the size of deficit, are smaller than under current procedure in which votes on expenditures and taxes are unlinked. © 1994.

Title: Inside information and management buyouts of closely held firms
Abstract: I study a buyout game in which management has inside information, produces a known gain upon buyout, and bargains with a single owner. The major result is that the buyout premium is negatively related to the gain. © 1994.

Title: Daily seasonality in stock returns
Abstract: Daily seasonality in stock markets is one of the most intriguing problems in financial economics and a true challenge to the efficiency hypothesis. This paper examines daily seasonality in the New York, Tokyo, London, Frankfurt, Paris and Madrid stock markets in recent years. The results obtained are quite different from the patterns described in existing literature which examines earlier periods. © 1994.

Title: The transfer problem in the context of public goods
Abstract: It is argued that if each country is egalitarian then the standard Samuelsonian proposition, that an international transfer benefits the recipient and harms the donor nation, remains valid in the context of privately provided public goods. © 1994.

Title: Price-preference vs. tariff policies in government procurement auctions
Abstract: This paper compares tariff policies with price-preference policies in auctioning government procurement. I demonstrate that the two policies are equivalent both in terms of the government's expected procurement costs and the domestic and foreign bidder's expected profits. © 1994.

Title: Tariff behavior in five European countries: Further evidence
Authors: Alok K. Bohara, William H. Kaempfer
Abstract: Temporary movements in the average tariff rate for a country can lead to intertemporal substitution effects. A five-country model of tariff movements is estimated in a generalized system. The tariff formation process follows a random walk for the United Kingdom, Denmark, Sweden, and France, which implies that tariff changes can be viewed as permanent in those countries. However, in Switzerland the cumulative impulse responses to a tariff shock imply not only shock persistence, but shock magnification. © 1994.

Title: Optimal policies in a dynamic oligopoly model of international trade
Abstract: The paper generalises the static Cournot oligopoly model of international trade to a dynamic context and derives optimal trade policies. It is found that an export subsidy is the optimal instrument for intervention by the domestic country when the domestic and foreign firms compete only in a third market. When domestic consumption is allowed for the optimal policy is a production subsidy. It is found that unlike the static Cournot case, in the dynamic version the reaction curves of both firms shift when a tax/subsidy is imposed. © 1994.

Title: The random walk hypothesis of the exchange rate
Abstract: We show that the exchange rate can follow a random walk without assuming risk neutrality. We are thus able to derive a random walk hypothesis for the exchange rate which is associated with a risk premium that may differ from zero. © 1994.

Title: Social efficiency of bubbles in the Grossman and Helpman endogenous growth model
Abstract: Using a particular specification of the expectation process, I show that a weak but permanent over-evaluation of financial assets may exist in the Grossman and Helpman (1991, Innovation and growth in the global economy, MIT Press, Cambridge, MA) endogenous growth model with horizontal produce differentiation and that the resulting competitive equilibrium is socially optimal. © 1994.

Title: Homothetic non-parametric production models
Abstract: A test for homotheticity in the context of non-parametric production models is proposed. We also show how a homothetic piece-wise linear technology can be constructed from an observed input-output data set. © 1994.

Title: Repeated decisions and attitudes to risk
Abstract: In contrast to the underpinnings of expected utility, the experimental pilot study results reported here suggest that current decisions may be influenced both by past decisions and by the possibility of making decisions in the future. © 1994.

Title: A simple extension of the Dasgupta-Maskin existence theorem for discontinuous games with an application to the theory of rent-seeking
Abstract: I state that upper-semi-continuity of the sum of payoffs is not necessary for the classical existence result in symmetric games by Dasgupta and Maskin. This is then applied to the theory of rent-seeking to show that there always exists some Nash equilibrium in mixed strategies in the simultaneous-move game by Tullock in which no `overdissipation can occur. © 1994.

Title: The Nash solution and Independence of Revealed Irrelevant Alternatives
Abstract: This paper shows that Nash's Independence of Irrelevant Alternatives (IIA) axiom can be replaced with a weaker independence axiom, Independence of Revealed Irrelevant Alternatives (IRIA). © 1994.

Title: Optimal properties of exponentially weighted forecasts in the presence of different information sources
Abstract: Muth (Journal of the American Statistical Association, 1960, 55, 299-306) showed that the exponentially weighted average of past observations of a random walk plus noise process minimizes the mean squared forecast error of the series. This paper generalizes Muth's result to the case where agents have access to different sources of information which can be used to improve their forecast. © 1994.

Title: Statistical inference for decile means
Authors: Charles M. Beach, K.Victor Chow, John P. Formby, George A. Slotsve
Abstract: This paper provides a simple set of formulas to compute standard errors, variances, and covariances for a set of decile mean incomes. This facilitates the statistical implementation of the Rank Dominance criterion for comparing two income (or wealth) distributions. © 1994.

Title: Some forecasting applications of partially adaptive estimators of ARIMA models
Abstract: This paper investigates the relative forecasting performance of some partially adaptive estimators of ARIMA models based on flexible parametric error distributions which allow for kurtosis and skewness. These methods are used to obtain forecasts of some well-known data sets. © 1994.

Title: Prewhitened unit root test
Abstract: It is known that the Phillips-Perron's modified Z α test as an approximation to the Dickey-Fuller test does not perform well when the process is generated by the unit ARMA(1, 1) model: y t = y t-1 + e t + θe t-1 with θ close to - 1. This paper shows that if the process is suitably prewhitened the performance of the modified Z α test is dramatically recovered in such a case. © 1994.

Title: A comparison of tests of linear hypotheses in cointegrated vector autoregressive models
Abstract: This paper compares the performance of alternative asymptotic tests of linear hypotheses on the cointegration space and the adjustment space. It is shown that application of simple correction factors typically improves the properties of likelihood ratio test statistics in small-sample situations. © 1994.

Title: Non-parametric test of derivative restrictions robust to functional misspecification
Abstract: This paper proposes non-parametric test of derivative restrictions using a goodness of fit measure of the regression. The test statistic is constructed using the sum of squared residuals from the non-parametric kernel regression. © 1994.

Title: Computation of the GLS estimator of a model with anticipated and unanticipated effects
Abstract: This paper demonstrates that the two-step GLS estimator of a model with current anticipated and unanticipated effects can be computed from an artificial double length regression using any standard econometric software. This computational procedure follows from a simple matrix inversion result. © 1994.

Title: Partial vertical integration under market uncertainty
Abstract: This paper shows that partial vertical integration arises in a market environment with risk-averse producers, cost and demand uncertainties, and production lag. © 1994.

Title: A note on product tampering
Authors: Chong Ju Choi, Stephen Gettings, Carlo Scarpa
Abstract: Although product tampering has become an increasingly prevalent issue in recent years, as far as we know there have been no theoretical attempts to analyse its possible public policy implications. This paper tries to present some preliminary theoretical approaches to aspects of produ ct tampering. © 1994.

Title: A microscopic model of the stock market
Authors: Moshe Levy, Haim Levy, Sorin Solomon
Abstract: We present a model of the stock market based on the behavior of individual investors. Simulations exhibit rich phenomena which include cycles, booms, and crashes. Low dividend yield and more homogeneous market participants are shown to induce crashes. © 1994.

Title: Persistence in real variables under alternative exchange rate regimes
Authors: Guglielmo Maria Caporale, Sarantis Kalyvitis, Nikitas Pittis
Abstract: In this paper we try to establish empirically whether a different degree of persistence is found in real variables under alternative nominal exchange rate systems. The measure of persistence employed is the modified rescaled range statistic proposed by Lo (Econometrica, 1991, 59, 1279-1313), which tests for the presence of long-range dependence after having accounted for a wide class of short memory processes. The empirical results indicate a systematic increase in persistence in real variables under floating. © 1994.

Title: Temporary foreign exchange subsidies, anticipated devaluation, and the Mexdollar anomaly
Abstract: Prior to Mexico's economic crisis of 1982, a dramatic drop in the 'dollarization ratio' coincided with higher expected peso depreciation. I hypothesize that the anomalous result is due to convertibility risk, and provide a formal interpretation using an optimizing model. © 1994.

Title: Can revenue maximizing export taxes yield higher welfare than welfare maximizing export taxes?
Abstract: In this paper we show that commodity exporting countries may obtain a higher welfare under revenue maximizing export taxes than under welfare maximizing export taxes. This result cannot be obtained in the traditional two-country models. © 1994.

Title: Risky storage and the value of money
Abstract: This paper investigates the valuation of fiat money in a Wallacian overlapping generations economy with idiosyncratic storage risk. Unlike Wallace's own result, the value of money can be positive independent of the rate of population growth. © 1994.

Title: The importance of monetary shocks
Abstract: Monetary innovations explain more of output fluctuations than interest rates do in a variance decomposition using pre-Federal Reserve data. This is consistent with McCallum's (Economics Letters, 1983, 13, 167) conjecture that the relative importance of interest rates in postwar data results from the Federal Reserve targeting interest rates. © 1994.

Title: Should we test the life cycle—permanent income hypothesis with food consumption data?
Abstract: Most household consumption studies use food consumption data. I show that in aggregate data one cannot reject the life cycle hypothesis using food, but can reject it using other goods. Existing micro tests of the life cycle hypothesis thus may have low power. © 1994.

Title: Money and markets
Abstract: In a search model of endogenous money it is shown that the introduction of markets increases the efficiency of the economy. Markets help the agents to coordinate their actions. The organization of the economy in markets becomes feasible only with the introduction of money. Unlike in a marketless economy the commodity holder's decision to actively move and search or to wait for a buyer becomes irrelevant. © 1994.

Title: Three-moments ranking and expected-utility maximization
Abstract: The ranking of prospects based on three-moments implies the ranking based on expected-utility maximization under consistently risk-averse utility functions if the distributions defined on a positive domain have equal means and a first-order stochastic dominance relationship. © 1994.

Title: Increases in prudence and increases in risk aversion
Abstract: This paper determines necessary and sufficient conditions for increases in absolute prudence to lead to increases in risk aversion, and vice versa. © 1994.

Title: Empirical evidence of political influence on the size distribution of income in the United States (1959–1991)
Abstract: Political influence on the size distribution of income is tested in a statistical model using annual U.S. data for 1959-1991. We present empirical evidence that both Democratic administration and reelected president appear to have significant downward redistributive effects. © 1994.

Title: An alternative characterization of the extended claim-egalitarian solution
Abstract: Some monotonicity conditions for bargaining problems with claims are presented. They are used to provide a characterization of the extended claim-egalitarian solution. © 1994.

Title: Estimation of sample selection bias models by the maximum likelihood estimator and Heckman's two-step estimator
Abstract: In this paper, methods of estimating models with sample selection biases are analyzed. Finite sample properties of the maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) and Heckman's two-step estimator are compared using Monte Carlo experiments. © 1994.

Title: Is there a unit root in U.S. real GNP?
Abstract: To avoid the controversy surrounding the Dickey-Fuller tests for unit roots, this paper estimates a flexible trend model for U.S. GNP. Four different data sets that span the years 1869-1991 are used. For all sub-periods, and for all series there is strong evidence of a stochastic trend. © 1994.

Title: Aggregate output dynamics in the twentieth century
Abstract: This study shows that annual output data of the G7 countries in the twentieth century are better characterized as transitory deviations from a (shifting) growth trend than as integrated processes. Furthermore, I find no two countries share common business cycles. © 1994.

Title: A diagnostic test for the sources of persistence in individuals' decisions
Abstract: This paper presents a diagnostic test for the different sources of persistence in individuals' decisions (like brand loyalty): (1) state dependence, (2) serial correlation and (3) a direct dependence of current decisions on previous exogenous variables. This test successfully distinguishes among the different sources 95% of the time. © 1994.

Title: On the power of unit root tests against fractional alternatives
Abstract: We investigate the probability of rejecting the I(1) hypothesis when unit root tests are applied to fractionally integrated time series. Especially the augmented Dickey-Fuller test performs poorly. Our analytical arguments are supported by Monte Carlo experiments. © 1994.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Revelation in informational dynamic settings (Economics letters 33, 1990, pp. 237–239)
Who should abate carbon emissions?
Abstract: We review the optimal pattern of carbon emission abatements across countries in a simple multi-country world. We model explicitly (with the model in Chichilnisky, 1993b) the fact that the atmosphere is a public good. Within this framework we establish conditions for it to be necessary for optimality that the marginal cost of abatement be the same in all countries. These conditions are quite restrictive, and amount to either ignoring distributional issues between countries or operating within a framework within which lump-sum transfers can be made between countries. These results have implications for the use of tradeable emission permits, which as normally advocated will lead to the equalization of marginal abatement costs across countries. The observation that the atmosphere is a public good implies that we may need to look at a Lindahl equilibrium rather than a Walrasian equilibrium in tradeable permits.

Title: Regional capital imbalances and the removal of interstate banking restrictions
Abstract: An analysis of differences in the openness of interstate banking laws suggests that both regional banking difficulties and the strategic concerns of large banking organizations influenced the recent movement toward nationwide banking in the United States. © 1994.

Title: A cointegration test of the optimal seigniorage model
Abstract: This paper tests Mankiw's (Journal of Monetary Economy, 1987, 20, 327-341) optimal seigniorage model. Under quadratic cost functions of taxation and inflation, the rates of inflation and taxes have unit roots and they must be cointegrated. The hypothesis of optimal policy is rejected in five countries. © 1994.

Title: Should we care? psychological barriers in stock markets
Authors: Kees G. Koedijk, Philip A. Stork
Abstract: For three out of five major stockmarkets it is found that those levels which are a multiple of a hundred are approached and transgressed relatively infrequently. We explicitly test for the effect of sample bias and conduct a forecasting experiment. © 1994.

Title: Pricing of permanent and transitory volatility for U.S. stock returns
Abstract: This study presents a new GARCH model decomposing total volatility into a permanent and a transitory component. It is examined whether there are any differences in pricing between these two volatility components. © 1994.

Title: Import prices, export prices and the current account
Abstract: We demonstrate that there is an important asymmetry between the effects of temporary import and export price shocks on the current account that is ignored in theoretical and empirical work. This asymmetry is found to hold for U.S. and U.K. data. © 1994.

Title: On an additional condition for factor-price equalisation in intertemporal Heckscher-Ohlin models
Abstract: In order that factor-price equalisation results from free trade in intertemporal Heckscher-Ohlin models, individual discount rates must be equal. When this condition is violated and both countries lie within the cone of diversification, they produce both goods though factor prices are not equalised. © 1994.

Title: What is the neutrality of money?
Abstract: Two objections are made to the concept of superneutrality of money. It is not the logical counterpart to static neutrality of money. Secondly, it would be preferable to focus on the impact of real balances not solely on the capital-labor ratio and the real rate but on a broader range of real variables. © 1994.

Title: Duality between discounted and undiscounted models of optimal growth for a class of utility functions
Abstract: Optimal growth theory has restricted comparison between optimal programs from discounted and undiscounted models to the case where the discount factor is arbitrarily close to unity. This paper extends the comparison to any value of the discount factor by demonstrating the following duality for the class of homogeneous felicity functions: if there exists an optimal program in the discounted utility model, then the discounted version of the optimal program is optimal in the catching up sense in a transformed undiscounted utility model. © 1994.

Title: An alternative proof of the Hurwicz (1972) impossibility theorem
Abstract: Hurwicz (in: C.B. McGuire and R. Radner, edn., Decision and organisation, 2nd edn. (University of Minnesota Press, Minneapolis) pp. 297-336) proved that for any classical private goods environment with two or more individuals, there is no incentive-compatible direct revelation mechanism whose dominant strategy equilibrium outcomes are Pareto efficient and individually rational. I present a simple alternative proof which is constructive. © 1994.

Title: Vanity, superstition and auction price
Abstract: Applying the hedonic approach, we find substantial and significant effects of vanity and superstition on the price of a Hong Kong license plate auctioned during 1989-1991. The superstition effect is culturally dependent. What is considered to be unlucky in Western Societies is dismissed in Hong Kong. By the same token, a Hong Kong license plate thought to bring good fortune is meaningless to a non-Cantonese-speaking person. © 1994.

Title: Maximal elements of not necessarily acyclic binary relations
Abstract: The existence of maximal elements for binary relations is analyzed without imposing transitivity or convexity conditions. An acyclic relation is constructed in such a way that some maximal elements of this new relation characterize maximal elements of the original one. © 1994.

Title: Arrow's choice axiom
Abstract: If a choice correspondence satisfies Arrow's choice axiom then it has a complete and transitive rationalization, even if the domain does not include any sets with fewer than m members, where m is a given positive integer. © 1994.

Title: Strongly consistent two-player game forms
Abstract: A two-player game form is Nash-consistent if and only if it is tight. Nash-consistency therefore depends only on the effectivity function associated with the game form. This fact is no longer true for strong consistency. We introduce the joint exact effectivity set which is a proper refinement of the effectivity function and prove that a two-player game form is strongly consistent if and only if it is tight and jointly exact. Joint exactness states that the new set coincides basically with the effectivity function. © 1994.

Title: Coalition formation in games of fair division
Abstract: I consider economies with a single indivisible good and money. Allowing agents to form coalitions, I show that the set of equilibrium allocations in the manipulation game associated with any subcorrespondence of the no-envy correspondence coincides with the set of envy-free allocations for the true preference profile. © 1994.

Title: Forecasting performance of seasonal-dummy models relative to some alternatives
Abstract: Abeysinghe (Economic Letters, 1991, 36, 175-197; Journal of Econometrics, 1994, forthcoming) showed that seasonal dummies in regressions may lead to spurious inference. This paper evaluates the post-sample forecasting performance of a seasonal-dummy ARIMA model with four other models. The results, in general, do not stand in favor of the seasonal-dummy approach. © 1994.

Title: Discriminating between errors-in- variables/simultaneity and misspecification in linear regression models
Abstract: A two-part test procedure is proposed to assist in discriminating between errors-in-variables/simultaneity and other misspecifications of a linear regression model. A result on the asymptotic independence of tests is established and a numerical example is provided. © 1994.

Title: Hedonic price indexes for personal computers
Authors: Students, Zvi Griliches, Daniel S. Hamermesh
Abstract: New data on the attributes of several hundred PCs offered for sale in the United States in August 1992 and April 1993, and in Moscow, Russia, in April 1993, are used in hedonic regressions. Various indexes show the rate of change in prices in the United States, and the relative price in Moscow. Combining the two gives the lag in Russian prices and illustrates how to make interspatial hedonic comparisons. © 1994.

Title: Semiparametric median estimation of the Type 3 Tobit model
Abstract: This paper considers estimation of the Type 3 Tobit model. The estimator is a two-step LAD estimator when a bivariate version of the median restriction is imposed on the error terms. A consistent estimator for the asymptotic covariance matrix is proposed. © 1994.

Title: The optimal extraction rate of a natural resource under uncertainty (economics letters 43, no. 2, 1993, pp. 231–234)
Currency substitution and the optimal inflation tax (economics letters 42, no. 1, 1993, pp. 65–70)
Authors: Pablo E. Guidotti, Carlos A. Végh

Title: Taxing pollution in an international duopoly context
Abstract: In the present analysis the effects of a pollution tax are examined in an international duopoly model. A new formula for the optimal pollution tax is derived, and then discussed in the strategic framework that arises from tax competition among rival international jurisdictions. © 1994.

Title: Why does schooling generate economic growth?
Abstract: This paper examines the relationship between schooling and GNP growth found in cross-country growth regressions. Using a standard decompositional technique, I divide education's effect on economic growth into three parts: (1) an effect from the change in the returns to schooling over time; (2) an indirect effect coming from schooling's positive effect on schooling growth; and (3) a direct effect coming from education's raising income growth even holding education growth constant. The lion's share of the schooling-GDP growth connection comes from the schooling-schooling growth connection. © 1994.

Title: The empirical specification of price-cost margins
Abstract: This paper examines why results for profit margin regressions may depend on whether the margin is deflated by industry sales or value added. It attributes disparate results to stage of production effects which occur because the price elasticity of demand is an omitted variable. © 1994.

Title: Sequential or non-sequential employers' search?
Abstract: This paper studies employers' search by analyzing the duration of vacancies notified at public employment offices. It appears that employers use a non-sequential search strategy to find new employees. © 1994.

Title: Explaining language proficiency
Abstract: Serious error-in-variable bias results when a self-assessed measure is used to estimate the determinants of literacy. When Instrumental Variables is used to account for the joint determination of earnings and literacy, the measurement error does not affect parameter estimates in a standard earnings equation. © 1994.

Title: German wage curves, 1979–1990
Abstract: This paper presents evidence for a wage curve, i.e. a negative relationship between the wage level and the regional rate of unemployment, in Germany. © 1994.

Title: U.S. nursing homes
Abstract: Utilizing a system of allocative efficiency functions and a short-run variable cost frontier, the following analysis avoids many statistical problems associated with measuring efficiency. Using an underutilized data base, the authors find that inefficiency increases costs only a trivial amount. © 1994.

Title: Too much conformity?
Authors: Bolko Hohaus, Kai A. Konrad, Marcel Thum
Abstract: This paper considers a new dimension in the choice of local public goods: quality. The quality decision that is made by median voters in a Hotelling model of product differentiation leads to too much conformity from a welfare point of view. © 1994.

Title: Uncertain liquidity and interbank contracting
Abstract: We study a version of the Diamond and Dybvig (Journal of Political Economy, 1983, 91, 401-419) model, where banks would like to obtain insurance against shocks on returns on liquid assets through an interbank borrowing and lending program. We show that if investments in liquid assets and their realized returns are private information to individual banks, the first-best allocation is not incentive-compatible; we then characterize the second-best interbank contract. © 1994.

Title: Sticky import prices and J-curves
Abstract: We show that devaluations lead to a J-curve when imported goods are durable and import prices adjust slowly to exchange rate changes. The J-curve effect is caused by intertemporal speculation as import prices are low relative to future prices immediately after a devaluation. © 1994.

Title: Does comovement among exchange rates imply market inefficiency?
Abstract: This paper argues that, contrary to what has been reported in the empirical literature previously, cointegration between pairs of exchange rates does not necessarily rule out informational efficiency in currency markets. The basic reason is that market efficiency does not rule out predictable exchange rate movements, but only rules out arbitrage opportunities from predictable exchange rate movements as the usual parity conditions dictate. © 1994.

Title: Evaluating multiperiod survey forecasts of real net exports
Abstract: Examination of the ASA-NBER survey data on real net exports indicates that the multiperiod professional forecasts are all unbiased. The short-term as well as the four-quarter-ahead forecasts are also rational, suggesting their usefulness in policy-making. © 1994.

Title: Present value based portfolio choice
Abstract: We formalize a modified present value rule for portfolio decisions under uncertainty based on a state-dependent valuation with opportunity costs. This decision rule is shown to select a unique portfolio which also maximizes the expected logarithmic utility of payoffs. © 1994.

Title: Walrasian and constrained Walrasian correspondences and Nash implementation
Abstract: This paper investigates the following classical question: Under what conditions are all Pareto-efficient and individually rational Nash allocations of some mechanism Walrasian or constrained Walrasian allocations? The work is largely motivated by Hurwicz (Journal of Economic Theory, 1979, 21, 140-165). © 1994.

Title: The effects of discounting opportunities in laboratory posted-offer markets
Authors: Douglas D. Davis, Charles A. Holt
Abstract: This experiment isolates the effects of allowing sellers to offer private discounts from posted prices. Although discounting was pervasive when permitted, it did not always improve performance. High prices and low efficiencies were observed in half of the discount markets. © 1994.

Title: Rational risk valuation given sequential reduction opportunities
Authors: Jason F. Shogren, Thomas D. Crocker
Abstract: We design experimental auctions with sequential risk reduction opportunities between private and collective self-protection or self-insurance. We reject two hypotheses of rational risk valuation-individuals do not prefer self-protection to self-insurance, and the sequencing of private and collective mechanisms matters. © 1994.

Title: Implementing the fluctuation and moving-estimates tests in dynamic econometric models
Abstract: We suggest modified versions of the fluctuation and moving-estimates tests and show that their empirical sizes improve significantly in dynamic models. © 1994.

Title: Bootstrapping cointegrating regression
Abstract: In this paper we use a Monte Carlo study to examine the small sample properties of an estimator of a cointegrating regression. We present some bootstrap methods to construct an appropriate confidence interval for the cointegrating estimator. The results show that while the Student-t distribution provides poor coverage of the confidence interval for the conventional OLS estimator, the bootstrap percentile-t method does provide reliable confidence intervals. © 1994.

Title: Periodic properties of interpolated time series
Abstract: Although linearly interpolated series are often used in economics, little has been done to examine the effects of interpolation on time-series properties and on statistical inference. We show that linear interpolation of a trend stationary series superimposes a 'periodic' structure on the moments of the series. Using conventional time-series methods to make inference about the interpolated series may therefore be invalid. Also, the interpolated series may exhibit more shock persistence than the original trend stationary series. © 1994.

Title: Cross-sector export ‘externalities’ in developing countries
Abstract: Feder's model (Journal of Development Economics, 1982, 12, 59-73) has been used extensively to measure the externality and productivity enhancing effects of one sector on the whole economy. We argue that the model is misspecified, make three modifications, estimate it for the export vs. non-export sectors, and compare our results with Feder's. © 1994.

Title: Strict liability and negligence rules when the product is information
Abstract: If the product is information, a strict liability rule is never efficient while a negligence rule sometimes is; nevertheless, in some cases society is better off with a strict liability rule. First best actions can only be determined given the set of feasible judicial/regulatory institutions. © 1994.

Title: A specification test of the determinants of male-female occupational differences
Abstract: This paper investigates by means of a simple specification test whether gender differences in occupational distributions arise from gender differences in preferences or from gender differences in hiring. Results obtained from estimating a bivariate choice model on NLSY data indicate that neither hypothesis can be rejected. © 1994.

Title: Ricardian equivalence for local government bonds
Abstract: It is shown that if consumers own land, the free rider problem does not occur because a change in local government financing is completely reflected in the price of land. This means that the Ricardian equivalence theorem holds not only for national government bonds but also for local government bonds. © 1994.

Title: Risk aversion, imperfect competition, and long-lived information
Abstract: This paper presents a methodology for characterizing the optimal dynamic behavior of risk-averse, strategic agents with private information, by building on Kyle (Econometrica, 1985, 53, 1315-1335). It is shown that both monopolistic and competing informed traders choose to exploit rents rapidly, causing market depth to be low in the initial periods and high in later periods, and causing information to be revealed rapidly, unlike in the case of a risk-neutral monopolist considered by Kyle. © 1994.

Title: Abnormal expected utility and event study abnormal returns
Abstract: Event study is employed by measuring the abnormal return around the event date. If risk changes this methodology is questionable. We suggest the concept of abnormal expect utility which relies on the whole distribution and not just the mean return. © 1994.

Title: The forward exchange rate premium
Authors: D.P. Tang, S.R. Lee, Benjaporn Thangkasemvathana
Abstract: Using weekly data of the Hong Kong foreign exchange market, we perform a test suggested in Fama (Journal of Monetary Economics, 1984, 14, 319-338) to analyze the source of variation in the three-month forward exchange rate premium. Prior to the visit to China by the Governor of Hong Kong to discuss the '1997' issue, we find that the source of variation in the forward premium is not clear. After the visit to China, however, we find that the source of variation in the forward premium is mostly due to the variation of the risk premium. © 1994.

Title: Capital markets, the separation property and hedging
Abstract: We consider a risk-averse firm facing exchange rate and interest rate uncertainty. When international capital markets are accessible the separation property holds. However, these hedging instruments are not equivalent to creating missing interest rate futures markets. © 1994.

Title: On the imperfect substitutability of policy regimes
Abstract: Exchange rate targetting is always an imperfect substitute for explicit policy coordination, but succeeds when economies are either structurally dissimilar with symmetric shocks, or structurally symmetric with dissimilar shocks. A joint commitment then generates economies of scale in interventions. © 1994.

Title: Market equilibrium effects of incentives to foreign direct investment
Abstract: This note shows that a country may want to give a certain type of incentive to foreign direct investment (subsidy to marginal costs of the foreign firm), even if no further gains (job creation, technology transfer and the like) are available. The crucial element is that subsidies may change the market equilibrium in a favorable way to the country. © 1994.

Title: Win-win indirect tax reform
Authors: Panos Hatzipanayotou, Michael S. Michael, Stephen M. Miller
Abstract: The literature on tariffs and that on commodity taxes have established sufficient conditions under which tariff or commodity tax reform improves welfare. Since less developed countries need to raise certain revenue from indirect taxation, we consider a policy reform within the complete indirect tax structure (i.e. an increase in consumption taxes combined with a decrease in tariffs) that improves welfare and raises government revenue. We demonstrate that when uniform reductions in trade taxes accompany offsetting increases in consumption taxes, so that consumer prices remain constant, welfare improves and government revenue increases if the initial position provides a net subsidy to producers. © 1994.

Title: Quantitative assessment of tariff endogeneity
Abstract: The paper provides a quantitative assessment of the tariff endogeneity hypothesis in the macro context for the interwar and postwar U.S. economy. There is an almost unidirectional causality running from unemployment and trade deficit to the average tariff rate during the interwar period while more interactive relationships hold in the postwar period. Compared with the interwar era, there is a decline in the dependence of tariff on unemployment and trade deficit. But the individual effect of unemployment on tariff has increased and that of trade deficit has decreased. Furthermore, unanticipated shocks exert smaller and less persistent effects of tariff. © 1994.

Title: On the symmetry between inflation and exchange rate targets
Abstract: Although several countries recently have adopted formal inflation targets for monetary policy, little research has been done on the implications of such targets for prices. This paper shows that there is a symmetry between exchange rate and inflation targets. © 1994.

Title: Monetary uncertainty in discrete-time utility-of-money models
Abstract: In a discrete-time model, higher variability of the future money supply affects current macroeconomic variables when beginning-of-period money is the argument of utility, but not when end-of-period money is. The effect is through the existence of a precautionary money demand. © 1994.

Title: Composition effect and economic fluctuations
Abstract: The asymmetric information approach has developed the idea that if agents differ from one another, the representative agent hypothesis no longer holds true. We show that in that setting several composition effects may arise which affect economic fluctuations: it is shown that even if the aggregate equity base does not change, total output may do. © 1994.

Title: Inflation and relative price variability
Abstract: The unconditional variance of the rate of nominal price change can always be expressed as a function of the unconditional mean. Therefore the relationship between the unconditional variance and the unconditional mean cannot be used to distinguish among alternative theories. © 1994.

Title: The information in diffusion indexes for forecasting related economic aggregates
Abstract: Time-series techniques are used to assess whether diffusion indexes add unique information to forecasts of some key economic variables. The results indicate that diffusion indexes for industrial production and employment add significantly to the explanation of related aggregates. © 1994.

Title: Capital subsidy and the saving— investment correlation in a model with perfect capital mobility
Abstract: In this paper we provide an example of a positive saving-investment correlation in an open economy with perfect capital markets that is caused by an anticipation of government policy. © 1994.

Title: Experimentation and learning with networks effects
Abstract: This paper considers learning in an competitive setting. By allowing an opponent a 'head start', unsuccessful unilateral experimentation may jeopardize future sales and profits. We show that even in the absence of spillover and signalling effects, competition can inhibit the scope of learning, relative to a monopoly. © 1994.

Title: Inada's condition implies equilibrium existence is rare
Abstract: In this paper I generalize and simplify my results with A.P. Araujo on the non-existence of equilibria in finance models. It turns out that separability is not necessary for the negative results. © 1994.

Title: T-period economies with incomplete markets
Abstract: A very simple proof is given for the existence of stochastic equilibria in a T-period economy with an incomplete financial structure. © 1994.

Title: Sequential auctions of stochastically equivalent objects
Abstract: We show that in sequential auctions of a large enough number of stochastically equivalent objects with bounded values, prices will on average have a downwards trend. © 1994.

Title: A class of differential demand systems
Abstract: The Rotterdam, Almost Ideal Demand System, CBS, and NBR models constitute a class of differential demand systems. They correspond to alternative assumptions made concerning the constancy of certain parameters. This paper discusses the restrictions that they impose on the evolution of demand elasticities over time. © 1994.

Title: General consumer demand systems
Abstract: This paper introduces a generalisation of Roy's Identity and Shephard's Lemma which is applicable where the resource constraining expenditure level of a consumer's utility maximisation problem is not observable but is replaced by some observable proxy variable such as conditional expenditure. Implications for testing for Slutsky symmetry and separability are explored. © 1994.

Title: On the exploitation of additional duality relationships in consumer demand analysis
Abstract: This paper advocates more extensive use of the (Frisch) profit function in static consumer demand studies and intorduces its inverse, the price of utility function, paralleling the well-known relationships between indirect utility and expenditure functions. An examination of the relationship between these four functions suggests: (i) a fourth 'system' complementing Marshallian, Hicksian and Frisch demand systems; and (ii) a fourth 'theorem' complementing Roy's Identity, Shephard's Theorem and Hoteling's Lemma. © 1994.

Title: Optimal consumption dynamics with non-concave habit-forming utility
Abstract: We study the dynamics of optimal consumption when preferences exhibit habit formation without imposing global concavity conditions on utility. We provide a complete characterization of the dynamics despite possible multiplicities in optimal policies and steady states. © 1994.

Title: Enhancing bargaining power with most-favored-customer pricing
Abstract: A monopolist faces a finite sequence of identical buyers and negotiates with each buyer individually. Most-favored-customer pricing allows the firm to exploit its position as the repeat player in the game and extract more of each buyer's surplus. © 1994.

Title: A note on beliefs formation in signalling games
Abstract: We present a new criterion, called incentive dominance, for belief formation in signalling games, which subsumes refinements criteria such as equilibrium dominance and divinity. It captures the principle of forward induction through explicitly modelling the player's thought process when forming preliminary beliefs. © 1994.

Title: Homeomorphism between Leontief and Cobb-Douglas input-output models
Abstract: A linear one-to-one mapping is established between the variables, equations, and parameters of two regional multisectoral general equilibrium input-output (I-O) models. One model is based on Leontief micro foundations and the other on generalized Cobb-Douglas micro foundations. Consequently, many I-O applications in the Leontief framework, enen if apparently dependent on Keynesian assumptions, can be re-interpreted as applications in a strictly neoclassical framework. © 1994.

Title: Strong hysteresis versus zero-root dynamics
Authors: Bruno Amable, Jérôme Henry, Frédéric Lordon, Richard Topol
Abstract: This paper presents the properties of remanence and of dependence on history pertaining to strong hysteresis through a foreign trade model. These properties reveal that it is impossible to assimilate zero-root dynamics to hysteresis. © 1994.

Title: Excess volatility
Abstract: A testing strategy for excess volatility in asset prices is proposed by combining a number of already existing econometric estimators. The strategy is valid when asset prices are integrated of order one, the real rate of interest is variable and the underlying economic model is non-linear. The strategy is applied to annual U.S. stock prices. The evidence for no excess volatility is weak. © 1994.

Title: Estimating labor supply with panel data
Authors: Karen Smith Conway, Thomas J. Kniesner
Abstract: We investigated the robustness of linear labor-supply functions incorporating income taxes using recently developed techniques for estimating simultaneous equations with latent heterogeneity using panel data. Our results suggest an econometric model acknowledging the intertemporal progressive taxation of labor and non-labor income. © 1994.

Title: Preliminary-test estimation in a dynamic linear model
Authors: David E.A. Giles, Matthew C. Cunneen
Abstract: This paper considers the estimation of a dynamic linear regression model after a pretest of exact linear restrictions on the coefficient vector. Monte Carlo evidence illustrates that pre-testing can be risk-superior to both ordinary and restricted least squares. © 1994.

Title: Exploiting cross-section variation for unit root inference in dynamic data
Abstract: This paper considers unit root regressions in data having simultaneously extensive cross-section and time-series variation. The standard least squares estimators in such data structures turn out to have an asymptotic distribution that is neither O p (T-1) Dickey-Fuller, nor O p (N 1 2) normal and asymptotically unbiased. Instead, the estimator turns out to be consistent and asymptotically normal, but has a non-vanishing bias in its asymptotic distribution. © 1994.

Title: A generalization of the non-parametric Henriksson-Merton test of market timing
Abstract: The paper shows that the Henriksson-Merton (1981) test (Journal of Business 54, 513-533) of market timing is better interpreted as an exact test of independence within a 2×2 contingency table in which the column and row sums are fixed. We provide a generalization of the test of market timing from the special case of a 2×2 contingency table to the case with n categories. This generalization has a number of potential applications in the forecasting and finance literature. The generalized test is applied to analyze the market timing performance of a two-fund investment strategy in the presence of transaction costs. © 1994.

Equilibria of generalized games with -majorized preference correspondences (economics letters 41, no. 4, 1993, pp. 379–383)
A curvature condition ensuring uniqueness of Cournot equilibrium, with applications to comparative statics (economics letters 41, no. 1, 1993, pp. 29–33)
Increasing scarcity rent A sufficient condition
Abstract: If the elasticity of extraction cost exceeds the elasticity of demand, the scarcity rent of an exhaustible resource increases monotonically over time. © 1993.

Title: The optimal extraction rate of a natural resource under uncertainty
Abstract: The objective of this paper is to derive the optimal rate of depletion of non-renewable natural resource by a monopolist under uncertainty conditions on the evolution of the reserve stock of that natural resource. © 1993.

Title: Intergenerational mobility
Abstract: I examine the degree of intergenerational mobility in Turkey, through the effect of parental education on economic welfare. Parental education is important for the quantity of education received but has no further impact on economic well-being. Turkish intergenerational mobility is less than in the United States, particularly for women. © 1993.

Title: Exchangeable arbitrator behavior
Abstract: A theoretical model developed in this paper seeks to compare the optimal conventional arbitration awards of arbitrators deliberately seeking to replicate the behavior of past arbitrators with those who do not. The implications suggest that the optimal awards under both strategies will be the same. © 1993.

Title: The international impact of Federal Reserve Bank discount rate changes
Authors: Vittorio Bonomo, Stephen P. Ferris, Gregory Noronha
Abstract: Previous studies have found that American equity values move inversely to the direction of announced discount rate changes by the Federal Reserve Bank. In this study of the return behavior of a simple of American depository receipts (ADRs) to announcements of discount rate changes, we find no evidence of such a relationship. Indeed, ADRs exhibit no significant response to either rate increases or decreases. Our results hold for both market realignment and policy motivated changes. These findings suggest that ADRs can provide diversification to the American investor as international economies and monetary policies remain incompletely integrated. © 1993.

Title: Dynamic effects of a terms-of-trade shock on a small open economy
Abstract: Using a neoclassical one-sector model extended to include investment installation costs, this paper investigates the dynamic responses of consumption and external debt of a small open economy to a negative terms-of-trade shock. In contrast to the existing literature, we allow the divergence of the rate of time preference and the world interest rate. The instantaneous change of net borrowing depends on the divergence of these rates and the existence of investment installation costs, supporting the pattern of movement described by the J-curve. The instantaneous consumption change depends on whether or not the country is a debtor when the shock occurs. © 1993.

Title: Temporary cuts in government spending as an anti-inflationary device
Abstract: We examine an open one-good economy where money is kept for transactions purposes, the tax base is elastic to the tax rate, and the financial markets are well integrated. It is shown that a sharp but temporary cut in government spending gets inflation down. © 1993.

Title: A solution to a class of agency problems, with application to the question of limited liability
Abstract: A complete solution is provided for a class of principal-agent problems where the principal is risk neutral, the agent is risk averse with a piece-wise linear utility function and where the distribution of outcomes is binomial. Incentive schemes with limited and unlimited liability are compared and shown to be efficient in the limit. © 1993.

Title: Consistency of mean-variance analysis and expected utility analysis
Abstract: A risk-averse individual's expected utility is a function of mean and variance if and only if the class of random variables to be ranked is completely ordered by Rothschild-Stiglitz increasing risk after normalization by their means. © 1993.

Title: The principal—agent problem when the agent has access to outside markets
Abstract: Principal-agent models assume that the agent must consume the payments he receives under the incentive contract. This paper shows that if the agent can trade his payments on frictionless state-contigent markets, only a flat-wage or a full residual claim for the agent are viable. © 1993.

Title: Income distribution, Pareto laws and regular variation
Authors: Arnold H.Q.M. Merkies, Ivo J. Steyn
Abstract: Various properties of the tail behaviour of the income distribution have been formulated. It is shown that the best-known of these, the Weak Pareto Laws, are all equivalent to a property known as regular variation, and that the relations between the various Weak Pareto Laws (Mandelbrot, Kakwani and Esteban versions) are not as stated in the literature. © 1993.

Title: Russell on Gorman's Engel curves
Abstract: Russel [Economics Letters, 1983, 11, 223-224] claims to show that the main theorem in Gorman's 'Some Engel curves' [in A.S. Deaton, ed., Essays in the theory and measurement of consumer behavior, 1981 (Cambridge University Press, Cambridge)] follows from Lie's (1988) theory of transformation groups [Theorie der Transformationsgruppen (B.F. Teubner, Leipzig)]. That claim is incorrect, but Russell's argument can be used to prove a special case of Gorman's theorem. © 1993.

Title: Weak exogeneity and dynamic stability in cointegrated VARs
Abstract: This paper shows that weak exogeneity is violated when dynamic stability is imposed in VAR models. This result can have important implications when one conditions a cointegrated VAR. © 1993.

Title: Cointegration, causality and export-led growth in Portugal, 1865–1985
Abstract: This paper considers the relationship between cointegration and causality and uses tests of cointegration as pre-tests for Granger tests of causality. Such methods are utilized on Portuguese data, 1865-1985, where the export-led growth hypothesis is rejected in favour of reverse causality. © 1993.

Title: More on Laspeyres price index
Abstract: In a recent article Selvanathan (Economics Letters, 1991, 35, 35-38) uses the stochastic approach to derive the Laspeyres price index and its standard error. In this paper we extend this approach by allowing for systematic changes in relative prices. © 1993.

Title: Do standards of living converge?
Abstract: This paper examines whether consumption per capita (a measure of the standard of living) converges across economies. In addition to the standard convergence test, which is known to be consistent only under implausible assumptions, we use a recently developed valid specification. In general, our estimates provide evidence against divergence of standards of living across countries. On the other hand, convergence of standards of living can be rejected for all but a sample of rich countries. © 1993.

Title: On the power of point optimal tests of the trend stationarity hypothesis
Abstract: This paper considers tests of the hypothesis that a series is trend stationary. It provides simulation results showing the gain in power from using a point optimal test. © 1993.

Title: Estimating fractionally integrated time series models
Abstract: This paper compares an easily implemented approximate (Gaussian) maximum likelihood estimator of fractionally integrated ARMA models with a recently developed full maximum likelihood procedure. It is shown that except for the case of a pure long memory process, the exact procedure should always be used. © 1993.

Title: Misspecification tests, unit roots and level shifts
Abstract: In this paper we provide some illustrative Monte Carlo evidence on the usefulness of the well-known misspecification test in the case of testing for a unit root against an exogenously determined break in the level of a series. We also investigate the small sample behaviour of Perron's (Journal of Business and Economic Statistics, 1990, 8, 153-162) unit root test in the presence of an erroneous location of the break point. © 1993.

Title: Missing measurements in econometric models with no auxiliary relations
Abstract: In this paper it is argued that maximizing the complete data (log) likelihood function with respect to the missing data and the unknown parameters will not improve the efficiency of the estimators but may affect consistency instead. If no auxiliary relations are available or additional assumptions are made, the maximum likelihood estimator based on the observed data is (asymptotically) the most efficient estimator. © 1993.

Title: Late-mover advantage and product diffusion
Abstract: The diffusion of a new product, the price of which is expected to fall progressively, is modelled as a sequence of Wars of Attrition. The likely pattern of diffusion is found to be reasonably consistent with the empirically observed S-shape. © 1993.

Title: The added worker effect
Abstract: This paper uses the Gross Change data and cointegration, error-correction modeling to test the hypothesis of added worker effect in the U.S. labor market. It is shown that prime-age males' unemployment (U m ) and flows from unemployment to out of the labor force (UN m ) cause an increase in prime-age and young females' flows from not in the labor force ('keeping house') to employment and decrease their flows into unemployment. © 1993.

Title: Execution lags and imperfect arbitrage
Abstract: This paper presents a simple equilibrium model of stock index arbitrage with endogenous execution lags. We show that the resulting execution or immediacy risk reduces arbitrage activity and causes price differences between the two markets to persist. © 1993.

Title: Old information and market efficiency
Abstract: In an efficient market, agents will reuse old information in the aftermath of corrections in the subjective model. However, this does not create exploitable profit opportunities. This paper studies the difference between the objective and subjective model, and the implications for the random walk. © 1993.

Title: Direct crowding out, optimal taxation and pollution abatement
Authors: Frederick van der Ploeg, A. Lans Bovenberg
Abstract: The interactions between direct crowding out, the provision of public goods, optimal taxation, and environmental policy are explored. Greener preferences induce a larger tax rate by raising the non-distortionary level of the tax rate. If the marginal productivity of public abatement diminishes rapidly, environmental quality improves mainly through a fall in economic activity and emissions. In this case, public consumption increases which crowds out labour supply and private consumption. However, if environmental policy is very effective, public consumption falls in order to make room for public abatement. In this case, if labour supply is inelastic with respect to the after-tax wage and direct crowding in is strong, labour supply and economic activity may expand. © 1993.

Title: Impulse dynamics and propagation mechanisms in a real business cycle model
Abstract: In a typical real business cycle model, we find that output dynamics are determined primarily by impulse dynamics and that endogenous propagation mechanisms are weak. Consequently, the model must rely on external sources of dynamics in order to replicate the univariate dynamics of U.S. per capita GNP. © 1993.

Title: Experimental tests of prospective reference theory
Abstract: Prospective reference theory (PRT) explains anomalies of expected utility theory by assuming individuals have prior probabilities over lottery outcomes. Two lottery choice experiments demonstrate systematic violations of PRT challenging the theory's explanation of expected utility theory anomalies. © 1993.

Title: Relationships among some risk premia
Abstract: We consider several risk premia associated with providing insurance through income and factor prices and obtain relationships among them. Our most interesting result is that certain factor price risk premia are marginal versions of the Arrow-Pratt income risk premium. © 1993.

Title: Network or pay-per-view?
Abstract: The welfare effects of pay-per-view television and advertising-supported networks are compared. It is shown that pay-per-view television admits third-degree price discrimination and may involve a large loss of consumer surplus. © 1993.

Title: The Lorenz-ordering of Singh-Maddala income distributions
Abstract: This paper gives a complete characterization of the family of Singh-Maddala income distributions in terms of Lorenz-ordering, in the sense that given any two distributions from this family, we show how to determine from the respective parameters whether or not one Lorenz-dominates the other. © 1993.

Title: First-mover advantage and organizational structure
Abstract: This paper looks at first-mover advantage and its effects on organizational structure and size. The framework is the project-selection model and the key assumption is that managers are fallible so that decision-making is imperfect. The analysis suggests that when there is a first-mover advantage, decentralized and smaller organizations, such as the polyarchy and the committee, are preferable since they are speedier in making decisions despite the reduced accuracy in selecting projects. © 1993.

Title: Recovering homothetic preferences
Abstract: A method is given for recovering all homothetic preferences implicit in a set of consumption data. © 1993.

Title: Decision-making by an authority under influence
Abstract: A characteristic set of decision problems is given when an authority has to choose between a finite number of alternatives and is being influenced by a number of parties. For instance, the location of a firm when local authorities are competing for being the host, various types of lobbyism, or when a manager is being influenced by deputies. This paper argues that these problems can be analyzed as decision-making in a hierarchy using a common-agency framework. The main result is that even when the influential parties act simultaneously and the strategy sets are discrete, solutions to such decision problems as pure-strategy equilibria exist. © 1993.

Title: Strategic choice of waiting and reaction times in bargaining
Abstract: If two players first commit to waiting times in a Sakovics bargaining technology, and then bargain over the division of a known surplus, zero waiting times are not subgame perfect choices, and any division of the surplus is possible. © 1993.

Title: On the contribution of an additional player to a convex game
Abstract: The addition of a player into a convex game may give rise to some different non-convex games. The marginal contribution allocation allows us to prove very easily the non-emptyness of the core of these games. © 1993.

Title: Security market returns and the social discount rate
Abstract: We show that a securities market equilibrium cannot implement the social optimum in an overlapping generations model. © 1993.

Title: The coverability problem in input-output systems
Abstract: The notion of a vector replacement system, developed in the computer science literature, is used to analyze the reachability problem in integer-valued input-output models. An integer-valued input-output system with initial resources is a 5-tuple 〈n, m, A, B, μ〉, where n is the number of commodities, m the number of production processes, A is the n × m input matrix, B is the n × m output matrix and μ ε{lunate} Rn is the initial vector of resources. The elements of A, B an μ are non-negative integers. A vector μ' is reachable from μ if it is possible to transform μ into μ' through a sequence of production processes, without ever violating the feasibility constraint represented by the available resources. © 1993.

Title: A note on the score test for neglected heterogeneity in the truncated normal regression model
Abstract: The score test for neglected heterogeneity in the truncated normal regression model is derived. The test is not an information matrix test [Cheshter (Econometrica, 1984, 52, 865-872)] but it can be interpreted as a combination of score tests for non-normality and heteroskedasticity. © 1993.

Title: Testing for measurement errors in expectations from survey data
Authors: Robert W. Rich, Jennie E. Raymond, J.S. Butler
Abstract: This paper examines the issue of measurement errors in expectations from survey data in the testing of models of expectations formation. We demonstrate that tests for measurement errors can be conducted through a generalized method of moments specification test and apply our estimation strategy to the SRC expected inflation series. © 1993.

Title: Estimating daily seasonals in financial time series
Abstract: It is demonstrated that combining time domain and frequency domain analyses results in a considerable improvement in modelling seasonal patterns in daily exchange rate changes. A high-pass filter is used, followed by the usual time domain analysis with a GARCH model, to estimate day-of-the-week effects in the spot return on U.S. dollars relative to British pounds and the results are seen to compare favorably with those from a pure time domain approach. © 1993.

Title: Editorial Board
Announcement
Category index
Author index
Resource price dynamics with non-malleable extraction capital
Abstract: Non-renewable resource extraction is nearly always capital-intensive and extraction capital tends to be non-malleable. In thispaper we present and discuss a dynamic discrete-time model of resource extraction embodying non-malleable capital which can generate highly diverse patterns of price behaviour. © 1993.

Title: What is the effect of bid-rigging on prices?
Authors: Luke M. Froeb, Robert A. Koyak, Gregory J. Werden
Abstract: This paper develops and applies a method for estimating the price effects of bid rigging and price fixing conspiracies. A fairly typical bid-rigging scheme is found to have raised prices by over 20% for over 4 years. © 1993.

Title: The determinants of success in educational choice
Abstract: This paper proposes that all students are not able to enter the specialisations that they initially desire, therefore research in educational (or occupational) choice must take this into account. In general ability, some school characteristics and sex significantly affect success in educational choice. © 1993.

Title: A benchmark measure of income for assessing the distributional effects of tax reform
Abstract: A basic difficulty inherent in analyzing tax-induced changes in the distribution of income is to identify a concept of income that is economically meaningful and unaltered by changes in tax laws. The present paper introduces a concept of income that is, as much as possible, invariant to changes in the tax code. Comparisons of the distribution of total cash income with those of other measures of income that are directly affected by tax reforms can shed light on the distributional effects of changes in tax laws. © 1993.

Title: A Ricardian Equivalence Theorem on the taxation of pension funds
Abstract: We compare the three main alternative ways of taxing pension funds of the defined-contribution variety. Specifically, the alternatives considered are equal-yield taxes on contributions, earnings, and benefits. Analogous to the Ricardian Equivalence Theorem, the contributor's after-tax benefit will be the same in each case. © 1993.

Title: A simple model of spatial banking competition
Authors: Kit Pong Wong, Derek K. Chan
Abstract: This paper applies the financial intermediation and optimal contract theories to the standard Hotelling model. In it, we demonstrate that too little investment is undertaken and too much costly monitoring is involved in the unregulated banking industry. Thus, our model suggests a rationale for the government to regulate bank locations. © 1993.

Title: Common stochastic trends in European stock markets
Authors: A. Corhay, A. Tourani Rad, J.-P. Urbain
Abstract: The objective of the paper is to investigate whether price indices of different European stock markets display a common long-run trending behaviour. Using cointegration analysis, we provide empirical evidence of common stochastic trends among five important European stock markets over the period 1975-1991. © 1993.

Title: The term structure of interest rates in a model with heterogeneous agents
Abstract: This paper examines the term structure of interest rates in a stochastic overlapping generations model. Several discrete time, discrete state models show that the term structure premium is generally positive. This paper demonstrates that these results hinge upon the assumption of a single representative agent, and if heterogeneous agents are introduced a negative term structure premium cannot be ruled out. © 1993.

Title: A cross-sectional variance bounds test
Authors: John Board, George Bulkley, Ian Tonks
Abstract: Using data on individual stocks we apply a cross-sectional variance bound test for each year 1926-1979. We find that for every year up to 1959, except 1928, the variance bound is satisfied, whereas in all subsequent years the bound is violated. © 1993.

Title: Money creation system in the Real Business Cycle theory
Abstract: This paper attempts to provide the first model to include the money creation system in the Real Business Cycle theory. Impulse response functions of equilibrium show that financial intermediation is a very powerful propagation mechanism. © 1993.

Title: Time consistency, indexation and the costs of inflation
Abstract: We examine the effects of indexation measures on inflation, costs of inflation and economic welfare within the Barro-Gordon (Journal of Political Economy, 1983, 91, 589-610) model. The main result is that wage indexation in addition to making the Phillips curve steeper, also reduces the marginal cost of inflation, which is inflationary. © 1993.

Title: Comparative dynamics of fixed versus flexible discount rate growth models
Abstract: From any given initial stock, for convex and non-convex technologies, the flexible discount rate model maintains a higher level of capital input in each period than the fixed discount rate model. Hence constant discount rate models used to study sustained growth may show bias because they ignore how consumption affects the discount factor. © 1993.

Title: Revealed preference and portfolio choice
Abstract: We show that the necessary and sufficient conditions for expected utility rationalizability of a single observed portfolio choice are identical to the necessary and sufficient conditions for non-expected utility rationalizability. © 1993.

Title: Infinite Chichilnisky rules
Abstract: Topological aggregation in an infinite context depends crucially upon the type of topology. Tychonov topologies do not admit an infinite Chichilnisky rule, while box topologies based upon an appropriate topology do. © 1993.

Title: In search of the right middleman
Abstract: This paper shows that when traders go to a middleman only if they cannot get a better price somewhere else, the two popular evaluation criteria for middleman - low bid-ask spreads and low inventory holding costs - may be inconsistent. © 1993.

Title: Some improvements for bootstrapping regression estimators under first-order serial correlation
Abstract: Standard t-tests can be severely biased in the presence of trended regressors and serially correlated errors. Veall (Economics Letters, 1986, 21, 41-44) presented simulation evidence that traditional bootstrapping does not substantially reduce this bias. Subsequent research has developed a number of refinements to the bootstrap including accelerated bias correction, prepivoting and iterated bootstrapping. The models considered by Veall were re-examined employing these refinements. It was found that substantial improvements are possible, particularly from prepivoting and iterated bootstrapping. © 1993.

Title: On the relationship between impulse response analysis, innovation accounting and Granger causality
Abstract: We derive a general characterization of Granger non-causality between two vectors, X 1 and X 2 , in terms of impulse responses, when a third vector of auxiliary variables, X 3 , is also used to forecast. It is observed that the usual characterizations of non-casuality in terms of impulse responses or variance decompositions can be misleading in such situation. A numerical illustration is also provided. © 1993.

Title: On the corrections to the Wald test of non-linear restrictions
Authors: Silvia L. de Paula Ferrari, Francisco Cribari-Neto
Abstract: This paper derives a Bartlett-type correction to the Wald statistic for the test of non-linear restrictions. The test based on this improved statistic and the test based on the transformed critical values that can be suggested based on Phillips and Park's (Econometrica, 1988, 56, 1065-1083) results are equivalent to order n-1. © 1993.

Title: Recent advances in evolutionary economics: comments
Evolutionary stability and efficiency
Abstract: 'One of the advantages of moral philosophy over game theory is that moralists give sensible advice to moral agents while game theory can give stupid advice to game theorists' - Ian Hacking. © 1993.

Title: Perpetual randomness in evolutionary economics
Economic natural selection
Symposium on evolutionary economics
Knowledge diffusion in an endogenous growth model
Abstract: R&D models of endogenous growth have the unwelcome implication that the growth rate of an economy increases in the size of its labour force. However, the introduction of a diffusion process through which new technology is gradually incorporated into the economy-wide stock of knowledge can reduce and eliminate the dependence of the growth rate upon the size of the economy. © 1993.

Title: Entry-inducing technology adoption
Abstract: When spillovers are important, potential entry may lead incumbents to refrain from implementing costless improvements in production technology or working practices. Thus it is concluded that endogenous changes in market structure may exacerbate disincentives to do R&D. © 1993.

Title: On the Todaro paradox
Abstract: This paper presents a version of the Harris-Todaro model in which the rural labour market is characterised by monopsonistic behaviour. It is shown that the 'Todaro paradox', i.e. that the creation of jobs in the urban sector actually increases urban unemployment, does not hold if the urban employed outnumber the urban unemployed. The latter is the rule in all LDCs. © 1993.

Title: Competition in airline networks
Abstract: This paper is concerned with the effect of competition in airline hub-and-spoke networks. Using constant elasticity demand functions, we demonstrate that competition in a single market may generate positive or negative network externalities, depending on price elasticities of demand. © 1993.

Title: A note on vertical relations when the input supplier is a labor union
Abstract: Upstream and downstream monopolists can increase joint profits by vertically integrating or designing a contract which replicates the vertically integrated structure. Such arrangements are shown to be infeasible when the upstream firm is a labor union controlled by union insiders. © 1993.

Title: Speed variance, enforcement, and the optimal speed limit
Authors: Philip E. Graves, Dwight R. Lee, Robert L. Sexton
Abstract: A model of the optimal speed limit is developed which explicitly recognizes the roles of average speed, speed variance, and the level of enforcement. An unusual result emerges, namely that a higher speed limit may be optimal when reducing the variance in highway speeds reduces accident externalities. © 1993.

Title: ‘Voting with your feet’ and the quality of life index
Abstract: This paper develops a new technique that uses the utility-maximizing migration decisions of rational voters/consumers to construct QOL rankings. We apply our technique to Canadian inter-provincial migration data for 1970-1990. © 1993.

Title: South African divestment decisions and shareholder wealth
Authors: Norman H. Moore, Stephen W. Pruitt, K.S. Maurice Tse
Abstract: Empirical analysis of the South African divestment decisions announced by U.S. firms suggests that such actions resulted in an approximately 3% decline in share values. © 1993.

Title: Monetary variability and real output
Abstract: Utilizing Engel's (Econometrica, 1982, 50, 987-1008) autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity (ARCH) model to consistently parameterize the conditional variance of money growth, I find an inverse relationship between monetary variability and real output. This provides some additional evidence in favor of Friedman's (Journal of Political Economy, 1977, 85, 451-472) famous conjecture. © 1993.

Title: Optimum quantity of money instability
Abstract: It is shown that optimum quantity of money equilibria are unstable in the simplest models. Getting back to the desired path requires a temporary suspension of the money growth rule. © 1993.

Title: On relative price variability and hyperinflation
Abstract: During the Chinese hyperinflation (1946:1-1949:4), both anticipated inflation were found to influence relative price variability positively. The non-neutral effect of anticipated inflation rejects the conventional Lucas island model, while lending empirical support to the price adjustment-cost theory. © 1993.

Title: Efficiency wages and economic growth
Abstract: This paper examines the positive and normative implications of introducing efficiency wages into a standard growth model. A number of useful findings are obtained under the empirically justifiable assumption that the elasticity of substitution between capital and labor is less than unity. It is shown that an increase in thrift shifts downward the whole path of equilibrium unemployment to leave it permanently lower in the new steady state. A level increase in the measure of, as well as an increase in the rate of Harrod-neutral technical progress, are contractionary for equilibrium employment. The market economy underinvests. © 1993.

Title: Learning partitions
Abstract: Information can be imparted according to structures which are not partitional. Partitions, however, are important because they characterize agents with the highest degree of rationality. This paper gives conditions for a partition to emerge asymptotically from possibility correspondences. © 1993.

Title: Signalling by middlemen
Abstract: Two variations on signalling models which arise in markets with middlemen are presented. First, if middlemen are risk-neutral, then pooling always occurs in (Nash) equilibrium. Second, if middlemen are risk-averse, then pooling reactive equilibria may exist. The analysis offers insights into the absence of contracts designed to separate agents in many middlemen relationships. © 1993.

Title: On some generalizations of a mean voter theorem
Authors: Barry K. Ma, Jeffrey H. Weiss
Abstract: Caplin and Nalebuff (Econometrica, 1991, 59, 1-23) established the existence of an unbeatable proposal in a super-majority voting problem. We show this result holds for more general parametric representations of voters' preferences. © 1993.

Title: A note on majorization theory and the evaluation of income distributions
Abstract: This paper applies the branch of the theory of inequalities known as 'majorization theory' to the evaluation of income distributions. Majorization theory enables one to 'factor' the generalized Lorenz criterion-combining efficiency and equity-into the rank and Lorenz conditions. © 1993.
