Title: Dynamic efficiency of steady-state equilibria in an overlapping-generations model with productive capital
Abstract: This paper establishes sufficient technological conditions under which, for any feasible set of well-behaved preferences, stationary over-investment relative to the Golden Rule is ruled out and the economy's steady-state equilibria are therefore dynamically efficient. © 1991.

Title: Psychological features affecting valuation of life
Abstract: Economists have studied a variety of consumer, technological and workplace hazards to determine the value of life. These studies have produced widely divergent results. This paper investigates whether or not cognitive characteristics of different hazards may explain part of the diversity. Our findings are that while catastrophic hazards such as nuclear accidents engender heightened psychological fear and a high willingness-to-pay to reduce risks, the same is not true for more everyday hazards. Small sample size and dubious source data may be responsible for this counter-intuitive result, which suggests there is a need for additional joint work by psychologists and economists. © 1991.

Title: Optimum subsidies for education in two-sector economies
Abstract: This note presents a view on educational subsidies based on the recognition that educational cost is a kind of turnover cost from unskilled to skilled labor. The level of optimum educational subsidies is given for three types of two sector economies - a pure two sector economy, economy of income sharings in the traditional sector, economy with unemployment in the manufactural sector. © 1991.

Title: Optimal inspection interval in a search model
Abstract: This paper studies an aspect of search behavior, not previously discussed in the literature: A searcher may not continuously inspect the availability of jobs but may do it at a certain interval if inspection is costly. © 1991.

Title: Discretion in reporting managerial performance
Authors: Ronald A. Dye, Robert P. Magee
Abstract: In a single period agency model in which the agent has some discretion regarding how to report his period's performance, we show when the agent's contract is increasing in his report regardless of the characteristics of his production technology, and how to rank changes in the agent's reporting technology according to the expected cost of compensating the agent. © 1991.

Title: Finite complexity and the folk theorem in repeated games
Abstract: We show that the folk theorem for repeated games with discounting will hold if strategies and threats are allowed to have only finite complexity, even without the fully dimensionality requirement that is required for the perfect folk theorem for repeated games with discounting. It is then quite easy to see that the perfect folk theorem for repeated games without discounting is the limit of the perfect folk theorem with finite complexity and discounting. © 1991.

Title: Coincidence probabilities for simple majority and proportional lottery rules
Abstract: Proportional lottery rules select the winner in a pairwise election by a random process, in which the probability that an alternative is selected is proportional to the number of votes that it receives in the election. This study develops a closed form representation for the expected likelihood that the proportional lottery rule selects the same winner as simple majority rule for a two candidate election. When three candidate elections are considered, pairwise comparisons are made on all pairs of alternatives to determine the winner. Closed form representations are developed for the expected likelihood that the proportional lottery rule has the same winner, and the same complete linear ranking on alternatives, as simple majority rule, given that there is a simple majority rule winner. © 1991.

Title: Labor force participation in an LDC
Abstract: An aggregate labor participation rate model based on a neoclassical two-period labor supply model is derived and estimated using annual time-series data for the Philippines. The findings cast doubts on LDC labor market modes that posit an infinitely elastic labor supply curve. © 1991.

Title: Are new firms an important source of innovation?
Authors: Thomas J. Prusa, James A. Schmitz
Abstract: We examine data from the PC software industry to determine if new forms play an important role in the advance of technology in this industry over the period 1982-1987. We find that new firms have a comparative advantage (over established firms) in creating new software categories, while established firms have a comparative advantage in developing subsequent improvements in existing categories. © 1991.

Title: The impact of asymmetric information on entry deterrence: An example
Abstract: A simple non-pathological example demostrates that, when an incumbent firm has private information about the state of demand, an entrant's profits and the likelihood of entry may be decreasing in the state of demand. © 1991.

Title: Taxable and tax-exempt interest rates
Authors: Scott E. Hein, Jeffrey M. Mercer
Abstract: A single-equation model utilizing taxable/tax-exempt yield spreads is developed to test restrictions required by the Darby-Feldstein inflation/tax hypothesis. Evidence indicates these restrictions generally can be rejected for post-Accord data and that there is important information in both yields linking them to inflation. © 1991.

Title: Innovation, firm size and corporate finance
Authors: Zoltan J. Acs, Steven C. Isberg
Abstract: The empirical results presented here suggest that asset-specificity as measured by innovation may be significantly related to corporate capital structure. © 1991.

Title: Some evidence on the efficiency of the sterling-dollar and sterling-franc forward exchange rates in the interwar period
Abstract: We present new evidence on the time series properties of spot and forward exchange rates for the sterling-dollar and sterling-franc exchange rates in the interwar period. Unlike previous researchers we examine the stationarity of the data. Our results are consistent with the hypothesis that the forward rates for both currencies exhibited a time-varying risk premium but that this was non-stationary for the former rate and stationary for the latter. © 1991.

Title: Testing the endogeneity of tariff policy in the U.S.
Authors: Alok K. Bohara, William H. Kaempfer
Abstract: Endogenous tariff theory suggests tariffs are created in response to self-interested political pressure. Using a VARMA model covering the period 1890-1970 in the U.S., we show that macroeconomic variables which proxy political pressure Granger-cause the tariff. © 1991.

Title: The relationship between on-budget and off-budget government
Abstract: This paper studies the hypothesis that controls on on-budget government spending leads to greater off-budget activity. Existence of a substitution effect suggests that our ability to control and measure the size of government is more difficult than previously thought. © 1991.

Title: Economic determinants of trading volume in futures markets
Abstract: In this paper, we test first, the hypothesis that the volume of trade in futures markets follows a random walk process. Next, we examine the role of several monthly macroeconomic variables and find that these variables have a statistically significant impact on the trading volume. The economic consequences of our findings indicate that futures traders, futures exchanges, regulatory agencies and others associated with futures markets activities act rationally in watching closely these macroeconomic variables. © 1991.

Title: A log-change index number formula for multilateral comparisons
Abstract: This paper provides a multilateral generalization of the well-known Theil-Tornqvist binary log-change index number. The index derived in the paper is shown to be transitive, base-invariant and posseses useful least-squares properties. © 1991.

Title: Extensions of the Hansen-Sargent prediction formulas to sampled and aggregated data
Abstract: This paper uses a state-space framework to extend the prediction formulas of Hansen and Sargent (1981) to sampled and aggregated data. The formulas contained in this paper can be used, for example, in Rational Expectations models in which the decision horizon of the agent is longer than the time interval between successive observations of the exogenous forcing variables. © 1991.

Title: Over-rejections in rational expectations models
Abstract: Standard tests for rationality may not have the correct size if there is feedback from innovations to future values of the regressors. It is shown that nonparametric tests reject at their nominal level and display good power in a variety of specifications of a model involving feedback. © 1991.

Title: Identifying and estimating efficient markets models with contemporaneous instruments
Abstract: This paper considers instrumental variables techniques to estimate reduced form efficient markets models while controlling for the effects of a subset of innovations variables on the main variable of interest. Asymptotic properties of the estimators are derived which correct for the generated regressors problem. © 1991.

Title: Unit roots and seasonal unit roots in macroeconomic time series
Authors: Hahn Shik Lee, Pierre L. Siklos
Abstract: Unit root tests are conducted to determine whether the unit root found in seasonal adjusted data may be due to seasonal adjustment filters typically applied by government agencies (i.e., ARIMA X-11). We find that a unit root exists in both the raw and adjusted data (except for the unemployment rate). Second, we also find that the commonly used seasonal adjustment filter introduced by Box and Jenkins (1970) is generally inappropriate. © 1991.

Title: Communication and superior cooperation in two-player normal form games
Abstract: In many games, players may be able to cooperate for their collective benefit without jeopardizing individual rationality However, attaining such superior cooperation requires that players conform to a specific axiom of behavior. In this paper, I demonstrate that pre-play communication also stimulates superior cooperation. © 1991.

Title: The disparity between willingness to pay and compensation demanded
Abstract: The existence of a disparity between willingness to pay and compensation demanded is tested in three controlled experiments. The results indicate a modest initial disparity which is reduced in a learning environment. © 1991.

Title: On the theory of repeated games with private information
Abstract: We consider repeated games with private information, discounting and communication. Similarly to Abreu et al. (1986, 1987), we characterize supergame-equilibrium allocations with truthful revelation. In the two-player case, efficiency cannot be attained with supergame equilibria with truthful revelation. © 1991.

Title: On the theory of repeated games with private information
Abstract: We consider repeated games with private information and discounting. We present an example in which the repetition of the one-shot equilibrium is the only reasonable supergame equilibrium, even though each player can almost perfectly monitor the other players' choices. © 1991.

Title: Asymmetric bidding in second-price, common-value auctions
Abstract: Two comparative static characterizations for common-value auctions under second-price rules are extended to heterogeneous bidders: the willingness-to-pay of the two highest bidders is enhanced on average by the release of public information, and best responses are less aggressive when facing more rival bidders. © 1991.

Title: Protecting the winner
Abstract: In oral auctions, unlike sealed-bid second-price auctions, the winner never reveals his reservation price. We investigate bidders' strategies in the two auctions when third-parties can exploit information revealed by the auction. When exploitation is likely, oral auctions are more efficient than sealed-bid second-price auctions, and preferred by all participants. © 1991.

Title: The value of public information in majority decisions
Abstract: The public disclosure of information can harm none, some or even all voters in majority decision. We distinguish cases in which a minority, a majority or the whole electorate are negatively affected by public information. © 1991.

Title: Hypergraph conflict analysis
Abstract: This paper gives an overview of the further elaboration of the hypergraph conflict model, introduced by Paelinck and Vossen (1983), allowing of describing a conflict situation in a very concise manner. Moreover, some properties of choice situations, interesting from a conflict-theoretical point of view, can be translated directly into hypergraph parameters. © 1991.

Title: Market structure and the empirical specification of profit margins
Abstract: We present evidence from a panel of U.K. manufacturing industries to test the sensitivity of the margins-concentration relationship to specification changes in the dependent variable. Instrumental variable estimates demonstrate that a positive association between profit margins and concentration is contingent on how the margin is formulated. © 1991.

Title: The predictive power of January returns in foreign and domestic markets
Abstract: In the post World War II era, cumulative returns from February through December in the US and in other large equity markets relate positively to the preceding January's returns in those markets. However, in the US, the January return in the pre-War era is negatively related to the cumulative February-December return over the same period. Thus, although risk premia vary over time in a manner that can be predicted ex ante, exogenous shocks to the economy (e.g., war) can disrupt the relation one is accustomed to observing. © 1991.

Title: Debt-equity choice under asymmetric information and taxes
Authors: Jayant R. Kale, Thomas H. Noe
Abstract: Under asymmetric information regarding the quality of investment opportunities and a tax advantage to debt, it is demonstrated that a separating equilibrium in which higher-quality firms issue equity and lower-quality firms issue debt may exist. Thus, the 'pecking order' theory may break down when debt financing enjoys a tax advantage. © 1991.

Title: On the instability of financial patterns of failed firms and the predictability of corporate failure
Abstract: The empirical evidence of this study indicates that financial patterns of failed firms are clearly more unstable than those of non-failed firms. This instability apparently causes significant problems when predicting corporate failure using financial ratios. © 1991.

Title: The Marshall-Lerner condition reconsidered
Abstract: The usual Marshall-Lerner condition à la the price adjustment process is inadequate, and we obtain the true stability condition for international equilibrium. Paradoxical comparative statics results follow naturally for the stable equilibrium, while they all vanish under constant-returns-to-scale. © 1991.

Title: Simple rules to order irreversible income alternatives sequentially
Abstract: We identify a simple sufficient condition for optimal sequential exploitation of a set of income generating alternatives. If these are identical except for differences in the standard deviation of income, the condition implies that the optimal ordering is obtained by always setting the most uncertain alternative up front. If the alternatives are identical except for differences in flow-fixed operating costs, then, depending on the magnitudes of cost differentials, the optimal sequential ordering may or may not be to produce in order of increasing costs. © 1991.

Title: On Wiener-Granger causality, information and canonical correlation
Abstract: A simple procedure is suggested for testing Wiener-Granger causality in stationary multivariate time series, which is based on Geweke's measure for Wiener-Granger causality and canonical correlation coefficients. The procedure is direct in the sense that no auto-regressive (AR), or mixed autoregressive moving average (ARMA), models have to be estimated first, in this way avoiding potential estimation problems, such as multicollinearity, which may occur. © 1991.

Title: Generalized instrumental variables estimation of autoregressive conditional heteroskedastic models
Authors: Robert W. Rich, Jennie Raymond, J.S. Butler
Abstract: This paper considers an alternative to maximum likelihood (ML) estimation of the autoregressive conditional heteroskedastic (ARCH) model introduced in Engle (1982). Specifically, the analysis demonstrates that Hansen's (1982) generalized method of moments (GMM) procedure can be applied for estimation of ARCH models. As an illustration, we compare the results from ML estimation and GMM estimation of Engle and Kraft's (1983) ARCH model of U.S. inflation. © 1991.

Title: On BLU-estimation with data of different periodicity
Abstract: We study a classical regression model where observations on n endogenous variables are annual, while their sum as well as explanatory variables are given on a quarterly basis. The BLUE is shown to be a linear combination of common least-squares estimators, even when the dependent variables are correlated. © 1991.

Title: Efficiency bound calculations for a time series model, with conditional heteroskedasticity
Abstract: This note presents an algorithm for calculating an efficiency bound among a class of estimators for a continous time financial economics model and a martingale taxation model. © 1991.

Title: Instrument choice and tests for a unit root
Abstract: In this paper we report evidence from a small simulation on the impact of instrument choice on the finite sample distribution of an instrumental variables based test for a unit root in a time series proposed by Hall (1989a). © 1991.

Title: On the power of Dickey-Fuller tests against fractional alternatives
Authors: Francis X. Diebold, Glenn D. Rudebusch
Abstract: We examine the properties of Dickey-Fuller unit root tests under fractionally-integrated alternatives and find that these tests have quite low power. © 1991.

Title: Artificial regressions and C (α) tests
Abstract: Any artificial regression that can be used to compute Lagrange multiplier tests can just as easily be used to compute C (α) tests. This also makes it possible to compute Wald-like tests by means of artificial regressions. © 1991.

Title: The important econometric features of a linear regression model with cross-correlated random coefficients
Authors: Karen Smith Conway, Thomas J. Kniesner
Abstract: Theoretical and empirical research presented illustrates how adding cross-correlated components to the Hildreth-Houck random coefficient regression model can eliminate negative estimated variances and uncover coefficient randomness otherwise masked. © 1991.

Title: Human capital investment in wealth-constrained families with two-sided altruism
Abstract: It is well known that, with one-sided altruism a bequest-constrained household will under-invest in their child's human capital. Government transfers to such a household will unambiguously increase human capital investment. We show, with two-sided altruism and an operative gift motive, human capital investment will be efficient under a subgame perfect equilibrium, but will remain inefficiently low under a Nash equilibrium. Government transfers cease to affect investment under either equilibrium notion. © 1991.

Title: Government purchases and real interest rates with endogenous time preference
Abstract: The observation of low real interest rates during periods of high temporary government purchases, such as wars, can be reconciled with the neoclassical growth model extended to allow for endogenous time preference. Temporary increases in government purchases lead to a fall in the instantaneous rate of time preference. This may result in rising investment and falling real interest rates along an adjustment path. © 1991.

Title: On the specification of accelerator coefficients in dynamic factor demand models
Authors: Ingmar R. Prucha, M. Ishaq Nadiri
Abstract: Recent empirical application of dynamic factor demand models employed different formulae for the accelerator coefficient. In this note we compare and analyze the respective formulae used for the accelerator coefficient. © 1991.

Title: Bubbles and inefficiencies
Abstract: We study speculative behavior in a stochastic overlapping-generations model and we show how the link between the existence of bubbles and dynamic inefficiency, which has been established for the deterministic case, is broken when risk-related factors, such as risk premia and capital gains, are explicitly taken into account. © 1991.

Title: An error correction system for integrated consumption and portfolio allocation decisions
Abstract: In this paper I show how an error correction system arises for the determination of consumption and portfolio allocation decisions. The influential work of Hendry and von Ungern-Sternberg (HUS) is extended to provide equations for consumption and the disaggregation of wealth into n(>1) components. © 1991.

Title: Cross-sectional versus panel estimates of union wage effects
Authors: Phanindra V. Wunnava, Albert A. Okunade
Abstract: The main objective of this paper is to compare and reconcile the cross-sectional and the panel estimates of union wage effects. It uses Panel Survey of Income Dynamics (PSID) data for a period of 6 years (1979-1984). Unlike what Freeman (1984) predicted (i.e., panel union wage estimates would be smaller than pure cross-sectional estimates due to the cumulative nature of the errors in reporting union status in the former), both the cross-sectional and panel estimates of union wage effects are very similar ranging from 11 to 13%. Unions seem to have flattering effect on the age-earnings profiles. Not surprisingly, the rate of return to schooling of non-union members is larger than that of the union members. © 1991.

Title: Investment, profit-sharing and the degree of centralization
Abstract: This paper examines monopoly unions which are strong enough to use two-part tariffs (i.e., basic wages plus profit shares). It is shown that decentralization in bargaining increases the total pay per worker and lowers the levels of capital stock and income. © 1991.

Title: The relative effects of unemployment insurance parameters on search strategy
Abstract: This paper theoretically examines the relative effect of two unemployment insurance parameters on search behavior. The relative influence of each parameter is found to depend upon what an individual could expect to earn if he worked part-time while searching. © 1991.

Title: The role of employers' authority when jobs are partially enforceable
Abstract: The paper extends Simon's notion of authority to the case of partial job enforceability and shows that, besides allowing the adjustment of jobs to the state of the world, it is also useful as a device for the control of worker shirking. © 1991.

Title: Price elasticities for residential demand for telephone calling time
Abstract: The paper shows how price elasticities for telephone calling time can be estimated when there is little or no variability in the telephone tariff, taking into account the fact that the price per minute of calling time differs across distance zones as well as according to when the call is made. We apply this method to data on residential demand for telephone calling time in Sweden. © 1991.

Title: Exchange rate pass-through
Abstract: The pass-through relationship between exchange rate and prices of manufactured exports is examined for Korea. It is found that exporters take competitors' prices at the prime mover of price setting and let profits bear the brunt of adjustment to the exchange rate changes. © 1991.

Title: Taxation of foreign capital and the optimum tariff
Abstract: Given that the host country has the monopoly power in the exportable market, this paper has been concerned with the optimum tariffs in a specific model where the internationally mobile capital is specific to the import-competing sector. The distinctive feature of this paper is approaching the optimal trade policies as an illustration of the theory of second-best. The second-best tariff rate depends on the given rate of tax on foreign capital yields. When the tax on foreign investment is greater (smaller) than the optimum rate, a tariff greater (smaller) than the traditional formula is required to correct the distortion and restore the equilibrium. © 1991.

Title: Target zone exchange rate
Abstract: This paper attempts to rationalize the target zone exchange rate system's width proposed by Williamson (1983). The model is a special case of the Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) function. Given the time series distribution, estimated means and variances are plotted on a bounded (upper and lower) standard normal distribution. © 1991.

Title: Optimal public good provision in the Ramsey tax model
Abstract: For the single-consumer Ramsey tax model, the use of distortionary taxation to finance public good provision is shown to lower the optimal level of public good provision below its optimal value ina first-best economy, where lump sum taxation is available. The assumptions used in the proof include a previous Cobb-Douglas example as a special case. © 1991.

Title: Positioning banks for acquisitions
Abstract: Previous research on band mergers examines the phenomenon from the perspective of the acquirer, not the potential target firm. Data on small non-failing independent banks are subject to discriminant analysis in this paper. Findings suggests that positioning banks for acquisition can be analytically delineated so as to crystallize a strategic option. © 1991.

Title: A random coefficient qualitative choice model of telecommunications demand
Authors: Joseph Gatto, Harry Kelejian, Scott Stephan
Abstract: A random coefficient panel data probit model is specified. Estimators are suggested for the realized values of the coefficients, and the parameters of their generating process. Some large sample results are given; others are suggested to stimulate further research. © 1991.

Title: Factoring spectral matrices in linear-quadratic models
Abstract: A spectral factorization method that yields closed form solutions for symmetric matrix functions that arise in linear-quadratic economic models is presented. The method builds on a preliminary factorization using the zeroes of the matrix. © 1991.

Title: Standard errors for Laspeyres and Paasche index numbers
Abstract: In this paper we use the regression approach to index numbers to derive the standard errors for Laspeyres and Paasche index numbers. These standard errors are simple to evaluate. We show that these standard errors are linked to the variability of relative prices. When there are more changes in relative prices, the standard errors are higher. © 1991.

Title: A note on testing for switching regressions
Abstract: This note shows that a well-known version of the switching regression model is not suitable for testing for parameter stability in a regression model because standard regularity conditions are not satisfied under the null hypothesis of parameter stability. © 1991.

Title: Equilibrium misperceptions
Abstract: There has been a growing interest among economists in behavior which appears to be anomalous with respect to the axioms of economic rationality. A number of recent papers have analyzed the effects of agents' misperceptions about the relationship between actions and outcomes. The 'rationality' of these misperceptions has not been considered, however. In this paper we prove the existence of an equilibrium with misperceptions in which misperceptions are 'rational' and can be sustained. © 1991.

Title: On hoarding in contract theory
Abstract: This paper examines the practice of ignoring hoarding in the theory of repeated contracts by analyzing a two-period signalling game. It is shown that (a) hoarding could be an equilibrium, and (b) excluding it from the model is equivalent to adding assumptions on the optimal contract. © 1991.

Title: Moral hazard and cooperation
Abstract: We consider a situation in which a principal hires two agents whose cooperation is profitable from a technical point of view. The characteristics of the optimal contract are strongly dependent on the agents' commitment capacity, that allows them to reach more efficient outcomes. © 1991.

Title: Why real wages do not fall when there is unemployment
Authors: James M. Holmes, Mike Dowd, David C. Black
Abstract: Erroneous anticipations of fiscal policy results in involuntary unemployment. If mutually agreeable, unemployment may be eradicated by recontracting the real wage and employment level. However, if labor demand is inelastic, unit elastic, or within a bounded elastic range, unemployment persists. © 1991.

Title: Uninformed customers and nonprofit organization
Abstract: When product quality is unobservable before purchase, the equilibrium price may be inefficiently high in order to signal high quality. We present a reputation model where under reasonable assumption nonprofit organizations can credibly charge lower prices than for-profit organizations. © 1991.

Title: Finitely optimal allocation in countably large-square exchange economies
Abstract: A countably large-square exchange economy is said to be of overlapping-generations type if an allocation can be Pareto-improved upon through a trade involving only a finite number of agents if it can be improved upon through a trade involving only finite numbers of agents and commodities. A necessary and sufficient condition is given for economies to be of overlapping-generation type. © 1991.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Further evidence on the job search theory
Abstract: The prediction of the job search theory that there is a negative correlation between reservation wage and the re-employment probability is tested. It is found that the unemployed who find a job are a self-selecting group of individuals with a relatively low reservation wage. © 1990.

Title: The effect of conviction on the legitimate income of criminals
Abstract: I show that for many crimes the effect of reduced income from conviction constitutes a major penalty and that the absolute size of this penalty seems to be positively related to the level of the criminal's preconviction income. © 1990.

Title: The fleeting effect of advertising
Abstract: This paper adds to the evidence that advertising effects depreciate rapidly. Inclusion of lagged advertising in empirical models may be unnecessary. In addition, the notion that accumulated advertising effects may be a barrier to entry is called into question. © 1990.

Title: Optimality of coupon-bearing debt under asymmetric information
Abstract: We show that a zero-coupon bond, despite its attractive features, will be dominated in equilibrium under asymmetric information by a fixed-coupon bond as a result of unfavorable market beliefs regarding the quality of firms which choose to issue zero-coupon bonds. © 1990.

Title: Entering a preannounced currency band
Authors: Masaki Ichikawa, Marcus Miller, Alan Sutherland
Abstract: Krugman (1988) provides a stationary characterisation of an exchange rate inside a currency band. Here we derive the non-stationary solution for a floating exchange rate which applies when currency dealers expect such a band to be imposed at a known future date. © 1990.

Title: Tax arbitrage and the redistributive properties of progressive income taxation
Abstract: Contrary to the popular view, this paper shows that tax arbitrage may reduce inequality. We also show that tax arbitrage is likely to benefit individuals located at the tails of the income distribution at the expense of those located at the center. © 1990.

Title: Does correcting for heteroscedasticity help?
Abstract: This paper conducts Monte Carlo simulation experiments for a particular example in the literature using the Hansen-Hodrick-Newey-West-White methodology and concludes that correcting for heteroscedasticity can substantially worsen statistical inference even when heteroscedasticity is present in the data. © 1990.

Title: Some evidence on the accuracy of Phillips-Perron tests using alternative estimates of nuisance parameters
Abstract: Simulation evidence is presented on the performance of the Phillips-Perron correction to the Dickey-Fuller tests, using three different spectral windows. The choice of spectral window does not make an important difference. However, knowledge of the true value of the spectrum at zero improves the test considerably. © 1990.

Title: Testing for the correct error term distribution
Authors: Richard A. Hofler, Lee C. Spector
Abstract: This paper presents a simple and easy to use test for selecting the appropriate model to estimate when the alternatives differ as to the distribution of their respective error terms: symmetric vs. skewed. The test is conducted in two steps, each employing a simple and time-honored test statistic and provides another tool in the spirit of the specification test literature. That is, this test permits the analyst to determine the correct characteristics of his model rather than assuming incorrect characteristics and, hence, drawing erroneous conclusions. © 1990.

Title: Shock persistence and the measurement of prewar output series
Abstract: Recent studies find that shocks to U.S. output series for 1869-1929 are not persistent. The note argues that this finding may be an artifact because linear interpolation was used for constructing U.S. prewar output series. © 1990.

Title: Contractual delay and efficiency in delegation games
Abstract: In a two-principal delegation game by Fershtman et al. (1987), we characterize strict implementation of joint actions, where each principal can decide a compensation schedule of her agent after observing the other principal's decision with some small positive probability. © 1990.

Title: A multiple-object auction with superadditive values
Abstract: A multiple-object auction is studied in which bidders' valuations are determined in a production game. The objects could be operating licenses or capacity. Expected revenue is maximized when they are all sold to a single bidder. © 1990.

Title: Additive non-transitive preferences
Abstract: This note summarizes recent contributions to multiple-factor non-transitive preference theory. It considers representations in which preferences are reflected by positive sums of intrafactor utilities. © 1990.

Title: Minimal cooperation in bargaining
Abstract: Mid-point domination requires that the solution outcome dominate or be dominated by a reference point. By investigating two different formulations of the condition, we present characterizations of the Nash and the Kalai-Rosenthal solutions for n-person bargaining problems. © 1990.

Title: The effects of non-binding price announcements on posted-offer markets
Abstract: We report four posted-offer triopolies which examine the effects of 'trade-press' style price announcements. Although the injection of announcements increases prices initially, sellers uniformly defect from announced intentions, and prices tend toward pre-announcement levels. © 1990.

Title: Heterogeneous matching, mismatch and the macro U-V curve
Abstract: Standard measures of mismatch in the labor market are based of the assumption of homogenous matching technologies. This paper presents a simple model of heterogeneous matching and shows that equilibrium heterogeneity has drastic effects on the standard measures of mismatch. © 1990.

Title: English language proficiency and the economic progress of immigrants
Abstract: This paper studies the impact of English language proficiency on the wages of immigrants and second-generation persons in the U.S. using a data set providing test-based measures of English reading proficiency. The results indicate that English reading proficiency is a major factor constraining the wage rates received by immigrants. © 1990.

Title: Placement service and offer arrival rates
Abstract: Determinants of job referrals by the Austrian employment exchange are analyzed concentrating on three issues: The validity of the Poisson assumption, allocation strategies of scarce vacancies and the stationarity of offer arrival rates over time. © 1990.

Title: Non-permanent jobs and search theory
Abstract: In a simple search theoretical framework it is demonstrated that introducing promotion chances as a job characteristics might be very relevant. © 1990.

Title: Market structure, incentive to patent and the pace of innovation
Abstract: In a model of sequential innovations, it is shown that the simple monotone relationship between the number of firms and the speed of innovation [see, e.g., Loury (1979)] no longer holds if we explicitly take account of the incentive to patent. © 1990.

Title: Exchange rates and the trade balance
Abstract: The impact of the exchange rate on the trade balance is examined for a number of developing countries. Non-structural techniques indicate that a depreciation of the real exchange rate is not strongly associated with a significant improvement in the trade balance. © 1990.

Title: On the estimation of a fixed effects model with selectivity bias
Abstract: In case of sample selectivity the maximum likelihood estimator of the parameters in a model with fixed effects will not be consistent when the number of time periods is small. In this paper, we present a transformation to eliminate the fixed individual effects and show that the corresponding marginal maximum likelihood estimator is computationally feasible and can be used to estimate the remaining parameters consistently even if number of time periods is finite. © 1990.

Title: Bootstrap tests for generalized least squares regression models
Abstract: This paper shows that certain statistics in the normal linear regression model may be bootstrapped to obtain test procedures with faster rates of convergence than the usual normal approximation. Specifically, bootstrapping a standardized estimator of the regression coefficients is shown to produce errors with smaller order than n-1, and bootstrapping a variance-adjusted statistic gives errors of smaller order than n-2. An advantage of the bootstrap is that it provides an additional step in asymptotic accuracy without the necessity of explicitly calculating correction terms. © 1990.

Title: Cointegration and I(0) measurement error bias
Abstract: This note investigates the properties of Granger's proposition, if x t and y t are integrated of order one, but are only observed with measurement error, then the two observed series will also be cointegrated if all measurement errors are I(0). The Monte Carlo experiments reveal that the proposition holds, however at the expense of committing a type 1 error. © 1990.

Title: A state space representation of sequential estimators
Abstract: The paper shows how sequential estimation problems, which use regressors generated in auxiliary equations, can be transformed into state space representations. This allows estimation by exact full information maximum likelihood via the Kalman filter. © 1990.

Title: Long-term partnership in a repeated prisoner's dilemma with random matching
Abstract: We consider a repeated prisoner's dilemma with random matching. According to the unanimity principle, players can continue their long-term partnership. The Folk Theorem holds on the assumption that strategies are time-and-history-independent. © 1990.

Title: Is the Allais paradox robust to a seemingly trivial change of frame?
Abstract: The Allais choices over uncertain prospects are reframed so that lotteries are presented without reference to decimals or fractions, but utilize the mechanism of numbers on a wheel. A statisticallysignificant reduction in violations of the independence axiom is observed. © 1990.

Title: Revelation in informational dynamic settings
Abstract: The most natural extension of the revelation principle does not apply to situations where outcomes are chosen in several periods in which agents receive private signals. A correct extension for this situation is provided. © 1990.

Title: Consumption and asset returns under non-expected utility
Abstract: This paper implements on quarterly time series data for Israel the orthogonality conditions derived from an intertemporal consumption-based asset pricing model with non-expected utility. The model's restrictions are not rejected by the sample information and there is evidence against the commonly used expected-utility formulation. © 1990.

Title: On the non existence of envy-free and egalitarian-equivalent allocations in economies with indivisibilities
Abstract: We consider economies with indivisible goods (houses, jobs) and one infinitely divisible good. An allocation is envy-free if no agent prefers someone else's consumption to his own. An allocation is egalitarian-equivalent if there is a reference bundle that every agent finds indifferent to his consumption. We show that in such economies there may be no allocation that is both egalitarian-equivalent and envy-free. © 1990.

Title: Monotonicity of solutions in certain dynamic cooperative games
Abstract: We consider cooperative games in which new players are sequentially added, while the underlying structure is held constant, and examine monotonicity of the core and value for convex games, linear production games, and minimum cost spanning tree games. © 1990.

Title: Optimal sales to users who hold inventory
Abstract: This paper solves the optimal inventory policy when both the supplier and the users can hold inventory: The supplier can hold the good until such a time as a buyer wishes to purchase it; a user can purchase a good before he needs it and hold it until the need arises, or delay the purchase and incur a shortage. The welfare-maximizing policy is shown to require periods of shortage in which no sales are made. We also show that the profit-maximizing policy will involve shorter periods of no-sales than does the welfare-maximizing policy. © 1990.

Title: Market power and the institutional asymmetry of the posted offer trading institution
Authors: Douglas D. Davis, Arlington W. Williams
Abstract: This paper reports a series of market experiments examining the conjecture that the institutional asymmetry inherent in posted-offer pricing can suppress the exercise of market power by the non-posting side of the market. The data clearly support this conjecture if market power is defined as a unilateral incentive to manipulate the market price via strategic quantity withholding. © 1990.

Title: Second-best subsidies in monopolistic competition
Abstract: In the Spence-Dixit-Stiglitz model of monopolistic competition, an output (or input) subsidy is welfare-improving, under competitive conjecture. The significance of this result is that it holds even when the subsidy exacerbates the potential problem of excess product diversity. © 1990.

Title: Erratum
Consumption and transitory income
Abstract: The French survey concerning households expectations allows to prove on the actual anticipations declared by the households the influence of non-anticipated (transitory) income upon the realization of their intentions to purchase durables, contrary to the Friedman permanent income hypothesis. © 1990.

Title: Male/female earnings differentials and the measurement of skills
Abstract: In this note we suggest coupling occupation data with educational data to construct a better measure of labour skills using the Laspeyres index approach. With the resulting measure of the female/male skills ratio we are able to corroborate estimates of the decomposition of earnings obtained using the standard Oaxaca methodology. © 1990.

Title: Tax-induced bias in forward rates, term premiums, and the term structure of interest rates
Abstract: This paper's analysis on the tax-induced bias in forward rates enables us to better understand the structure of term premiums and the term structure of interest rates and to obtain a better estimate of the future interest rate. In particular, the anomaly of negative term premiums regarding long maturities as reported by Fama (1984) is resolved. © 1990.

Title: Do general and firm-specific employer payroll taxes have the same incidence?
Abstract: This paper shows that there are theoretical reasons to distinguish between general payroll taxes and firm-specific payroll taxes and that their incidence can be different. Data for collective agreements, signed in Quebec by large firms in the secondary sector for the 1975-1984 period, are used to estimate their incidence. © 1990.

Title: The effect of federal deficits and debt on the tax-adjusted, short-term, real interest rate
Abstract: The stock versus flow effect of the federal debt/deficit on a real interest rate is examined in a reduced-form equation. The evidence shows a positive and significant linkage between the federal debt and an ex-post, tax-adjusted, short-term, real interest rate. © 1990.

Title: Examining statistical differences between using returns and yields to maturity in bond market event studies
Abstract: This paper investigates the statistical differences between using returns and using yields in bond market event studies. The analysis shows that there are systematic differences between the statistical tests of the two methodologies. The differences depend on the bond's duration, whether the new is perceived to be good or bad, and the size of the bond's yield change. © 1990.

Title: The informational efficiency of the stock market
Authors: Chyong-Chiou Jeng, J.S. Butler, Jin-Tan Liu
Abstract: The stock markets and money supplies of ten countries in the 1920s are examined. Most stock markets are found to be informationally efficient, but not those of the United States and United Kingdom. © 1990.

Title: A note on the Lagrange multiplier and F-statistics for two stage least squares regressions
Abstract: The asymptotic properties of a regression-based Lagrange multiplier test for omitted variables in the context of two stage least squares is discussed, and an F-statistic for 2SLS regressions is proposed. The choice of instruments under the null and alternative models is explicitly considered, thereby clearing up some unresolved issues in the literature. © 1990.

Title: Choosing among multiple nonlinear non-nested regression models with different dependent variables
Authors: Marlene A. Smith, David J. Smyth
Abstract: The linearly-embedded regression model approach of Davidson and MacKinnon (1981) is used to construct joint tests of seven non-nested, autoregressive money demand equations with different regressands. The results support the Holmes-Smyth (1972) hypothesis that taxes affect money demand. © 1990.

Title: A computational algorithm for multiple equation models with panel data
Abstract: By stacking observations by individuals across equations, we propose a simpler computational algorithm to estimate multiple-equations error-components models with or without simultaneity using the Choleski decomposition of the resultant covariance matrix of residuals. This generalizes the Fuller-Batesse transformation to the multiple equation case. © 1990.

Title: The conditional logit estimator for unequal panels
Abstract: The paper generalizes the conditional logit estimator available for equal panels to the case where panels may be unequal. It is then applied to estimate the parameters of the capital idling decision rule at a micro level. © 1990.

Title: Specification errors and the Chow test
Abstract: Predictive forms of the Chow test are used in investigating structural change when the number of predictors exceeds the number of observations. This test has been argued to be more powerful than the more widely used analysis of covariance test even when the number of predictors does not exceed the number of observations. In that circumstance we show that either the hypothesis claimed is not testable or the test is not uniformly most powerful excepting a fortuitous coincidence between the number of predictors and the number of observations. We suggest an alternative test for structural change conditional on a prior specification test adapted from McAleer and Tse (1988). © 1990.

Title: GAITL: A generalised version of the almost ideal and translog demand systems.
Abstract: AI and Translog are popular models in empirical demand literature. In this paper we present a generalised model (GAITL) which nests both and, moreover, the Lewbel (1989) demand system. Estimation and statistical testing based on Italian household data suggests rejection of both in favour of the GAITL, also when demographic effects are considered. © 1990.

Title: The policy anticipation hypothesis and the expected inflation hypothesis
Authors: D.A. Peel, P.F. Pope, K. Paudyal
Abstract: Using price index linked and conventional bonds issued by the UK Government, estimates of expected inflation and the expected real interest rate are derived. These estimates are employed to investigate the relationship between components of the nominal interest rate and surprise monetary change. The empirical results support the expected inflation hypothesis rather than the policy anticipation hypothesis. © 1990.

Title: Seasonal unit-root tests on Canadian macroeconomic time series
Abstract: In this note we subject some Canadian macroeconomic time series to test of seasonal and non-seasonal unit roots. Overall we find evidence that the series are integrated at some of the seasonal frequencies as at a zero frequency. © 1990.

Title: How big is the random walks in macroeconomic time series
Abstract: The paper applies the Lo and MacKinlay (1988) and Cochrane (1988) variance-ratio test to the data sample used by Nelson and Plosser (1982), who studies the stationarity properties of 14 macroeconomic variables. The results of our empirical tests indicate that the macroeconomic time series have significant random walk components, with the exception of unemployment, real wages, real per capita GNP and industrial production. These results generally agree with those reported earlier by Nelson and Plosser who found that 13 out of 14 macroeconomic variables followed random walk and with Cochrane who, more recently, found that GNP had a small random walk component. The contribution of this paper lies in its use of a very recent methodology to estimate the magnitude of the random walk component of certain macroeconomic time series. © 1990.

Title: Dominant strategy mechanisms with mutually payoff-relevant private information and with public information
Abstract: We present a necessary and sufficient condition for truthful revelation in dominant strategies in the collective choice problem with full transferability, where private information is mutually payoff-relevant and there exists verifiable public information. We present a tractable sufficient condition. © 1990.

Title: A note on the strategic transmission of endogenous information
Abstract: Crawford and Sobel (1982) discuss the role of the transmission of unverifiable information. It is shown that when the information is about the players' actions this kind of communication does not affect the outcome of the game. © 1990.

Title: On the penalties for unfair labor practices
Abstract: The impact of various types of unfair labor practices (henceforth ULPs) on their likelihood of being penalized is evaluated in the presence of geographical differences in the propensity of courts in the U.S. to penalize ULPs. © 1990.

Title: An international comparison of sector wage differentials
Abstract: Using internationally comparable micro data interindustry wage differentials are estimated for men in five countries. Contrary to a widely shared view the patterns of differentials seem to be different across the countries. © 1990.

Title: Labor supply, unemployment benefits in an open economy model of interwar Britain
Abstract: We estimate a labor supply function in an open economy setting for interwar Britain. The results are generally negative. This suggests that high unemployment benefits did not work directly on shifting labor supply in a market clearing model. © 1990.

Title: Estimating seat belt effectiveness with seat belt usage data from the Centers for Disease Control
Abstract: A state cross-sectional model of traffic fatalities estimates the effectiveness of seat belts with data on usage from the Centers for Disease Control [Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (1987), henceforth BRFSS]. Seat belts have no statistically significant effect for total or driver or overall occupant fatalities. However, deaths for non-occupants and passengers increase with seat belt usage. The results suggest offsetting consumer behavior as driver drive more dangerously, due to seat belt laws, and non-occupants and passengers may be killed as a result. Care should be exercised in using these results, since the BRFSS data are based on telephone surveys. However, it has been shown here that the carefully gathered North Carolina observational data can be explained with BRFSS data. © 1990.

Title: An empirical analysis of a firm's decision to franchise
Abstract: Hypotheses from monitoring and search cost explanations for the existence of franchising are discussed and tested. The evidence offers strong support for the search theory, somewhat weaker support for the monitoring/shirking theory, and no support for the monitoring/cheating hypothesis. © 1990.

Title: Unions, taxes and the structure of multinational enterprises
Abstract: This note analyzes how a firm's relationship with unions or tax authorities influences its basic structure. In particular, it is shown that the prospect of capture by unions or tax authorities of part of the rents associated with the firm's investments leads it to open more plants than is technologically efficient. Thus unions and taxes are an independent reason for a firm's expansion nationally and for foreign direct investment. © 1990.

Title: Export composition and the impact of exports on economic growth of developing economies
Abstract: Employing an augmented production-function framework, a number of studies have found that export growth exerts a positive impact on GDP growth in less developed countries (LDCs), even when capital and labor are controlled for. Using a similar framework but recognizing the possible heterogeneity of exports, the present paper finds, for the 1960-1980 period, that while the primary export sector exhibits little or no effect on GDP growth in LCDs, there is a differential positive impact by the manufacturing export sector. © 1990.

Title: Tax-based incomes policies and productivity deals
Abstract: A model is constructed in which a tax-based incomes policy operates and where firms pay productivity bonuses to their employees. The optimal rate of tax is derived under various assumptions. © 1990.

Title: A test of the arbitrage pricing theory using accounting information
Abstract: In this note we present a method to test the Arbitrage Pricing Theory (APT) using aggregated accounting information. Empirical evidence indicates that this method offers a fruitful way to test the APT. © 1990.

Title: Testing the replication hypothesis
Abstract: Between the time OLS estimates are computed on N observations and replication is attempted, the data matrix accumulates C rows of gross errors. Fitting the reported OLS estimates to the contaminated data will produce N-C residuals which agree exactly with the original residuals. This fact serves as the basis of a test for replication. © 1990.

Title: CORE: For decision models under uncertainty
Authors: T.V.S. Ramamohan Rao, Saraswati P. Singh
Abstract: In Rao and Singh (1987) the analysis of a specific class of identification problems that arise in the context of estimating decision models of the firm under uncertainty was initiated. In that paper a maximum likelihood estimator was presented in the context of a simple model. When a generalization of the result was attempted it appeared that a class of constrained regression estimators (henceforth CORE) can also be developed. This note is a report of the alternative estimators of this general class of identification problems. © 1990.

Title: A chi-square test for a unit root
Abstract: The present paper develops a chi-square test for a unit root that has higher power than Dickey-Fuller tests when the sample size is small and the autoregressive root is close to one. © 1990.

Title: Cointegrating exogeneity
Abstract: Cointegration exists in open loop systems, but existing theory provides no way to distinguish between cointegration amongst exogenous and endogenous variables. We provide a condition for distinguishing between such cointegration effects, that is also valid for open loop systems. © 1990.

Title: Preliminary-test estimation of the standard error of estimate in linear regression
Abstract: This paper considers the estimation of the 'standard error of estimate' after a preliminary test of restrictions in a linear regression model. A finite-sample expression for the risk of a family of such pre-test estimators is derived and evaluated numerically. The results suggest that, generally, pre-testing is the preferred strategy. © 1990.

Title: Quantifying the Allais paradox
Authors: James D. Hess, Duncan M. Holthausen
Abstract: Weighted linear utility explains Allais' paradox, yet preserves much of the analytic structure of standard expected utility. This paper identifies the two crucial parameters of weighted linear utility - risk aversion and eccentricity. Eccentricity is a measure of how much the decision maker systematically distorts the probabilities in choosing between lotteries. © 1990.

Title: Impossibility results with resoluteness
Abstract: There does not exist a resolute Social Choice Rule that satisfies universal domain, neutrality anonymity and Pareto (or responsiveness) if the number of individuals is not relatively prime to six. © 1990.

Title: Profit sharing and work sharing
Abstract: This paper considers the employment and labour utilisation responses of a firm shifting from a conventional to a profit sharing compensation system. The standard Weitzman model is extended to incorporate both extensive and intensive labour margins. © 1990.

Title: A feasible Nash implementation of Walrasian equilibria in the two-agent economy
Abstract: In this paper, we construct a weakly balanced and continuous mechanism which Nash-implements a Walrasian equilibrium correspondence in the two-agent economy, whereas there are several impossibility results in this economy. © 1990.

Title: The global correspondence principle
Authors: Murray C. Kemp, Yoshio Kimura, Makoto Tawada
Abstract: The Global Correspondence Principle is generally invalid if there are more than two goods. However, attenuated forms of the Principle, valid for any number of goods, can be found by restricting the Jacobian of the excess-demand functions. © 1990.

Title: Editorial Board
Category Index
Author index
Multivariate exogeneity tests and poverty
Authors: Kathy Hayes, D.J. Slottje, Michael Nieswiadomy
Abstract: Many recent studies presume direction of the relationship between poverty and other economic factors is one way, that is, they assume that the various economic phenomena cause or affect poverty and that there is no feedback. However, if feedback is present it is possible that the level of poverty or the perception of poverty may not only impact public policy decisions aimed at eradicating poverty, but may have indirect effects on other economic variables as well. We test that hypothesis in this paper using multivariate exogeneity tests. © 1990.

Title: Quits, layoffs and contracts on sharing investments in specific human capital
Abstract: When the worker is risk averse and has no access to capital markets then the sharing of specific human capital investments with the firm is complicated by considerations for consumption smoothing and productive efficiency. Sharing is no longer solely determined by the fact that one party can inflict a capital loss on the other unilaterally separating. Using a contract framework this paper shows that restricting the right to separate to either the worker or the firm does not necessarily result in that party taking full responsibility of the investments. Whether no sharing remains optimal in such cases will depend on the relative magnitude of the worker's subjective discount rate and the market discount rate for investments. © 1990.

Title: Imperfect information and wage flexibility
Abstract: Differences in the mixture of sectoral to aggregate shocks across economies cause structurally identical economies to respond differently to similar disturbances. Evaluating the flexibility of labor markets in different countries thus requires knowledge of the relative importance of sectoral and aggregate shocks. © 1990.

Title: Regulatory policies in markets for delicate medical procedures
Abstract: This paper examines regulation in markets where firms choose price-liability combinations. Our work implies that a recently suggested regulatory rule, restricting the maximum liability that can be assumed, does not increase consumer welfare. We also study a rule inspired by the German audit market, in which maximum liability is restricted but only as a multiple of the price. This reduction in the dimensionality of firm's strategy space is shown to reduce consumer welfare, if the liability-price multiple is smaller than the multiple observed under no regulation. However, even larger liability-price multiples could leave consumers worse off. © 1990.

Title: A new test of the price-concentration relationship in grocery retailing
Abstract: Using a new data set and including income in the specification, this paper finds that retail grocery prices are not significantly related to market concentration. © 1990.

Title: Optional time-of-use pricing can be pareto superior or pareto inferior
Abstract: Many public utilities offer a choice between time-of-use and flat rates. Two points are established: (1) optional TOU (time-of-use) schedules exist that Pareto dominate both mandatory flat and mandatory TOU rates; but, (2) optional TOU prices based on marginal costs can be welfare-decreasing, even Pareto inferior. © 1990.

Title: How mobile is capital in developing countries?
Authors: Nadeem Ul Haque, Peter J. Montiel
Abstract: The paper develops a technique for measuring the degree of financial openness in financially-repressed economies and applies it to a large sample of developing countries. The results suggest that developing countries, in general, can be characterized as financially-open economies. © 1990.

Title: Efficiency wages and currency devaluation
Abstract: This paper applies the efficiency wage theory, which is a powerful instrument to shed light on why involuntary unemployment is persistent in the labor market, to evaluate the effect of currency devaluation in an open economy. It is found that a currency devaluation will definitely depress the domestic output in the presence of the efficiency wage consideration. This framework can be viewed as a theoretical structure in explaining the empirical findings of contractionary devaluation. © 1990.

Title: Temporary trade taxes, welfare and the current account
Abstract: The welfare and trade balance effects of temporary import tariffs and export subsidies are compared. Ruling out complementarities, a reduction in tariffs improves welfare while increasing export subsidies may not. In general, tariffs or export subsidies have an ambiguous effects on trade balance. © 1990.

Title: A note on the efficiency of the London metal exchange
Authors: Peter S. Sephton, Donald K. Cochrane
Abstract: In this note we examine the market efficiency hypothesis with respect to six metals traded on the London Metal Exchange (LME). Using overlapping data and both single and multimarket models, we find evidence contradictory to the tenet that the LME is an efficient market. © 1990.

Title: On the decomposition and normalization of interindustry linkages
Abstract: A new decomposition of total interindustry linkages into backward and forward linkage components is presented, along with a discussion of the proper way to normalize linkage measures. © 1990.

Title: Global asymptotic stability of non-linear difference
Abstract: A sufficient condition for global asymptotic stability of the origin for non-linear difference equations is presented without assuming the differentiability of the iteration function. This conditions is a generalization of the results of Okuguchi (1977), Fujimoto (1987), and Wu and Brown (1989). © 1990.

Title: A simple test for exogeneity in probit, logit, and poisson regression models
Abstract: Several tests for exogeneity currently exist for single equation probit models, most based on variants of limited information maximum likelihood estimators. This paper develops an alternative test by recasting the estimation problem in a non-linear least squares framework. The test is applicable to logit models as well as probit models, and is also extended to provide an exogeneity test for the Poisson regression model. © 1990.

Title: Steady-state productivity relationships
Abstract: This paper investigates the relative importance of short run disequilibrium dynamics and long run equilibrium growth factors in current wage change using a cointegration relationship suggested by steady-state growth theory. © 1990.

Title: Common agency with adverse selection
Abstract: A model of common agency under adverse selection is analysed. We determine the conditions under which a separation equilibrium of the non-cooperative game exists and is unique. This equilibrium can be obtained at minimum cost. © 1990.

Title: Transitivity and consistency
Abstract: In the presence of the Weak Chernoff property, the expansion consistency property known as β characterises transitivity of the base relation. It is shown that β may be replaced by a new property. The new property is a substitution property. Since it is not an expansion consistency property, it is argued that it is some form of equivalent treatment rather than expansion consistency that is the essential requirement for transitivity of the base relation. The content of this paper is taken from the section on collective rationality in Baigent (1989), which contains more results similar to the one offered here. © 1990.

Title: A time-varying model of rational learning
Abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the stability of the rational expectations equilibrium for a version of the cobweb model under time-varying learning. It is shown that for appropriate values of a stability parameter the agents can learn how to form rational expectations forecasts using Kalman filtering estimation techniques. © 1990.

Title: Variable returns to scale and the global correspondence principle in the theory of international trade
Abstract: The global correspondence principle is applied to obtain global theorems on the price-output response and the Rybczynski and Stolper-Samuelson effects for an economy with variable returns to scale. The Marshallian output adjustment process is used to obtain these results. © 1990.

Title: Errata
On a non-cooperative theory of technology transfer
Abstract: This paper shows that it might be profitable for a firm with advanced technology to sell the knowledge to a competing firm with less efficient technology and still remain in the business. A non-corperative equilibrium with technology transfer may Pareto-dominate the initial equilibrium without technology transfer. In this paper it is shown that technology agreement is likely to occur between firms which are reasonably close in terms of their initial technologies. Such an equilibrium is an interesting possibility in the absence of credibly sustainable collusive outcomes. © 1990.

Title: Optional two-part tariffs constrained by price caps
Abstract: Cost reducing incentives possibly generated by price cap regulation may invoke allocative inefficiencies. However, if the regulated firm can offer optional (two-part) tariffs in addition to the price caps, then Pareto optimal outcomes will be reached under quite general conditions. © 1990.

Title: The divergence of SIC industries from antitrust markets
Authors: Russell W. Pittman, Gregory J. Werden
Abstract: A comparison between the size of markets alleged in Justice Department merger cases and SIC industries indicates that SIC industries generally are far larger than antitrust markets. © 1990.

Title: Price and quantity elasticities in U.S. foreign trade
Abstract: A GNP function for the United States, 1948-1987, is estimated. Output is disaggregated between consumption, investment, government purchases, exports, and imports. The 1987 price elasticities of the demand for imports and supply of exports are -0.8 and 1.4, respectively. © 1990.

Title: On the impact of government spending on consumption patterns
Abstract: This study examines the impact of government spending on private consumer expenditure via a theoretically plausible static demand system. Our results are fully consistent with the evidence presented in studies based on macroeconomic models. © 1990.

Title: The solution of time-varying linear rational expectations models and the role of terminal conditions
Abstract: An analytic solution is given to a class of linear rational expectations models with time-varying coefficients. It makes explicit the importance of terminal conditions in linear rational expectations models with implications for the solution of nonlinear models. © 1990.

Title: Leader and maximum independence for a class of discrete choice models
Abstract: For an entire class of multivariate distributions corresponding to a random vector, the maximum value of the components of the random vector is independent of the leader, which is the index of the maximal component of the random vector. This class includes the Generalised Extreme Value (GEV) models and the Generalised Logit Models (GLM) often employed in discrete choice analyses. © 1990.

Title: Bartlett's correction and the bootstrap in normal linear regression models
Abstract: This paper shows that a bootstrap Bartlett adjustment to the likelihood ratio statistic may be used to estimate p values, with errors of order n- 3 2, for tests of linear restrictions in the normal linear regression model. The results help to explain the encouraging performance of the bootstrap in some simulation evidence reported recently by Rocke (1989) in the case of the seemingly unrelated regressions model. Bartlett-type adjustments to the Wald and Lagrange multiplier tests are also investigated. © 1990.

Title: A Monte Carlo comparison of system Tobit estimators
Authors: Lennart R. Flood, Ali C. Tasiran
Abstract: Maximum Likelihood (ML) and two-stage estimation methods will be compared for the Amemiya (1974) and the Nelson and Olson (1978) specifications of the Tobit-system. The two-stage method proposed for the Amemiya specification has poor properties, however, for the Nelson and Olsen specification it performs better than the ML-estimator. © 1990.

Title: Quality, measurement errors, and profit function estimation
Abstract: A producer demand/profit function estimator is developed which uses the structure of clustered samples to estimate the importance of variations in factor quality and errors in measurement of the wage, and to correct for biases caused by these factors. © 1990.

Title: Ordinal probit model with random bounds
Abstract: We derive a general ordinal probit model by specifying the break points or bounds as random functions of explanatory variables. The proposed technique makes it possible to reduce classification errors caused by imperfections in the data collection process. The standard model with constant break points or bounds is expressed as a special case of the proposed model. © 1990.

Title: On debt neutrality in life-cycle models
Abstract: A parallelism is established between pure life-cycle models and those in which altruism is one-sided in the discussion of the public debt neutrality. It is argued that when indiduals behave as pure life cyclers, the coercive transfers necessary to offset the effects of the debt have the same nature, and take place under the same conditions, as the voluntary intrafamily bequests and gifts which constitute the usual basis for the 'Ricardian equivalence theorem'. © 1990.

Title: On the regulation of procurement bids
Abstract: It is shown that a rational buyer should not put any restriction on the non-price components fo procurement bids, when both her utility and the seller's profit functions are linear in price, and her preferences are common knowledge. © 1990.

Title: Principals and agents
Abstract: The allocation of information determines the bargaining position of buyers and sellers. Low variability in buyer type or producer cost implies a smaller distortion from asymmetric information with informed buyers; high variability implies a smaller distortion with informed sellers. © 1990.

Title: A refinement and extension of the no-envy concept
Abstract: We propose a new criterion of equity in the spirit of Foley's (1967) no-envy concept. We prove the existence of efficient allocations satisfying this criterion for a class of economies containing many for which envy-free and efficient allocations do not exist; when a large set of the latter exists, our criterion selects a small subset of it. © 1990.

Title: The inverse problem of asset price under non-expected utility
Abstract: In a Lucas (1978) model, under non-expected utility, this paper solves the inverse problem: Given an asset price, a unique preference ordering that produces the asset price is identified in the equilibrium. © 1990.

Title: The welfare implications of collusive duopoly
Abstract: If colluding duopolists can only reallocate profits by reallocating outputs, then under reasonable conditions the market would be allocatively more efficient if it were monopolized. © 1990.

Title: Equilibrium in abstract economies with a non-compact infinite dimensional strategy space, an infinite number of agents and without ordered preferences
Abstract: The purpose of this note is to prove the existence of an equilibrium for abstract economies with a non-compact infinite-dimensional strategy space, a countably infinite number of agents and without ordered preferences. We do so by generalizing the result of Yannelis and Prabhakar to a non-compact strategy space. © 1990.

Title: Signalized intersection queuing theory and central business district auto congestion
Abstract: Central city auto congestion has been modelled by urban economists as flow congestion and by traffic engineers as signalized intersection congestion. This note demonstrates that both classes of models have similar economic properties, and argues that neither provides a satisfactory treatment of downtown auto congestion. © 1990.

Title: On the optimality of equal class sizes
Abstract: Coupling the Glass and Smith (1979) meta-analysis of class size studies with a well-known result on stochastic dominance produces a theorem which suggests that, holding the average number of students per class constant, student achievement increases as the variation in class size decreases. Thus, when class size is the only variable considered which has an impact upon student achievement, equalization of class size is the optimal allocation of students to classrooms and, in addition, entails equity in the application of teacher resources. © 1990.

Title: Externalities in migration
Abstract: The paper compares the labor mobility of high order to low order waves migrants. It presents a model which concludes that low order waves provide positive externalities to higher order waves. The model is applied to two waves of political migrants to Israel. © 1990.

Title: Race and employment in the federal sector
Authors: John S. Heywood, Madhu S. Mohanty
Abstract: The use of probit analysis with partial observability demonstrates the presence of a queue for federal jobs and confirms that race plays a role in determining who works for the federal government. Specifically, non-whites are disproportionately represented among federal workers not because they are disproportionately in the queue, but because they are disproportionately chosen from the queue. Thus, the federal government acts as a 'model' employer by being more likely to hire minorities instead of having a pool of potential employees which differs in racial composition from that available to the private sector. © 1990.

Title: An information based model of industrial exit
Abstract: This paper develops an information based approach to firm closures. It is argued that non-bankrupt exit firms will be older than firms forced out by creditors. Support for this and other hypotheses comes from U.K. survey data. © 1990.

Title: On the variance of stock price distributions
Abstract: A stochastic approach is used to describe the temporal behaviour of stock prices. It is shown that standard techniques are unable to give the correct variance of the stock price distribution if the trend of variation is price dependent. © 1990.

Title: Testing for covariance stationarity in stock market data
Abstract: This paper proposes several non-parametric tests for covariance stationarity and applies them to common stock return data from 1834-1987. Recursive variance plots, post-sample prediction tests, Cumulative Sum (henceforth, CUSUM) tests and modified scaled range tests all show strong non-stationarity in stock returns, primarily due to the large increase in volatility during the Great Depression. These tests should be useful as diagnostics for data where the assumptions underlying the desired statistical procedure require stationarity. © 1990.

Title: Asset price volatility and information structures
Abstract: In this paper the hypothesis that asymmetric information in financial markets can increase asset price volatility is examined. Within the framework of the Grossman and Stiglitz (1980) model, a sufficient condition for such a hypothesis to hold is derived. The intuition is that, while uninformed agents react in a 'damped' way to signals (which reduces volatility), they react to noise as well. This latter effect can become dominant. © 1990.

Title: Strategic aspects of exchange rate policy in a developing country
Abstract: In an economy facing inflation and external deficit the non-cooperative behavior of the players introduces an inflationary bias which is eliminated if the government acts as a Stackelberg leader. The terms of trade is altered only with excess supply in the non-traded goods sector through fiscal contraction. © 1990.

Title: Equivalence properties of the Hausman statistic based on a generalized inverse
Abstract: The Hausman statistic based on a generalized inverse is numerically equivalent to statistics that are based on a subset of the parameters and do not require the use of a generalized inverse. In a general non-linear setting there exists at least one such statistic. In the case of the linear model a number of such statistics are obtained by arbitrarily selecting parameter subsets. © 1990.

Title: The computation of test statistics for multivariate regression models in event studies
Abstract: Event studies are often estimated with Zellner's seemingly unrelated regressions (SUR) estimator and hypothesis tests are applied to cross equation combinations of the coefficients corresponding to event dummy variables.
