A number of recent event studies fail to point out a useful computational simplification for obtaining the necessary covariance matrix and test statistics. © 1990.

Title: An improved rate for non-negative definite consistent covariance matrix estimation with heterogeneous dependent data
Abstract: This paper improves on previous rates at which lag lengths are allowed to grow for consistent covariance matrix estimation with heterogeneous dependent data. Using a WLLN, we give a consistency result for growth rates of o(n 1 3); the previous rate was o(n 1 4). This new rate equals that of Berk's autoregressive spectral density estimator (1974) for well behaved stationary contexts, and thus may be best possible outside of very special cases. © 1990.

Title: Preference functionals with prize-dependent distortion of probabilities
Abstract: It is shown that a class of models of decision making under risk, generalizing the theory of rank-dependent probabilities (henceforth EURPD), has a certain kind of completeness property with respect to a set of simple lotteries and contains preference functionals explaining some well-known paradoxes like the common ratio effect and the Allais paradox by a kind of behavior which cannot be modelled in EURPD theory. © 1990.

Title: The relative profitability of Nash bargaining on the labour demand curve or the contract curve
Abstract: Given the Nash bargaining solution with parametric bargaining strengths and threat points, it is shown that profits are often higher if the bargaining agenda between a union and a single firm, or two unions and Cournot duopolists, excludes employment. © 1990.

Title: Bargaining without convexity
Authors: T.C.A. Anant, Badal Mukherji, Kaushik Basu
Abstract: It is shown that Kalai and Smorodinsky's result - that their solution is the only one satisfying certain reasonable axioms - is true even if we generalize the domain of bargaining games to allow for non-convex utility feasibility sets. The paper defines a property called 'Nash equilibrium (henceforth NE) regularity' and shows that the result is true as long as the feasibility sets happen to be NE-regular. © 1990.

Title: Transitory consumption, durability and different approaches to test the life cycle model
Abstract: Transitory consumption and durability of consumption goods cannot be separately identified using Euler equations tests of the life cycle model. This problem can be solved by adopting a permanent income framework to test the theory. © 1990.

Title: Marshallian stability and long-run equilibrium in the theory of international trade with factor market distortions and variable returns to scale
Abstract: We show that perverse comparative statistics paradoxes associated with factor market distortions and variable returns to scale vanish if the equilibrium is Marshallian stable, and that the equilibrium is Marshallian stable iff it is a stable long-run equilibrium. © 1990.

Title: The influence of income on international capital movements
Abstract: Changes in income, via their influence on asset demands, affect portfolio allocation and, potentially, international capital movements. This hypothesis derives empirical support, albeit limited and correspondingly tenuous, from the identification of a consistently significant influence of income on non-official Australian portfolio investment abroad. © 1990.

Title: Tariff-induced capital inflow and welfare under variable returns to scale
Abstract: This paper extends recent studies on tariff-immiserization in the presence of internationally mobile sector-specific capital to include the possibility of non-constant returns to scale. It is shown that Brecher and Diaz-Alejandro's (1977) proposition does not necessarily hold; that is, under certain conditions tariff-induced capital inflow improves the host-country's welfare even if the foreign capital receives the full (untaxed) value of its marginal product. © 1990.

Title: Discouraged applicants for consumer credit
Authors: Clifford B. Hawley, Edwin T. Fujii
Abstract: Discouragement among potential applicants for consumer credit, controlling for income, net worth, past debt payment practices, and stability of lifestyle, is significantly greater among non-white households, households with female heads, and single females. © 1990.

Title: Unifying Chow's demand for money via the multiple Cox test
Authors: Marlene A. Smith, David J. Smyth
Abstract: The multiple Cox test developed by Sawyer (1984) is used to discriminate between four non-nested models of money demand. The results show that the short-run, real partial adjustment transactions model dominates a nominal adjustment mechanism and two long-run assets models. © 1990.

Title: A specification test for models estimated by the Cragg estimator
Abstract: This paper uses the Cragg (1983) estimator to develop a new specification test. The test statistic is asymptotically distributed as an F and can be calculated from a particular linear artificial regression. © 1990.

Title: A diagnostic check for model specification
Authors: Salih N. Neftci, Paul D. McNelis, Michael J. Harrison
Abstract: In this paper we present a diagnostic procedure that can be used for model specification in time series, using stochastic simulations and the notion of sufficient statistics for stochastic processes. The procedure rests on the idea that, given knowledge of the sufficient statistics and the form of the probability distribution, one should in principle be able to obtain simulated samples that replicate all systematic properties of economic time series. One can then assess to what extent observed time series behave as a typical realization relative to these simulated time series. With this procedure we call into question the acceptability of the random walk model for the behavior of the yen-dollar exchange rate. © 1990.

Title: A simple approach to the identifiability of the proportional hazards model
Abstract: This paper provides a simple proof of identification in the proportional hazards model. Our approach emphasizes the role which observables play in influencing the self-selection of unobservables. We show that the proportional hazards assumption provides overidentifying restrictions that can be evaluated to determine the appropriateness of the specification. © 1990.

Title: Small sample properties of the multiple rank F-test with lagged dependent variables
Authors: James M. Holmes, Patricia A. Hutton
Abstract: The parametric and multiple rank F-tests are compared using Monte Carlo methods in a leading linear lagged dependent variable model for different error distributions, sample sizes and strengths of relationship. © 1990.

Title: Inflation and relative price variability
Authors: Emmanuel I. Kaparakis, George M. Katsimbris, Stephen M. Miller
Abstract: We examine the link between inflation and relative price variability for internationally traded primary commodities. Larger and unexpected movements in commodity prices induce greater relative price variability. Thus, our results generally mirror similar findings for the prices of finished products. © 1990.

Title: Aggregate output, capital, and labor in the post-war U.S. economy
Abstract: New estimates of an aggregate long-term production function for the post-war U.S. economy are reported. The results indicate that this long-term aggregate production function exhibits a slight but statistically significant increasing returns to scale. Since virtually all econometric growth studies assume constant returns to scale, my finding raises serious doubts about the validity of this common practice. I also find that since the war real output has become more sensitive to changes in capital and less sensitive to changes in labor. In particular, I show that the long-run capital and labor elasticities of real output are both in the range of 0.44-0.55. Similar estimates for the capital and labor elasticities of output from earlier studies covering pre-war and the inter-war periods are 0.25 and 0.75, respectively. © 1990.

Title: Equilibrium bid functions for auctions with an uncertain number of bidders
Authors: Ronald M. Harstad, John H. Kagel, Dan Levin
Abstract: The number of rivals may be unknown when a bidding strategy is formulated in an auction. In a symmetric model with risk-neutral bidders holding independent information, we obtain explicit equilibrium bidding functions for first-price and second-price auctions with uncertainty about the number of rivals. Five auctions are revenue-equivalent: first-price and second-price auctions, each with the number of bidders known or uncertain, and English auctions. © 1990.

Title: Egalitarian solutions and uncertain disagreement points
Abstract: We consider bargaining problems with uncertain disagreement points. We search for solutions providing agents the incentive to reach agreements before the uncertainty is resolved. We identify the weighted Egalitarian solutions as being the only ones in the family of 'directional solutions' characterized in an earlier paper [Chun and Thomson (1987)] to satisfy three alternative lists of complementary conditions. We also show that on the class of coalitional form games, the Kalai-Samet (1985) extension of the Egalitarian solutions does not provide this incentive for early agreement. © 1990.

Title: A further test of a simple economic explanation for the existence and nature of political ticket splitting
Abstract: Extending earlier work, this paper examines whether a noted ticket splitting pattern is amplified by increasing legislative subdivision. While the results are not supportive of a recently advanced theory for ticket splitting, they also do not allow one to conclusively reject the theory. © 1990.

Title: On the meta-strategic inconsistency of a Paretian liberal
Abstract: It is shown that if we insist on the complete mutual prediction on the part of both players in a symmetric sense, then the meta-rational exercising of rights will fail to resolve the paradox of a Paretian liberal. © 1990.

Title: On the economics of nonmarket transfers
Abstract: We examine altruistically motivated consumption transfers in an effort to account for nonmarket transfers. We find that altruistic linkages lead to autonomous, negotiation-free transfers, and that such transfers positively respond to stronger altruism. We also find that given fairly natural assumptions concerning the altruism parameters, mutual altruism does not necessarily result in group (social) harmony, even though its rise narrows the conflict range. In spite of enhanced transfers prompted by such a rise, both parties may end up worse off. These results help explain why in some social environments a shift toward market-oriented transfers and exchanges may be quicker than in others, as the disadvantages (decline in utility) associated with intragroup altruistic linkages outweigh the advantages. © 1990.

Title: Vertical product differentiation can imply the Friedman-Savage utility function
Abstract: A model of vertical product differentiation is shown to provide a theoretical foundation for the Friedman-Savage utility function. © 1990.

Title: Durable good monopoly with one-hoss-shay depreciation
Abstract: This paper analyzes the effects of one-hoss-shay depreciation on the equilibrium stock path in a monopoly market for a durable good. It is shown that the stock path oscillates, converging to a stationary level lower than the competitive level. © 1990.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
The union-nonunion wage differential and monitoring costs
Abstract: This paper presents an efficiency wage explanation of the countercyclical behavior of the union-nonunion wage differential and identifies conditions under which unions are more likely to gain such a differential. © 1990.

Title: Union effects on wage dispersion in Canadian industry
Abstract: This paper analyzes the effects that unions have on the dispersion of wages in Canada. The empirical results indicate that unions have a significant effect in reducing wage dispersion. The standard deviation in hourly wages is smaller for unionized workers than it is for non-unionized workers. This result holds not only for the more general case but also for narrowly defined demographic, industrial and occupational categories. Finally, regression estimates indicate that the coefficients on the wage determining variables are smaller in the unionized sector. © 1990.

Title: Plant size and the decline of unionism
Authors: William E. Even, David A. Macpherson
Abstract: Declining plant size is shown to explain a significant portion of the recent decline in unionism, particularly in manufacturing. The paper also shows how to use the probit model to decompose the change in unionism into explained and unexplained components. © 1990.

Title: Wage rounds
Abstract: A new explanation for the high correlation between wage rates negotiated by firms belonging to the same industry is offered. Unions observe the price of the industry's output with error but they also use data from previously negotiated wage settlements in their negotiations. We show that negotiated wage rates tend to increase as the wage round proceeds. © 1990.

Title: Okun's ladder reexamined
Abstract: The empirical characterization of the American labor market made by Okun (1973) is reexamined. Industries which experience disproportionate employment growth during expansions pay high wages and employ disproportionate numbers of prime-age, white and male workers. These proportions do not vary over the business cycle. © 1990.

Title: Literacy skills and the wages of young black and white males in the U.S.
Abstract: This paper provides empirical evidence on the link between skills and wages using the 1985 Young Adult Literacy Survey. It is found that basic literacy skills have a substantial effect on wages for both Blacks on Whites in the sample. © 1990.

Title: The effects of benefits and duration dependence on re-employment probabilities
Abstract: Forgone earnings have a greater effect on re-employment probabilities than unemployment and other benefits. Education and age are important determinants of unemployment duration. A negative duration dependence effect is found. Correcting for unmeasured heterogeneity does not improve the model. © 1990.

Title: The equilibrium effort-wage elasticity in efficiency-wage models
Abstract: It has been objected that the equilibrium effort-wage elasticity of unity in the standard efficiency-wage model is quite high and that many of the results in the efficiency-wage theory depend critically on the existence of some region of increasing returns of work effort to wages. These two objections do not appear in the presence of fixed employment costs, which e.g. implies that the equilibrium effort-wage elasticity is less than unity. Finally, some comparative-static results are derived. © 1990.

Title: Abatement vs. cleanup
Abstract: Endogenous investment in cleanup can more than offset the potential damage of an increase in gross pollution levels. Consequently, a reduction in effluents may lead to greater net damage. This result, proved for both increasing and decreasing returns to cleanup, suggests conditions under which public policy might focus more usefully on cleanup rather than abatement. © 1990.

Title: Learning-by-doing and the emergence of monopoly
Abstract: The implications of learning-by-doing on the structure of an industry are studied through an example where firms are assumed to be non-identical. It is shown that, under certain circumstances, the industry may experience growing concentration, leading eventually to monopoly. A comparison between the effects of learning-by-doing in a socially managed industry and in a Cournot duopoly is made. © 1990.

Title: Hypothesis testing with the sharpe and Treynor portfolio
Abstract: Using the Scholes and Williams (1977) model, consistent estimates of the variances and covariances of security returns under conditions of non-synchronous trading are derived. The effects of using such corrected estimates on the measurement of portfolio performance are illustrated by assessing the performance of a value- and equally-weighted portfolio of all the stocks issued under the Quebec Stock Savings Plan (QSSP). © 1990.

Title: Purchasing power parity
Abstract: This paper examines the purchasing power parity (henceforth PPP) using historical data and the cointegration approach. The results indicate that the exchange rate is cointegrated with the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) ratio but not with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) ratio. The cointegrating vector is close to (0, -1). For the CPI-based real exchange rates, however, we cannot reject the random walk hypothesis. The findings caution us on the use of general price indexes that give a large weight to nontraded goods and are therefore subject to long-run deviations from PPP. © 1990.

Title: How should ignorance of response to incentives affect tax rates?
Abstract: Our knowledge of labour supply response is limited. How should this affect tax rates? We provide an example in which greater uncertainty about the responsiveness of labour supply to the wage would have no effect on taxes. © 1990.

Title: Financing decisions and the ‘crowding out’ effect
Abstract: This study empirically assesses the relevance of the 'crowding out' effect in the case of a developing country, the Philippines. The finding of a 'crowding out' effect from the issue of government debt is not due to a lack of rationality. © 1990.

Title: Measurement methods for technological change embodied in inputs
Abstract: This paper shows how unmeasured quality change embodied in purchased materials input may be estimated as part of a cost function model. The methods presented simultaneously incorporate quality-adjusted price and quantity of the materials input into the model. © 1990.

Title: The unprofitability of mixed-strategy equilibria in two-person games
Abstract: In this paper, it is demonstrated that the payoffs of mixed-strategy equilibria are equal to the maximin values for all (2X2) matrix games if maximim implies completely mixed strategies. This characterizes a subclass of unprofitable games. Maximin, instead of Nash equilibrium, has been suggested as an appropriate solution concept for these games. © 1990.

Title: Induced global risk preference
Abstract: Risk preference may be induced by scale economies unrelated to taste structure. For an important set of functions exhibiting scale economies, we give (a) the necessary condition for global risk preference induction, and (b) sufficient conditions that preserve risk aversion. © 1990.

Title: A model of electroral competition with interest groups
Authors: Peter J. Coughlin, Dennis C. Mueller, Peter Murrell
Abstract: This letter specifies and analyzes a model of electoral competition with interest groups. The assumptions used in the model are drawn from the existing literature. We (i) show that certain assumptions that have been used in empirical analyses of voting provide a sufficient condition for the existence of an electoral equilibrium, and (ii) characterize the equilibrium strategies. Embodied in the characterization is a set of parameters that can be said to measure the electoral strengths of the interest groups. We also state the appropriate definition of the Pareto relation for our model and note that each of the equilibrium strategies is Pareto optimal. © 1990.

Title: Efficient union labour contracts under seniority employment rules
Abstract: A firm and worker sign a price-contigent wage-employment contract under LIFO ly-off rules. A worker may prefer a contract which lays him off at low prices to one under which he is guaranteed employment at all prices. © 1990.

Title: Lay-offs by seniority and equilibrium employment
Abstract: In a bargaining model of wages a median voter will in the neighbourhood of the firm's equilibrium (or below it) press for the maximum wage. Given LIFO and finite lives, the resulting bargain will nevernormally imperil his employment. Above equilibrium, he will normally select the wage which keeps him the median voter. © 1990.

Title: Age-related minimum wages and hysteresis in unemployment
Abstract: R&D activity has similar effects on the market value of small and large-scale firms. Using this criterion, size alone does not emerge as a prime determinant of R&D effectiveness. © 1990.

Title: Are efficient contracts on the labour demand curve?
Abstract: Consider a duopoly in which each firm announces its production plan. If both approve, the plans get implemented. Otherwise the plans are rejected and the firms play the Cournot game. In this model each firm's perfect equilibrium output may be much smaller than in the usual Cournot model. © 1990.

Title: Firm size and R&D effectiveness
Abstract: This paper reports the results of a meta-analysis of the estimates of the price elasticity of demand for recreation sites using the travel cost method. By using econometric methods to summarize empirical literature, meta-analysis assists in identifying research conclusions despite the non-experimental nature of most empirical research in economics. In this application, the results suggest that modeling decisions based on theory, as well as those relying on fitting criteria, were important influences to the estimated price elasticities across studies. © 1990.

Title: Duopoly equilibria when firms can change their decision once
Abstract: A log-normal interpretation of international capital asset pricing models is used to generate a risk premium that separates the forward rate form the expected future spot rate. Application to daily overlapping data suggests this premium changes sign with major events in the Australian foreign exchange market. © 1990.

Title: What have we learned since hotelling's letter?
Abstract: Stigmatization of long-term unemployed by employers generally causes no hysteresis in unemployment if employers are rational and when there is no direct effect of unemployment on productivity. However, if wages are age-related hysteresis may well occur. © 1990.

Title: The discretely time-varying risk premium on the AUD
Authors: Michael J. Buchanan, Bruce S. Felmingham
Abstract: This note introduces a dynamic element into recent models of wage determination in unionized firms. This element is the probability of promotion to a higher rank. A non-zero probability of promotion generates interesting results. In particular one can show that there exists a substantial range of employment growth, where the distinction between labour demand and contract curve is meaningful even if the median union voter has a survival probability equal to one. © 1990.

Title: A simple production model in trade and its applications
Abstract: In a simple production model, some counter-intuitive results are derived. (a) Increase in the relative price of good might reduce its production and reduce the absolute return to the specific factor exclusively used in this sector. (b) Uniform technical progress in two sectors might lead to a contraction in one of those sectors. Later other applications of such a structure are discussed. © 1990.

Title: Friedman's velocity hypothesis
Abstract: The purpose of this note is to report tests of Friedman's velocity hypothesis that money growth volatility affects velocity in the case of France. The evidence provides some additional support for this hypothesis. However, the evidence is less clear-out than the one found in studies of other industrial countries. © 1990.

Title: Relative-price variability in the United States
Abstract: Following the Clements-Nguyen methodology, relative-price variability in the United States is decomposed into the components due to real factors, inflation, and their interaction. Overall, inflation accounts for about half of relative-price variability, but its share is the largest during 1973-1980 and the smallest during 1981-1986. Cross-commodity distribution of relative-price variability shows rather dramatic changes. © 1990.

Title: An exact test for linear restrictions in seemingly unrelated regressions with the same regressors
Abstract: In this paper, we derive an exact test for linear restrictions on regression coefficients in seemingly unrelated regressions with the same regressors in each equation. The test statistic is distributed as the T2 distribution, and thus critical values can be obtained from the F distribution. Since the test for symmetry in demand systems is a special case of the test for linear restrictions, our test gives an exact test for symmetry. © 1990.

Title: The consequences of misspecification in time series processes
Abstract: This paper examines the effects of misspecifying a stochastic process in terms of the distance between the true process and the 'closest' in the incorrectly specified class, or the one estimated within the incorrect class. For stationary stochastic processes a natural distance measure is provided by the expected mean square error which determines the distance in the appropriate Hilbert space. The distances between MA(1), AR(1) and uncorrelated processes and classes of such processes are easily computed and provided here. The comparisons of different cases of misspecification within these classes lead to conclusions regarding relative severity of the consequences of misspecification in statistical models of stochastic processes and in dynamic models. © 1990.

Title: Missing measurements in discrete response models
Abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of whether or not incomplete observations contain any information about the parameters that could be used in their estimates for general discrete response models. The results differ from the cases of linear models [e.g. Kmenta and Balestra (1986)] and binary response models [e.g. Lien and Rearden (1988)]. © 1990.

Title: Lindley-like mean correction in the improved estimation of regression models with non-scalar covariance matrix
Abstract: In the linear regression model with disturbances covariance matrix depending upon a few unknown parameters, the risks of the feasible generalized least squares and improved estimators with and without Lindley-like mean correction are derived and dominance conditions of one estimator over the other are obtained when sample size is large. For a specific choice of the loss function it has been observed that the improved estimator without Lindley-like mean correction dominates the FGLS estimator whenever the number of explanatory variables is greater than three, whereas the estimator with Lindley-like mean correction dominates the FGLS estimator whenever the number of explanatory variables is greater than six. © 1990.

Title: Manufacturing output and labor productivity
Abstract: Formulating the so-called Verdoorn's law in terms of cointegration and Granger-causality between manufacturing output and labor productivity, quaterly U.S. data for 1950-1988 are used to test the pattern implied by the law. Evidence is lacking to support the predicted pattern. © 1990.

Title: The incidence and duration of unemployment
Abstract: Census data from 1910 reveal the average non-farm male worker faced higher probabilities of entering and leaving unemployment than in the 1970s. Long-term occupational shifts explain a significant fraction of the decline in the entry hazard. © 1990.

Title: Decision weights and the normal form axiom
Abstract: In 'decision weight' theories of behavior under uncertainty, individuals choose between uncertain prospects to maximize a weighted average of utilities, where utility is defined over outcomes and decision weights depend upon the probability distribution of outcomes as well as, perhaps, other characteristics of the uncertain environment. The 'Normal Form Axiom' (NFA) requires that an individual be indifferent between two prospects which assign identical total probabilities to respective outcomes. Under NFA, decision weight theories reduce to Expected Utility theory if decision weights depend only upon the probability distribution of outcomes and not, in particular, on the nature of the uncertain outcomes. © 1990.

Title: Staggered price setting with endogenous frequency of adjustment
Abstract: A model of staggered price setting in which the frequency of price changes is endogenous is presented. © 1990.

Title: Consistent linkages across markets
Abstract: Consistent conjectures are derived within and across markets in a two-market duopoly. When marginal costs are not constant, intermarket linkages arise which can have an adverse impact on competition. This is the first formal derivation of such linkages in a static model with full information. © 1990.

Title: Using grouped data for constructing inequality indices
Abstract: This paper discusses the relative merits of parametric versus non-parametric methods in constructing indices of income inequality utilizing grouped data. The information content is higher from the parametric specifications with a cost of possibly misspecifying the functional form. We conclude that the indices should be constructed using the parametric method and then the results checked using a non-parametric method. © 1990.

Title: Multidimensional inequality comparisons
Abstract: This paper is addressed to comparing inequality in distributions of two or more variables. Based on the Lorenz curve criterion, a theorem is proved which says that inequality in total income is no greater than in the most unequal income component. In addition, some results are given in the occurence of inequality mitigation for various classes of inequality measures. © 1990.

Title: The case of risk premia for risky jobs revisited
Abstract: The empirical evidence concerning the existence of risk premia for risky jobs is contradictory. Some results support the existence of these premia, while others do not. This note provides a theoretical justification for these contradictory results in a fairly general model where firms and workers can effect the probability of a workplace accident. © 1990.

Title: On the determination of nominal wage dispersion
Abstract: This paper studies sectoral wage dispersion. It is shown that, in Spain, expected inflation reduces wage variability. In a more complete specification, however, neither actual nor expected inflation affects variability, which is significantly increased by fluctuations in unemployment and productivity. © 1990.

Title: Estimating the impact of government R&D
Abstract: If we do not pay for an input it is important? It is suggested that the R&D literature, by ignoring the fact that government R&D is given away, has confused zero value of marginal product with zero marginal physical product. © 1990.

Title: The long-run effects of alternative monetary policies under two-tier exchange rates
Abstract: This paper first develops a portfolio balance model of a small open economy under two-tier exchange rates, and uses it to examine the long-run impact of alternative money creation rules. It is found that a monetary expansion may be either powerful or powerless to affect the economy, crucially depending upon whether the money stock is increased through 'inside' or 'outside' money creation. © 1990.

Title: The impact of mortgage activity on recent demand deposit growth
Abstract: This study quantifies the substantial effects of mortgage activity on recent demand deposit growth, and finds that estimates and forecasts of recent demand deposit growth are considerably more accurate using data adjusted for mortgage activity. © 1990.

Title: A resolution of the equity premium puzzle
Abstract: The introduction of a simple non-time additive utility function can explain the equity premium puzzle noted by Mehra and Prescott with a reasonable value for the relative risk aversion coefficient. © 1990.

Title: Relative trading volume, risk measures and other firm characteristics during the market crash
Authors: Uri Ben-Zion, Eyal Gutman, Emanuel Egbe, Steven Brahams
Abstract: The crash of 1987 led to significant increases in the trading volume in the N.Y.S.E. The paper uses individual data of 473 S&P 500 firms to analyze the relation between said increases in trading volume and firm and security characteristics. © 1990.

Title: Input substitution and technical change in U.S. high tech industries
Abstract: The paper shows that in U.S. high-tech industry sector, capital and non-production worker are complementary to each other. Capital and production worker, however, are substitutes. Also, technical change in the sector concerned is material using and capital and labor saving. The major saving is in production worker. © 1990.

Title: How much better is disaggregate data?
Authors: James K. Binkley, Carl H. Nelson
Abstract: The estimation efficiency of aggregate and disaggregate data is compared for the two-group case. Conditions for a maximum and minimum difference between the two approaches are obtained. © 1990.

Title: Money growth and inflation dynamics
Abstract: This paper shows that the inflation rate overreacts to changes in the money growth rate if (i) the rate and the volatility of money growth are related, and (ii) the unpredictability of inflation reduces the demand for money. © 1990.

Title: Exports and Japanese economic development
Authors: Richard Grabowski, Subhash C. Sharma, Dharmendra Dhakal
Abstract: The Granger causality test used in this paper indicates that Japanese growth in the prewar period was caused by the growth of the labor force and improvements in agricultural productivity. In the postwar period, growth in exports, labor force, and agricultural productivity caused output growth. © 1990.

Title: Multi-choice problems and the essential order among decision rules
Abstract: When a team's skill vector is different for different parts of a multi-choice problem one can draw inference on the optimal decision rule by using information about the essential order which prevails among decision rules. © 1990.

Title: On the possibility of price wars when firms use a ‘Tit-for-tat’ strategy
Authors: Paul W. Dobson, C. Donald Sinclair
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to illustrate how price wars can periodically occur in an industry even when all the firms behave cooperatively, and each firm has no intention of 'cheating' by attempting to undercut the other firms. © 1990.

Title: Elasticity of substitution in a regulated firm
Abstract: We derive the analogue of the Morishima elasticity of substitution for a regulated firm and show that it is simpler, yet more informative, than the corresponding analogue of the Allen/Uzawa elasticity derived by V.K. Smith. © 1990.

Title: A limit theorem on the core
Abstract: The result that an allocation which remains in the core of a replicated economy for any number of replications is the allocation of a competitive equilibrium is proved without assuming convexity of preferences, transivity of preferences, strict monotonocity of preferences, or positive individual endowments. However, the economy is assumed to be irreducible. © 1990.

Title: Call for papers for European journal of political economy
Erratum
Application of the ‘Oaxaca decomposition’ to probit estimates
Abstract: Using several standard approaches this paper presents estimates of the effect of unions on benefit provision consistent with those in the literature. A new estimation approach is then presented which embodies several advantages and amounts to an Oaxaca decomposition performed on two probit equations. The resulting estimates depart sharply from those in the literature suggesting unions may have far less direct influence on benefits than originally thought. © 1990.

Title: An empirical analysis of self-employment in the Netherlands
Authors: Gerrit De Wit, Frans A.A.M. Van Winden
Abstract: Using an endogenous switching model, applied to a unique data set, it is found that the choice between self-employment and paid-employment depends - among others - on the score of an IQ test applied at the age of 12, the employment status of the father, and the income differential. © 1990.

Title: Non-nested tests of efficient bargain and labour demand models
Abstract: In this paper efficient bargain and labour demand models derived from a variety of product market structures are compared using non-nested test procedures. Data on wage/employment outcomes are drawn from actual contract data from the Canadian unionised sector. Results indicate that efficient bargain models are preferred to labour demand models. © 1990.

Title: Employer seniority discrimination
Abstract: This research examines the theories presented in the human capital literature by Becker (1975), Lazear (1979, 1981), and others that the relative paths of earnings and value of marginal product (henceforth, VMP) diverge over the worklife. The findings support Lazear's work incentive theory for professionals, but reject its application to non-professionals. As predicted by orthodox human capital theory, documentation is also developed that earnings for non-professionals equal their VMP over the job life-cycle. On the other hand, the analysis provides no support to Becker's specific training model. © 1990.

Title: A partial characterization of a history-dependent, subgame-perfect equilibrium
Abstract: If there is a quasi-fixed cost of production from an exhaustible resource, there may exist history-dependent, subgame-perfect equilibria other than those where duopolists produce an equal amount in each period. The model exemplifies the relevance of Chakrabarti's theorem on existence of such equilibria. © 1990.

Title: Market structure, union rent seeking, and firm profitability
Abstract: Unique survey data on firm union coverage, market share, and concentration are used to examine the hypothesis that profits deriving from market power provide a primary source for union gains. Based on evidence from 247 companies during 1972-1980, no support is found for this hypothesis. © 1990.

Title: Predicting the quantity of LDC debt rescheduling
Authors: H. Lloyd-Ellis, G.W. McKenzie, S.H. Thomas
Abstract: In this paper we estimate a Type 2 Tobit model to explain both the timing and quantity of developing country debt rescheduling using an annual data set for 27 countries from 1977-1981 and six-monthly data for 59 countries from 1977-1985. We obtain a satisfactory model for both the timing and quantity of rescheduling which will be more useful for country risk analysis than models which predict the timing alone. © 1990.

Title: An evaluation of survey exchange rate forecasts
Abstract: A non-parametric test of direction is employed to evaluate the survey forecasts provided by the Money Market Services. Empirical results suggest that the forecasts are useful for predicting the direction of exchange rate changes. The results are consistent with a weaker form of rationality than unbiasedness. © 1990.

Title: Cointegration-based tests of daily foreign exchange market efficiency
Abstract: An immediate implication of cointegration is the existence of Granger-causal orderings among cointegrated series. This implies that asset prices determined in a weakly efficient market cannot be cointegrated. This proposition is tested using daily data for 18 foreign currencies. Tests are conducted for both pairwise combinations of currencies and higher-order systems. No significant evidence of cointegration among exchange rates is found. © 1990.

Title: Forward rate biases and inconsistencies with tax-modified fisher conditions
Abstract: The perfect mobility and perfect substitutability models of international finance derive the uncovered interest arbitrage (international Fisher) condition under the assumption of no taxes. This model also implies that the forward rate is an unbiased predictor of the future spot rate. Tax wedges have two effects. One is that the forward rate is not the market forecast of future spot rates if tax codes treat capital gains differently from interest income. The second is that differences in tax codes across nations will lead to an inconsistency in regards the international Fisher condition. © 1990.

Title: A gradual switching regression model with a flexible transition path
Authors: Kazuhiro Ohtani, Sumio Kakimoto, Kenzo Abe
Abstract: In this paper, we set up a switching regression model with a transition path specified by a polynomial of time. To select the order of a polynomial, the minimization principle of Akaike's information criterion (AIC) and Schwarz's criterion (SC) is used. The model is applied to an import demand equation for Japan. It is shown that using a flexible transition path can yield a more plausible result than using a transition path specified by a linear function of time. © 1990.

Title: Weighted least squares estimation of the linear probability model, revisited
Abstract: Efficient GLS estimation of the linear probability model is hindered in practice by the possibility that predicted probabilities may yield some negative point variance estimates. This note proposes an alternative estimator may sometimes yield efficiency gains over OLS and will in general be efficient relative to alternative estimators that have been proposed. © 1990.

Title: Small sample properties of simultaneous error components models
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to investigate the small properties of the simultaneous error components model's estimators in the static case, and to analyse the small sample and 'semi-asymptotic' properties of these estimators in the dynamic case. © 1990.

Title: Orthogonality tests with de-trended data
Authors: Anindya Banerjee, Juan Dolado, John W. Galbraith
Abstract: We extend previous results concerning the behaviour of a finite-sample approximation to the distribution of the t-statistic used in testing orthogonality of a variable to a given information set. In particular, we look at the case in which the data are de-trended, innovations in the explanatory variable are correlated with the regressand, and the explanatory variable is substantially autocorrelated. © 1990.

Title: Phantom bidding against heterogeneous bidders
Authors: Daniel A. Graham, Robert C. Marshall, Jean-Francois Richard
Abstract: If IPV bidders are distributionally heterogeneous then a revenue maximizing English auctioneer will, in general, find it optimal to use a non-constant reserve price that is a function of the observed bid sequence. An example is provided. © 1990.

Title: Inflation, terms of trade, and debt capacity
Abstract: The optimal level of debt for an economic entity is a function of, among other things, the variability of its cash flows. Since real and inflationary shocks which cause the variability may not influence various components of the cash flows by equal proportions, a project's financial risk, and hence its debt capacity, will depend upon the correlation between its cash inflows and outflows. A developing country's external debt capacity depends upon cash flows arising from its foreign trade. In this research, we analyze the impact of inflation on the foreign currency cash flows of developing countries and find that inflation affects very few countries in a symmetrical manner. Results indicate that an assumption that unexpected inflation has a neutral impact on the debt capacity of a borrower is supportable neither in theory nor in practice. © 1990.

Title: Non-market reopening, time-consistent plans and the structure of intertemporal preferences
Abstract: For the Arrow-Debreu model of pure exchange under uncertainty, those consumers are characterized who never recontract in any situation. These are also the consumers who guarantee the non-market reopening property. © 1990.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Equivalence scales
Abstract: The paper uses a cost minimization version of Becker's household production analysis and microdata from household expenditure and time-use surveys to estimate equivalence scales or relative costs for the intrafamily classes of adults and children in Australia for the period 1975-1976. The findings set reference standards for further research with economic welfare policy applications in Australia. © 1989.

Title: The effect of migration on black incomes
Abstract: Evidence from the 1940 census reveals that southern-born blacks who left the region prior to 1935 had higher incomes than non-southern born blacks. The income gap between migrants and non-migrants declined with schooling. © 1989.

Title: Small firms in U.S. manufacturing
Authors: Zoltan J. Acs, David B. Audretsch
Abstract: We find that the presence of small firms in U.S. manufacturing industries is negatively related to the existence of structural barriers, positively related to the extent to which small firms rely on a strategy of innovation, and negatively related to the efficiency differential between small and large enterprises. © 1989.

Title: Dollar currency in Latin America
Authors: Michael Melvin, Gonzalo Afcha de la Parra
Abstract: The stock of U.S. dollar currency held in Bolivia is estimated using two alternative methods. Incorporating estimated dollar currency balances in M 2 results in more reasonable movements in velocity than the unbelievable gyrations in official velocity. © 1989.

Title: Empirical evidence on the properties of exchange rate forecasts and the risk premium
Abstract: The purpose in this note is to examine the properties of the risk premium obtained from a new source of market expectations derived from survey data. © 1989.

Title: Tariff burdens and optimal tariffs under alternative transport cost and market structures
Abstract: Trade policy models ignore or exogenize the transportation sector. This note suggests that, as a result, conventional economic estimates of trade policy actions and optimal tariff calculations may be biased. © 1989.

Title: Some empirical evidence on government purchase multipliers
Abstract: A multiplier effect of state and local government purchases is found when estimating a vector autoregression of components of GNP. Military purchases, on the other hand, are only slightly expansionary in the very short term. Government purchases account for a substantial part of the variance of GNP. © 1989.

Title: The asymmetric prime
Authors: Shawn M. Forbes, Lucille S. Mayne
Abstract: This paper applies a limited-dependent variable approach, the friction model, to an empirical examination of the two-dimensional nature of asymmetry in the prime rate, one corresponding to an unchanging prime and a second to adjustments in the rate. © 1989.

Title: The sample spectrum of time series with trading day variation
Authors: Mark S. McNulty, Wallace E. Huffman
Abstract: A time series that is constructed as the monthly total of the daily levels of some activity will contain trading day variation. This letter presents the sample spectrum of a trading day variable. The presence of the identified patterns in the sample spectrum of an observed time series indicates the presence of trading day variation. © 1989.

Title: System estimation of generalized working models
Abstract: System estimation of a complete model of m generalized Working equations of the Phillips/Tukey form with unknown exponent function is often unsatisfactory due to computational instability encountered in practical studies. A semiparametric economic-theoretic procedure is proposed. Some illustrations of the new procedure are also given. © 1989.

Title: On testing for revealed preference conditions
Abstract: A procedure to test for the significance of violations of revealed preference conditions is described. The procedure is simple and hence may especially be appropriate for large data sets. An application to consumption data is presented. © 1989.

Title: Extended tabulations for Dickey-Fuller tests
Abstract: The previously available tabulations of the distributions of the Dickey-Fuller τ̂ τ and π̂ τ statistics are surprisingly limited in the number of sample sizes and critical levels covered. This paper supplies more detailed tables. © 1989.

Title: Model comparison when the endogenous variable is uncertain
Abstract: A common problem in applied econometric work occurs when a researcher is interested in explaining a certain variable but there exist two or more different empirical measures of that variable. The purpose of this note is to show that the non-nested testing procedures of Davidson and MacKinnon can be adapted to provide a test of the relative value of the information contained in the different empirical measures of the endogenous variable. A simple modification of the P test delivers a consistent estimator of the optimal linear combination of the different measures of the endogenous variable to be used in estimating the true value of the endogenous variable, and thus offers a method of testing the value of the information contained in the different measures. The asymptotic variance of this estimator is 'too large', and thus limits the range of application of the suggested test. However, there are still many situations in which the test should prove a simple and useful diagnostic. © 1989.

Title: Some results on the finite sample significance levels of instrumental variable tests for non-nested models
Abstract: Monte-Carlo estimates of the finite sample significance levels of a number of instrumental variable tests for non-nested models are provided. A simple generalization of the J-test performs better than other procedures. © 1989.

Title: A note on the Anderson-Hsiao estimator for panel data
Abstract: The asymptotic variances of the IV estimators for dynamic panel data proposed by Anderson and Hsiao (1982) are obtained for some simple models. With an autoregressive exogenous variable, the estimator that uses differenced instruments has a singularity point and very large variances over a significant range of parameter values. On the contrary, the estimator that uses instruments in levels has no singularities and much smaller variances. © 1989.

Title: Sectoral change, catching up and slowing down
Abstract: Regression analysis of GDP growth since 1950 on pooled OECD cross-sections indicates uniform technological catch-up in all sectors but lower marginal labour productivity in agriculture. The decline in opportunities to reallocate labour explains some of the post-1973 productivity slowdown. © 1989.

Title: Income taxation and endogenous growth
Abstract: This paper examines the long-run effects of income taxation by using a perfect-foresight optimizing model in which the steady-state rate of economic growth is endogenously determined due to technical progress activities of private agents. We show that a rise in the rate of income tax depresses the rate of economic growth in the long run. We also show that the assumption concerning production structure of technical knowledge is crucial to our main conclusion. © 1989.

Title: Fairness in bargaining requires a context
Abstract: Recent experiments on non-cooperative bargaining have observed that subjects behave more like 'fairmen' than the 'gamesmen' theory predicts. In a Coasian bargaining experiment, we demonstrate that this result is reversed if fairness is defined in the context of loyalty. © 1989.

Title: Bounded price variation models with rational expectations and price risk
Abstract: The bounded price variation model under rational expectations is extended to include higher moments of price in the supply equation. The resulting framework is then used to estimate a disequilibrium model of the U.S. corn market that includes price risk. © 1989.

Title: A note on asymptotical strategy-proofness
Abstract: In this paper we examine a Social Choice Function choosing plurality winners. We find that the frequency of ties and incentives to manipulate goes to zero with increasing number n of individuals at the rate of n- 1 2. © 1989.

Title: The discrete bid first auction
Abstract: In a first auction in which buyers can bid only multiples of an increment and have uniformly distributed values, the expected price is less than the continuous bid expected price. © 1989.

Title: On the stability properties of the long-run stationary equilibrium in macro-dynamic models under perfect foresight and static expectations
Abstract: This paper shows that the long-run stationary equilibrium of a wide class of macro-dynamic models is a saddle point under perfect foresight if and only if it is dynamically stable under static expectations. © 1989.

Title: Evidence on the fit of the log-linear income model versus a general statistical specification
Authors: Charles A. Diamond, Curtis J. Simon, John T. Warner
Abstract: Using the March 1985 Current Population Survey, we predict the size distribution of family income as a function of various family characteristics. Pitting the 'standard' log-linear specification against a multinomial specification, we find the multinomial model reproduces more closely the actual distribution. © 1989.

Title: Subjective versus technical risk estimates: do risk communication policies increase consistency?
Authors: V. Kerry Smith, William H. Desvousges
Abstract: This paper reports the first comparison of subjective and technical risk estimates for a real source of risk, exposure to radon. The analysis also considers the effects of the information framing for this comparison of risk estimates. The results suggest that the framing of the risk explanations does affect how individuals adjusted their subjective risk perceptions in response to differences in the amount and duration of their radon exposures. Thus, our findings support the need to describe the role of cognitive factors involved in processing risk information within economic models of the formation of risk perceptions. © 1989.

Title: Smoke detector effectiveness and the value of saving a life
Abstract: Engineering estimates of home smoke detector effectiveness are around 50 percent. An economic model finds an effectiveness estimate of about 9 percent. Based on this result, the value of life saving from smoke detector purchases is increased fivefold. © 1989.

Title: Technological diffusion, vertical product differentiation and quality improvement
Abstract: A diffusion model with vertical product differentiation, myopic buyers and a monopolist supplier is analysed. It is argued that the diffusion path may involve a period of rising product quality followed by a period of fixed quality and falling price. © 1989.

Title: Viability in multiproduct industries
Abstract: This paper introduces a new concept, called viability, useful for characterizing firms in multiproduct industries, and relates it to existing concepts. © 1989.

Title: Dividend policy and tax structure
Abstract: We show that a certain class of progressive tax structure induces an optimal dividend policy which is autogressive in nature. The theoritical model is consistent with empirically observed dividend policies. © 1989.

Title: Co-integration tests for long run equilibrium in the monetary exchange rate model
Abstract: The monetary model of exchange rate determination is tested as a long run equilibrium relation. Tests of co-integration among the variables in this model over a wide range of specifications are generally unfavorable to the monetary approach. © 1989.

Title: Trade deficit announcements, intervention, and the dollar
Abstract: The effect of U.S. trade deficit announcements on the dollar exchange rate from 1980-1988 is examined. The announcement is found to affect the dollar only after mid-1984. Central bank intervention does not appear to have had a consistent impact on the dollar on the day of the announcement. © 1989.

Title: The information in the term structure of eurodollar interest rates
Abstract: This paper uses Fama's regression approach to measure the relative importance of time-varying term premiums and expected future spot interest rates embedded in forward Eurodollar interest rates. The forward-spot spread always has reliable power in predicting future spot interest rates, especially during the October 1979 to September 1982 period. © 1989.

Title: Incorporating contemporaneous residual relationships for security prices
Abstract: Using a recent procedure developed by Jalilvand and Kryzanowski (1985) to capture the contemporaneous residual dependencies in a system of regression equations, this paper tests the impact of such residual based relationships in explaining security prices. Utilizing a multi-industry sample of securities over two non-overlapping periods, the empirical findings show that not only are these contemporaneous residual relationships statistically significant but their inclusion significantly improves the explanatory power of the underlying return-generating model. © 1989.

Title: A computationally simple heteroskedasticity and serial correlation robust standard error for the linear regression model
Abstract: A simple method for computing a heteroskedasticity and serial correlation robust standard error for an OLS coefficient is proposed. The computations can be carried out using any regression package that supports basic data manipulation. © 1989.

Title: Rules of thumb for comparing multinomial logit and multinomial probit coefficients
Abstract: A rule of thumb is suggested for comparing multinomial logit coefficients with multinomial probit coefficients in the special case where the normal errors are distributed N(0,1). The rule is a generalization of the '1.6' rule for comparing logit and probit coefficients. © 1989.

Title: Structural change and unit root econometrics
Abstract: The paper analyzes the systematic bias in tests for I(d) models with constant parameters against I(d-1) models with time varying parameters. It is shown that, if the true process has deterministic structural change we will accept the unit root hypothesis against a model corresponding to the true one but in which data of structural change is misspecified; moreover, if the true process is a random walk, a 'goodness of fit' criteria will lead one to accept the hypothesis of structural change against that of no change. © 1989.

Title: Solution and estimation of a bivariate interdependent adjustment cost model
Abstract: A simplified method is proposed for solving and conducting inference in the context of a bivariate adjustment cost model. The formulas presented here allow one to use standard OLS regressions to derive consistent, though not fully efficient, estimates of objective function parameters. A straightforward application of 'the delta method' then delivers consistent standard errors. © 1989.

Title: Profit-sharing in cournot oligopoly
Abstract: It has been argued that, even if there are macroeconomic benefits, individual firms will not switch from a conventional wage system to profit-sharing. We show that while true for a monopolist, it does not generally hold under Cournot oligopoly. © 1989.

Title: Advertising and consumer demand: a differential approach
Abstract: This paper uses a differential approach to derive demand equations to deal with advertising and show that the demand equations are natural extensions of the usual differential demand equations. © 1989.

Title: A globally concave, symmetric, flexible cost function
Abstract: This paper describes a cost function that is globally concave, flexible, and treats all prices symmetrically. The derivation of this 'CSFLEX' cost function includes a new technique for proving flexibility of models. © 1989.

Title: Updating estimates of union non-union wage differentials in the United States
Abstract: This study updates earlier research by calculating union wage premiums using both single-equation and simultaneous equations models. It also examines many more subgroups within the population than have earlier studies. © 1989.

Title: Market structure and inter-industry wage differences
Abstract: This note reports the structure and the determinants of inter-industry wage differences in the manufacturing sector of Taiwan. It was found that market concentrations are significantly correlated with wage differentials. From this outcome we tentatively conclude that market structure is an important factor in generating wage-income differentials. © 1989.

Title: More on the properties of a tax cum subsidy pollution control strategy
Abstract: A modification in a tax cum subsidy pollution control strategy proposed by Yohe and MacAvoy to mitigate against the effects of moral hazard on the effectiveness of self-reporting strategies is shown capable of eliminating the dead weight welfare loss of regulating the emissions of an imperfectly competitive polluter. © 1989.

Title: Guaranteed lowest prices: do they facilitate collusion?
Authors: John W. Logan, Randall W. Lutter
Abstract: The effects of a policy guaranteeing lowest price are analyzed in a two-stage game where firms first decide whether to adopt such a policy and then choose prices. Symmetric and asymmetric games are solved to examine the extent to which prices can rise to collusive levels. © 1989.

Title: Structuring an option to facilitate replication with transaction costs
Abstract: Using Leland's model of option valuation with transaction costs, it is shown that an interior solution does not exist which minimizes total transaction costs over the life of the option. However, it is possible to structure an option so as to reduce the change in the hedge ratio over time, and attack the replication or hedging costs from this direction. © 1989.

Title: The extended linear expenditure system with financial assets
Abstract: We use the technique of stochastic dynamic programming to derive a generalized form of Lluch's extended linear expenditure system which covers the case of multiple investment opportunities. The system generated retains the high degree of empirical tractability possessed by its predecessor. © 1989.

Title: Using country balance sheet data to predict debt rescheduling
Authors: H. Lloyd-Ellis, G.W. Mckenzie, S.H. Thomas
Abstract: In this study we utilise data relating to the balance sheets of developing countries (e.g. short-term debt) in a logit model of debt rescheduling. We find that such variables are theoretically and empirically superior to those conventionally used (such as debt-export ratios). The study is based upon an annual sample of 27 countries for 1977-1981 and a six-monthly data set involving 59 countries from 1977-1985. © 1989.

Title: Tariffs, employment and wage bargaining
Abstract: This paper shows that tariffs are usually expansionary in employment and output in an unionized economy independent of the use of tariffs revenues. It raises the utility of the union but has an ambiguous effect on welfare of households. © 1989.

Title: Optimal commercial policy for an open economy with domestic distortions
Authors: Winston W. Chang, Michael S. Michael
Abstract: This paper formulates the optimal commercial policies with domestic distortions when the unconstrained first-best policy options are unavailable. Explicit formulae for the values of the interventionist variables are presented. The results synthesize and clarify previous formulations, and provide some exact conclusions beyond the usual 'indefinite' second-best outcomes. © 1989.

Title: Should a factor-market distortion be widened?
Abstract: In a two-sector, two-factor model of a price-taking small, open economy suppose one sector has to pay a distortionary higher wage than the other and that only one policy instrument is available: a tax or subsidy on the use of capital in the distorted sector. It is unambiguously optimal for the country to tax capital despite the induced widening of the factor-market distortion. © 1989.

Title: North American money surprises and financial market reactions
Abstract: In the late 1970s, U.S. and Canadian weekly money supply announcements occurred almost simultaneously. The unanticipated components of these announcements are shown to be correlated, and the importance of this factor for findings in the money surprise-market response literature is explored. © 1989.

Title: Optimal inflation and the government revenue mix
Abstract: This paper examines the question of optimal inflation and taxation as a government optimal control problem. By inclusion of bond finance and portfolio decisions by private agents in a perfect foresight framework it is shown that: (i) optimal steady state inflation is independent of government revenue requirements, (ii) inflation and tax rates do not necessarily move together in optimum. © 1989.

Title: The Kalman filter model under the assumption of the first-order autoregressive process in the disturbance terms
Abstract: This paper extends the EM algorithm (Shumway and Stoffer (1982)) to the Kalman filter model with AR(1) disturbance. We disentangle parameter variation from serial correlation, and test the existence of AR(1) error terms. © 1989.

Title: Symmetric paths and evolution to equilibrium in the discounted prisoners' dilemma
Abstract: We consider an alternating best response process for strategies in two-player, discounted repeated games. Properties of this process in general games are studied and a sharp convergence result is proved for a class of strategies in the discounted prisoners' dilemma. © 1989.

Title: The expected stop-out price in a discriminating auction
Authors: Paul A. Spindt, Richard W. Stolz
Abstract: Optimal bidding strategies and expected seller revenues in price discriminating auctions have been derived in previous studies. We extend this research by characterizing the behavior of the expected stop-out price for such auctions. © 1989.

Title: Firm-specific training in an incentive-compatible contract
Abstract: If upon entering a firm, a worker becomes immobile a firm may exploit this immobility by paying a less than promised wage. In this paper, firm-specific training can enable the firm to offer an incentive compatible contract with the result that training may exceed that in a world with costlessly enforced contracts. © 1989.

Title: Effect of time preferences on indexation
Abstract: Differences in the rate of time preferences of two transactors can explain why Pareto optimal contracts do not appear to be fully indexed. © 1989.

Title: Modelling technical and allocative inefficiency in a translog production function
Abstract: This paper develops a method of estimating technical and allocative inefficiency for each firm using a translog production function. Based on expected profit maximization hypothesis, the method uses the production function and the first order conditions as the basis of parameter estimation. © 1989.

Title: Binary choice probabilities and rankings
Abstract: Two denumerable sequences of necessary conditions for binary choice probabilities to be induced by a probability distribution on rankings are presented. No finite set of simple necessary conditions is sufficient for inducement when the alternative set is finite but can be arbitrarily large. © 1989.

Title: Migration equilibrium and variational inequalities
Abstract: In this paper, an equilibrium model of human migration is presented which can handle many classes of migrants and locations, in addition to equalities and inequalities. The equilibrium conditions are stated and then formulated as a variational inequality problem. Qualitative properties and computational aspects are briefly discussed. © 1989.

Title: Korean trade union growth during the period 1962–1984
Abstract: This paper reports empirical results obtained from an econometric analysis of trade union membership data for South Korea during the period 1962 to 1984. The findings indicate that the Western-based Bain-Elsheikh model of trade union growth applies to the experience of South Korea. © 1989.

Title: Collective bargaining, firm size and pensions in Canada
Abstract: The following paper analyzes the provision of job-related pensions in Canada. The empirical results indicate that both unions and firm size have significant effects on the distribution of pensions. The significance of unions on the provision of pensions does decline as firm size increases. © 1989.

Title: Discrimination in the provision of fringe benefits
Abstract: Minorities and women are shown to be less likely to receive fringe benefits than those with comparable characteristics but equally likely to receive benefits as those with comparable characteristics and earnings. This is shown to be consistent with a model in which earnings are the primary determinants of benefit provision and in which minorities and women suffer earnings discrimination but not direct discrimination in benefit provision. © 1989.

Title: Non-neutral technical change, capital, white-collar and blue-collar labor
Authors: P. Kugler, U. Muller, G. Sheldon
Abstract: The empirical analysis of recent quarterly data for West German industries indicates that technical change is biased in favor of white-collar labor and equipment, while it is biased against blue-collar labor. © 1989.

Title: Optimal regulation of a consistent conjectures duopoly
Abstract: Previous regulatory incentive schemes have focused on monopoly or on competition with externalities. This note examines a consistent conjectures duopoly, deriving a specific tax function that induces optimal output even if the regulator is ignorant of demand and knows the cost function only up to an affine transformation. The solution readily generalizes to symmetric oligopoly. © 1989.

Title: Exchange rate pass-through and the relative concentration of German and Japanese manufacturing industries
Abstract: This note examines the rank correlation of export price markups and industrial concentration in German and Japanese manufactures in 1984 and 1986. It gives the most current measures of Japanese manufacturing concentration available in English. © 1989.

Title: (s,S) Pricing policy when adjustment costs affect demand
Abstract: Adjustment costs in a typical (s,S) pricing policy model are respecified so that price stability affects revenues rather than costs. The (s,S) pricing result holds even when menu costs are removed. © 1989.

Title: Perfect option hedging and the hedge ratio
Abstract: This paper examines the common practice of combining stock options and the underlying stock to eliminate risk using solely the hedge ratio. It provides necessary and sufficient conditions on the stock price process for this approach to work. © 1989.

Title: Fiscal policy, monetary policy and the efficiency of the stock market
Abstract: This paper tests the semi-strong form of the Efficient Market Hypothesis (EMH) with respect to anticipated and unanticipated monetary and fiscal variables. Using lagged values of these estimates it was found that the hypothesis holds for both types of policy actions. © 1989.

Title: Purchasing power parity and administered exchange rates
Abstract: This paper develops and tests a 'discrete' short run version of the purchasing power parity hypothesis using data from five developing economies with fixed exchange rate regimes. Two versions of a model where the exchange rate responds to inflation differential only when the latter is sufficiently large in absolute terms, are tested. The multinomial discrete choice model used for this purpose seems to draw reasonable support from the data. © 1989.

Title: Differential taxation and the encouragement of risk-taking
Abstract: In the framework of expected utility maximization with risk aversion it is shown that the standard result about the tax encouragement of risk taking in a two-asset model, can be extended to the case of many risky assets. There are no tax substitution effects within the set of risky assets; in particular there is no substitution from less to more risky assets. It is also demonstrated that the qualitative response pattern is independent of the assumed existence of a safe asset. The by now common conclusion that capital income taxation encourages risk-taking must therefore be interpreted with some care. © 1989.

Title: Evidence on taxation and charitable giving from the 1983 U.S. treasury tax model file
Authors: William S. Reece, Kimberly D. Zieschang
Abstract: We have applied our model of taxation and charitable giving developed in Reece and Zieschang (1985) to the 1983 Treasury Tax Model File and found no response of giving to marginal tax rates and a small response to income. © 1989.

Title: Financial innovations and the interest elasticity of money demand in Canada
Abstract: Using Canadian data for the period 1934-86, the paper empirically tests the Gurley-Shaw hypothesis that innovations in the financial markets raise the interest elasticity of money demand. The results provide sufficient evidence to reject the Gurley-Shaw hypothesis in Canada. © 1989.

Title: On complete securities markets and the martingale property of securities prices
Abstract: This paper provides a counterexample to the 'equivalent martingale measure' (EMM) characterization of complete securities markets given by Harrison and Pliska (1981, 1983) and establishes an EMM characterization by introducing a condition on securities price processess, which is easy to verify. © 1989.

Title: Testing non-linearities in world stock market prices
Abstract: The results of two non-linearity tests on 27 stock market prices traded on five world stock exchanges are reported and bilinear time series models are fitted to the stock return data. © 1989.

Title: Comparative properties of sums of independent binomials with different parameters
Abstract: This paper presents some results on how certain kinds of changes in parameters induce a first-order stochastic change in the sums of independent binomials with different parameters. These results are useful for qualitative economic analysis. For example, in situations in which a decision-making unit receives observations from a variety of sources or subsamples, these results help predict the effects of changes in the composition and sizes of subsamples on the economic variables under consideration. © 1989.

Title: Semiparametric estimation and efficiency bounds of binary choice models when the models contain one continuous variable
Abstract: This paper considers semiparametric estimation and efficiency bounds of binary response models under the condition of 'zero median of the error terms' when the models contain one continuous variable. The estimator proposed in this paper is based on the idea of the generalized maximum likelihood estimator and its rate of the convergence of the estimator is faster than that of Manski's maximum score estimator which is known to be T 1 3-consistent. The efficiency bounds of the estimator is determined by differentiability of the density function of the error terms. © 1989.

Title: Estimation of multiplicative measurement-error models and some simulation results
Abstract: Hwang's (1986) multiplicative errors-in-variables model is extended to include both scrambled dependent and independent variables. Simulation results show that the derived estimator yields estimates closely approximating the true parameters. OLS's estimates are seriously biased. © 1989.

Title: Bayesian estimator of the linear regression model with an interval constraint on coefficients
Abstract: In this paper we show the Bayesian estimator for regression coefficients subject to an interval constraint, derive its sampling theoretic risk function and compare the risk performance of the Bayesian estimator with that of the sampling theoretic estimator. © 1989.

Title: The kalai/smorodinsky solution with time preferences
Abstract: Even under complete information, the Rubinstein scheme does not generate a unique (subgame) perfect equilibrium partition unless the players are risk neutral. In the standard cooperative bargaining literature, on the other hand, time preferences of players do not play any role. It is assumed that players negotiate as long as they want to without foregoing any portion of the pie. The discount factors are not used, even when they are available; this amounts to limiting the available information use in the bargaining problem. By characterizing a modified Kalai/Smorodinsky solution axiomatically the above problems have been tried to be solved. © 1989.

Title: Rational performance and gibbard's pareto-consistent libertarian claim
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to introduce a new condition, called the rational performance, and hereby point out that the Gibbard's Pareto-consistent libertarian claim has a certain defect from this point of view. © 1989.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Redistributive impact of ‘optimal’ commodity taxes
Abstract: Optimal commodity tax rates are computed for different objective functions and their redistributive impact is studied using Indian data. The results indicate that while in general one should expect a limited impact on redistribution the redistributive impact at the observed tax rates is much below the potential. © 1989.

Title: The screening hypothesis and the marginal productivity theory
Abstract: Using micro level data from an Indian private sector company, hierarchy and earnings functions for each schooling group are estimated. The results support the weak as well as the strong versions of the screening hypothesis besides establishing the diminishing marginal productivity theory. © 1989.

Title: Rates of return in the Indian private sector
Abstract: Using micro level data from an Indian private sector company, we obtain a clearcut pattern of diminishing rates of return to schooling well in keeping with conventional human capital theory. © 1989.

Title: Determinants of earned rates of return on equity of U.S. electric utilities, 1976–1984
Authors: Anil K. Makhija, Michael H. Spiro
Abstract: This paper presents findings that suggest that electric utility regulators take into account industry-wide changes rather than individual firm differences when they set allowed rates. This evidence is consistent with the view that state-level commissions pursue 'generic regulation'. © 1989.

Title: Trade balance and exchange rate with the PPP theory
Abstract: With a multi-good Dornbusch-type model,this paper shows that the real and nominal exchange rates and trade balance move together, implying the existence of Laursen-Metzler effect and positive money effect on trade balance. © 1989.

Title: Purchasing power parity during the 1920s
Abstract: In this note the Purchasing Power Parity theory during the 1920s is tested using the co-integration approach. The results do not support the theory. Although exchange rates and prices are non-stationary in the levels, no equilibrium relationship holds among them. © 1989.

Title: The flypaper effect and the revenue impact of grants-in-aid
Authors: Muhammed N. Islam, Saud A. Choudhury
Abstract: Using a median voter model, which assumes grants as endogenous, this paper finds strong evidence of the flypaper effect of unconditional grants to Ontario Municipalities. Unconditional grants are therefore not expected to reduce the tax burden of local residents. © 1989.

Title: Money demand instability: has it ended?
Abstract: Some researchers suggest that much of the seeming instability in the post-1973 money demand occurred because of financial innovation and deregulation; money demand was in transition. Further unprecedented declines in the income velocity of circulation during 1985 and 1986 indicate that this hypothesized transition continues. Have the effects of financial innovation and deregulation run their course? Do additional unexpected shifts in velocity loom in the near future? Or has the transition come to a halt? These questions are examined using the methodology of Hafer and Hein (1982) as modified by Miller (1986).
