No evidence of structural shifts exists beyond 1986; M1 growth may have become a reliable monetary-aggregate target again. Further, the missing money has more than returned; more money is held today than predicted by the pre-1973 money demand function. Since M1 now includes interest-bearing transactions accounts and incorporates a saving motive, the finding is not counterintuitive. © 1989.

Title: Quasi-concave optimisation
Abstract: Two results are presented - one for equality constraints and the other for inequality constraints. Each result provides conditions which together with the relevant first-order necessary conditions are sufficient for a maximum of a quasi-concave function subject to constraints. © 1989.

Title: ‘Optimal’ model selection when the true relationship is weak and occurs with a delay
Authors: James M. Holmes, Patricia A. Hutton
Abstract: A Monte Carlo comparison of five model selection criteria indicates that when the true relationship is weak and delayed, Theil's (1961) criterion or the selection of the most significant lag structure is most likely to result in the correct inference. © 1989.

Title: A note on rational speculative bubbles
Abstract: Diba and Grossman (1987) show that conditions which rule out certain deterministic bubbles, also rule out all rational stochastic bubbles of the form suggested by Blanchard and Watson (1982). The conditions appear to be fairly weak. Their conclusion, that if a bubble exists - a deterministic bubble, which cannot burst - it must have started at time zero, replicates a result contained in Sargent and Wallace (1973); a characteristic of all saddlepoint unstable systems. There is, as yet, no acceptable model which characterizes a speculative bubble; when, at any time t > 0, it begins, how long it persists. © 1989.

Title: On allocating the variance of output growth to trend and cycle components
Authors: Thomas E. Hall, T. Windsor Fields, M. Andrew Fields
Abstract: Given any decomposition of real GNP into trend and cycle components, we describe a simple statistical procedure by which the proportions of the variance of GNP growth attributable to each of these components can be calculated. © 1989.

Title: On non-negative solvability of nonlinear input–output systems
Abstract: Sufficient and necessary conditions are given for the existence of unique non-negative solutions of non-linear input-output systems. As special cases linear and differentiable systems are analyzed. © 1989.

Title: Portfolio choice with non-expected utility in continuous time
Abstract: Non-expected utility preferences, which can distinguish intertemporal substitution from attitudes towards risk, are extended to continuous time. The consumption/savings and portfolio problem is solved for constant intertemporal elasticity of substitution and constant relative risk aversion. © 1989.

Title: On ‘Maxwell's laws’ of individual behaviour
Abstract: Any theory of choice under uncertainty in which choice depends on locally linear evaluations of univariate probability density functions has precisely two testable implications. These are 1. (a) dũ = Ω 2. (b) {black star}d{black star}ũ = φ. Here φ, ũ, and Ω are differential forms, φ a zero-form, ũ a one-form, and Ω a two-form. d is the exterior derivative operator on forms, and {black star} is the Hodge star operator. In this letter we explain in a non-technical way the meaning and import of equations (a) and (b). A fuller treatment will be found in Russell (1989). © 1989.

Title: Interchangeability of equilibrium points in extensive games with complete information
Abstract: In this note we prove the interchangeability of equilibrium points in extensive games with complete information. © 1989.

Title: Asymptotic efficiency in principal-agent models with hidden information
Abstract: In the hidden information model a simple but general argument is given to show that first-best utility levels can be approached for low enough discount rates. © 1989.

Title: A cross-institutional comparison of the extent to which political representatives' voting behavior reflects constituents' preferences
Abstract: When casting roll call votes, members of the U.S. Senate appear to be at least as representative of their constituents' preferences as members of the U.S. House are. Several explanations are offered for this apparent anomaly. © 1989.

Title: Four paradoxes in U.K. GDP
Abstract: Evidence is presented for the U.K. to support Rose's findings of four important paradoxes in the time series structure of real output for the U.S. © 1989.

Title: On brand proliferation with vertical differentiation
Abstract: It is known that under horizontal differentiation whenever firms decide sequentially upon locations and prices, they give up the possibility of proliferation. We propose a spatial model of vertical differentiation to check the robustness of such an outcome to the specification of product differentiation. © 1989.

Title: Being identical, behaving differently: A theorem on technological diffusion
Abstract: Adoption of a new technique is analysed in the framework of an infinitely repeated, symmetric Bertrand duopoly. It is shown that asymmetric Subgame Perfect Equilibria, i.e. equilibrium diffusion, exist. © 1989.

Title: Rational expectations with imperfect competition
Abstract: We study a model in which price-setting oligopolists have private information about the commodity they sell. We construct an equilibrium in which some, but not all, of the information is transmitted by prices. We show that when the number of sellers increases, this equilibrium converges in distribution to the perfectly revealing competitive equilibrium. © 1989.

Title: Attitudes towards unions and union membership
Abstract: This paper argues that the conventional treatment of the attitudes of workers in union status models is poorly motivated. One result is that the model may be incapable of tracking large changes in union membership, if these derive from shifts in attitudes. © 1989.

Title: Specific and general training in the theory of labor turnover
Abstract: This paper shows that an increase in the degree of firm-specificity of training may lead to an increased probability of firing if ex post exchange of private information entails significant transaction costs. © 1989.

Title: Can the concentration-collusion hypothesis be refuted empirically?
Authors: Gregory J. Werden, Michael A. Williams
Abstract: Simulations based on the multiple equilibria property of repeated game models are used to demonstrate that conventional cross-section regressions may be incapable of detecting a relationship between concentration and performance. © 1989.

Title: A note on partial vertical integration
Abstract: A simple model is constructed to show how partial vertical integration may emerge as an equilibrium market structure in a world characterized by rationing, differences in the reservation prices of buyers, and in the risk attitudes of buyers and sellers. The buyers with the high reservation prices turn out to be vertically integrated. © 1989.

Title: Testing for long run purchasing power parity
Abstract: Long run purchasing power parity (PPP) for six drachma bilateral exchange rates is tested by means of unit root and cointegration tests. The results reject long run PPP. © 1989.

Title: On the measurement of employment segregation
Abstract: A new index of occupational segregation is proposed, which is related to Gini's Concentration Ratio. An illustration based on French data (1987) indicates that similar conclusions are drawn whether the famous dissimilarity index [Duncan and Duncan (1955)] or the one proposed here is used, but the new index might have some advantage over the one suggested by the Duncans. © 1989.

Title: Unit root behavior in velocity
Abstract: Recursive least squares is used to test for the presence of a unit root in velocity for a long series of annual U.S., Canadian, and U.K. data, and postwar quarterly U.S. data. Results reveal structural shifts in velocity and these are cause for concern if one uncritically accepts the random walk hypothesis. © 1989.

Title: Money-velocity causality detection
Abstract: This paper is an attempt to test Friedman's hypothesis that the variability of money growth causes velocity to change. The Granger-causality method is applied to test this hypothesis using quarterly data from 1974.I to 1985.IV for seven developing countries-Indonesia, Nigeria, Qatar, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Venezuela. These countries are characterized by relatively narrow but expanding money markets. © 1989.

Title: Government capital and private output in the United States
Abstract: Aggregate production functions for private output are estimated from annual U.S. data for the period 1948-1985. The estimates indicate government capital has an important positive effect on private output. The effect of state and local governments' capital is large and significant whereas the effect of federal capital appears small and statistically insignificant. © 1989.

Title: Some fine-tuning for dominant diagonal matrices
Abstract: Given a linear system Ax = b, where A is a dominant diagonal matrix with positive diagonals and non-positive off-diagonals, but b has both positive and negative components, necessary and sufficient conditions on b j are derived to guarantee that x j is positive. © 1989.

Title: Expected MSE of errors-in-variables and omitted variables models
Abstract: In regression analysis, should one include or exclude a proxy for an unobservable if interest is on another regressor? We consider expectations of a loss function for several priors for unobserved parameters in errors-in-variables models. © 1989.

Title: A note on bias from proxy variables with systematic errors
Authors: John H. Herbert, Khoan T. Dinh
Abstract: An expression for bias in regression coefficients from using a proxy variable with a systematic measurement error as an explanatory variable in a regression analysis is derived. The expression for bias is shown to be related to previously published, but much less general, expressions for bias. © 1989.

Title: Preliminary-test estimation of the scale parameter in a mis-specified regression model
Authors: David E.A. Giles, Judith A. Clarke
Abstract: We consider the pre-test estimation of the scale parameter (after a test of linear restrictions on the coefficients) in a regression model which is mis-specified through the omission of variables. The exact finite-sample risk of the pre-test estimator is derived, illustrated, and explored. © 1989.

Title: The advantageous nature of risk aversion in a three-player bargaining game where acceptance of a proposal requires a simple majority
Abstract: In a three-player bargaining game in which acceptance of a proposed allocation requires only the approval of a simple majority, it is shown that the most (least) risk averse player receives the highest (lowest) expected share when the preferences of the players are not too diverse. © 1989.

Title: Fixed rules and decision rules
Abstract: The paper investigates the relationship between time consistency and subgame perfection. We show that despite some suggestions in the literature, the two are not equivalent. Subgame perfection is a stronger refinement. The paper also discusses the classes of games in which time consistency and subgame perfection are equivalent. © 1989.

Title: Accommodation, price flexibility and fluctuations
Abstract: We show that in an economy where output fluctuations are driven primarily by aggregate demand shocks, allowing a contemporaneous response of nominal wage contracts to actual market conditions in the period of the reopening of a contract, invalidates Taylor's 'second order' Phillips curve and Delong and Summers' destabilizing output effects of increased price flexibility. © 1989.

Title: Union responses to changes in non-labour input prices
Abstract: The paper extends results on the microeconomics of trade union behavior by deriving a more usable expression for the effect on union wage choices of changes in non-labour input prices. © 1989.

Title: Efficiency wages and local versus central wage bargaining
Abstract: A simple efficiency wage model is extended to allow for the presence of unions. The presence of unions aggravates the unemployment caused by efficiency wage considerations. Provided the labour demand elasticity is not too much larger than one, local (firm level) wage bargaining gives a higher negotiated wage than central wage bargaining, implying higher unemployment under local wage bargaining than under central wage bargaining. © 1989.

Title: Immigration and real wages
Abstract: This paper derives conditions under which immigration may raise nominal and real wages in a small open economy. The mechanism for such a paradoxical outcome is a demand-induced increase in the prices of labour-intensive non-traded goods. © 1989.

Title: A note on pricing of hub-and-spoke networks
Abstract: The difference between competitive and monopolistic pricing of airlines' hub-and-spoke networks is examined. It is found that under reasonable cost conditions pass-through passengers pay lower prices per mile than those originating or ending at the hub. Thus, higher per-mile prices in large hubs do not necessarily signal market power. © 1989.

Title: Mergers, stock prices, and industrial production
Abstract: Economic theory has been developed to correlate mergers and stock prices and mergers and industrial production. This study tests for significant relations among annual mergers, stock prices, and industrial production and examines whether multiple time series models can forecast annual mergers more accurately than a univariate merger model. We do not find that the mean square forecasting error of the multivariate time series model is significantly less than the mean square forecasting error of the univariate merger model. The stock price series does not aid in forecasting mergers. © 1989.

Title: Are announcement effects time dependent?
Abstract: The constancy assumption for the announcement response coefficient is relaxed, and is modelled through a time-varying Kalman filter. We find that the announcement effect is not time dependent for the post-1979 non-borrowed reserves regime. © 1989.

Title: Two exact, non-arbitrary and general methods of decomposing temporal change
Abstract: A common goal in economics is to attribute changes in a variable Y between two points in time to various causes, when the only information available is an equation expressing Y as a matrix product of several variables, and the values of all variables at the two dates. Past methods of decomposing temporal changes into various components are found to suffer from one or more of the following problems: they can be arbitrary due to the uncertainty concerning whether to expand about the initial or final time period, inexact due to a residual term, and specific to cases in which the variable is a product of two matrices. This paper presents two decomposition methods which overcome all three shortcomings of earlier methods. © 1989.

Title: Mean square error matrix superiority of estimators under linear restrictions and misspecification
Abstract: In this paper attention is focussed on the mixed regression estimator (MRE), which is based upon incorrect prior information, and on the restricted least squares estimator (RLSE), which uses valid or invalid restrictions. With respect to the mean square error (MSE) matrix criterion we can derive conditions, under which MRE and RLSE are better than the ordinary least squares estimator (OLSE), especially in the case that the regression model is misspecified. Finally we examine the superiority of the MSE-predictor over the OLS-predictor. © 1989.

Title: On testing the properties of directly obtained expectations data
Abstract: This paper demonstrates the correct procedure for making appropriate inferences concerning the properties of directly observed survey data on expectations. © 1989.

Title: A test for heteroscedasticity and non-normality of regression residuals
Abstract: This paper discusses alternative and relatively easier tests for heteroscedasticity and non-normality of regression residuals. The estimates of the test statistics are obtained along with the estimates of other regression coefficients and involve no additional calculations. The advantage is that there is no need for a priori information on sources of heteroscedasticity and non-normality. © 1989.

Title: An approximation theorem for the polynomial inverse lag
Authors: Gregory M. Gelles, Douglas W. Mitchell
Abstract: The polynomial inverse lag (PIL) of Mitchell and Speaker (1986) is a flexible distributed lag technique which is easy to estimate, because it requires only a brief nested search for the polynomial degree and estimation is otherwise linear. This paper presents an approximation theorem for the PIL, showing that a PIL of sufficient degree can arbitrarily closely approximate any absolutely summable sequence of true lag weights, with distance measured by the L1 metric. © 1989.

Title: Efficiency wages, wage indexation and macroeconomic stabilization
Abstract: This paper examines the effects of nominal wage indexation on output variability when effort affects the productivity of labor inputs. Given this specification, it is shown that, contrary to Gray's (1976) result, full wage indexation is not destabilizing in the presence of supply shocks. © 1989.

Title: Technological change and embodiment hypothesis
Abstract: We introduce vintage capital into optimal growth models to explore the implications of technological change and economic growth. Our model predicts a positive association between growth rates in GNP and the savings rate, which is consistent with some empirical observations. © 1989.

Title: Equivalent variation with uncertain prices
Abstract: Government interventions in markets often distort prices. When the price consequences are uncertain, due to objective uncertainty in the economic environment, compensating and equivalent variation must be defined with respect to a cardinal indirect utility function that could be observed from consumer choices on lotteries of price vectors. I discuss the bias in approximating the true equivalent variation with measures that depend only on the ordinal (not cardinal) properties of the indirect utility function, which is easier to observe. © 1989.

Title: Intra-experimental income effects and risk aversion
Abstract: Harrison's (1986) modification of the Bekker, DeGroot and Marshak (1964) mechanism for eliciting risk preferences is employed to test the hypotheses of expected utility theory (with respect to changes in income): increasing relative risk aversion and decreasing absolute risk aversion. Subjects in the laboratory are shown to exhibit such behavior. © 1989.

Title: A refinement and extension of the no-envy concept
Abstract: We propose a new criterion of equity in the spirit of Foley's (1967) no-envy concept. We prove the existence of efficient allocations satisfying this criterion for a class of economies containing many for which envy-free and efficient allocations do not exist; when a large set of the latter exists, our criterion selects a small subset of it. © 1989.

Title: Correlated effectivity functions
Abstract: We introduce the α- and β-effectivity functions of game forms with random outcomes and where coalitions are allowed to use correlated strategies. Several nice properties of the α- and β-effectivity functions appear in this context. Mainly a super game form is defined and it is proved that its effectivity function (α or β) is the same as the β-effectivity function of the original game form. As a consequence, the latter is super additive and is the best of the two to represent the power of coalitions. © 1989.

Title: Quasi-rational expectations
Abstract: Using a convergence approach in decentralized models of the economy, it is shown that agents are able to form an expectation of an endogenous aggregate variable which is almost equal to the rational expectation, with minimal information only. © 1989.

Title: The beckmann-zipf effect and plant location under uniform pricing
Abstract: This paper examines the impact of Beckmann-Zipf effect on location choice. Under the uniform price policy, it shows that the delivery cost minimization approach can not be applied, and the median location is unlikely to be chosen, even if the delivery cost function is linear. © 1989.

Title: A note on union-non-union benefit differentials and size of establishment
Authors: Donald G. Bramley, Phanindra V. Wunnava, Michael D. Robinson
Abstract: This research note has expanded Podgursky's (1986) results concerning union-non-union differentials to benefits. Explicitly, union impacts on pension and health insurance coverage are obtained by plant size. Our empirical results are based on May 1983 CPS data of random sample of white males. They indicate that the pattern of differentials for health insurance are very similar to those obtained by Podgursky (i.e., the union-non-union differentials are largest in small plants). However, the results for pension coverage indicate a U-shaped union-non-union differential (i.e., the smallest and largest plants are found to have the largest differential). © 1989.

Title: The effect of occupational segregation on the relative earnings of black males
Abstract: An earnings model which incorporates racial differences in occupational attainment is employed to investigate sources of the earnings differential between black and white males. Our results suggest that occupational segregation of black men accounts for nearly half of the observed racial earnings differential. © 1989.

Title: The role of consensus and disagreement in portfolio adjustment
Abstract: This paper shows that the diffusion of opinions slows down the portfolio adjustment. A variance component model of trading volumes is used to analyze NYSE and S&P 100 index option trading volumes. © 1989.

Title: Tariffs and the current account with short-run capital specificity
Abstract: Permanent tariff reductions are shown to result in a deterioration of the current account, even under intertemporal optimising by consumers. This is due to the assumption of short-run fixity and long-run mobility of capital. © 1989.

Title: The firm size effect on stock returns in a developing stock market
Abstract: The empirical relationship between firm size and returns on the stocks listed on the Stock Exchange of Singapore is examined in this study. The results show that the stocks of small firms have earned higher returns than the stocks of large firms, and that the firm size effect is still significant when risk-adjusted returns are controlled for difference in earnings/price (E/P) ratios. © 1989.

Title: Computing returns to scale under alternative models
Abstract: This paper provides a comparison of returns to scale when computed with a non-parametric (linear programming) and a parametric (linear programming) method. The two models are applied to a data set for the Japanese agricultural sector and the comparison shows that scale characteristics obtained are method-independent. © 1989.

Title: An application of extended rational approximants to White's information matrix test
Abstract: Phillips' (1982) ERAs are modified to approximate inverse distribution functions. An approximant is then used to correct the size bias of White's information matrix test. © 1989.

Title: A proof of the asymptotic validity of a test for perfect aggregation
Abstract: An asymptotic proof is presented for a test of perfect aggregation in linear models developed in Pesaran, Pierse and Kumar (1989). The limiting distribution is derived by letting the degree of disaggregation increase without bound for a fixed sample size. © 1989.

Title: On the robustness of the F-test to autocorrelation among disturbances
Abstract: This note examines the F-test for a set of linear restrictions on the parameters in the standard linear regression model. For regressions without an intercept, it is shown that the F-test is extremely non-robust to autocorrelation, in the sense that the size of the tests tends to either one or zero as correlation among disturbances increases. © 1989.

Title: Comparison of hazard functions with duration dependence and stayer-mover structure with an application to divorce
Abstract: Performances of hazard functions with an implicit stayer-mover structure are examined in Monte Carlo samples. The results are then applied to data on duration of first marriages. © 1989.

Title: The box-cox transformation
Abstract: We show that a Box-Cox transformation on the dependent variable of linear regression models is invariant to power transformations of that variable even without the presence of a regression constant and, consequently, can sometimes be interpreted as a simple power transformation the estimation of which will then admit of a non-degenerate solution. © 1989.

Title: Risk characteristics of a stein-like estimator for the probit regression model
Abstract: A shrinkage estimator is proposed for the probit regression model and its risk characteristics are studied in a Monte Carlo experiment. © 1989.

Title: Anticipated monetary policy in Canada
Abstract: In this note I examine the policy ineffectiveness proposition for Canada using monthly income data due to Milbourne et al. (1988). I find that anticipated monetary policy altered the evolution of real output in Canada. Recent work by Ambler and Phaneuf (1988) can be used to attribute this result to a purely New Keynesian model of the business cycle, although this inference is found to be fragile with respect to the choice of the level of significance used in the hypothesis tests. © 1989.

Title: Classification of budget-invariant monotonic preferences
Abstract: A linear utility representation theorem due to Blackwell and Girshick (1953) is used to answer the question as formulated by Grandmont (1987) whether Cobb-Douglas representable preferences are the only ones which are budget-invariant. © 1989.

Title: The effect of demand uncertainty on a precommitted monopoly price
Abstract: Under plausible conditions on the shape of a monopolist's or a monopolistic competitor's cost function, multiplicative demand uncertainty is shown to raise the firm's optimal precommitted price. It is argued that this effect can be substantial. © 1989.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
A note on mechanization and wage bargaining
Abstract: Collective wage bargaining may bias firms' choice of production techniques, but not in favour of mechanization. It is most profitable to install relatively more equipment which is complementary to labour power than equipment which is a substitute. © 1989.

Title: Migration and job search in a dualistic economy
Abstract: By introducing optimal search behavior, à la Stigler, into a Todarian dual sector urban economy, the probability of urban-formal sector entry as a function of the rural-urban migrants' optimal search intensity is derived and its implications studied. © 1989.

Title: The structure of adjustment costs for labour in the Dutch manufacturing sector
Abstract: This paper investigates the appropriateness of the hypothesis of symmetric adjustment costs for labour (ACL) in dynamic labour demand models. © 1989.

Title: The wiles test revisited
Abstract: This paper uses a sample of Egyptian graduates to investigate a method of testing the screening hypothesis proposed by Wiles (1974) and tested by Miller and Volker (1983). The results do not tend to support the screening view. © 1989.

Title: Manufacturing margins
Authors: A.R. Thurik, W.H.M. Van Der Hoeven
Abstract: The influence of labour costs, concentration, capacity utilization, exports and firm size on manufacturing profit margin is studied with a discrimination between small and large firms. © 1989.

Title: A causality-effect between bid premium and outcome of tender offer
Abstract: This is a note which analyzes the impact of bid premium on the outcome of friendly versus hostile tender offers. The impact seems to have opposite effects and we suggest a general model to avoid this confusion. © 1989.

Title: Theoretical foundations of constant-proportion portfolio insurance
Abstract: Under HARA preferences and a standard opportunity set, constant-proportion portfolio insurance is optimal if and only if the investor has declining absolute and relative risk aversion. The optimal floor is the capitalized value of the investor's subsistence consumption rate if and only if the investor's family size is constant. © 1989.

Title: Are survey forecasts trusted?
Abstract: Heterogenous expectations are considered to be reflected by strategic intention or wishful thinking and/or by private information. Using survey data of the Tokyo foreign exchange market, tests are performed to determine whether heterogenous expectations contain private information. © 1989.

Title: Bank failures as Poisson variates
Abstract: The elasticity of bank failures with respect to a set of explanatory variables is estimated using a maximum-likelihood Poisson estimator. The resulting estimates are compared with their OLS counterparts. © 1989.

Title: The dividend ratio model and small sample bias
Authors: John Y. Campbell, Robert J. Shiller
Abstract: Small sample properties of parameter estimates and test statistics in the vector autoregressive dividend ratio model [Campbell and Shiller (1988a,b)] are derived by stochastic simulation. The data generating processes are cointegrated vector autoregressive models, estimated subject to restrictions implied by the dividend ratio model, or altered to show a unit root. © 1989.

Title: Competition in the U.S. banking industry
Abstract: A non-linear, simultaneous-equation test of market power proposed by Bresnahan (1982) is applied to several decades of U.S. banking data. The results strongly reject collusive behavior and are consistent with perfect competition. © 1989.

Title: Model selection criteria and granger causality tests
Abstract: In this note, we use several statistical criteria for model selection for Granger causality detection. The results indicate some sensitivity to the chosen criterion. © 1989.

Title: Some evidence on the performance of size correction factors in testing consumer demand models
Abstract: Simulation experiments with the Rotterdam model show that restricting the covariance matrix and using its unbiased estimate is quite helpful when performing the Wald test, while application of Italianer's correction factor works quite well when using the likelihood ratio test. © 1989.

Title: Relative uncertainty
Abstract: In models of price level or inflation uncertainty the budget constraint is not linear in the random variable. We show that in a wide class of these models the appropriate measure of uncertainty is a relative one. © 1989.

Title: Tacit collusion in differentiated cournot games
Abstract: In a simple oligopoly with quantity setting firms, we analyze the conditions under which more product differentiation makes tacit collusion easier. It is found that the net effect can go either way. © 1989.

Title: Fixed cost of work and the demand for lotteries
Abstract: A fixed cost of work is sufficient to induce risk-averse individuals, who obey the expected utility hypothesis, to demand lotteries. The critical assumption needed to generate this demand is that leisure is a normal good. © 1989.

Title: An information inequality for agency problems
Abstract: Mirrlees (1974, 1975) has shown in the standard principal agent problem, that under certain conditions the first-best solution can be approximated arbitrarily closely - the agency costs can be made arbitrarily small. It is of interest therefore to derive conditions under which the agency costs are bounded from below by some positive number. This paper exploits the often noted parallel between the principal-agent problem and certain aspects of statistical theory and use what is essentially the information inequality (Cramer-Rao lower bound) to bound the agency cost as a function of the Fisher information and a parameter depending on the agent's utility function. © 1989.

Title: Stable implementation of Lindahl allocations
Abstract: The resource allocation mechanisms using Nash equilibrium as the solution concept in economies with incomplete information rely on the assumption that agent's disequilibrium messages converge to a Nash equilibrium. The mechanisms implementing Lindahl allocations are, however, extremely unstable under the most used process to represent disequilibrium behaviour in games of incomplete information: the Cournot process. We provide a new mechanism overcoming the instability difficulty in the case of quasi-linear preferences. © 1989.

Title: A measure of the U.S. output gap
Abstract: An autoregressive-distributed lag regression of the unemployment rate on output growth is structurally stable over the 1890-1986 period. Inverting this equation yields a measure of the output gap which is not subject to the spurious detrending problem. © 1989.

Title: A simple model of product quality with elastic demand
Abstract: In various models starting with Klein and Leffler (1981), sellers produce high quality for the sake of future profits. These models have assumed that a consumer demands one or zero units, but a simple model with elastic demand and entry costs can illustrate the same point with fewer problems of existence or determinacy of equilibrium. © 1989.

Title: Errata
On the estimation of localization economies
Abstract: This paper proposes a new method for testing for the existence of localization economies for growing industries. The key concept is the elasticity of the growth rate of a local industry with respect to the base year level of activity in the local area. If this elasticity is positive, the industry tends to centralize as it grows; if this elasticity is negative, the industry decentralizes as it grows. © 1989.

Title: The statistical structure of real-income changes
Abstract: An autoregressive process for real-income changes is considered. This process is useful for statistical simulation in demand studies. © 1989.

Title: Insiders and outsiders and efficient asymmetric information contracts
Abstract: The employment levels implied by an efficient contract with asymmetric information are shown to deviate from Walrasian levels if a distinction if drawn between 'insiders and outsiders'. If insiders alone negotiate the contract there will be over-employment for low levels of demand and there may be either over or under-employment for high levels. © 1989.

Title: Individual versus social discount rates in allocating depletable natural resources over time
Abstract: This paper demonstrates that individuals express different preferences with respect to intertemporal allocation of depletable natural resources. Those who obtain direct private control of these resources may be relatively less likely to conserve than society in general. © 1989.

Title: The information content of post tender offer movement in the price of target shares
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to show that in the specific case of hostile tender offers, movements in the prices of target stocks, after announcement of a tender, are not good predictors of the outcome. © 1989.

Title: Volatility-invariant hedging
Abstract: We seek to configure an option so that its hedge ratio is unaffected by measurement error in volatility. This is shown to be possible only in a special case, but one which is fortuitously satisfied by recent market conditions. © 1989.

Title: Perfect option hedging and the hedge ratio
Abstract: This paper examines the common practice of combining stock options and the underlying stock to eliminate risk using solely the hedge ratio. It provides necessary and sufficient conditions on the stock price process for this approach to work. © 1989.

Title: Contagion effect on sovereign interest rate spreads
Abstract: This paper analyzes the extent to which sovereign default risk in contagious. That is, contagion tests are conducted to determine whether 'news' regarding the creditworthiness of a sovereign borrower affect the spreads charged to others. The empirical results support the view that a systematic risk element enters into the default risk perceptions of lenders implying the existence of significant contagion effects in international lending. © 1989.

Title: Ranking mobility matrices
Abstract: A sufficient condition is given for one mobility matrix to display more mobility than another in the sense of Kanbur and Stiglitz. © 1989.

Title: A note on the distribution of the least squares estimator of a random walk with drift
Abstract: It is shown that the application of the result that the Dickey-Fuller 'T' obtained from a regression with an intercept is asymptotically normal if the DGP is a random walk with drift may be of little use in small samples unless the drift is enormous. In fact the Dickey-Fuller distribution may give a better approximation in many case. © 1989.

Title: Testing for the length of a distributed lag with a differencing transformation
Abstract: It is shown that inclusion of the level of the independent variable jointly with lagged values of its first difference provide a simple statistical test for the length of a finite distributed lag when the weights all have the same sign. © 1989.

Title: The max-min solution for variable threat games
Abstract: In this paper we obtain general inequality properties that max-min strategic solutions to variable threat games satisfy under a set of very plausible assumptions. © 1989.

Title: The demand theory of the weak axioms of revealed preference
Abstract: Simple proofs are given for theorems that relate revealed preference axioms for demand and excess demand functions to restrictions on the Jacobian and Slutsky matrices. © 1989.

Title: Competition between and within teams
Abstract: We consider the effect of team size, the observability of effort, and the competitiveness of the team's environment in determining team-members' allocations of effort between team-oriented and selfish efforts. © 1989.

Title: Uncertain monopoly rent and the social cost of rent seeking
Abstract: Assuming that monopoly rent is uncertain, we derive a dissipation rate formula that generalizes the Hillman and Katz formula. We show that for large enough variance, the dissipation rate increases with mean monopoly rent. © 1989.

Title: Imprecise testing and endogenous limits to bonds
Abstract: When testing is imprecise, given heterogenous labor and shirking, bonding can be costly because non-shirkers are discharged (Type II error). Thus firms must pay higher wages to compensate for this possibility. In this case, an inefficient allocation of labor results. © 1989.

Title: The distribution of lifetime earnings
Abstract: Assuming that earnings at a particular age are distributed log-normally, it is shown that the distribution of lifetime earnings can be simulated. For that purpose estimations for the course of μ t and σ2 t are made. © 1989.

Title: A new approach to the economic inequality based upon the permanent income hypothesis
Abstract: We propose a new inequality measure based upon the permanent income hypothesis. Tracing its historical changes in Japan, we compare it with some traditional inequality measures for the income distribution. © 1989.

Title: Market structures, price-cost margins, and unionism
Abstract: Empirical results show the existence of a non-linear relationship between concentration and price-cost margins. A non-linear specification provides substantial evidence that unions reduce profits, especially in more oligopolistic industries. © 1989.

Title: Endogenous monitoring intensity, the period of contractual precommitment, and the slope of the wage-earnings profile
Abstract: We consider the determination of the shape of the wage-earnings profile as well as the pattern of monitoring intensity in a model where marginal monitoring cost is positive. Since the contract specifies that a worker detected shirking will be fired immediately, monitoring intensity can be interpreted as the conditional probability of job separation given shirking. We argue that a crucial determinant of the shape of these two profiles is the length of the contractual horizon, and hence, the length of the firm's precommitment to future job rent. The longer this horizon is, the steeper is the rent profile derived from the wage-earnings profile and the more sharply falling with seniority is the monitoring intensity profile. When this contractual horizon is short, both profiles tend to be flat. Thus, the length of contractual horizon may help to reconcile with received theory some recent evidence on the return to seniority. © 1989.

Title: Central bank intervention with sample selection
Abstract: This paper shows that Japanese foreign exchange market intervention during the late seventies was aimed at resisting dollar depreciation. This is contrary to IMF guidelines. © 1989.

Title: An empirical study of optimal taxation on Australian financial institutions
Abstract: The paper estimates direct and cross price elasticities for a complete model of ten stochastic financial asset share equations and derives Ramsey's optimal tax rates for ten major financial transactions in Australia for the period 1967/1968 to 1984/1985. © 1989.

Title: A many good, many person, Corlett-Hague tax rule
Abstract: Generalising the Corlett-Hague rule yields an insight into the case for differentiated commodity taxation when the linear income tax is not optimal, thus complementing earlier work by Deaton. © 1989.

Title: On approximating the minimum risk estimator in linear regression models
Abstract: For improving the performance of the least squares estimator for the coefficient vector in a linear regression model, the minimum risk estimator under a general quadratic loss function is picked up from a class of biased estimators. Since this estimator involves unknown quantities, two approximate (feasible) versions of it are presented and their risks are studied. © 1989.

Title: Small sample properties of modified Prais-Winston estimators in hypothesis testing in a linear model with ar(1) errors
Abstract: This paper considers small sample properties of estimators for an autocorrelation coefficient (p) and of test statistics based on Prais-Winston (henceforth, P-W) estimators in a linear model with AR(1) errors. We propose two types of new modified P-W estimators (i.e., the bias-corrected P-W estimators) making use of the second-order approximation suggested by Ullah et al. (1983). It is shown by Monte Carlo experiments that one of the modified estimators performs remarkably better in hypothesis testing that the original P-W estimator especially in highly autocorrelated cases. © 1989.

Title: Four tests for the random walk hypothesis
Abstract: In economics and finance, the null hypothesis of random walk is sometimes tested with a larger number of observations in a fixed time span. This suggests that the alternative hypothesis may simply be an iid observations model. This paper investigates the power of two coefficient based tests and two t-ratio based tests for the random walk hypothesis under the alternative hypothesis of iid observations. We argue that the more robust tests proposed by Phillips (1987) will in general have less power than the conventional coefficient based test and t-ratio test. Our analysis is supported by the results of a simulation experiment. © 1989.

Title: Inflation and relative price variability in Yugoslavia
Abstract: Granger causality tests show that inflation Granger-causes relative price variability, but the feedback relationship cannot be excluded. © 1989.

Title: A simulation model of saving, residential choice, and bequests of the Japanese elderly
Abstract: This note develops a life-cycle simulation model of the Japanese elderly's saving behavior. The model shows that the observed lack of dissaving by the elderly can be explained by a strong bequest motive and a constraint on borrowing from home equity. © 1989.

Title: Equivalent variation with uncertain prices
Abstract: Government interventions in markets often distort prices. When the price consequences are uncertain, due to objective uncertainty in the economic environment, compensating and equivalent variation must be defined with respect to a cardinal indirect utility function that could be observed from consumer choices on lotteries of price vectors. I discuss the bias in approximating the true equivalent variation with measures that depend only on the ordinal (not cardinal) properties of the indirect utility function, which is easier to observe. © 1989.

Title: Manipulation of the Pareto semi-optimal rule
Abstract: The Pareto semi-optimal rule is shown to be strictly non-manipulable under certain assumptions on individual preferences over sets of alternatives. This gives an example of a non-manipulable social choice rule which avoids extreme concentrations of power. © 1989.

Title: Public debt, voluntary intergenerational transfers and overlapping generations
Abstract: This paper deals with the characterization of overlapping generations models with voluntary intergenerational transfers when altruism is one-sided. It is argued that the qualitative conclusions derived about debt neutrality do not depend on the way the intergenerational concern is modelled. With operative bequests (gifts), the steady-state interest rate is greater (less) than the population growth rate regardless of whether individuals have a concern about a representative descendant's (ancestor's) utility or the total welfare enjoyed by all their children (parents). When the criterion of total utility of the ancestors is adopted, their utility must not be discounted but compounded, since otherwise the model has no significant solution, although there must be effective discounting of a representative ancestor's utility. © 1989.

Title: On controlling the maintenance of durable goods when contractual enforcement is costly
Abstract: In a model of durable goods with costly maintenance enforcement contracts, monopolist may not control maintenance and perfectly competitive firms never will. This differs from the results of similar models with costless contractual enforcement. © 1989.

Title: Quick responses in duopoly ensure monopoly pricing
Abstract: If firms in a homogeneous duopoly game can respond with negligible delay to their rival's price changes, equilibrium is unique at the monopoly price. © 1989.

Title: Wage discrimination by race and gender in the public and private sectors
Abstract: Previous research suggests that the federal government may act as a model employer by discriminating less on the basis of race and gender. The evidence supporting this suggestion is based primarily on data from the late 1960s and early 1970s. Data from the 1980s demonstrate that if any level of government acts as a model employer it is local government and that the federal government appears to discriminate at least as much as the private sector. © 1989.

Title: Establishment size, public administration and government wage differentials
Abstract: This study presents new and more comprehensive estimates of government wage differentials. They improve on previous estimates by including the influence of establishment size and by estimating separate differentials for public administrators and non-administrators. These improvements result in a more complex set of differentials and a more sophisticated understanding of government wage patterns. © 1989.

Title: On-the-job leisure-income tradeoffs
Abstract: The assumption that workers can optimally equate on-the-job leisure with income (piece-rate production) is tested by utilizing individual production data based on a multi-layered bonus scheme. The results support the notion that workers are able to calibrate their effort-production levels appropriately, given the specific bonus incentive structure. © 1989.

Title: Individual overtime functions with double correction for selectivity bias
Abstract: Empirical overtime functions are estimated using German individual microdata. The sample is restricted to employees who have worked overtime and split into workers with short and long tenure. Consequence is a double correction for selectivity bias. © 1989.

Title: Predatory entrapment
Abstract: A class of markets is described in which informational asymmetry between consumers and firms creates opportunity for a form of predation in which the victim of predation, not the perpetrator, would likely be erroneously identified as a predator under conventional economic and legal standards. © 1989.

Title: Vertical integration in a spatial setting
Abstract: We extend earlier analyses of spatial markets to a vertical setting, in which firms at both the upstream and downstream level face transportation costs and sunk cost investments. Depending on the costs of integration and the size of the successive monopoly distortion loss, vertical integration may be partial, total or not at all. © 1989.

Title: Firms' fiscal years, size and industry
Abstract: Most U.S. corporations choose their fiscal years to coincide with the calendar year. We document that the larger the firm, the more likely it is to begin its fiscal year in January. This finding holds across industries. © 1989.

Title: Foreign exchange market efficiency and cointegration
Abstract: In this note we examine an implication of the cointegration literature for the efficiency of foreign exchange markets. In particular, if foreign exchange markets are efficient, then two spot exchange rates cannot be cointegrated. This proposition is tested for 10 dollar bilateral exchange rates over the period January 1973-December 1985. © 1989.

Title: Is greater exchange rate flexibility stabilizing?
Abstract: This paper examines the hypothesis that greater exchange rate flexibility is stabilizing in external adjustment processes. The results indicate that floating exchange rates tend to magnify changes in relative prices without stabilizing income as the trade balance adjusts. © 1989.

Title: Who profits from taxpayer confusion?
Abstract: When taxpayers are uncertain of true taxable income, they must decide whether to resolve their uncertainty by seeking tax advice, and then decide how much taxable income to report. Since tax advisors must sign their advisees' tax returns, the audit policy can depend on whether tax advice was sought. In the optimal audit policy, some taxpayers will not resolve their uncertainty, and the optimal policy yields higher net revenue with uncertainty than without. © 1989.

Title: Debt neutrality, Professor Vickrey and Henry George's ‘single tax’
Abstract: In OLG models without operative intergenerational gift motives, positive birth rates destroy debt neutrality only if the lump-sum tax under consideration falls on the income from human capital, or any other factor not fully owned by those currently alive. © 1989.

Title: Repeated lending and business fluctuations
Abstract: A borrower-lender relationship is modelled, and the effects of temporary shocks on lending policy are studied. The loan rate is shown to respond sluggishly, thereby influencing shocks' effects on borrower survival, in some cases dampening them. © 1989.

Title: On the calculation of the information matrix test in the normal linear regression model
Abstract: In this paper we propose a simplified method of a calculating the information matrix test in the normal linear regression model. A simulation study demonstrates that our test has considerably better size properties than the Chesher (1983)-Lancaster (1984) version of this test. Our test converges to its asymptotic distribution by n = 600, whereas for the same model Taylor (1987) reports the Chesher-Lancaster test statistic has not converged to its asymptotic distribution by n = 8000. © 1989.

Title: An arbitrariness-free method of detecting structural changes
Abstract: An alternative application method of MAIC is proposed to identify the points in time of structural change. Its advantage is that it can avoid arbitrariness in two respects: that arising from choosing significance levels and that from specifying regression models. © 1989.

Title: Simple games of market manipulation
Abstract: This paper presents two simple games of market manipulation which are relevant to financial economics. © 1989.

Title: Multivariate decisions with unknown price vector
Abstract: We consider a class of decision makers who have to choose among different random bundles of commodities. It is assumed that they maximize expected utility, and their utility functions depend only on the monetary value of the bundles of commodities. Stochastic dominance conditions are provided when the price vector is assumed unknown. Risk aversion and constraints on the price vectors are considered as particular cases. The results are compared with other approaches to multivariate decisions. © 1989.

Title: Is there a conflict between authors and publishers over royalty terms?
Abstract: For typical publishing contracts involving a 'royalty rate' it has been argued that publishers prefer profit-maximisation while authors prefer sales maximisation. It is shown here that there need be no conflict where a fixed fee is negotiated in addition to a royalty rate. © 1989.

Title: Zero time preference with discounting
Abstract: For the Uzawa class of utility functionals, ∑ t=1 ∞v(c t )e- ∑ i=t ∞φ(c i ) we investigate the case of v(c t )=a(1-e-φ(c t )). The case has a zero rate of time preference and the functional attains a maximum in finite horizon problems of economic growth. The 'curvature' of the production function is crucial in determining the nature of the solution to problems in economic growth with the above optimand. © 1989.

Implementation in dynamic job transfers
Abstract: The implementation problem in a dynamic incentive contract with job transfers is studied. We find that in the job transfers contract, there are multiple equilibria, in some of which the agents can lie. We construct a mechanism to uniquely implement the principal's desired equilibrium under job transfers. © 1988.

Title: Different selling strategies in Bertrand oligopoly
Abstract: I analyse a Bertrand oligopoly game where firms can choose between selling strategies: (i) price announcements; (ii) price announcements and offers to price match. I establish the set of Nash equilibria and show that only the monopoly price Nash equilibrium satisfies iterative dominance. © 1988.

Title: A note on increasing returns to advertising
Abstract: This note shows that increasing advertising effectiveness and quantity discounts are two sources of increasing returns to advertising or entry barriers. But larger firms may not be able to carry out the threat to increase advertising to forestall entry. © 1988.

Title: Life-cycle saving and comparative advantage in the long run
Abstract: This paper reformulates Findlay's (1970) analysis by solving for life-cycle saving explicitly. The key parameters are the rate of population growth and the consumer's discount factor. It is shown that Findlay's result carries over even after the effect of population growth on the saving rate is taken into account. © 1988.

Title: Optimum tariff and its optimum revenue distribution
Authors: Winston W. Chang, Michael S. Michael
Abstract: This paper examines the problem of optimum distribution of tariff revenues and the associated optimum tariff rate. It derives the first- and second-best tariff formulas and also the conditions for the latter to reduce to the former. © 1988.

Title: Effects of social security on personal saving
Abstract: To fill a gap in literature, we formulate and estimate a simultaneous equation model to separately measure the substitution and retirement effects of social security on personal saving, taking explicit account of the influence of pension saving. © 1988.

Title: The oligopoly solution tested
Abstract: Bresnahan's econometric technique for estimating the type of pricing behavior is applied to an early antitrust case. The empirical results are plausible and suggest that it may be appropriate to use this technique in future antitrust cases. © 1988.

Title: A direction of bias result for the standard errors of a sequential least squares single equation rational expectations estimator
Abstract: A condition is established under which the direction of asymptotic bias of the standard errors of a widely used single equation rational expectations estimator can be determined. © 1988.

Title: The necessary and sufficient conditions for the uniform dominance of the two-stage stein estimators
Abstract: The paper proves the necessary and sufficient conditions for the uniform dominance in quadratic loss of the c-class two-stage Stein estimators over the Stein estimator in the linear models. © 1988.

Title: Using bivariate autoregressive representations in testing exact expectations relations
Abstract: The restrictions implied by exact expectations on the parameters of bivariate autoregressive representations can form an inconsistent set if the variables involved are filtered prior to modelling. Thus, we will reject the hypothesis with certainty when first differencing, a filter commonly applied in empirical work, is applied. A sufficient conditions for a class of filters to remain consistent with the underlying hypothesis is presented. © 1988.

Title: A test for spatial autocorrelation in seemingly unrelated regressions
Abstract: A Lagrange multiplier test is proposed for spatial autocorrelation in the error term of the equations in a seemingly unrelated regression (SUR) model. This test extends approaches developed for single equation models to the SUR context. © 1988.

Title: The effect of inflationary pressure on government expenditure
Abstract: Using a sample of 115 nations with internationally comparable data from Summers and Heston (1984) I test the hypothesis that inflation increases government expenditure share as a consequence of political pressure brought about by unsettled implicit social contracts. Using OLS regression with primarily stationary time-series the hypothesis is broadly but not universally supported for the nations in the sample. © 1988.

Title: The variability of inflation
Abstract: This note tests the variability of inflation using a new simple approach and pooled cross-country OECD data, 1960-1980. The estimated equation reported shows that the variability of inflation depends upon the variability of money supply over time. © 1988.

Title: Further turnpike properties for general capital accumulation games
Abstract: We consider a class of finite and infinite horizon discrete-time N-player capital accumulation games. Three turnpike results for the case of open-loop Nash equilibrium solutions are derived under fairly weak conditions. © 1988.

Title: Farmer education and economic efficiency
Abstract: A non-parametric production frontier approach is used to analyze the influence of education on the productivity of a sample of U.S. farms for the year 1860. This approach avoids many of the pitfalls of traditional approaches to measuring the impact of education on farmer productivity. © 1988.

Title: Working stocks and speculative stocks
Abstract: This paper presents theoretical results that are useful for determining the magnitudes of speculative stocks and working stocks held in a commodity market. It is shown that the level of working stocks is a function of the expected discounted price spread. Implications of the results for empirical work are considered. © 1988.

Title: A characterization of simple majority rule for restricted domains
Abstract: May's axioms imply majority rule even when the proof is restricted to the use of profiles in some maximal domain over which majority rule is acyclic. The case of three alternatives is considered. © 1988.

Title: Derived strengths of preference relations on coordinates
Abstract: A way is indicated to derive, from a preference relation on a Cartesian product, strength of preference relations on the coordinate sets. These strengths of preference relations are then used to reformulate several well-known properties of preference relations, and make their meaning more transparent. A new result for dynamic contexts is given. © 1988.

Title: Dualistic economic structure and money non-neutrality
Abstract: In this paper a model is outlined in which the presence of a dualistic economy and of real costs in adjusting nominal prices can give account of differences in firms' pricing behaviour and of business cycle and money non-neutrality. © 1988.

Title: Growth and equity in Sri Lanka 1963–1982
Abstract: This study measures inequality in three distinct eras of Sri Lankan development: 1956-1970 in which the mixed economy alternative predominated; the period 1970 to 1977 when the degree of State regulation peaked and a period of market liberalisation beyond 1977. Equality measures based on income data appear to be negatively correlated with the growth rate: incomes tend to equalise as growth declines. However, equality assessed from household expenditure data is declining throughout the entire sample. Both expenditure and income data associate more rapid growth with increasing inequality in the period of liberalisation. © 1988.

Title: Self-selection bias in longitudinal estimation of wage gaps
Abstract: Cross-sectional regression analyses of wage gaps may be biased by omission of unobserved worker characteristics. Recent studies therefore have used longitudinal data to 'difference out' the effects of such variables. This paper, however, shows that self-selection of job changers may cause longitudinal estimation of wage gaps to be inconsistent. © 1988.

Title: Self-employment and married women
Abstract: This paper examines the determinants of self-employment among married women. The study uses these results to assess the impact of selectivity bias, due to self-employment decisions, on the earnings of wage/salary and self-employed workers. © 1988.

Title: Devaluation and non-traded goods in a labor migration model
Abstract: In a three-sector model with labor migration, a devaluation which lowers non-traded goods prices must raise labor's expected real wage as a group, though in some sectors the real wage may fall ex post. © 1988.

Title: Insurance provision under a solvency requirement
Abstract: In a model which includes a costly-to-maintain bankruptcy constraint as justification for the standard deviation pricing principle for insurance, knowledge about heterogeneity of risks (insureds) leaves the pricing principle intact but has some effects on industry structure. © 1988.

Title: Simulating currency substitution bias
Authors: Martin Boon, Clemens Kool, Casper De Vries
Abstract: The sign and size of estimates of the elasticity of currency substitution critically depend on the definition of the oppurtunity costs of holding money. We investigate possible biases by means of Monte Carlo experiments, as sufficient real data are not available. © 1988.

Title: Exchange rate variability and wage formation in open economies
Authors: Torben M. Andersen, Jan Rose Sørensen
Abstract: Exchange rate variability is shown to influence wage formation in open economies with strong unions. Increased exchange rate variability may thus increase real- and product wages and lower employment. Hence, a stable and predictable exchange rate policy may have some gain. © 1988.

Title: Long-run limits on the US Federal debt
Abstract: This letter distinguishes three nested long-run constraints on the U.S. Federal debt, tests and rejects the strongest of the three, and illustrates how hazardous it is to base inference regarding unit roots on misspecified test regressions. © 1988.

Title: Risk aversion and stock price volatility when dividends are difference stationary
Abstract: The relationship between stock price volatility and agents' risk aversion is studied within a recursive equilibrium asset pricing model in which the endowment growth rate is assumed to follow a two-state stationary process. In contrast to a model that is stationary in the level of the endowment, the volatility of stock prices is not generally an increasing function of agents' risk aversion. The specific relationship between risk aversion and stock price volatility is shown to depend on the autorcorrelation properties of the growth rate. © 1988.

Title: Margin requirements and stock market volatility
Authors: Stephen P. Ferris, Don M. Chance
Abstract: It has long been recognized that margin requirements, through leverage, affect the volume of speculative activity. Controlling speculative behavior is one approach to inhibiting overvaluation in stocks and reducing the potential for a precipitate price decline fueled by the involuntary selling that stems, for example, from margin calls. © 1988.

Title: Information gathering and cost of living differences among searchers
Authors: Paul M. Anglin, Michael R. Baye
Abstract: This note extends recent work on cost of living index numbers for a population of individuals who face imperfect and costly information about prices. It is known that individuals with identical preferences but different incomes will require different cost of living adjustments unless preferences are homothetic. However, this result in based on a model of consumer behavior under costless information. We analyze differences in the cost of living among searchers with different incomes, and show that even if preferences are homothetic, expected cost of living indices will generally vary across searchers with different references standards of living. The reason for the differences is that, under homothetic preferences, reservation prices are a decreasing function of the searcher's standard of living. © 1988.

Title: An index of prices and taxes
Abstract: A model is formulated which, consistent with the methodology of the Spanish Consumer Price Index, evaluates and explains the incidence of personal taxes in the evolution of purchasing power implicit in each unit of gross income. © 1988.

Title: Inflationary expectations and policy preferences
Authors: Paul Webley, J.Richard Eiser, Russell Spears
Abstract: A questionnaire study demonstrated that policy preferences and economic optimism are significant predictors of short-term inflationary expectations. © 1988.

Title: Interest rates and budget deficits
Abstract: This paper examines the question of whether budget deficits raise nominal interest rates. The empirical analyses make use of cross-country data from 16 countries covering the period 1924-1938. Contrary to some recent studies (by e.g., Evans), it turns out that budget deficits affect nominal rates positively and thus the Ricardian equivalence proposition can be questioned. © 1988.

Title: State-space estimates of international business cycles
Abstract: This paper uses GNP data, spanning 1973.I-1987.I, for Canada, France, Germany, Japan, the U.K. and the U.S., and presents evidence that business cycles in these countries can be accounted for by an unobservable components model with one serially correlated international component, and serially uncorrelated domestic components. © 1988.

Title: Some international evidence on inventory fluctuations
Abstract: This paper shows some international evidence that production is more variable than sales in most developed countries but the reverse is true in most developing countries. From international perspectives, cost shocks do not appear to be the predominant source of fluctuations in inventories, contrary to the widely accepted evidence in the postwar United States Demand shocks and serial correlations in demand, on the other hand, appear to be of roughly equal importance for inventory fluctuations. © 1988.

Title: The unique perfect equilibrium of an n-person bargaining game
Abstract: We analyze an n-person bargaining game, and show that there exists a unique perfect equilibrium outcome. © 1988.

Title: Betting bias in ‘exotic’ bets
Abstract: The evidence from racetrack betting is that the subjective probabilities to win expressed through the public's bets are good approximations to the objective probabilities on the whole, but that a betting bias exists in that favorites are underbet and long-shots overbet. We examine these questions for exactas and trifectas which the aid of a new database. The approximation of subjective to objective probabilities is good for exactas and no betting bias is evident. For trifectas the findings are more ambiguous and suggest that a taste for long-shots or a misperception of true probabilities may play a role. © 1988.

Title: The sensitivity of consumer search to wages
Abstract: While intuition suggests that an increase in wages should increase the time cost of consumer search for low prices, this note shows that under reasonable conditions, the resulting increase in consumption actually increases search intensity. © 1988.

Title: Complete irreflexive preferences
Can event studies detect anticompetitive mergers?
Abstract: Using standard event study methodology, we examine a challenged horizontal merger known ex post to be anticompetitive. The event study shows no evidence that the merger was anticompetitive. This result casts doubt on the ability of event studies to detect anticompetitive mergers. © 1988.

Title: The divergence of SIC industries from antitrust markets
Abstract: Evidence from price fixing cases is used to demonstrate that SIC four-digit industries often are far broader in product and/or geographic scope than antitrust markets and that the divergence between the two is greater than suggested in the literature. © 1988.

Title: Public sector expansion in a mixed open economy with a real wage restriction
Abstract: The effects on the private sectors of a public sector expansion in an open economy with real wage rigidities are shown to depend upon substitutability in consumption between private and government goods, and on the marginal productivity of government labor. © 1988.

Title: Explaining pay-as-you-go financed public pension systems
Abstract: The existence of pay-as-you-go (PAYG) financed public pension plans is usually explained by median-voter models or by strategic non-saving behavior by young generations. Here it is claimed that both types of models are neither sufficient nor necessary for explaining PAYG-systems. © 1988.

Title: On interest rate innovations and anticipated monetary policy
Abstract: In this note I investigate whether anticipated money matters by following McCallum's (1983) suggestion that nominal interest rates be included in a VAR system estimated on data spanned by a policy of interest rate targeting. The evidence is in favour of Gordon's (1982) 'natural rate hypothesis - gradual price adjustent' model of policy ineffectiveness. Ambler and Phaneuf (1988) have shown the results can be interpreted as evidence in favour of contract-based models of the business cycle. © 1988.

Title: The technical efficiency of US banks
Authors: Nanda Rangan, Richard Grabowski, Hassan Y. Aly, Carl Pasurka
Abstract: The paper uses a non-parametric frontier approach to measure the technical efficiency of a sample of U.S. banks. The results indicate that these banks could have produced the same level of output with only 70% of the inputs actually used. In addition, most of this inefficiency is due to pure technical inefficiency (wasting inputs) rather than scale inefficiency (operating at non-constant returns to scale). Finally, regression analysis indicates that the technical efficiency of the banks is positively related to size, negatively related to product diversity, and not at all related to the extent to which branch banking is allowed. © 1988.

Title: A simple rule for managing the maturity structure of government debt
The incompatibility of valued money and equilibrium policy
Abstract: In an overlapping generations economy, an equilibrium is defined such that at each date, the young agent determines values for that period's monetary and fiscal instruments. A proposition showing money cannot have value in any such equilibrium is proved. © 1988.

Title: Optimal levels of significance of a pre-test in estimating the disturbance variance after the pre-test for a linear hypothesis on coefficients in a linear regression
Abstract: In this note, we compare sampling properties of a pre-test estimator of the disturbance variance in a linear regression after a pre-test for a linear hypothesis on coefficients with those of an improved estimator of the variance proposed by Stein (1964). It is shown that the pre-test estimator with an optimal level of the pre-test is in fact the improved estimator proposed by Stein (1964). © 1988.

Title: The estimation of allocation models with autocorrelated disturbances
Abstract: The estimation of singular allocation models, with errors which are spatially autocorrelated or exhibit a serially correlated component, is considered. The restrictions implied for the error process parameters are identical to those for autoregressive or moving average errors. © 1988.

Title: Inflation and relative-price variability
Abstract: The effect of temporal aggregation on the relation between inflation and variability of relative-price changes in the United States is studied by using monthly consumer price index (CPI) data as well as quarterly observations derived by averaging the monthly series. Estimates from monthly and quarterly data show major differences for the periods 1973-1986 and 1980-1986. © 1988.

Title: Productivity and growth
Authors: M.M.G. Fase, P.J. Van Den Heuvel
Abstract: This paper presents causality tests on manufacturing output and labour productivity to examine the so-called Verdoorn law. The conclusion is that a modified Granger test supports Verdoorn's law. © 1988.

Title: Bargaining and strategic search
Abstract: This paper specifies an alternative type of switching friction, in a model of sequential bargaining, to that suggested by Shaked and Sutton (1984). An imperfect and costly search technology gives the current 'insider' a bargaining advantage over alternative partners for the firm. Where all potential partnerships generate the same rent, search has a purely strategic value. © 1988.

Title: An application of cremer's planning procedure to the optimal commodity taxation problem
Abstract: Using a computational technique developed by Cremer, we present a decentralized procedure which determines optimal commodity taxes iteratively, under minimal information requirements. This analysis extends the class of non-convex optimization problems to which Cremer's procedure is applicable. © 1988.

Title: Strategic renegotiation
Abstract: We provide a deterministic example in which parties sign a contract which they anticipate will be subsequently renegotiated. The renegotiation is socially desirable. In the example, the cost of writing and enforcing contracts increases their complexity. © 1988.

Title: On multiplicity of consistent conjectures in free entry oligopoly
Abstract: If we allow free entry into oligopoly, we should take into account the fact that the number of firms is variable. Therefore, we should include it in the arguments of the conjectural variation functions, and consider a conjectural variation for the change in the number of firms. We will show that for such conjectural variation functions, there exist multiple consistent conjectures equilibria in free entry oligopoly. © 1988.

Title: Tied-in credit with a monopoly product market
Abstract: We show that when the consumer is credit-constrained at the opportunity cost of funds faced by the producer, then a monopolist may gain by offering a contract which offers both credit and goods. © 1988.

Title: Generating conditional expectations from models with selectivity bias
Abstract: This paper discusses how conditional expectations should be generated from models with sample selectivity. We argue that the conventional method ignores relevant and available information and produces unreliable results. An alternative approach is suggested and the empirical example of black/white wage differentials is presented. © 1988.

Title: Divergent trends in the discouragement of adult men, adult women, and teenagers: 1970–1986
Abstract: Discouragement is found to mainly vary with group long-term unemployment and to be negatively related to the minimum wage. Discouragement of adult men (women) was found to have increased (decreased) by 2.2% (1.6%) per year relative to their labor force. © 1988.

Title: A note on the modelling of circular smallholder migration
Abstract: It is argued that circular migration should be seen as an optimization problem, where the household allocates its labour resources across activities, including work which requires migration, so as to maximize the joint family utility function. The migration problem is illustrated in a simple diagram, which makes it possible to analyse economic aspects of migration. © 1988.

Title: A new approach to modelling the effects of incomes policies
Authors: Philip E.T. Lewis, Michael G. Kirby
Abstract: In this paper an exciting alternative to the traditional Phillips curve approach to analyzing the impacts of incomes policies is presented. This provides a method of estimating directly the effects of policies on real wages and employment. The model is applied to Australia, a country which currently has an incomes policy as the cornerstone of its macroeconomic strategy. © 1988.

Title: Risk-taking by firms near bankruptcy
Abstract: Using the Rothschild-Stiglitz notion of mean-preserving spreads, I show here that, when 'me-first' rules are not enforced, increases in risk can make bankruptcy less likely. © 1988.

Title: Rational expectations in second moments, the J-curve, and the Harrod effect
Abstract: The plausibility of the Harrod effect under a flexible exchange rate regime is examined using the model in Black (1985), opportunely modified to include J-curve effects. It is shown that at least in one of the two polar cases considered the existence of the Harrod effect is confirmed. © 1988.

Title: On the accuracy of the mean-variance approximation for futures markets
Abstract: Simple approximate fomulae for the volume and gains from futures trading are derived using the mean-variance model. The errors involved are exactly quantified and shown to be negligible for the futures price and welfare gains, though potentially larger for volumes. © 1988.

Title: Increasing the likelihood value by adding constraints
Abstract: The difference between infinite precision mathematics with which theorems are proven and finite precision mathematics with which computations are performed is often ignored. Taking this difference into account one can demonstrate that adding constraints can improve the computed maximum. © 1988.

Title: Stability analysis by means of modern linear systems theory
Abstract: By means of modern tools from linear systems theory we give a new procedure to calculate all stable solutions of a set of homogeneous difference equations. We apply our procedure to a small model analyzed by Anderson and Moore (1985). © 1988.

Title: Statistical model selection criteria
