Abstract: Within the context of conventional model selection criteria and a normal linear statistical model, questions are pursued which relate to (i) the statistical implications of using model selection criteria in the pure noise case, (ii) the asymptotic properties of alternative variable selection procedures and (iii) an abbreviated computational solution. © 1988.

Title: An agency theoretic explanation of capital flight
Abstract: Overvalued exchange rates, high and variable interest rates and over expansionary fiscal policies are known to encourage capital flight. Capital flight can also result from an agency problem between the population and the political leaders. The agent borrows more funds abroad than can be profitably invested in the domestic economy and appropriates some of the funds. Low rates of return in the domestic economy encourage the capital flight. © 1988.

Title: Multidimensional auctions
Abstract: If the selling agency's preferences are known, the multidimensional procurement problem can be mapped back into the familiar one-dimensional private-value auction model, obviating the need for a new theory. © 1988.

Title: Payoffs in generalized sequential bargaining games
Abstract: The main result of this note is that the set of payoffs supported by subgame perfect equilibrium in an n-person generalized sequential bargaining game is a convex set in Rn. This observation stems from the fact that in many game trees subgame perfect equilibria yields a conservative stable standard of behavior for the tree situation, thereby providing a new characterization of the set of subgame perfect equilibrium paths. © 1988.

Title: Nash solution and timing of bargaining
Abstract: We analyze bargaining problems with unknown feasible sets and known disagreement points. Two characterizations of the Nash solution are presented by formulating axioms specifying how bargaining solutions should respond under such circumstances. © 1988.

Title: Heterogeneous distribution of information and convergence to rational expectations equilibrium in a partial equilibrium model
Abstract: In models of convergence to rational expectations equilibrium it is usually assumed that information is (initially) concentrated upon a group of agents. We argue that this assumption is relevant for convergence results, and we show that when it is removed convergence may disappear. © 1988.

Title: Ioffe's normal cone and the foundations of welfare economics
Abstract: We announce an example of an economy with an infinite dimensional commodity space for which the extension of the second fundamental theorem of welfare economics is valid if marginal rates of substitution are formalized in terms of either the Clarke normal cone or the Ioffe normal cone but in which the former is strictly contained in the latter. This is in direct contradiction to the finite dimensional situation. © 1988.

Title: Inside money and real output
Abstract: An example shows that anticipated, non-neutral, monetary policy disturbances can result in correlation between real output and lagged inside money that is observationally equivalent to the 'real business cycle' interpretation. © 1988.

Title: Memory and market stability
Abstract: When optimizing agents use their memories in a non-linear cobweb model, it will be asymptotically stable: instability and chaos cannot occur. This contrasts with the results when agents are forgetful. However, short run fluctuations are erratic and sensitive to initial conditions. © 1988.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
A reformulation of the Harris-Todaro mechanism with endogenous wages
Abstract: Wages in the modern sector are set by firms to deter shirking, while urban unemployment is a process of waiting for modern sector jobs. Rural urban migration equalizes rural incomes to the expected incomes of those in the urban unemployment pool. © 1988.

Title: Firm behavior in the rate design phase of the regulatory process
Abstract: If the revenue requirement is established using historical data, a public utility still has the flexibility to maximize future profits by proposing rate changes and counting on quantity responses. The results of such behavior differ from those of Ramsey pricing. © 1988.

Title: Economic surprises and the behaviour of asset prices
Authors: David A. Peel, Peter F. Pope
Abstract: This paper examines the implications of serial correlation in asset prices for market efficiency and announcement effect tests. The impact of four types of economic surprise is examined after allowing for observed serial correlation in three asset price series. © 1988.

Title: Does conditional covariance or conditional variance explain time varying risk premia in foreign exchange returns?
Abstract: This paper questions the economic underpinning and the empirical findings of single equation ARCH-M models. It demonstrates that it is conditional covariance and not conditional variance that explains the time varying risk premia in foreign exchange returns. © 1988.

Title: The long-run effects of income taxation under endogenous technical progress
Abstract: This study examines the long-run effects of income taxation by using a perfect-foresight optimizing model. Unlike the existing literature, we assume that technical progress is endogenously evolved. Under this assumption, income taxation will affect not only capital accumulation but also inventive activity of private agents. We demonstrate that a rise in income tax could increase the level of income in the long run. © 1988.

Title: New tests of the theory of optimal seigniorage
Abstract: This paper tests the implication of the theory of optimal seigniorage that over time higher tax rates are associated with higher inflation rates and higher nominal interest rates. In particular, the study investigates whether knowledge of past tax rates improves the prediction of future nominal interest rates (or inflation) beyond predictions that are based on past nominal interest rates (or inflation) alone. This is the empirical definition of Granger causality. © 1988.

Title: Velocity and the variability of money growth
Abstract: Using data from four countries, the paper tests Friedman's hypothesis that the volatility of money growth causes velocity to change. Despite a wide variety of patterns in the movements of velocity in these countries, support is evident for the hypothesis. © 1988.

Title: A transformation for heteroscedastic error components regression models
Abstract: An observation-by-observation data transformation is derived for heteroscedastic error components regression models. The transformation permits generalized least squares (GLS) or feasible GLS estimates to be obtained from an ordinary least squares program. © 1988.

Title: Tests of non-nested linear regression models subject to linear restrictions
Abstract: The standard methods for testing between non-nested or separate regression models require that the models have the same dependent variable. If the models are subject to non-homogeneous linear restrictions, substituting out these restrictions results in a redefinition of the dependent variable before estimation and the standard results will not apply. We derive a Wald-type test statistic to cater for this situation. © 1988.

Title: On the inadequacy of sufficient conditions under ‘limited information’ identification
Abstract: It is shown that the sufficiency conditions of Hausman and Taylor are misleading since their conditions, under 'limited information' could show an equation identified when, actually (under full information) it is not. © 1988.

Title: On the rationality of the Michigan monthly survey of inflationary expectations
Abstract: Based on Pearce's (1979) definition of rationality, it is shown in that the Michigan monthly survey of inflationary expectations are rational. © 1988.

Title: Are productivity fluctuations due to real supply shocks?
Abstract: Shapiro (1987) draws support for real business cycle theories from the behavior of cost-based and output-based measures of productivity. This evidence is examined and shown to rely on spurious correlations. © 1988.

Title: Comparative risk aversion
Abstract: Even when some risk prospects have no certain equivalents, increases in risk aversion are equivalent to concave transformations of the utility function. Strict or sharp increases in risk aversion correspond to concave and non-linear or strictly concave transformations, respectively. © 1988.

Title: A re-examination of Harrison's experimental test for risk aversion
Authors: Edward L. Millner, Michael D. Pratt, Robert J. Reilly
Abstract: This paper examines several aspects of Harrison's (1986) test for the risk attitudes of experimental subjects. We identify specific refinements to Harrison's test that must be adopted in order to establish correctly a subject's risk posture. © 1988.

Title: Probability calculations for transitivity of the simple majority rule
Abstract: Let P(n,k) denote the probability that n voters who are engaged in pairwise voting by simple majority rule on k candidates will have a complete set of pairwise voting comparisons that are transitive. Values of P(n,k) are computed under the condition of impartial culture for values of n and k that are well beyond those for which P(n,k) values have been previously computed. P(n,k) values are obtained by computer enumeration for n equals three, by Monte Carlo integration for n→∞, and by direct computations from a new representation for P(n,4). © 1988.

Title: Price fluctuations when only prices reveal information
Abstract: This paper provides a qualitative explanation for the observation that prices in financial markets fluctuate even in periods in which no agents receive any new information. This phenonmenon is explained in the framework of an equilibrium of prices, plans and price expectation in the style of Radner (1972) in the case of asymmetric information. © 1988.

Title: Testing the relevance of job search for job mobility
Authors: Joop Hartog, Eddie Mekkelholt, Hans Van Ophem
Abstract: Statistical tests for differences in the mobility (and the search) behavior of male and female, searching and not searching individuals indicate that there indeed exist differences, particularly with respect to whether the individual is searching or not. © 1988.

Title: Price vs. quantity competition in oligopoly supergames
Abstract: In a repeated oligopoly with differentiated products and firms following trigger strategies, quantity competition leads to a less efficient outcome than price competition. This result contrasts with the repeated duopoly result, where price competition is less efficient under certain conditions. © 1988.

Title: Quality competition and threat of entry in duopoly
Abstract: Threat of entry, sequential entry and cost of production are taken into account in a duopoly game in quality within the vertical product differentiation framework. A multi-stage perfect equilibrium solution is shown to exist and is fully characterized. © 1988.

Title: Interest rate determination in a small open economy
Abstract: This paper is an attempt to explain the behavior of ex-ante real rates of interest in Singapore during the period 1961-1981. This is done within a model which explicitly allows for the role of supply shocks, inflation uncertainty, and foreign interest rates. © 1988.

Title: Optimal export subsidies and marginal cost differentials
Abstract: This paper examines the relationship between the difference in optimal subsidies and that in marginal costs for different exporting countries. It shows that this relationship crucially depends upon the concavity of the market demand curve. This result provides policy-makers with useful information when implementing trade policies. © 1988.

Title: Partial revenue seeking and welfare
Abstract: In this note, a resource-using revenue seeking is introduced into the standard H-O-S model. We suppose that part (or all) of the revenue is competitively sought and the remainder is handled as a lump-sum transfer. We discuss the welfare implication of a small country when the ratio of the revenue which is competitively sought to the total revenue changes. © 1988.

Title: Marshallian stability, long-run equilibrium and the pattern of specialization under factor-market distortions in the pure theory of international trade
Abstract: Using a simple general-equilibrium, small open economy model, we show that the principal comparative statics paradoxes under factor-market distortions disappear if the equilibrium is Marshallian stable, and that the latter holds if it is a stable long-run equilibrium under capital adjustment. © 1988.

Title: Scale economies, perverse comparative statics results, the Marshallian stability and the long-run equilibrium for a small open economy
Abstract: Using a simple general-equilibrium model, we show that the perverse comparative statics results can occur under scale economies. These paradoxes disappear iff the equilibrium is Marshallian stable, and the latter holds iff it is a stable long-run equilibrium under capital adjustment. © 1988.

Title: On exact small sample properties of ordinary ridge estimators
Abstract: In this paper, we examine the exact small sample properties of the ordinary ridge estimator and the bias-corrected ordinary ridge estimator. © 1988.

Title: A simple model for heterogeneity in binary logit models
Abstract: This paper introduces unobserved heterogeneity in the binary logit model by adding a uniformly distributed disturbance term which enters the model additively with the observed regressor variables. The model is analytically simple and is observationally very similar to the more complicated model which assumes a normally distributed heterogeneity term. © 1988.

Title: Variability of inflation and the dispersion of relative prices
Authors: Munir Quddus, Jin-Tan Liu, J.S. Butler
Abstract: This paper uses data from the Chinese hyperinflation of 1946-1949 to focus on the relationship between the variability in the general price level and the dispersion in relative prices. The issue is important because it bears on the 'natural rate hypothesis' which supports the postulate that these two monetary variables are independent. Our results reinforce the bulk of previous evidence which suggests a positive correlation between the variation in inflation rate and the dispersion in relative prices during inflationary episodes. © 1988.

Title: Political business cycles in the parliamentary system
Abstract: In the parliamentary system, the cabinet may call a general election before the term of the House members matures, if the timing is judged favorable. Econometric tests to differentiate the following two hypotheses are proposed and applied to the Japanese data. Under the manipulative cabinet hypothesis, the cabinet decides the timing of the election by political reasons and manipulates an economy to have a boom in time, i.e., elections cause booms, similar to the presidential system; while the opportunistic cabinet hypothesis states that the cabinet does not manipulate the economy, but calls an election, when positive private-sector shocks cause high growth and low inflation, i.e., booms trigger elections. Findings indicate that the Japanese cabinet has acted opportunistically rather that manipulatively. © 1988.

Title: Dynamic specification and the demand for money function
Abstract: This paper investigates the existence of a stable demand for money function in three Asian countries using the error correction methodology proposed by Hendry et al. (1984). Particular attention is paid to the role of both financial and real assets as substitutes for real cash balances. © 1988.

Title: Precautionary saving and risk aversion
Authors: Uzi Segal, Avia Spivak, Joseph Zeira
Abstract: Yaari (1987) proved that within the anticipated utility framework, a risk averse decision maker will have precautionary saving regardless of the sign of the third derivative of his utility function. In this note we extend (a modification of) this result for an n-period model. © 1988.

Title: Information dependent games
Abstract: This paper attempts to study the consistency of several basic game-theoretic axioms. Two by-products are the introduction of information-dependent games, and a formal treatment of the framework of game theoretic axioms. In this setup a version of the Surprise Test Paradox is used to prove that common sense cannot be common knowledge. © 1988.

Title: Communication, coordination and Nash equilibrium
Abstract: I note a methodological problem in studying the role of pre-play communication in ensuring equilibrium. To deal with this problem, I define a solution concept for the extended game (in which talk is followed by play) that is intermediate between Nash equilibrium and rationalizability. In some games our solution concept implies a Nash outcome, while in others it does not. © 1988.

Title: Asymmetric equilibria in symmetric games with many players
Abstract: We show that in symmetric games with many players, an asymmetric pure-strategy equilibrium can be thought of as the approximate outcome of the play of a specific symmetric mixed-strategy equilibrium. © 1988.

Title: Measuring the size of revisions of regional data
Abstract: A measure from statistical information theory is proposed for the size of revisions of regional data. © 1988.

Title: Distance functions and the comparison of development levels
Abstract: Three distance functions are used to measure the distance between income distributions as well as that between distributions of ages at death. These distances may be used for the comparison of development levels as shown in an illustration based on cross section data. © 1988.

Title: The union wage profile of women: Potential vs. actual experience
Abstract: Previous research suggests that unions attempt to enforce standard wage rates for production workers. Yet, studies confirming a flatter union experience profile use measures of potential, rather than actual, experience. This creates a distinct possibility of measurement error. This study confirms such error and demonstrates it to beparticularly acute for female workers. © 1988.

Title: The trade union wage gap in Britain: Some new estimates
Abstract: New estimates of the union/non-union wage gap in Britain, derived from household data, are reported. The results, about 12% for manual and about 4% for non-manual workers, expand upon the tentative conclusions of the few earlier similar British studies. © 1988.

Title: On the separable industry performance evaluation function
Abstract: It has been suggested in the literature that an industry performance evaluation function, which is used for ranking alternative output distributions, can be expressed as a trading-off of the total output and a 'numbers equivalent', an inverse index of industrial concentration. It is shown that if this evaluation function is to be strongly separable, then the numbers equivalents become a subclass of the Hannah-Kay family of numbers equivalents. When the performance of the industry is determined by the volume of output produced, the numbers equivalent becomes the Shannon entropy numbers equivalent. © 1988.

Title: Determinants of the spread in a two-tier foreign exchange market
Abstract: The determinants of the spread between the commercial and financial exchange rates are analyzed in a two-tier exchange market model derived from utility maximization. Contrary to popular belief, it is found that domestic policy and non-policy variables have no effect on the spread; only foreign factors matter. © 1988.

Title: A note on optimal commodity taxation in India
Abstract: Optimal commodity tax rates are calculated and their redistributive impact is studied in the Indian context using a new PIGLOG demand system introduced in Coondoo and Majumder (1987). The results are compared with those obtained by Ray (1986) on the same data using LES and RNLPS. © 1988.

Title: The impact of tax reform on investment and saving incentives in Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Japan
Authors: Michael J. Daly, Pierre Mercier, Thomas Schweitzer
Abstract: This paper summarizes the impact of tax reform on investment and saving incentives in Canada using marginal effective tax rates, and compares these incentives with those provided by the tax systems of the United States, the United Kingdom, and Japan. © 1988.

Title: Money announcements and the risk premium
Abstract: The risk premium hypothesis is tested within the weekly M1 announcement framework. Although ARCH processes were detected, the ARCH-M modelling technique revealed no traces of a time varying risk premium. © 1988.

Title: A theorem regarding elasticities of the transactions demand for money
Abstract: This paper considers the class of inventory-theoretic transactions demand for money models and proves the following theorem: the sum of the income elasticity of money demand plus the absolute value of the interest elasticity is equal to unity. This result is often ignored in empirical simulation studies and Bayesian estimation. © 1988.

Title: A non-linear model of interdependent consumer behaviour
Abstract: Interdependent consumer behaviour in R2 is studied in this paper. While for various parameter constellations the Feigenbaum scenario, well-known from R1 is observed, there are quite remarkable reversals of a bifurcation for other values of the system's parameters. © 1988.

Title: Autoregressive conditional heteroscedasticity: A comparison of ARCH and random coefficient models
Abstract: In this paper it is shown that the popular Autoregressive Conditional Heteroscedasticity (ARCH) models are closely related to more traditional random coefficient models. It is demonstrated that for every ARCH model a simple random coefficient model can be formulated which implies exactly the same conditional variance pattern for the variable of interest. © 1988.

Title: Critical bounds for MA(2) and MA(3) processes
Authors: J.A. Lane, P.R. Ceuppens, D.A. Peel
Abstract: The purpose in this note is to investigate the critical bounds on the significance points for testing hypotheses using the t-values based on ordinary least squares computations when the true disturbances aregenerated by MA(2) and MA(3) errors. © 1988.

Title: Relation between inflation and relative-price variability in the United States: Evidence from data for the 1980s
Abstract: Monthly CPI data for 1967-1986 in respect of 10 major categories are utilized. The most significant result is a strongly negative association between relative-price variability and inflation as well as its expected and unexpected components during the 1980s. Variations in the estimated coefficients for the three subperiods studied also seem interesting. © 1988.

Title: Uniqueness of nash equilibrium points in bimatrix games
Abstract: This note is concerned with techniques for constructing bimatrix games with predetermined unique Nash equilibrium points. The result obtained here extend the constructions presented by Heuer (1979) and Quintas. © 1988.

Title: A new parametric test for the structure of risk preferences
Abstract: A moment-based test of constant relative and partial relative risk aversion as defined in Pratt and Menezes and Hanson (1970) is proposed. The test is very general in the sense that it does not hinge on a single random variable nor on the linear asset model. The test is for a particular specification of 'almost homogeneity'. © 1988.

Title: Consistent conjectures equilibria: A reformulation showing non-uniqueness
Authors: Paul D. Klemperer, Margaret A. Meyer
Abstract: We interpret both Bresnahan's original (1981) definition of consistent conjectures equilibria and his generalized (1983) definition as dominant strategy equilibria in reaction functions. We employ a simple constructive argument to show that every outcome satisfies the generalized definition. © 1988.

Title: Natural team sharing and team productivity
Abstract: We show that when effort levels are observable, natural team sharing where one's proportional share in total output equals one's proportional share in total input, sustains a first-best production level only for a function unique up to a constant of proportionality. © 1988.

Title: Consumption, leisure and earnings-related liquidity constraints
Authors: Rob Alessie, Bertrand Melenberg, Guglielmo Weber
Abstract: The life-cycle model with liquidity constraints produces a Euler equation with unobservable Kuhn-Tucker multipliers. If borrowing restrictions depend on earnings, preferences are non-separable between goods and leisure, and individuals are employed, we derive a Euler equation involving only observable variables. © 1988.

Title: The earnings function under test
Abstract: Earnings functions of the well-known Mincer type based on data from five samples of German male full-time workers are estimated and tested. The hypotheses of normally distributed, homoscedastic errors, and a correctly specified functional form are nearly always rejected. © 1988.

Title: The effect of taxation on labor supply when on-the-job amenities are endogenous
Abstract: In a labor supply model where on-the-job amenities are endogenous, the tax on earnings affects both the net price of leisure and the net price of amenities. Contrary to the traditional model of labor supply, the compensated tax effect on desired work hours in this case is not necessarily negative. © 1988.

Title: Market value and patents
Abstract: This paper finds a large, positive and statistically significant effect op patent statistics on firm market values. Furthermore, these effects are robust to a variety of alternate specifications of our underlying model. We conclude that patent data provide economically meaningful information on the scope and relative effectiveness of a firm's R&D program. © 1988.

Title: The impact of market share, tariffs and quotas on the performance of international cartels
Abstract: We consider an international 'dominant-group' cartel consisting of a subset of k 'domestic' firms and a subset of t 'foreign' firms. We analyse the impact of changes in the relative sizes of k and t, and of tariffs and quotas, on the performance of the domestic firms, measured in terms of profits and price-cost margins. © 1988.

Title: A non-parametric test of a first-order Markov process for regimes in a non-cooperatively collusive industry
Abstract: Models of collusion under incertainty imply that an industry switches between high and low profit regimes. We find evidence in favor of this theory's prediction that regime switches follow a first-order Markov process. © 1988.

Title: The black market for foreign exchange
Abstract: The Dornbusch et al. (1983) model for the determination of the black market foreign exchange premium is modified and then estimated for 19 countries for various periods during 1970-1979 in which we identified the existence of a black market for foreign exchange. The outstanding result is the almost total uniformity of the estimated coefficients of the explanatory variable, expected profits from black market transactions, and the small spread of the elasticities of the black market premium with respect to the expected profits and the real official exchange rate. © 1988.

Title: The measurement of export instability
Abstract: A general theory of the instability index is developed using spectral analysis. Depending on the assumptions pertaining to aversion towards fluctuations of different frequencies, the generalized instability index derived here can be reduced to some commonly used instability indices. © 1988.

Title: The non-optimality of the over-the-counter options dividend protection
Abstract: Although no such adjustments are made in exchange listed options, options in the over-the-counter (OTC) market are adjusted for cash dividends by reducing their striking prices by the amount of the cash dividend on each ex-dividend date. We prove that if a call is either out-, at- or in-the-money (just before the ex-dividend dates), the OTC-dividend-protection procedure generates a sure loss to the call buyer, but it tends to be correct if a call is very-deep-in-the-money. © 1988.

Title: Estimation of error variance in linear regression models with errors having multivariate student-t distribution with unknown degrees of freedom
Abstract: Linear regression model y=Xβ+μ, where the components of the disturbance vector u have jointly multivariate Student -t distribution with unknown degrees of freedom, is considered. An estimator of the degrees of freedom parameter is provided. This estimator is used to provide estimates, computable from the data, of the usual unbiased and minimum mean square error estimators of the error variance and of their variances, which are, otherwise, not computable from the data. © 1988.

Title: Invariance of expected utilities in logit models
Abstract: An unnoticed and restrictive property of the logit model is proved: the expected utility (or expected utility change) conditional on having selected an alternative i is invariant over all alternatives in the choice set. This limits the use of logit in situations where expected utilities should realisticly vary by choice made. The probit model is not subject to this restriction. © 1988.

Title: Price inflation and wage inflation
Abstract: The question of whether or not price inflation is endogenous with respect to wage inflation has long been a source of theoritical contention between the neoclassicists and post-Keynesians. This paper applies a formal test of causality to examine this price-wage inflation relationship. The findings suggest a unidirectional causation from prices to wages, if the percentage annual rate of change of hourly wages of production workers is taken as a measure of wage inflation; and a feedback relationship (partially implied), if the wage inflation is measured by the percentage rate of change of average annual earnings of manufacturing employees. © 1988.

Title: Are saving and investment co-integrated?
Abstract: The observation of a strong positive correlation between national saving and domestic investment rates calls into question the assumption of highly-mobile international capital. I re-examine the question of a high correlation by considering the time-series relationship between national saving and domestic investment rates in the U.S., using newly-developed co-integration techniques. National saving and domestic investment appear to be co-integrated prior to 1971 but appear not to be co-integrated after 1971. © 1988.

Title: Rothschild-Stiglitz competitive insurance market under quasilinear preferences
Abstract: In a heterogeneous agents economy under quasilinear preferences, if preferences are unidirectional, the pooling equilibrium may exist. If so, it is Pareto optimal; if not, the separating equilibrium (which is Pareto optimal) may or may not exist depending on preferences. If the preferences are multidirectional, the pooling equilibrium always exist and is Pareto optimal. © 1988.

Title: Dynamics sales discriminate against uninformed consumers in a competitive market
Abstract: A dynamic version of the Salop and Stiglitz (1977) model of price dispersion is presented whose unique perfect equilibrium is a continuous function of the number of uninformed consumers in the market. In the limit as the number of uninformed consumers approaches zero, the equilibrium approaches the perfectly competitive one. © 1988.

Title: A characterization of employment distortions in labor contracts with asymmetric information
Abstract: Employment distortions are characterized for different combinations of firm's risk aversion and the degree of normality of leisure in worker's preferences. Using a novel method all previously established results are derived and the previously unresolved cases are worked out. © 1988.

Title: The stability of Canadian macroeconomic data as measured by the largest Lyapunov exponent
Abstract: We examine the stability of certain Canadian macroeconomic series by looking at an algorithm due to Kurths and Herzel (1987), designed to calculate a lower bound to the largest Lyapunov exponent in a computationally easy way. © 1988.

Title: A limit theorem on the core
Abstract: The classical theorem of Debreu and Scarf (1963) on the relation of the core of an economy to its competitive equilibrium does not depend on an assumption that the preferences of consumers are convex, much less that they are strictly convex. © 1988.

Title: A note on an optimal garnishing rule
Abstract: A low information, optimal bankruptcy rule is described and analyzed for an exchange economy with credit. © 1988.

Title: Note on equilibria without ordered preferences in topological vector spaces
Abstract: This note contains an equilibrium existence result with a commodity space which can be any topological vector space. Agents' preferences need not be ordered. © 1988.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Families, migration and adjusting to disequilibrium
Authors: Gail M. Shields, Michael P. Shields
Abstract: Unlike the case for individual migration, education may reduce the migration of families by enhancing their ability to adjust to local disequilibrium and stay at their preferred location. Estimates of family migration probabilities in Costa Rica support this hypothesis. © 1988.

Title: Product differentiation, oligopolistic interdependence, market share, and profits
Abstract: This paper attempts to infer the nature of the empirically observed positive relationship between market share and profits. Assuming constant returns to scale, the analysis reveals that profits should only be positively related to market share in those industries in which there is rivalrous interaction among the firms. © 1988.

Title: The impact of buyers' expectations on entry deterrence
Abstract: A model of entry deterrence is presented in which consumers are perfectly informed about an incumbent monopolist's product quality but are imperfectly informed about the qualities of potential entrants. To deter entry, the monopolist chooses a higher price and quality than he would in the absence of an entry threat. © 1988.

Title: Stationarity and outliers in annual accounting earnings
Abstract: The purpose of this study is to apply a unit root test to examine the stationarity of corporate earnings per share (eps) series. We find evidence to support the stationarity of corporate eps data. Furthermore, outlier analysis is employed and supports the long-run stability of corporate earnings series. © 1988.

Title: Rational expectations as long-run equilibria: Tests for Indian securities
Abstract: It is recommended that the standard 'bias test' for Muth-rational expectations should be augmented in the form of a dynamic model. Amongst other advantages, this approach permits the researcher to test unbiasedness as a long-run equilibrium of the underlying dynamic adjustment process relating expectations to realizations. The approach is applied to a new data set on traders' expectations in the Madras stock exchange. Although bias is generally found in the short-run, the long-run equilibrium is consistent with rational expectations in about half the cases studied. Significant steady-state biases are indicated for the remainder. © 1988.

Title: Does social cost-benefit analysis measure overall utility change?
Abstract: Social cost-benefit analysis generally ignores the changes induced in markets which interact with a project, on grounds that the changes are small. A simulation model of interaction shows that this is not generally so; when distortion, maldistribution and factor inertia exist, cost-benefit analysis will normally produce a seriously incorrect evaluation of the overall utility change resulting from a project. © 1988.

Title: Settlement system and the day-of-the-week effect
Abstract: In this paper, I empirically show that a settlement system matters importantly in determining the day-of-the-week effect of stock returns. © 1988.

Title: A note on global asymptotic stability of non-linear difference equations
Abstract: This paper introduces a generalization of the global asymptotic stability theorem of Brock and Scheinkman (1975). We shall also verify that in the case of linear first order difference equations with constant coefficients our sufficient conditions coincide with the well known necessary and sufficient condition that all eigenvalues of the matrix of coefficients are inside the unit circle. © 1988.

Title: Generalised portmanteau statistics and tests of randomness: A note on their applications to residuals from a fitted ARMA model
Abstract: This note examines what effects parameter estimates in a simple AR(1) model have on the relative performances of the Dufour-Roy (1986) and Ljung-Box (1978) statistics. The power tests indicate that there is no major gain by using the Dufour-Roy statistics as tests of model adequacy if the underlying model is a general ARMA (p,q) model. © 1988.

Title: An example of correlation among residuals in directly ordered data
Authors: Marc J.I. Gaudry, Ulrich C.H. Blum
Abstract: We distinguish between naturally ordered data and data that are ordered directly by the researcher. After ordering observations according to a behavioral criterion, we estimate a single-order correlation parameter of the residuals simultaneously with the other parameters and the functional form of a savings equation for higher-income white-collar German households. © 1988.

Title: Hopf bifurcations in multisector models of optimal economic growth
Abstract: This paper is to re-examine problems of limit cycles in the standard optimal growth model with two or more capital goods. We improve the results of study by Benhabib and Nishimura (1979). It is shown that expressions, period and stability conditions of the cycles can be explicitly determined. In order to obtain the results in this paper, only elementary mathematics are required. © 1988.

Title: Equilibrium in a market with sequential bargaining and random outside options
Abstract: The market equilibria for some indivisible object are derived when the object can be sold by one seller to one out of two groups of buyers, which are differing in their valuation of the object and their likelihood for entering the market. Which group will buy the object and at what price is found as a perfect bargaining equilibrium is examined. © 1988.

Title: The impossibility of stable renegotiation
Abstract: This note describes an example of a repeated game which has a unique renegotiation-proof equilibrium [Farrell (1983)] that, however, is not stable in the sense of Kohlberg and Mertens (1986). Hence, the requirements of renegotiation-proofness and stability may be mutually inconsistent. © 1988.

Title: The comparative statics of a competitive industry facing demand uncertainty
Abstract: The comparative statics of a competitive industry under uncertainty with free entry is clarified and extended using the general structure of random demand due to Leland (1972). While strong results are obtained for the industry, few unambiguous results can be derived for the firm. © 1988.

Title: Intransitive indifference and incomparability
Abstract: This paper presents the concept of an incomplete semiorder and the result that such a structure can be extended to a semiorder. Corresponding results exist for interval orders. An economic application is provided. © 1988.

Title: Interest rate innovations and the business cycle
Abstract: Recent evidence from vector autoregressions points towards the importance of interest rate innovations in explaining output variations. We show that this evidence supports an interpretation of business cycles based on nominal contractual rigidities rather than cotinuous market clearing. © 1988.

Title: On the constrained Walrasian and Lindahl correspondences
Abstract: This paper establishes conditions on preferences under the constrained Walrasian correspondence W c , the constrained Lindahl correspondence L c , and the weak Lindahl correspondence L w that is introduced in this paper are subcorrespondences of the (weak) Pareto-efficient correspondence P (P w ). © 1988.

Title: Errata
Large sample tests for absolute Lorenz dominance
Authors: John A. Bishop, S. Chakraborti, Paul D. Thistle
Abstract: We propose statistical tests for comparing the absolute Lorenz curves introduced by Moyes (1987). These tests allow absolute inequality comparisons using the tools of statistical inference. We apply the tests to U.S. state income distributions, obtaining rankings in 96 percent of the comparisons. © 1988.

Title: Black-white earnings ratios
Authors: Mark C. Berger, Jacqueline F. Allen
Abstract: While black-white earning ratios have been rising over time across cohorts there is some evidence that they have been dropping over time within cohorts of recent entrants to the labor market. This has coincided with the entry of the large baby boom cohorts into the labor market. This paper examines the role of race differences in cohort size effects on black-white earnings ratios for male high school graduates using Current Population Survey data. In larger cohorts, the black-white earnings ratio is lower at entry and falls as the cohort progresses through the career, consistent with recent evidence. © 1988.

Title: Small-firm mobility
Authors: Zoltan J. Acs, David B. Audretsch
Abstract: We find that the determinants of small-firm mobility are analogous to those for entry established in the literature. In particular, small-firm mobility is promoted in growing markets where skilled labor and technological change play an important role, and hindered in high capital and advertising intensive industries and in concentrated markets. © 1988.

Title: Taxation of capital gains on foreign exchange transactions and the non-neutrality of changes in anticipated inflation
Abstract: It has been established that in a two-country world, the existence of equal tax rates on interest income creates a distortion in the sense that fully anticipated changes in the inflation differential alter the real after-tax interest rate differential. This paper demonstrates that this distortion is created not by the existence of taxes on interest income but instead by the implicit assumption that capital gains are taxed as if they were interest income. When nominal interest is taxed, removing this tax on capital gains restores neutrality, while when real interest is taxed imposing this tax restores neutrality. © 1988.

Title: Inflation risk and the speed of adjustment in short-run money demand functions
Abstract: After 1973, money demand functions show a slow speed of adjustment. Including inflation risk does not help this; the SER shows multiple minima as a function of the estimated rho in the error, with higher speeds and rhos associated. © 1988.

Title: Testing separability of production using flexible functional form profit functions
Abstract: We show that the dual implications of separability depend crucially on whether profit is transformed non-linearly in modern flexible form production systems. In any case where profit is non-linearly transformed (as in the translog), homothetic separability is maintained. © 1988.

Title: Estimation of a general linear model with an unobservable stochastic variable
Abstract: This paper derives a maximum-likelihood estimation procedure for a class of general linear models in which there is an unobservable stochastic variable. The stochastic variable is assumed to follow an AR(1) process. Moreover, estimation of the trajectory of the unobservable stochastic variable is also considered. © 1988.

Title: Covariances between estimated autocorrelations of an ARMA process
Abstract: A method for the calculation of the covariances between estimated autocorrelations of an ARMA process is presented. This formula contains no infinite summations, only the inversion of matrices, the dimension of which is 2m+1 or less, where m=max(p, q). © 1988.

Title: The jackknife and regression with AR(1) errors
Abstract: In the linear regression model with strongly serially correlated errors, conventional methods often underestimate the standard errors, leading to excessive type I errors. A brief Monte Carlo study is presented showing that an application of Quenouille's half sample jackknife can reduce the type I error proportion substantially. Results using the bootstrap are also presented. © 1988.

Title: The real wage-employment relationship
Abstract: Estimates of industry differences in the strength and direction of the real wage-employment relationship are used to draw implications for the magnitude of aggregation bias and the role of employment contracts. © 1988.

Title: Intertemporal substitution, taste shocks and cointegration
Abstract: The intertemporal elasticity of substitution is estimated by cointegrating regressions for the U.S.A., the U.K., Switzerland and West Germany. The results of this approach, which is robust with respect to stationary taste shocks, indicate a substantial extent of intertemporal substitution. © 1988.

Title: A model of sequential auctions
Abstract: Early results in sequential auctions show that the first auction bid is less than would be bid were there no later auctions. This appears to be an attempt to deceive the opponents for possible gains in later auctions. However, at equilibrium there is no deception. This paper generalizes and extends these earlier results. © 1988.

Title: A strategic aspect of the strong positive association condition
Abstract: The purpose of this communication is to provide an explanation for the fact that the 'monotonicity', or 'strong positive association' condition has played a central role in the theory of implementation. (See definitions below.) The observation presented here is, at least mathematically, straightforward, but I know of no other intuitive reason that was suggested to account for the prominence of this condition. The observation below was noted when I applied my general 'theory of social situations' to the implementation problem. © 1988.

Title: Does GNP have a unit root?
Abstract: A number of recent studies have considered whether U.S. real GNP has a unit root with mixed results. In this letter a variety of tests are conducted to evaluate the evidence for the U.K. © 1988.

Title: Optimal shutdown decisions in resource extraction
Abstract: In this letter we give an analytic solution to the problem of when to stop production in resource extraction. The shutdown decision is irreversible. Both price and production follow geometric diffusion processes while extraction costs are fixed. © 1988.

Title: A regional analysis of food consumption in Spain
Abstract: Working's model of the Engel curve is applied to food and staple food expenditures with two years' Spanish provincial data. The functional form of Working's model is tested against two other specifications and cannot be rejected. The estimation results are quite comparable with those obtained by other authors. We also find that Spain has experienced a substantial change in the pattern of food consumption during the 1970s. © 1988.

Title: Equilibria in economies with countably many commodities
Authors: Manuel Besada, Margarita Estevez, Carlos Herves
Abstract: In this paper, we prove the existence of competitive equilibrium in an exchange economy in which commodity space is the sequence space Δ(P). © 1988.

Title: Separability of capital and labor in US manufacturing
Authors: Don P. Clark, Richard Hofler, Henry Thompson
Abstract: This paper investigates the separability of capital and six labor skill groups in U.S. manufacturing. It is found that no pair of inputs is even weakly separable. This result suggests that 'blackboard' production functions with two inputs should be used primarily for exposition. © 1988.

Title: Portfolio diversification and taxation
Abstract: In this paper we show that tax regulations may lead to portfolio diversification even if risk aversion is absent. We compare the effects of taxation with those of risk aversion and consider the implications for individuals and multi-market firms. © 1988.

Title: Measures of money and the monetary model of the Canadian-US dollar exchange rate
Abstract: Although the measurement of money is central to an empirical monetary modelof exchange rates, existing empirical studies rely on official aggregates as a measure of money. This paper uses superlative monetary aggregates in the context of a monetary model to explain the exchange rate between Canada and the United States. The parameters of the model are estimated using two-stage least squares with quarterly data for the period 1972-1985. The paper applies Davidson-MacKinnon tests to establish whether superlative and official monetary aggregates areobservationally equivalent in a monetary model of the Canadian-U.S. dollar exchange rate. © 1988.

Title: Self-defeating and welfare-improving DUP redistribution of capital assets
Abstract: The paper shows (a) that DUP redistribution of capital assets in large, open economies may make the terms-of-trade worsen so much that the redistribution becomes immiserizing for the group undertaking it, but also (b) that such activities may improve the terms-of-trade enough to improve the potential welfare of the entire society. © 1988.

Title: Second-best property value capitalization
Abstract: A simple model of distortive local finance shows how lump-sum finance models are misleading, what information local prices contain in the presence of distortions, and the feasibility of adjusting observed property value changes to infer resident net benefits of public goods. © 1988.

Title: An empirical re-examination of Wagner's law
Abstract: It is argued in this paper that for a more meaningful test of Wagner's law allowance must be made in regard to prevalence of peace and stability. Using six different versions and employing both nominal and real data from ten states of the United States, Wagner's law is vindicated. © 1988.

Title: A disequilibrium model of public spending
Abstract: This paper proposes a disequilibrium model of public spending. Empirical results show that public spending is constrained by the supply side for low per capita income countries and the demand side forhigh-income countries. © 1988.

Title: Predictive power of weekly money stock announcements
Authors: Yu-sheng Hsu, Chwen-chi Liu, Edwin F. Ulveling
Abstract: The objective of this study is to test if the weekly money stock can help to predict the monthly money stock using the data in the period of 1974 to 1985. Pitman's nearness measure and a statistic which is similar to the linear feedback statistic are used, respectively, for the qualitative and quantitative investigations. Other variables, such as interest rates and stock prices are also considered in the model. The results indicate that the weekly money supply provides little information concerning the monthly money stock. © 1988.

Title: Price formation in input-output analysis
Abstract: In this paper we study the effect of the insertion of fixed primary inputs into the static input-output model. Attention is paid to a number of price formation models, in particular to a model that is based on duality results. © 1988.

Title: A characterization of economies with the non-substitution property
Abstract: In this paper we provide a characterization of those economies exhibiting a non-substitution property. Whilst the assumptions of constant return to scale and a single primary input are necessary, this is not the case for the non-joint production hypothesis. Our characterization lies upon a result which in a sense can be seen as a converse of that in Johansen (1972). © 1988.

Title: On the computation of estimators in systems with implicity defined variables
Abstract: Estimators are often defined as the maximizing values of some objective function. This note introduces an algorithm for the computation of such estimators for the parameters of a system of equations where some of the variables are implicitly defined by an auxiliary set of equations. Systems of equations of this kind have been considered in the recent factor demand literature as well as in other areas. The algorithm is a gradient procedure. To keep the computational burden manageable it calculates the gradient from analytic expressions rather than by numerical differentiation. © 1988.

Title: Estimating covariances of parameter estimates from different models
Authors: Robert W. Turner, Mark L. Rockel
Abstract: This note presents a technique for estimating the covariances of parameter estimates from different models. This technique is useful for hypothesis testing for a non-linear function of the parameter estimates from different models with correlated observations. © 1988.

Title: A further theoretical result for generalized ridge regression estimators
Abstract: This paper derives a sufficient condition for the generalized ridge regression (GRR) estimator to be preferred to the ordinary least squares (OLS) estimator for all non-negative values of the biasing factors, when the performance of an estimator is measured by its mean squared error matrix. A test of this sufficient condition is outlined. © 1988.

Title: Seasonality and the estimation of dynamic demand systems
Abstract: This note presents empirical comparisons of alternative ways of introducing seasonal fluctuations in theoretically plausible dynamic demand systems derived from non-separable utility functions. © 1988.

Title: Testing exogeneity in a probit model
Abstract: A Hausman test of the exogeneity assumption in a probit model is derived by comparing the standard probit and Amemiya's simultaneous equations estimator. The challenge is that estimators must be transformed since normalizations must be consistent across estimators. © 1988.

Title: Macroeconomic aspects of the correlation between the level and variability of inflation
Abstract: In the context of a specific macroeconomic model it is shown that a positive association between the mean and variance of inflation could arise as a result of asymmetric stabilization policies. © 1988.

Title: Price instability and inflation
Authors: Ali F. Darrat, Franklin A. Lopez
Abstract: We test for a group of fourteen Latin American countries the hypothesis that as inflation accelerates, it also becomes more volatile. Our analysis uses time series data, a less arbitrary measure of inflation volatility, rational expectations models, and seemingly unrelated regressions. The empirical evidence supports the above hypothesis and strengthens the case against inflationary policies in Latin America. © 1988.

Title: Rational expectation equilibrium under quasilinear preferences
Abstract: Under quasilinear preferences, rational expectation equilibrium does not necessarily need the same subjective probabilities for heterogeneous agents, and equilibrium uniqueness is not guaranteed, either. © 1988.

Title: The equal-loss principle for bargaining problems
Abstract: We introduce a new bargaining solution, which we call the equal-loss solution. This solution equalizes across agents the losses from the ideal point. Two characterizations of the solution are presented by formulating axioms specifying how bargaining solutions should respond to changes in the feasible set and the ideal point. © 1988.

Title: Efficient union bargains with a random arbitrator
Abstract: Unionised contracts specifying wages and employment dominate contracts specifying only wages, yet most contracts specify wages only. With uncertain bargaining powers, both parties could be better off allowing the union to set the wage. © 1988.

Title: Earnings and the principal components of job performance
Abstract: Unlike earlier studies of the relationship between earnings and job performance, our study treats the latter as a multidimensional variable. We extract two principal components. We find that only the positive aspect of job commitment has a significant impact on earnings. © 1988.

Title: Intra-firm diffusion and the wage bargain
Abstract: If the time path of prices and wages are determined by rules based on the bargained labour contract and vintage assumptions apply to production, then the leading firm's decision to diffuse a new process is encapsulated in the optimal (intertemporal profit maximum) investment function for new vintage capital subject to these rules. The optimal diffusion speed accelerates with the inflation of prices and with technical change, but is depressed by marginal costs of adjusting new capital. The optimal trajectory of new capital has the familiar sigmoid shape. © 1988.

Title: Industry equilibrium with uncertainty and labor-managed firms
Abstract: This paper characterizes long-run industry equilibrium composed of labor-managed firms under demand uncertainty. Moreover, it is demonstrated how the number and size of firms in the industry respond to a change in uncertainty. © 1988.

Title: Balance-of-payments crises and monetary policy reactions in a model with imperfect substitutability between domestic and foreign bonds
Abstract: We show that if domestic and foreign bonds are imperfect substitutes for each other and the exchange rate is fixed, then, unlike under the perfect substitutability assumption, uncertainty about monetary policy reactions affects the timing of balance-of-payments crises. © 1988.

Title: Official Australian intervention in foreign exchange markets, 1977 to 1986
Abstract: The intervention behaviour of the Reserve Bank of Australia for a period both before and after the float of the Australian currency is analysed. It is found that 'leaning against the wind' is the intervention policy used by the Bank. © 1988.

Title: The welfare effects of capital inflow in the presence of a tariff (quota) with revenue (premium) seeking
Abstract: The paper re-examines the impact of capital inflow on the welfare of a small host nation in the presence of a tariff (quota) with revenue (premium) seeking. It is demonstrated that the welfare impact of capital inflow is neutral in the case of a tariff with revenue seeking but ambiguous in the case of a quota with premium seeking. © 1988.

Title: A simple model of technology transfer
Abstract: This paper is an attempt to model transfer of technology in a simple partial equilibrium structure where a single firm has access to different technologies for producing a homogeneous good. It is shown that a low-wage, less productive economy will receive relatively obsolete technologies whereas more advanced methods of production find their place in the high-wage, highly productive developed country. © 1988.

Title: Finite horizons and the non-neutrality of money
Authors: Frederick Van Der Ploeg, Giancarlo Marini
Abstract: This note re-examines the issue of monetary super-neutrality in an optimizing model with finite horizons. Mortality makes agents less patient and thus affects negatively the process of capital accumulation. This distortion can be reduced by increases in monetary growth. © 1988.

Title: Covered interest parity and UK monetary ‘news’
Abstract: In this note the effect of unanticipated sterling M3 announcements on the sterling-dollar covered interest parity relationship is investigated. It is demonstrated inter alia that unanticipated monetary announcements have a significantly positive effect on the one month euro-sterling interest rate, a significantly negative effect on the one month euro-dollar interest rate which in turn generates an expected exchange rate depreciation. © 1988.

Title: The positive-part Stein-rule estimator and tests of linear hypotheses
Abstract: When testing linear restrictions in the multiple regression model the usualF-test, based on the maximum-likelihood estimator, is uniformly most powerful invariant. We show that the counterpart to this test, based on the positive-part Stein-rule estimator, has this same optimal property. © 1988.

Title: Some asymptotic theory for the bootstrap in econometric models
Abstract: In econometric modeling it is often reasonable to make specific assumptions about the distribution of the true errors in a model (e.g. that they come from a symmetric population), in which case it may be of interest to know if a prospective bootstrap method is asymptotically robust - that it gives valid results whether or not the assumptions actually hold for the true errors. This paper discusses methods for getting asymptotic results insuch situations. © 1988.

Title: Comparing the Wald, LR and LM tests for heteroscedasticity in a linear regression model
Abstract: We compare the power of the Wald, likelihood ratio, and Lagrangian multiplier tests for heteroscedasticity between two sample regimes in a linear regression model through the asymptotic expansion of the non-null distribution for the three tests up to O 1 N, where n is the sample size. As a result, we see that the power of the three tests depends on both the nature of the explanatory variables and the direction of the alternative hypothesis and that no one statistic is uniformly superior to the others. However, if the moments of the explanatory variables are stable over the whole sample period, then the asymptotic power, up to O 1 N, is equivalent for the three tests. © 1988.

Title: Missing measurements in limited dependent variable models
Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem of whether or not incomplete observations contain any information about the parameters that could be used in their estimation, as they apply to limited dependent variable models. The answers differ between binary response models and Tobit models when serial correlation prevails, given missing observations on independent variables. If, instead, missing observations pertain to the dependent variable, we have negative answers for both models. © 1988.

Title: Biases in dynamic models with fixed effects
Abstract: This paper examines bias in dynamic models with fixed effects where both the number of time series observations and the number of cross-sectional replications are small. The formula bias estimate is in line with that in published Monte Carlo studies. © 1988.

Title: The characterization of savings under uncertainty
Abstract: We characterize savings behavior within an infinitely lived, representative agent economy in which output is a stochastic linear function of savings and the returns to savings are serially correlated. This characterization explicitly demonstrates the roles that agents' elasticity of intertemporal substitution and the pattern of serial correlation have in determining the value of the income elasticity of savings. © 1988.

Title: Revenue equivalence in multi-object auctions
Abstract: The theory of auctions suggests that, under certain conditions, seemingly different methods for auctioning a single object will result in the same expected price. This result extends quite easily to the case of more than one object. © 1988.

Title: Imperfect competition and the Keynesian cross
Abstract: This paper presents a simple general equilibrium model in which the only non-Walrasian feature is imperfect competition in the goods market. The model is shown to exhibit various Keynesian characteristics. In particular, as competition in the goods market becomes less perfect, the fiscal policy multipliers approach the values implied by the textbook Keynesian cross. © 1988.

Title: The excess utility functions and the welfare adjustment process
Abstract: This paper introduces the excess utility functions which are shown to have all the properties the excess demand functions have. Then, these functions are used to simplify the proofs of existing results about the stability of the welfare adjustment process. © 1988.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Erratum
The design of reward structures in career games
Abstract: To study performance incentives and reward structures we derive an equation based on the theory of relative deprivation. The equation is applied to obtain several fundamental properties of career games and, in particular, to identify new devices for intervention aimed at encouraging desirable behaviour in such games. © 1987.

Title: An upper bound for wealth distribution in a model of accidental bequests
Abstract: An explicit upper bound is calculated for wealth distribution in a model of overlapping generations with uncertain lifetimes and an imperfect annuities market. © 1987.

Title: A note on the estimation of Atkinson's index of inequality
Abstract: In this note, the resemblance between the family of inequality indices introduced by Atkinson (1970) and the Box-Cox transformation is exploited in order to provide a data-based procedure for choosing an inequality index within the family. © 1987.

Title: Do unions discourage economic activity?
Authors: John S. Heywood, Michael D. Deich
Abstract: Previous examinations of the influence of unions on economic activity fail to use a measure of unionization that varies both by state and industry. Such a failure introduces the possibility of serious specification errors, a possibility confirmed by comparing traditional estimates which suggest unions depress a state's economic activity with new estimates which reveal no such effect. © 1987.

Title: Pooled cross-section time-series examination of the effects of unemployment insurance compensation on unemployment rate and unemployment duration
Authors: Phanindra V. Wunnava, John R. Henley
Abstract: The main objective of this paper is to determine if there is a work disincentive effect associated with the Unemployment Insurance Compensation (UIC) program. We test our hypothesis that there is quite possibly a work disincentive effect which would result in higher rates of insured unemployment or longer average durations of insured unemployment (or both) in states with more generous UIC programs (because higher levels of UIC reduce the cost of remaining unemployed) using data for 18 years (from 1966 to 1983, the latest year for which data is available) for all of the 50 states. We conclude from our empirical results that a work disincentive effect exists. © 1987.

Title: An empirical examination of small firm growth
Authors: Zoltan J. Acs, David B. Audretsch
Abstract: We find that the extent of small firm growth is negatively related to industry capital intensity and advertising intensity, but it is positively related to the extent of human capital, total innovation activity, and small firm innovation activity, and the extent to which the productivity growth of small firms has exceeded that of large firms. © 1987.

Title: On the striking price bias of the Black-Scholes formula with an estimated variance rate
Abstract: The use of an estimated variance rate in the Black-Scholes formula produces biased estimates of the theoretical price. This study analytically examines the bias with respect to moneyness of the option. © 1987.

Title: The relation between money growth variability and the variability of money about target
Authors: Thomas F. Cosimano, Dennis W. Jansen
Abstract: An increase in the speed at which the Fed returns the money stock to its targeted path following a stochastic shock can cause a lower variance of money about the targeted level while causing a greater variance of the growth rate of the money stock. © 1987.

Title: The MSE of the least squares estimator over an interval constraint
Abstract: In this note, we examine the MSE performance of the interval constrained least squares estimator. It is shown that the shape of the MSE largely depends on the length of the interval in the constraint. © 1987.

Title: On the profitability of using forecasts
Abstract: The condition on the profitability of using a forecast of real wages is derived in an adjustment cost model of the firm. With costless information and a one period horizon the condition is the same as that derived in econometrics for the usefulness of a forecast as an input to a forecasting model. With costs of obtaining the forecast and in a multiperiod model the condition is more restrictive. © 1987.

Title: The class of ban estimators of a single structural equation with structural change
Abstract: Taking account of equality of structural variances in different samples, we characterize the class of BAN estimators of a single structural equation with structural change and propose an asymptotically efficient three-step estimator. © 1987.

Title: A note on collinearity, bootstrapping, and cross-validation
Abstract: A simulation study comparing several techniques for selection of the ridge regression parameter is described. Analysis strategies are suggested for data with various degrees of noise and collinearity. A method that combines bootstrapping and cross-validation is highlighted. © 1987.

Title: A new method for measuring technological change
Authors: R.L. Basmann, K.J. Hayes, D.J. Slottje, D.J. Molina
Abstract: This paper presents a new method for testing for technological change. The innovation here is the introduction of a production function which is sufficiently flexible to detect the change. The production function is assumed to be a function not only of the relevant inputs but also of technology-changing parameters. © 1987.

Title: No unit root conditions for bivariate series when a component univariate series has a unit root
Abstract: The root-locus method is used to derive conditions under which a bivariate series does not possess a unit root when a component univariate series does have a unit root. The bivariate series composed of the U.S. real GNP and civilian unemployment rate (1948.I-1973.IV) does not have a unit root. © 1987.

Title: Verifying the betweenness axiom with questionnaire evidence, or not
Abstract: Data are presented from questionnaires about preferences over hypothetical lotteries. The answers either support or reject the betweenness axiom, depending on which questions are picked. © 1987.

Title: A note on feasible implementations
Abstract: This paper is concerned with the problem of individually feasible outcomes in decentralized allocation mechanisms. We consider a well-known mechanism which achieves efficient allocations in equilibrium. This mechanism, however, may leave agents bankrupt, if they fail to reach equilibrium. It is shown that the bankruptcy problem can be avoided, if a voting stage is added to the original mechanism. © 1987.

Title: Intransitive social strict preference and the Arrow theorem
Abstract: This paper shows that the condition of transitivity of the social strict preference relation is not necessary to Arrow's dictatorship result, provided the weak Pareto principle is replaced by the strong Pareto principle and the Pareto indifference rule. © 1987.

Title: Rate-of-return regulated cost function
Abstract: In this note, we present the appropriate forms of Shephard's lemma, as well as the curvature and homogeneity properties, for the case of a rate-of-return regulated cost function where capital is a quasi-fixed input. © 1987.

Title: The unique minimal cash flow competitive equilibrium
Abstract: In a strategic market game with paper money used for exchange the control of the amount of money or credit issued and the selection of the level of the penalty for default make it possible to select a single competitive equilibrium which is feasible as a non-cooperative equilibrium. © 1987.

Title: Nash equilibria equal competitive equilibria
Abstract: With strictly monotone preferences and a continuum of traders, there is a game in which the set of Nash equilibria is exactly the same as the set of competitive equilibria. © 1987.

Title: Erratum
Regional differences and the components of growth and inequality change
Abstract: Inequality change can be decomposed simply in terms of per capita income and population changes, using the Gini index. An illustration based on U.S. data for the two intercensus periods 1960-1970 and 1970-1980 is given. This decomposition analysis is also applied to the study of changes in a welfare index originally proposed by Sen. © 1987.

Title: Further evidence on the screening hypothesis
Authors: Elchanan Cohn, B.F. Kiker, M.Mendes De Oliveira
Abstract: In two recent studies that have appeared in this journal, Katz and Ziderman (1980) and Psacharopoulos (1979) investigate the screening hypothesis using different methodologies and data sources (nation-wide household surveys for Israel and the United Kingdom, respectively). For this paper, we employ data for the United States and extend their analysis. Our general conclusion is that, regardless of the techniques used to test for its existence, the screening hypothesis draws no empirical support from United States data. © 1987.

Title: On requiring the durable goods monopolist to sell
Authors: David A. Malueg, John L. Solow
Abstract: Requiring a monopolist to sell its output (rather than renting it) my lead to beneficial output adjustments or harmful quality adjustments. In a durable goods model, we show that requiring sales decreases welfare in only a small fraction of cases, but it strictly increases welfare in a majority of cases. © 1987.

Title: Factor proportions and multinationals
Abstract: This article introduces and illustrates a concise analytical technique which enables differences in factor proportions among ownership groups to be decomposed into those due to differences within the same industry and those due to variations in industrial composition. © 1987.

Title: Sterilization policies in the EMS countries
Abstract: The paper analyses the extent to which fixed exchange rates within the EMS have hindered national monetary policies. The results show that the German authorities have relatively more freedom in pursuing domestic monetary objectives. The others may, notwithstanding foreign exchange controls, occasionally encounter severe exchange constraints. © 1987.

Title: Audit probabilities and tax evasion in a business simulation
Abstract: This paper examines the role of individual differences and audit probabilities in tax evasion and argues that more elaborate experimental studies of evasion are needed. © 1987.

Title: Linear errors-in-variables models
Abstract: The paper reports some substantive findings from an extensive Monte Carlo to evaluate the finite-sample performance of the polynomial IV estimator relative to the Durbin approach. © 1987.

Title: A Monte Carlo test of preference independence
Abstract: Theil (1987) recently developed distribution-free Monte Carlo testing procedures for demand homogeneity and Slutsky symmetry which do not use asymptotic theory. In this paper we introduce a similar procedure to test preference independence. The application of this procedure is illustrated with Dutch data. © 1987.

Title: Mean adjustment and the CUSUM test for structural change
Abstract: We show that the common practice of mean adjusting the data prior to regression and testing has serious implications for the null distribution of the CUSUM test for structural change. © 1987.

Title: Errors in variables in the multinomial response model
Abstract: In this paper we examine measurement error in the independent variables of multinomial response model. We show how not taking this error account biases the coefficient estimate asymptotically. We provide a bias-adjusted estimator, using the multinomial logit model as an example. © 1987.

Title: Rejections of orthogonality in rational expectations models
Authors: John W. Galbraith, Juan Dolado, Anindya Banerjee
Abstract: It is well known that many rationality tests do not have the correct sizes if innovations in the explanatory series are correlated with the regressand and the explanatory series are substantially autocorrelated. We argue, by considering somewhat more general data generating processes and models, that the importance of the over-rejections may have been over-emphasized. © 1987.

Title: Bounded-influence instrumental variables estimator
Abstract: The bounded-influence instrumental variables estimator (BIV) is shown to be consistent even if the scale parameter of the error term is unknown and has to be estimated. © 1987.

Title: Inflation and the Euler equation approach to consumption behaviour
Abstract: By using U.S. quarterly data on non-durable consumption over the period 1951.I-1986.II this note presents various pieces of evidence for the view that inflation variables - in the anticipated, 'surprise' and uncertainty forms - matter in the Euler-type consumption autoregression. Inflation variables are not only significantly negative and make the overall performance of the Euler type specifications better, but they also induce the 'wrong' sign for the real rate of interest. These results are puzzling and suggest that the question of why, in contrast with a Fisherian intertemporal optimization, inflation matters in the consumption autoregression should be an important area for research. © 1987.

Title: Inflation, indexation, and wage dispersion
Abstract: This study provides a theory of indexation to reconcile empirical findings that unanticipated inflation raises the dispersion of price changes among subaggregates while it lowers that of wage changes. Evidence on the relation between inflation and the dispersion of wage changes in Israel is presented to buttress the arguments. © 1987.

Title: Rationed and walrasian markets for the same good
Abstract: Consumers purchase a good on either a rationed or an equilibrating market. On the former, for price p 1 the good is obtained instantly or with delay τ with probabilities Π and (1 - Π) respectively. On the latter the good is obtained instantly for p 2 . W define and derive the conditions for a rational expectations equilibrium for this problem. © 1987.

Title: The robustness of multidimensional signalling equilibria
Abstract: This paper demonstrates upper hemi-continuity of a multidimensional signalling equilibrium correspondence. © 1987.

Title: Anticipatory pricing with negligible uncertainty
Abstract: If firms precommit to output, and price equates either expected excess demand or excess demand when demand takes its expected value to zero, then equilibrium price and output typically do not converge to their Walrasian levels as demand becomes decreasingly risky. © 1987.

Title: The consumption function under exponential utility
Abstract: A recent article by Cantor derived a closed-form solution for the consumer optimization problem with exponential utility and normal income shocks. This paper derives solutions without imposing the normality assumption, and investigates the effect of risk in this more general setting. © 1987.

Title: On the architecture of complex organizations
Abstract: We use results from information theory to show that the screening effectiveness of organizations which consist of many fallible agents can be arbitrarily improved, but only if organizational architecture is non-hierarchical. We also examine how any desired outcome may be implemented as a symmetric equilibrium, when agents are selfish. © 1987.

Title: Union membership and employment dynamics
Abstract: This note examines the behavior of a monopoly union that cares about its future membership and recognizes the dynamic dependence of membership on employment. A characterization is given both of the steady state and of the interdependent employment and membership dynamics out of that steady state. © 1987.

Title: Screening unemployment in a dual labor market
