Abstract: Increased survival probability and expected lifespan is shown to increase capital intensity and welfare in an overlapping generations model with uncertain lifetimes in the presence of annuities market and production. © 1986.

Title: Shared inputs, over-capitalization, and regulation
Abstract: When inputs are joint in production, a partially regulated firm has the incentive to allocate all joint inputs to the regulated jurisdiction. The regulated firm, if required to allocate costs, will have less of an incentive to over-capitalize. © 1986.

Title: Robust tests for unit roots in the foreign exchange market
Abstract: Empirical studies that have tested for unit roots in foreign exchange rate data have assumed independent and identically distributed errors in order to apply Dickey-Fuller test procedures. This assumption ignores the temporal dependence of the error sequence present in many simple efficient market tests, as discussed in Hansen and Hodrick (1980), as well as Krasker (1980). In this paper we apply unit root test statistics that allow for heterogeneously distributed and mildly dependent error processes, and thus provide superior tests of the unit root hypothesis in the case of foreign exchange rates. © 1986.

Title: Inadequacies of the strategic rationale of export subsidies
Abstract: A major attraction of strategic trade theory is that it appears to explain governments' desire to subsidise exports. We argue that this appearance is illusory. © 1986.

Title: Optimally uniform commodity taxes and non-linear engel curves
Abstract: A sufficient condition for optimally uniform commodity taxes is derived in the more realistic non-linear Engel curve case and in a form that allows easy checking from the various parameter estimates. This general condition is shown to yield certain well-known sufficient conditions as special cases. © 1986.

Title: Risk sharing in the adjustable-rate loan market
Abstract: A previous paper [Arvan and Brueckner (1986)] showed that in an optimal loan contract, interest rate risk should be shared between lender and borrower, with the slope of the loan-rate function (which relates the loan interest rate to the lender's uncertain cost-of-funds) lying between zero and one. Existing adjustable-rate mortgage (ARM) contracts violate this rule since they require complete risk absorption by the borrower when interest rate caps are not binding. The present paper shows that when the earlier model is modified by adding a second type of borrower, efficient loan contracts look more like existing ARMs. © 1986.

Title: Interaction between Wall Street and the London stock exchange
Abstract: This paper tests the daily relationship between the stock exchange movements on Wall Street and London. Because of time differences, the direction of causation is unambigous; the overlap, with both markets open, allows a test of the efficient market hypothesis. © 1986.

Title: Variable selection problem in the censored regression models
Abstract: In this paper we discuss the variable selection problem for the censored regression models. The Schme-Hahn (1979) estimator for the censored normal model and the Buckley-James (1979) estimator for the non-parametric censored model are discussed. It is shown, through the EM algorithm, that the variable selection problem for these estimators can be converted into a variable selection problem in a standard linear regression model. We show that the expectation of maximum likelihood residuals converges to zero in large samples. © 1986.

Title: A note on linear heteroscedasticity models
Abstract: The familiar practice of estimating residual variance functions via regression of squared estimated residuals is examined in a method of moments framework. In many situations, the covariance matrix estimator will reduce to White's (1980) heteroscedasticity-consistent computation. Extensions to higher moments and multiple equation systems are discussed. © 1986.

Title: Two misspecification tests for the simple switching regressions disequilibrium model
Abstract: Two specification tests for switching regimes disequilibrium models are developed. The first is an asymptotically locally optimal Lagrange multiplier test of endogeneity of a set of regressors, which takes the convenient form of a LM significance-test of certain regression residuals. The second is a Hausman specification test of the accuracy of regime classification information. © 1986.

Title: A note on competitive bribery games
Abstract: Within a competitive bribery game in which each player has incomplete information, we show that there exists a unique Nash equilibrium which is symmetric. Similar results hold for another bribery game form that prevails in the literature. Implications for corrupt practices in relation to economic development are also discussed. © 1986.

Title: Tax evasion is not a gamble
Abstract: A tax evasion experiment and an equivalent gambling experiment indicate that, contrary to the 'standard' model of evasion, tax evasion and gambling are quite different, although the standard model provides a good basis for analysis of evasion. © 1986.

Title: Global stability and the choice of policy targets under rational expectations
Abstract: It is shown that if the supply of capital is properly incorporated in a macromodel with rational expectations, the government cannot peg its expenditures wholly in real terms since, otherwise, the economy will be globally unstable. © 1986.

Title: Employment - restraining agreements in Weitzman's share system
Abstract: Weitzman (1983) argues that a profit-sharing system would automatically maintain full employment in the face of deflationary shocks. This note shows that such a virtuous disequilibrium behavior could be thwarted by the spread of employer-employee agreements, by which the firm is compensated to temporarily refrain from hiring the unemployed. © 1986.

Title: Corrigenda
A model of industrial location
Abstract: This note develops a model of spatial competition with an important asymmetry, namely that firms at different locations incur different costs. An equilibrium configuration given an artificial advantage at one point in the market is determined, and some implications drawn. © 1986.

Title: Ramsey optimality and a regulatory algorithm for optimal pricing by regulated multiproduct firms
Abstract: This paper describes, in a general equilibrium framework, an algorithm which determines Ramsey optimal prices for a regulated, multiproduct monopoly. © 1986.

Title: Time preference for price deviations and terms of trade
Abstract: Using a methodology that explicitly accounts for time preference for cash flows from commodity exports, this study finds that the terms of trade between export and import prices have declined for most commodities over the last quarter century. © 1986.

Title: Public investment and international policy coordination
Abstract: This note presents a simple example of the strategic interaction between two countries in the choice of optimal public investment. Whenever countries engage in net intertemporal trade (i.e., non-zero current accounts) there are gains from policy coordination. © 1986.

Title: Marshall-Lerner with imported inputs
Abstract: In this note we derive an extension of the famous Marshall-Lerner condition for the case where imports of the small, open economy under consideration consist of intermediate goods as well as finished goods. © 1986.

Title: The effect of a unilateral transfer between customs union partners on the terms of trade
Abstract: This paper analyzes the effect of a unilateral transfer between two customs union members on the terms of trade. In particular, it highlights that this transfer might create, under special conditions, a terms of trade deterioration for all countries. © 1986.

Title: Conditions for efficient tax rates
Abstract: In a standard model of optimal taxation, and for a small open economy, necessary and sufficient conditions for a tax rate to be efficient are derived. Those conditions are applied to Swedish 1982 data. Marginal tax rates in Sweden (1982) are the highest in the OECD countries, but not inefficient as evaluated on the basis of the present model. © 1986.

Title: Optimal tax progressivity under imperfect competition
Abstract: A general equilibrium model is constructed where the authorities choose a linear progressive tax to maximize social welfare in the presence of work incentive effects and imperfect competition. It is demonstrated that optimal progressivity varies with market concentration. © 1986.

Title: The behavior of the stock market in a developing economy
Authors: Ali F. Darrat, Tarun K. Mukherjee
Abstract: Applying Granger-type causality along with Akaike's final-prediction-error criterion on the Indian data over 1948-1984, this paper finds a significant causal (lagged) relationship between stock returns and some selected macro variables, including money supply, implying market inefficiency in the semi-strong sense. © 1986.

Title: Demand for money, exixtence and cointegrability
Abstract: Series of the same order of integrability can be tested for cointegration. This paper analyses a demand for money function and suggests that cointegrability can be found even when the original series are of different orders of integrability. © 1986.

Title: Evidence on the random behavior of weekly M1 data
Authors: William T. Gavin, Nicholas V. Karamouzis
Abstract: This paper provides empirical evidence showing that the weekly M1 series follows a stochastic trend. The implications of this finding for economic research are discussed. © 1986.

Title: Capacity growth in a clay-clay vintage model
Abstract: In this paper the growth rates of capacity output and capacity demand for labour are derived for a clay-clay vintage model. The results are simple and directly applicable in the sense that they only depend on parameters and measurable variables. © 1986.

Title: Convex functions on non-convex domains
Abstract: It is shown that a convex function, defined on an arbitrary, possibly finite, subset of a linear space, can be extended to the whole space. An application to decision making under risk is given. © 1986.

Title: Global asymptotic stability of non-linear difference equations
Abstract: A sufficient condition for global asymptotic stability of the origin for non-linear difference equations is presented. This condition is a generalization of a result due to Brock and Scheinkman (1975). © 1986.

Title: Improved finite-sample estimators in linear models
Abstract: The paper demonstrates the dominance, in terms of average mean squared errors, of the explicit positive-part Stein estimator over the generalized ridge estimator in normal linear regression models. © 1986.

Title: Some dominance theorems on the double-k class estimator in linear models
Abstract: The paper exhibits an explicit estimator that dominates, in terms of Wald risks relative to mean squared errors, the double-k class estimator in some normal linear multiple regression equations. © 1986.

Title: Conditional forecasting with a multivariate time series model
Abstract: Often, when forecasting with multivariate ARMA-time series models, one knows beforehand (or thinks so) which values will be taken on by certain outputs. This note derives predictions for the remaining unknown outputs, conditional upon such a priori knowledge. © 1986.

Title: Some small sample properties of tests for structural stability in a simultaneous equation
Abstract: In this note, we examine the small sample properties of Wald tests for structural stability in a single simultaneous equation by Monte Carlo experiments. It is shown that the Wald tests have an upward bias in the size but it can be considerably reduced by changing a nominal size. It is also shown that the use of the OLS estimator in the test for structural stability can be very risky in some cases. © 1986.

Title: Tests of Granger causality by the selection of the orders of a bivariate autoregressive model
Abstract: The problem of testing Granger causality is considered in bivariate autoregressive systems. Some testing methods based on the statistical criteria for model selection are proposed, and their asymptoticerror probabilities are derived. © 1986.

Title: On the efficiency gains from imposing symmetry constraints in demand systems
Authors: Carl H. Nelson, James K. Binkley
Abstract: This paper presents an easy to apply formula which can be used to assess the efficiency gains from imposing symmetry constraints on a system of demand equations. The interrelationship of the correlation between errors and the correlation between variables is shown to have a significant impact on efficiency gains. Standard results on efficiency gains from seemingly unrelated regression are shown to be inapplicable. © 1986.

Title: A test of the future expectations model
Abstract: This note gives a simple test of the future expectations model based on Lagrange principles, that is implemented through an instrumental variable criterion. The test can be computed easily with existing software packages. © 1986.

Title: Algebraic equivalences among Wald, LM and Hausman's tests in the linear regression model
Abstract: Under certain conditions, the Hausman's statistic is identical to the Wald statistic, if we use the unconstrained maximum likelihood estimate for the variance of disturbances, while it becomes identical to the LM statistic, if we use the constrained maximum likelihood estimate for the variance. © 1986.

Title: Wald tests of common factor restrictions
Authors: Allan W. Gregory, Michael R. Veall
Abstract: In this letter using Monte Carlo analysis, we investigate the sensitivity of Wald tests to alternative formulations of non-linear common factor restrictions. For there examples considered, there is no one form of the restrictions that performs well over the different parameter settings. © 1986.

Title: Exact maximum-likelihood estimation of autoregressive models via the Kalman filter
Abstract: The pth order autoregression is studied in state-space form, and a closed-form analytic expression is obtained for the unconditional covariance matrix of the initial state vector. It is shown that this covariance matrix depends only on the first p autocovariances, which makes exact maximum-likelihood estimation via the Kalman filter a straightforward task. © 1986.

Title: Risk aversion and preference distortion in deterministic bargaining experiments
Abstract: A number of predictions from game theory concerning the interaction of risk attitudes and bargaining behaviour are tested in a laboratory experiment. The evidence is clearly consistent with the theoretical predictions. © 1986.

Title: Effects of monetary and fiscal policy on inflation
Abstract: The paper applies the J-test to a simple IS-LM based economic model fitted to an aggregate cross-country and time-series dataset from 16 OECD countries for the period 1968 to 1985 to test for significant discriminant causes of inflation. The findings support a mix of fiscal and monetary policy for effective macroeconomic analysis. © 1986.

Title: Inflation, unemployment and the median voter
Abstract: We combine an econometric analysis of survey data on the relative seriousness of inflation and unemployment with the median voter theorem to derive the equilibrium rate of inflation. If the natural rate of unemployment is 7 percent, then the equilibrium inflation rate is 5.4 percent. © 1986.

Title: The lag relationship between producer and consumer prices
Abstract: Here a maximum likelihood estimation technique is derived for a linear regression model with geometrically distributed lag in an unobservable variable. Then the model and the estimation technique are applied in estimating the empirical lag relationship between inflation in consumer price index and inflation in producer price index. © 1986.

Title: The demand for money in China during hyperinflation
Abstract: During the period 1945-1949, China experienced a severe inflation, an increase of about 78 percent per month over 45 months. Based on a model of the demand for money in China during the hyperinflation, this paper examines the hypothesis of the variable coefficient of price expectation. A non-linear function of the price expectation model was formulated. The results indicate that (1) the path of the coefficient of the expectation reversed itself at the beginning of the hyperinflation process, and (2) the elasticity of demand for money with respect to the inflation rate is lower under a variable coefficient of expectation model than under a constant coefficient of expectation model. © 1986.

Title: On dominance solvable auctions in the general symmetric model
Abstract: A new class, of second-price auctions of the general symmetric model, is shown to be a dominance solvable game. Illuminating examples are provided. © 1986.

Title: On the hedging and output behavior of the competitive cooperative firm under price and production uncertainty
Abstract: We show that a separation of hedging and production decisions does not hold for a cooperative firm under price and output uncertainty and that its production decision is not sensitive to the functional form of the production function. © 1986.

Title: Endogenous cycles with uncertain lifespans in continuous time
Abstract: Endogenous equilibrium business cycles are found in a Blanchard (1985) model modified to include endogenous labor supply. With low elasticities of substitution in production and consumption, cycles arise around stationary states with positive real interest rates. © 1986.

Title: Does GNP have a unit root?
Authors: James H. Stock, Mark W. Watson
Abstract: The Nelson-Plosser finding of a unit root in real U.S. GNP is re-examined using additional data sets and a new statistical test The new statistical test carries out a non-parametric correction for serial correlation. © 1986.

Title: The stability of equilibrium in a model with a government budget restraint and endogenous bonds
Abstract: General conditions are given for asymptotic stability of full-employment equilibrium in a model with a government budget restraint and endogenous bonds. It is argued that even in the particular case where real government spending on goods is a datum the conditions are not obviously implausible. © 1986.

Title: Four paradoxes in GNP
Abstract: This note presents four paradoxes inherent in the time-series structure of real American GNP. © 1986.

Title: Distinguishing between rational expectations and ‘Keynesian’ models of the business cycle in the presence of a structural break in the money growth process
Abstract: This paper uses an apparent structural break in the post-war U.K. money growth equation to test the validity of the restrictions implied by a simple rational expectations model of the business cycle. The test suggests that those restrictions cannot be rejected. © 1986.

Title: Effects of multiple uncertainty on rationing
Authors: Stephen M. Goldfeld, Richard E. Quandt
Abstract: We analyze the problem of a policy maker who chooses an instrument and rations so as to minimize a loss function in the face of additive and multiplicative uncertainty. Theoretical and computational results are provided. © 1986.

Title: Some results on an approximation to joint distributions of utility functions
Abstract: Dalal and Klein (1985) obtained an approximation to discrete choice probabilities. This note justifies the use of this approximation in a forecasting context, where the forecast is made for a choice set of alternatives different from that used to initially estimate the model. © 1986.

Title: Multiple representative consumers
Abstract: This paper extends Muellbauer's (1975) notion of consistent aggregation of consumer demand through a single representative consumer to the case of multiple representative consumers, and obtains the condition for the representative total expenditures to be independent of prices. © 1986.

Title: Perfect competition as the limit of a hierarchical market game
Abstract: It is shown that competitive equilibrium can be seen as the limit of some hierarchical game in which the rights (or information) of the players can be strictly ordered. © 1986.

Title: Stochastic decentralization of competitive allocations
Abstract: When consumers and producers select weakly continuous probability distributions over ∈-indifferent actions, a price vector exists which clears mean aggregate demand, and the potential relative disequilibrium vanishes as the economy becomes large. © 1986.

Title: A note on the Gale-Nikaido-Debreu lemma and the existence of general equilibrium
Abstract: In this note, we give another version of the generalized Gale-Nikaido-Debreu lemma which has as direct corollary the usual statement without weakening any conclusion. We give also another simple way for discarding free disposability. © 1986.

Title: Market share inertia with more than two firms: An existence problem
Working's model for food in the four phases of the international comparison project
Abstract: The relationship found by Working between the budget share of food and the log of total per capita expenditure holds remarkably well at the cross-country level. © 1986.

Title: A class of generalized measures of mobility with applications
Abstract: A class of anonymous measures of mobility is defined that considers the relationship between the long-run and short-run distributions of income. Several measures of long-run income and inequalityare explored. Michigan panel data are analyzed. © 1986.

Title: Education, overlapping generations, and the existence of equilibrium
Authors: Murray C. Kemp, Ngo Van Long
Abstract: We describe a simple aggregative model, the essential features of which are that individuals are mortal (overlapping generations) and can invest in their own training (human capital). It is shown by example that if expectations are rational then there may be a unique steady state but no competitive path starting away from the steady state. © 1986.

Title: Revocable pricing can yield collusive outcomes
Abstract: Traditional models of Bertrand price competition assume irrevocable price announcements. In contrast, when price changes have zero direct costs but sales are thereby delayed, the collusive monopoly outcome is a subgame perfect outcome and is, moreover, the natural focal equilibrium. © 1986.

Title: Why are profits correlated with concentration?
Abstract: In a free-entry non-cooperative oligopoly a correlation between profitability and concentration arises from the indivisibility of firms. Although a 'perverse' negative correlation is possible, most distributions of entry fees across industries yield a positive correlation. © 1986.

Title: Market structure and cooperative advertising
Abstract: Cooperative advertising is advertising whose demand-stimulating effects do not accrue exclusively to the firm that makes the advertising expenditure. This paper examines the effect of market structure on the equilibrium level of cooperative advertising. © 1986.

Title: Monetary disinflation in a simple two-country model
Abstract: A two-country model with sluggish goods and labour markets, efficient financial markets, flexible exchange rates and perfect capital mobility is considered. The rational expectations dynamics are considerably simplified when the effects of real interest rates on investment are small. It can then be shown that simultaneous monetary disinflation has no real effects, whilst independent disinflation leads to output losses at home and gains abroad. © 1986.

Title: Competitive devaluation and the Great Depression
Abstract: Historical accounts indict the devaluations of the 1930s for worsening the Great Depression. To assess the consistency of these arguments, we develop a two-country model of the gold-exchange standard. Its analysis reveals that devaluation under a gold standard need not be beggar-thy-neighbor. Contrary to the thrust of the existing literature, competitive devaluations like those of the 1930s could have hastened recovery from the Great Depression. © 1986.

Title: A characterization theorem for unique risk neutral probability measures
Abstract: Given the existence of a unique risk neutral probability measure, this paper provides a characterization theorem which utilizes prices on traded call options to infer the implied probability law over asset payoffs. © 1986.

Title: Bank size and international lending patterns
Abstract: The exposures of the U.S. commercial banks of different sizes to individual borrowing countries conform to follow-the-customer explanations of international banking. Banks of different sizes, however, seem to give different weights to links with their home country customers. © 1986.

Title: Real versus monetary business cycle theory and the statistical characteristics of output fluctuations
Abstract: Doubt has been cast on the ability of monetary models to explain output fluctuations adequately, for conventional monetary models cannot account for non-stationarity or the permanence of output innovations. This note shows that purely monetary models can account for these characteristics once we allow technology to be endogenous, so that recent statistical work does not constitute a refutation of monetary models of the business cycle. © 1986.

Title: A multiproduct cost elasticity
Abstract: A cost elasticity with useful properties is proven to be inverse to multiproduct scale elasticity. The condition for the theorem is that the output combination as well as the input combination be cost minimizing. Ray output expansion is not needed. © 1986.

Title: Distribution-free estimation in a disequilibrium market model
Abstract: Estimation of disequilibrium market models has almost always been discussed with specific forms for the distributions of the error terms in the demand and supply equations. In this paper, we extend the maximum score method of Manski (1975) to the estimation of parameters in a disequilibrium market model with known sample partitioning. © 1986.

Title: The relative efficiency of a robust generalized Bayes estimator in a linear regression model with multicollinearity
Abstract: This paper uses Monte Carlo techniques to examine the performance of a robust generalized Bayes estimator for a linear regression model when multicollinearity is present. Unlike many improved estimators, this near-minimax estimator performs very well under squared error loss even when the data are ill-conditioned. © 1986.

Title: The exact initial covariance matrix of the state vector of a general MA(q) process
Abstract: The finite moving-average process is studied in state-space form, and its stochastic structure is exploited to derive a closed-form analytic expression for the covariance matrix of the initial state vector. The results provide interesting insight into the state-space structure of moving-average processes, and they minimize the computational requirements for exact maximum-likelihood estimation via the Kalman filter. © 1986.

Title: Inflation and growth
Abstract: In time series modelling, concepts of causality and co-integrability are relevant. This note examines the growth-inflation relationship using Jamaican data. The existence of a long-run relationship is found to be tenuous. © 1986.

Title: Empirical evidence on competitive bidding
Abstract: This paper compares the assumptions and predictions of common values auction theory with OCS leasing data. We find that the general assumption of continuous bid density functions is not supported by the empirical evidence. This leads us to suggest several lines for future theoretical, experimental and empirical research. © 1986.

Title: Non-cooperative bargaining of N ⩾ 3 players
Abstract: Extensions to N ≥ 3 players of Rubenstein's (1982) bargaining model with fixed common discount factor are considered. If voting takes place simultaneously, then any partition of the cake is a subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium outcome. © 1986.

Title: Income flexibility and the Frisch conjecture
Abstract: Frisch's (1959) conjecture on the behavior of the income elasticity of the marginal utility of income is tested by means of regional Italian data. Results offer some support to the empirical validity of the conjecture. © 1986.

Title: The computation of quantity-constrained equilibria by virtual taxes
Authors: O.J.C. Cornielje, G. Van Der Laan
Abstract: A method to compute Drèze equilibria is derived by defining virtual-tax equilibria, giving a constructional proof of the existence of such equilibria and showing the equivalence with Drèze equilibria. Some numerical examples conclude the paper. © 1986.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Evidence on the weak and the strong versions of the screening hypothesis in the United States
Abstract: This paper extends the works of Psacharopoulos (1979), Lee (1980), and Liu and Wong (1982) by controlling for differences in ability and testing both versions of the screening hypothesis. Using micro data from the United States, the empirical results do not support either the theoretical strong or weak versions of the screening hypothesis. © 1986.

Title: Forecasting the German population with Monte Carlo methods
Abstract: This paper presents an approach of constructing confidence intervals by means of Monte Carlo simulation. This technique attempts to incorporate the uncertainty involved in projecting the German population by letting the fertility, mortality and net immigration rates vary as a random variable with a specific distribution. Since fertility and migration are by far the most volatile, and therefore, the most critical components to population forecasting, this technique has the potential of accounting for this uncertainty, if the subjective distributions are specified with enough care. © 1986.

Title: Unemployment insurance and labor supply and demand
Abstract: A disequilibrium model of the U.S. labor market in which the unemployment insurance system plays a key role is estimated. An increase in the level of real unemployment benefits markedly lowers employment and raises real wages. © 1986.

Title: Strategic commitment with R&D
Abstract: When there is multiplicatively separable demand and firms compete in the price dimension, there is no room for strategic use of R&D by firms. Under a different demand situation, strategic use of R&D by firms competing in the price dimension reduces R&D spending, reduces output, increases price, and increases profits of each firm. © 1986.

Title: On the convexity of the portfolio choice set
Abstract: This paper studies the convexity of the set of optimal portfolios in asset space. Recently Dybvig and Ross (1982) have shown by counter example that the optimal set is not always convex. In this letter I provide a necessary condition for convexity and discuss the problem from a geometric point of view. © 1986.

Title: Government expenditure, real exchange rate and the ‘decline’ of the manufacturing sector
Abstract: I show that the increase in government expenditure in European countries during the 1970s raise the relative price of non-traded goods. This relative price movement may explain why the share of manufacturing in private sector value added declined in those countries. © 1986.

Title: Is the interest differential exogenous in interest rate parity?
Abstract: The paper examines the causal relationship between the interest rate differential (INTD) and the forward exchange-rates premium (EXP) with three types of test of daily data between 1979 and 1983 at the Tokyo money and foreign exchange markets and the Euro-dollar market. The tests indicate a strong instantaneous and a bidirectional causal relationship between EXP and INTD. Such relationship was enhanced in the second period after free capital transactions were permitted in December 1980, with INTD's effect on EXP being greater than that in the opposite direction. © 1986.

Title: Gross substitutes and immiserizing growth
Abstract: In a pure exchange economy immiserizing growth occurs when an increase in the endowment of one trader results in a new equilibrium where that trader has lower utility. This paper demonstrates that such perverse behavior is ruled out when excess demands satisfy a particular gross substitute condition. © 1986.

Title: Dynamic properties of error correction models with a stochastic target series
Abstract: This paper deals with error correction models for which the series of target values follow an ARIMA process. The objective is to specify conditions which will guarantee that the difference between the target values and the effective values is stationary of mean zero. The obtained conditions have the form of relations involving the parameters of the model. These relations are easy to verify in any particular case. © 1986.

Title: Assessing the relative efficiency of Hausman's test under Bahadur efficiency considerations
Abstract: This paper examines the relative efficiency of the Hausman test under the concept of Bahadur efficiency. It appears that relative efficiency comparisons depend not only upon the form of the non-centrality parameters, but also upon the value of the information matrix evaluated under the alternative hypothesis. © 1986.

Title: The inadmissibility of the 2SLS estimator in linear structural equations
Abstract: The paper proposes a new estimator for linear structural equations in simultaneous equations models and demonstrates the inadmissibility of the 2SLS estimator for every member of the c-class. As a by-product, the new estimator is also shown to dominate the Stein 2SLS estimator. © 1986.

Title: Minimum mean square error of a generalized Stein estimator
Authors: Lawrence C. Marsh, Michael J. Radzicki
Abstract: This paper generalizes Charles Stein's quadratic loss minimizing estimator and derives the minimum value of its risk. It also re-expresses the generalized Stein estimator as the ordinary least squares estimator using an appropriately transformed X matrix. © 1986.

Title: A test of the independence of subsets of instrumental variables and regressors
Abstract: A Wald statistic is presented to test for the independence of subsets of regressors and instrumental variables and the disturbance in a regression equation. The test does not require that the equation be identified under maintained conditions. © 1986.

Title: Preliminary-test estimation in mis-specified regressions
Abstract: We consider the pre-test estimator of the coefficients in a regression which is mis-specified through the inclusion of extraneous regressors. Risk comparisons of the pre-test, restricted and unrestricted least squares estimators are essentially unaffected by this mis-specification. © 1986.

Title: On an implication of a theorem due to Gorman
Abstract: This letter explores the robustness (in an approximating sense) of a class of demand systems which have been discussed by Gorman. This class is of fundamental interest because it is known to be the only class of demand systems which permits exact aggregation. We discuss the reasons which underlie the fact that one cannot guarantee that an integrable member of the Gorman class can be found which will be as close as one desires to an arbitrary, integrable demand system. © 1986.

Title: Speculative commodity holdings
Abstract: Adopting a mean-variance approach, we characterize the optimal commodity holdings for a risk averse speculator within a discrete time framework. A new factor, namely covariance risk effect, arises which essentially represents the difference between the optimal stock of a risk averse speculator and that of a risk neutral one. © 1986.

Title: Experience rating and premium risk
Abstract: When accident probabilities differ, experience-rated premiums depend on accident history. We calculate the resulting uninsured risk. If the premium rises more after a second than after a first accident, it must be because the distribution of risks is skewed. © 1986.

Title: Do consumers benefit from quantity discounts?
Abstract: A monopoly selling to identical consumers gains at their expense if non-linear pricing is permitted. In contrast, under duopoly non-linear pricing may benefit consumers and lower equilibrium profit. © 1986.

Title: Erratum
Union effects on wages and wage growth
Authors: Solomon W. Polachek, Phanindra V. Wunnava, Michael T. Hutchins
Abstract: This paper employs a pooled cross-section time-series error-variance-components model applied to panel data to present new estimates of the impact of unions on earnings profiles. It avoids union-status measurement errors alluded to by Freeman (1984) contained in current panel estimates by limiting analysis to a set of one-time union status switches for which union status data could be sufficiently cross-checked. It avoids heterogeneity biases by comparing entire earnings profiles for given workers before and after their union status change. Finally, potential selectivity biases in using a non-random sample of only union switchers, is found not to plague the reported results. © 1986.

Title: Selectivity bias and earnings differences by gender and race
Authors: Mark C. Berger, Darrell E. Glenn
Abstract: The effect of selectivity bias on earnings differences due to labor force participation decisions is investigated, using Current Population Survey and Census data. The magnitudes of observed earnings differences by both race and gender are clearly influenced by the presence of selectivity bias. © 1986.

Title: Imperfect information, specificity of schooling and rate of return-migration
Abstract: International migration is a dynamic process. Having moved into a country of destination, a migrant may, after a while, decide to return to his country of origin. The aggregate rate of return-migration among a group of migrants is studied. Imperfect imformation leading to unrealized expectation of the migrants and changes in rates of return to schooling across countries over time are modelled as factors contributing towards return-migration. Schooling is decomposed into schooling acquired before migration and after migration to take account of its specificity to the country in which it is acquired. © 1986.

Title: Are foreign exchange forecasts rational?
Abstract: Tests of rationality in foreign exchange markets have been inconclusive because of disagreement over the relevant asset pricing model. This paper uses a newly available set of data on foreign exchange expectations to directly test the rationality of four foreign currency markets. Overall, the results reject the rational expectations hypothesis. © 1986.

Title: International policy coordination in an uncertain world
Abstract: The gains from international macroeconomic policy coordination are seen to be a decreasing function of the degree of model uncertainty. In practice, therefore, despite the predictions of most theoretical models, the gains from cooperation may be relatively small. © 1986.

Title: Moments of OLS estimators in an autoregressive moving average model with explanatory variables
Abstract: In this paper we derive the moments of the ordinary least squares (OLS) estimators in an autoregressive moving average model by a straightforward technique compared to the one used in Carter and Ullah (1979). The model contains exogenous variables and the technique also provides simpler moment expressions and can be used to derive the moments in more general dynamic models. © 1986.

Title: Wald, likelihood ratio, and infinite induced test statistics for joint one-sided hypothesis
Abstract: The relationship between certain infinite induced test statistics and the Wald and likelihood ratio statistics for testing hypothesis with one-sided alternatives is considered. In addition, it is shown that one of these infinite induced statistics reduces to a simple finite induced test statistic when the Wald statistic is equal to zero. © 1986.

Title: A distribution function of the F-ratio when the Stein-rule estimator is used in place of the OLS estimator
Abstract: In this paper, we derive a distribution function of the improved F-ratio obtained by using the Stein-rule estimator in place of the OLS estimator. It is shown that the test given by the improved F-ratio for the null hypothesis that all regression coefficients are zero can be conducted based on an F distribution, and the power of the test given by the improved F-ratio is lower than that of the test given by the usual F-ratio. © 1986.

Title: Estimation of covariance components for random-walk regression parameters
Abstract: The Hildreth-Houck (1968) random coefficients method is generalized in order to estimate random-walk regression parameters whose covariance components are unknown. The technique contrasts with existing methods which assume the covariance structure is known at least to a scalar. © 1986.

Title: Some new estimators in spatial econometrics
Authors: J.-P. Ancot, J.H.P. Paelinck, J. Prins
Abstract: In the course of spatial econometric work the necessity arises to develop adequate parameter estimators. In what follows, three cases will be developed with the respective solutions that have been adopted. © 1986.

Title: A note on the variability of inflation and the cross-sectional dispersion of stock returns
Abstract: This paper documents a positive relationship between the variance of the inflation rate and the variance of cross-sectional common stock returns which is consistent with the imperfect information hypothesis. We also report that the relationship has changed over time. © 1986.

Title: Optimal consumption, the interest rate and wage uncertainty
Abstract: In an example, we compute optimal consumption policies with wage uncertainty and find that when the time horizon is large enough, wage uncertainty may be ignored. © 1986.

Title: Lexicographic arbitration
Abstract: This paper formulates an arbitration model under lexicographic preferences whose solution is a repeated application of Pareto optimality. If unique, the solution is characterized by four conditions similar to those of Nash (1950) for a bargaining problem. © 1986.

Title: Reversal of asymmetries of allocation mechanisms under manipulation
Abstract: Consider a two-person economy in which resources are allocated so as to maximize agent 1's utility subject to the condition that agent 2 remains at least as well off as he was initially. We show that agent 1, who is explicitly favored by the mechanism, gains nothing by manipulation, while agent 2 can reverse the asymmetry of the mechanism in his favor. We give two other examples of mechanisms for which an analogous reversal of asymmetries takes place. © 1986.

Title: On the stability of non-Walrasian equilibria
Abstract: We present a dynamic disequilibrium macro model which permits non-Walrasian or Keynesian equilibria as stationary states. Unlike the stability results obtained by Varian (1977), and Eckalbar (1979,1980,1981) in a series of papers in the same model, we show that such equilibria have the saddle point property when the real wage rate, the real money balances and expected output demand, all change in disequilibrium. © 1986.

Title: Disequilibrium models with rational expectations
Authors: S.G. Hall, S.G.B. Henry, A. Markandya, M. Pemberton
Abstract: This paper develops and estimates an explicit switching model for the U.K. labour market which includes expectations terms in the labour demand function. These expectations terms are dealt with by using the rational expectations hypothesis. © 1986.

Title: Fair prices exist always in production networks
Abstract: Given a network model of an economic system (e.g., a sector of a regional industrial economy, or an economic-technological system), inclusive the mutual commodity supplies of the nodes in the network and the costs for processing and transportation, it is shown that unique fair prices for the output commodities of the networks exist, provided that each node contributes to these output commodities. © 1986.

Title: The costs of using Frisch demand functions that are additive in the marginal utility of expenditure
Abstract: We outline the implicit restrictions involved in using Frisch demand functions that are additive in the marginal utility of expenditure. © 1986.

Title: Economics Letters
Earnings differentials and occupational segregation by gender
Abstract: Models of male/female earnings differentials which include explanatory variables such as occupational distribution and participation rates are criticized for failing to account for the simultaneity of the relationships involved. An alternative, eight-equation model of earnings differentials, participation differentials and occupational segregation is developed. Application of the model to Australian census data is discussed. © 1986.

Title: On the theory of international trade between capitalist and labour-managed countries
Abstract: This paper attempts to establish a model of international trade between capitalist and labour-managed countries and to reexamine whether or not the basic theorems of the traditional trade theory carry over to environments characterized by the coexistence of capitalist and labour-managed countries. © 1986.

Title: The sensitivity of effective marginal tax rate calculations to alternative arbitrage assumptions
Authors: Michael Daly, Jack Jung, Pierre Mercier, Thomas Schweitzer
Abstract: This paper reports some estimates of effective marginal tax rates under alternative assumptions regarding arbitrage and the relationship between inflation and market interest rates. It is shown that the pattern of tax rates is similar whatever assumptions are used. © 1986.

Title: Targeting rules for monetary policy
Abstract: We develop a framework for the analysis of targeting rules for monetary policy, derive the optimal money-supply rule, and use an explicit criterion to evaluate the relative desirability of other targeting rules governing the money supply process. © 1986.

Title: Comparative statics of degenerate critical points
Abstract: The correspondence principle is shown to apply to extremum problems whose Hessian matrix is degenerate, yielding, in principle, additional refutable propositions about economic relationships. © 1986.

Title: Asymptotic distribution of least squares estimator and a test statistic in linear regression models
Abstract: This paper presents a fairly general and sufficiently weak condition on the observation matrix for the asymptotic normality of the least squares estimator of coefficient vector in a linear regression model. The asymptotic distribution of a statistic for testing the nullity of coefficient vector is also considered. © 1986.

Title: A gradual switching regression model with autocorrelated errors
Abstract: In this note, we set up the gradual switching regression model with autocorrelated errors and show the maximum likelihood estimation procedure. As an empirical example, we examine structural change in the energy demand in Japan at the first oil crisis. © 1986.

Title: On the asymptotic bias and mean squared error of an improved estimator for coefficients in linear regression
Abstract: An estimator for regression coefficients of Kadiyala (1984) is considered. It is proved that the estimator is asymptotically unbiased. The asymptotic weak mean squared error of the estimator is also derived and it is proved that, under certain conditions, the estimator dominates a general class of estimators given by Vinod and Ullah (1981). © 1986.

Title: A simplified method of calculating the score test for serial correlation in multivariate models
Abstract: In this paper we derive the Lagrange Multiplier test for the error process in a multivariate regression model being a first-order vector autoregressive process and show it is asymptotically equivalent to nR2 from an auxiliary regression. © 1986.

Title: Weighted trace minimisation estimation of demand systems
Abstract: It is shown that the small sample performance of the ML standard errors in a symmetry-constrained demand system can be substantially improved by placing restrictions on the covariance matrix. © 1986.

Title: International evidence on output-inflation tradeoffs
Authors: Michael A. Williams, Michael G. Baumann
Abstract: A bootstrap analysis of existing data on international output-inflation tradeoffs is performed. In contrast to some previous empirical work, the results of the bootstrap analysis strongly support Lucas' (1973) rational expectations model of the natural rate hypothesis. © 1986.

Title: Firm's hedging behavior without the expected utility hypothesis
Abstract: In this note we analyze the behavior of a competitive firm under price uncertainty and in the presence of a futures market. We show that the 'separation property', i.e., the independence of the firm's production level of the stochastic price's distribution, holds even if the firm maximizes non-expected utility functional and is not risk averse. Secondly, we show that its behavior in the futures market is the same as in the classical environment, even if one asks for a weaker notion of risk averseness. Finally, we briefly analyze the state-dependent case. © 1986.

Title: Production and hedging decisions in futures and forward markets
Abstract: This paper establishes the properties of (1) separation between production and risk elements, and (2) full hedging under unbiased price even in the presence of basis risk in the futures market. Also, a comparative statics highlights the richer effect of a change in the risk aversion on hedging when futures and forward markets coexist compared to that in the presence of just one market for hedging. © 1986.

Title: A note on job matching with budget constraints
Authors: Susan J. Mongell, Alvin E. Roth
Abstract: Recent papers have obtained results for two-sided matching games in which agents may have complex preferences. This note observes that these results depend on the assumption that firms do not face budget constraints. © 1986.

Title: The bargaining problem: axioms concerning changes in the conflict point
Abstract: Two axioms concerning changes in the conflict point are introduced. A sufficient condition for a solution function to satisfy these axioms is that it satisfies the relatively weak adding requirement of Thomson-Myerson (1980). © 1986.

Title: A new model for decisions under uncertainty
Abstract: A representation for preferences between uncertain acts that is not unduly more complex than the Ramsey-Savage model can simultaneously accomodate Allais's paradox, Ellsberg's paradox, preference reversals and cyclic preferences. © 1986.

Title: On Hotelling's competition with non-uniform customer distributions
Abstract: Hotelling's competition in a two-stage (location, price) game is examined with increasing densities of consumers towards the centre. It is shown that there is a range of, rather even, distributions for which firms locate at opposite ends of the market. As the distribution becomes more concentrated, duopolists will tend to move inside the market. © 1986.

Title: Asymmetric fluctuations in consumption
Abstract: This paper develops simple models of consumption which allow for the possibility that decreases in consumption are less frequent but more severe than increases. Statistical tests provide some support for this asymmetry. © 1986.

Title: Rationing rules and Bertrand-Edgeworth equilibria in large markets
Abstract: In a market with concave downward sloping demand and symmetric firms which compete in prices with constant marginal costs and capacity limits it is shown that the supports of the symmetric (mixed strategy) Nash equilibria converge to the unique competitive price provided that unsatisfied demand is allocated according to the surplus-maximizing rationing rule. © 1986.

Title: Value allocation with economies of scale
Abstract: The Aumann-Shapley Value allocation is shown to be in the Core of a benefit allocation game with non-decreasing returns to scale. The value coincides with the competitive allocation for a cost function that is homogeneous of degree one. © 1986.

Title: On the generic existence of Radner equilibria when there are as many securities as states of nature
Abstract: We show that for a special class of economies with a sequence of markets, parametrized by the vector of initial endowments, Radner equilibria exist generically. © 1986.

Title: Addiction and satiation
Abstract: This letter develops a general model of rational habit formation. The conditions leading to addiction and satiation are compared, and Stigler and Becker's (1977) discussion of beneficial and harmful addiction is clarified and extended. © 1986.

Title: Labor mobility under asymmetric information with moving and signalling costs
Abstract: Information about the true skill level of individual workers may not flow freely across labor markets or between firms, and though available to the workers themselves may not be equally available to some employers. Consequently, the level and composition of labor mobility is affected. In this paper we derive some results concerning the impact of moving costs in conjunction with informational asymmetry upon the level of labor mobility, the skill level of those who move and the effect upon both these variables of costly signalling. © 1986.

Title: A theory of scar unemployment
Abstract: A job search model of scar unemployment is presented wherein it is demonstrated that the escape rate from unemployment decreases with unemployment duration, under fairly general conditions on the offer distribution. A striking and counter intuitive result is that the current reservation wage for a scarred worker and an unscarred worker is the same, when faced with identical search environments. © 1986.

Title: A note on the taxation of exhaustible resources under oligopoly
Abstract: The paper shows that when exhaustible resources are exploited under oligopoly, the optimal tax designed to capture quasi-rents is a sales tax, which also induces competitive behaviour. © 1986.

Title: Market share inertia with more than two firms
Abstract: When there is market share inertia, there may exist an equilibrium in pure price strategies in a duopoly. But when the number of firms is greater than two, such an equilibrium never exists. © 1986.

Title: A note on inertia in market share
Abstract: In a simple model in which market share displays inertia, I show that a larger firm will always charge a higher price and make more profits than its smaller rival, but its market share will remain larger than its rival's. © 1986.

Title: Minimal and maximal product differentiation in Hotelling's duopoly
Abstract: Hotelling's (1929) model of duopolistic competition is re-examined. A family of utility functions is used which has as a special case Hotelling's original utility function. In a two-stage location-price game it is shown that an equilibrium exists when the curvature of the utility functions in the space of characteristics is sufficiently high. The (subgame-perfect) equilibrium never exhibits minimum product differentiation. On the other hand, not all equilibria are at maximal product differentiation. © 1986.

Title: Alternative specifications of the errors in the Black-Scholes option-pricing model and various implied-variance formulas
Abstract: By choosing suitable specifications of the random-error component of the Black-Scholes option-pricing model, each of the commonly-advocated formulas for computing the implied variance of stock price returns is derived herein. © 1986.

Title: Tests of expected real profits in the forward foreign exchange market
Abstract: This paper tests the hypothesis that the expected real profits in the forward exchange contract are zero, as implied by Frenkel and Razin's (1980) stochastic prices model and the assumption of risk neutrality. © 1986.

Title: Sterilization and stability
Abstract: The relation between sterilization and monetization of foreign reserve movements is considered. Existing results of Turnovsky (1976), and Bond and Mitchell (1982) are briefly touched upon. © 1986.

Title: Asset price bubbles from poorly aggregated information
Abstract: We sketch a parametric example of bubbles, i.e., discrepancies between an asset's fundamental value (under full information aggregation) and market-clearing price. We demonstrate for our exponential/gamma example that bubbles exist and can exhibit momentum and overshooting for some values of the information parameters. © 1986.

Title: Biased predictors, rationality and the evaluation of forecasts
Abstract: Optimal, rational forecasts are often biased and thus the empirical finding that actual forecasts are biased is not necessarily evidence of irrational behavior. Using an asymmetric loss function and a regression forecasting problem, these points are explicitly demonstrated. © 1986.

Title: Bootstrapping regression estimators under first-order serial correlation
Abstract: It is well known that with highly trended time series data and strongly autocorrelated disturbances, there will be a marked tendency for standard GLS techniques to over-reject true null hypothesis in finite samples. There is also a potential problem because most applications of GLS are in conjunction with a pretest such as a Durbin-Watson test. An application of bootstrapping to these problems is considered here using a small Monte Carlo experiment; the results provide no evidence that standard bootstrapping provides an improvement. © 1986.

Title: Obtaining any Wald statistic you want
Abstract: While the Wald test can be used to test a non-linear hypothesis in a linear or non-linear regression model it is known that a particular hypothesis can be written in many ways when non-linear forms are permitted. This paper illustrates that it is possible to obtain virtually any value of the Wald statistic at different significance levels. It is also shown that in small samples the use of the χ2 or F approximation for the distribution of the Wald statistic can be misleading for some forms of the non-linear Wald test. © 1986.

Title: Alternative specification tests for Tobit and related models
Abstract: Recently Small and Hsiao (1985) proposed a specification test for the multinomial logit model as an alternative for the Hausman specification test. We show that Small and Hsiao's test procedure can also be applied to Tobit and related models. © 1986.

Title: Mixed regression estimator under misspecification
Abstract: It is shown that the mixed regression estimator (MRE) is better than OLS, under weak MSE criteria, even if the regression model is misspecified; however, if we are interested in prediction, MRE is not always superior to OLS under MSE of predictor criteria. © 1986.

Title: On using Durbin's h-test to validate the partial-adjustment model
Abstract: A Lagrange multiplier test for diagnostically checking the partial-adjustment model is presented. This test is more powerful than the commonly used Durbin h-test because a non-linear restriction on the parameters is taken into account. © 1986.

Title: Small sample properties in a heterogenous Weibull model
Abstract: Neglected heterogeneity implies bias for estimators in, e.g., the Weibull duration model. In a Monte Carlo experiment the proper maximum likelihood estimator is better than a new least squares estimator. The likelihood estimator neglecting heterogeneity is inferior. © 1986.

Title: Enterprise purchases and the expectation of rationing
Abstract: One reason why an excess supply of inputs is claimed not to occur in socialist economies is that the anticipation of future rationing makes managers by up all input materials even if not needed for current production. It is shown with a simple inventory model that such anticipations do shift some input purchases from the future to the present but that the effect can be small for many values of the parameters. © 1986.

Title: An experimental test for risk aversion
Abstract: This paper evaluates an experimental method to measure attitudes to risk in individual subjects. The method is applied to study the degree of risk aversion of 46 subjects. The results lead us to reject a working hypothesis of risk neutrality for such experimental subjects. © 1986.

Title: A new class of sufficient conditions for the first-order approach to the principal-agent problem
Authors: Murray Brown, Shin Hwan Chiang, Satyajit Ghosh, Elmar Wolfstetter
Abstract: The first-order approach can be shown to be valid if the agent's expected utility is pseudoconcave in effort. We derive new conditions on the agent's utility function which insures that the expected utility is pseudoconcave. There is a tradeoff of the stringency of the distribution function (exhibited by the Rogerson-Mirrlees conditions, the MLRC and the CDFC) for stringency of the utility function. The new conditions are independent of the MLRC and/or the CDFC and hence we cannot indicate which are more general. © 1986.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Advertising bans, tobacco and cigarette consumption
Abstract: Advertising of tobacco and cigarettes in the electronic media has been banned in Australia since 1976. Apart from a short-lived initial impact we find that it has not affected cigarette demand but does appear to have had some impact on tobacco consumption. © 1986.

Title: Inflation, relative prices and welfare redistribution in Spain, 1976–1984
Abstract: This paper studies the incidence of the change of consumer goods' relative prices on the welfare distribution among Spanish households between 1976 and 1984. © 1986.

Title: Testing the relationship between work and health
Authors: J.S. Butler, Kathryn H. Anderson, Richard V. Burkhauser
Abstract: A bivariate hazard model which allows the hazards to be correlated shows that decisions about work and health are significantly related. Failure to take the correlation into account will cause selectivity bias. © 1986.

Title: Monetary announcements and stock prices in Israel
Abstract: Responses of stock prices to monetary announcements in Israel are examined. Only the unexpected part of monetary injection announcements are found to have a significant impact on stock prices. Unlike findings for the U.S., this impact is positive. © 1986.

Title: Exchange rate models and innovations
Abstract: An explicit relationship between innovations in the spot exchange rate and innovations in its driving variables is derived in the context of the 'asset market theory' of the exchange rate. The relationship forms a theoretical basis for regression results in 'news' form that have been reported in the literature. © 1986.

Title: Foreign ownership, non-traded goods and the effects of terms of trade changes on national welfare
Abstract: This paper extends the theory of international trade in the presence of foreign ownership to incorporate non-traded goods. It is shown that, with non-traded goods, national and aggregate welfare might move in opposite directions in response to a terms of trade deterioration even when national and aggregate trade specialization patterns coincide. © 1986.

Title: Time-aggregated information and stock price volatility
Abstract: This paper shows that if the dividends of a given stock are paid out only at regular intervals, its price tends to be more volatile and does not follow the random walk process even if a sequence of the dividends follows the random walk process. © 1986.

Title: The causes of bank failures: deflationary spells
Abstract: Unexpected reductions in inflation induce debtor insolvency and bank failures with lags of up to eight years. Outside money is non-neutral because the default of marginal banks and the rising costs of surviving banks reduce the supply of monetary services. © 1986.

Title: Improved estimators in some linear errors-in-variables models in finite samples
Abstract: The paper uses a Monte Carlo study to demonstrate the dominance under mean squared errors or quadratic loss of a new improved estimator for some linear errors-in-variables models in finite samples. The new estimator is non-linear and biased in a conventional sense and has a smaller risk than the least squares and the Stein estimators. Standard errors for this estimator can be conveniently obtained by bootstrapping methods. © 1986.

Title: A simple and efficient estimation method for a non-linear demand system
Authors: Henri Theil, Baldev Raj, Eric M. Diamond
Abstract: A least-squares-type estimation method appears to be about as efficient as maximum likelihood with a known contemporaneous covariance matrix. © 1986.

Title: A necessary and sufficient condition for the dominance of an improved family of estimators in linear regression models
Abstract: This article presents a necessary and sufficient condition for the dominance, with respect to the risk under a general quadratic loss function, of the double k-class estimators (characterized by non-stochastic scalars) over the least squares estimator of coefficients in linear regression models. © 1986.

Title: On studentizing a test for structural change
Abstract: We show that the asymptotic null distribution of the CUSUM of squares test is not robust against deviations from normality, and propose a modification which overcomes this deficiency. © 1986.

Title: The bias of σ in dynamic models
Abstract: This note shows that the usual correction factor applied to the estimator of the residual variance in static models, to get unbiasedness, gives a bias of order O(T-2) in autoregressive models. © 1986.

Title: The bias of the least squares estimator over interval constraints
Abstract: We show that the interval constrained least squares estimator for a regression model is in general bias. The bias and some of its properties are given when the regression residuals are normally distributed. © 1986.

Title: Maximum likelihood estimation of sum-constrained linear models with insufficient observations
Abstract: A maximum likelihood procedure for estimating sum-constrained linear models is presented, which seems to provide a good balance between excessive observational requirements on the one hand and an unduly restrictive specification of the contemporaneous covariance matrix on the other. © 1986.

Title: Asymptotic inference in regression models with autoregressive errors having roots on the unit circle
Abstract: An inference procedure is proposed for regression models with stationary regressors and non-stationary autoregressive errors. It is shown that the usual GLS or Cochrane-Orcutt procedure should be done in reverse order by starting the estimation from the error structure. © 1986.

Title: Symmetric bidding in second-price, common-value auctions
Abstract: That second-price, common-value auctions have a unique symmetric equilibrium is shown by demonstrating a useful property: the equilibrium bid dominates any local common bias. © 1986.

Title: Stochastic rationing by waiting list
Abstract: In a stochastic queueing environment in which participants maximize expected utility, changes in queueing parameters have predictable impacts on waiting list size. For example, a decrease in mean service time cannot produce a decrease in waiting list size when arrival rate and mean service time are functionally independent. © 1986.

Title: Pareto optimal chains of reinsurance
Abstract: Extending Arrow (1963), we show that coinsurance is the optimal insurance scheme if all companies belonging to a chain of reinsurance are risk averse. The extent to which Borch's (1960) theorem and corollary are still valid in this context is investigated. © 1986.

Title: Insurance and Giffen's paradox
Abstract: The letter gives a brief account of how insurance appears as an inferior good in standard economic analysis. It is argued that this result is due to unrealistic assumptions about how insurance premiums are calculated. © 1986.

Title: The behaviour of the cost of living at different levels of real income
The heterogeneity of the consumer's preferences over time
Abstract: The paper uses the individual and overall tests of heterogeneity for two complete PIGLOG models of expenditure equations fitted to discrete survey data to investigate a possible change in the consumer's preferences in Australia between 1975/76 and 1983/84. The evidence lends support to the hypothesis of significant behavioral change and also indicates that this change is attributable mainly to the convolution of the consumption patterns in current housing costs and food. © 1986.

Title: Averting behavior: Does it exist?
Authors: V. Kerry Smith, William H. Desvousges
Abstract: This paper reports the first micro level information on households' reported adjustments in behavior - averting actions - to reduce the risk of exposure to pollutants. The findings are based on a survey of households in suburban Boston and their actions to avoid hazardous wastes. Probit analyses of the factors influencing decisions to undertake these actions indicate that attitude toward hazardous waste risks, confidence in local officials responsible for the problem and information are important determinants of their decisions. © 1986.

Title: Has deregulation decreased the risk of NYSE seat ownership?
Abstract: It is well known that regulatory change led to large capital losses for owners of New York Stock Exchange seats. I show here that deregulation may also have led to a decrease in the risk of seat-holding. © 1986.

Title: The sensitivity of partially regulated second-best prices to intercommodity cross elasticities of demand
Abstract: Ramsey prices for multiproduct monopolists with competitive fringe are shown to be sensitive to cross elasticities of demand. The sensitivity increases with size of cross elasticities, and with size of difference between ratios of cross elasticities and of own-price elasticities. © 1986.

Title: On the presence and absence of free entry in oligopoly equilibria
Abstract: This note provides sufficient conditions for the presence and absence of free entry at Cournot equilibria and some other oligopoly equilibria in a market for a homogeneous commodity. © 1986.

Title: On the desirability of input taxes
Abstract: If it is not possible to tax all final goods, and it is considered desirable to impose positive taxes on currently untaxed goods, then it is desirable to tax inputs and intermediate goods at positive rates. © 1986.

Title: Optimally uniform commodity taxes, taste differences and lump-sum grants
Abstract: Optimal commodity taxes for an economy with many households should be at a uniform proportional rate under certain conditions. These include (i) linear and parallel Engel curves with intercepts dependent on household composition, (ii) separability between goods and labour, and (iii) optimal demogrants. © 1986.

Title: Comparing evidence on Wagner's hypothesis from conventional and ‘real’ data
Abstract: Conventional and internationally comparable data for 34 countries are utilized to assess the relationship between general government expenditure and income. While the conventional data can be deemed as mildly supportive of Wagner's hypothesis, evidence from the ICP data suggests a decline in the share of general government as income per capita rises. © 1986.

Title: The statistical precision of a numerical methods estimator as applied to welfare loss
Abstract: In this paper we derive a variance estimator of a numerical methods technique applied to the calculation of compensated income. The variance calculations can be generalized to other numerical method techniques, and the results are shown to be useful in applied welfare analysis. © 1986.

Title: A conditional least squares estimation procedure for a disequilibrium market model with autocorrelated errors
Abstract: Maximum likelihood estimation of parameters in a market disequilibrium model with unknown sample separation and autocorrelated errors is computationally intractable [Quandt (1981) and Lee (1984)]. This paper presents a computationally convenient conditional least squares procedure for estimation of parameters in this model. © 1986.

Title: Multiple minima and the Cochrane-Orcutt technique
Authors: Leslie T. Oxley, Colin J. Roberts
Abstract: The paper reports the initial results of a Monte Carlo study into the occurrence of multiple minima (sum of squared residuals) in regression models. Likely reasons for such occurrences are discussed including 'symmetry' and the effects of sample size. © 1986.

Title: Utility correlations in probabilistic choice modelling
Abstract: Utility correlations are modelled for discrete choice models via the presence of common multivariate normal components with an additive extreme value random variable independent across choices. Integration of the normal variables by Gaussian quadrature leads to a weighted multinomial logit expression for choice probabilities. © 1986.

Title: Monte Carlo studies on the effectiveness of the bootstrap bias reduction method on 2SLS estimates
Authors: Yu-Sheng Hsu, Kin-Nam Lau, Hung-Gay Fung, Edwin F. Ulveling
Abstract: If first moments exist, two stage least squares estimators are consistent although biased. In this paper several bias correction methods are compared including bootstrap two stage least squares, Nagar's k-class and jackknife estimators for both parametric and non-parametric cases. Monte Carlo experiments on several models investigate the non-large sample properties of these estimators. The results strongly favor the bootstrap procedure judged by the amount of bias reduction and comparative variances. © 1986.

Title: Ideal Divisia moments, price dispersion and inflation
Abstract: Ideal Divisia price and quantity index numbers are computed for 18 countries using per capita consumption data for the 1970's. Correlation matrices of general price change and price dispersion are computed and determinants of price dispersion are analyzed. © 1986.

Title: Matrix scaling of subjective probabilities of economic forecasts
Authors: Robert E. Jensen, Roger W. Spencer
Abstract: This paper illustrates the application to economic forecasting of a recently developed subjective probability scaling technique. The technique entails eigenvector scaling of paired dominance response judgements. Empirical results, derived from conditional probabilities of pairs of economic scenarios, are encouraging. © 1986.

Title: Relative price changes and the real distribution of income
Abstract: The relative increase in the price of food in Brazil is found to significantly deteriorate the real distribution of income. © 1986.

Title: Collusive behaviour in finite repeated games with bonding
Abstract: In finite repeated games, it is not possible to enforce collusive behaviour using deterrent strategies if the state game has a unique Nash equilibrium, because of the 'unravelling' of cooperative behaviour in the last period. This paper demonstrates that under certain conditions, some cooperation among the players can be maintained if they can post a bond which they must forfeit if they defect from the cooperative mode. We show that the incentives to cooperate increase as the period of interaction grows in that the size of the bonds required to deter defection become arbitrarily small as the number of periods in the game increases. © 1986.

Title: Rent seeking and entry
Abstract: It is the purpose of this paper to develop a market equilibrium model of rent seeking with entry. The model determines the optimal amount of rent seeking activities by individuals, the equilibrium number of rent seekers and hence also the total amount of rent seeking in the industry. © 1986.

Title: On the uniqueness of Nash equilibria
Abstract: Although the use of Nash equilibria in economic models has been increasing, little attention has been paid to the uniqueness of these equilibria. This paper presents relatively weak conditions that are sufficient for the existence of a globally unique Nash equilibrium. © 1986.

Title: Erratum
An elegant price flexibility modification to the widely used linear expenditure system
Abstract: Despite the linear expenditure system's wide use, especially in forms accounting for dynamics and demographics, it is too insensitive to cross-price effects to survive without generalization. A price flexibility modification of the model is presented and empirically demonstrated. © 1986.

Title: Interpreting the wage gap estimate from selectivity correction techniques using micro data
Abstract: The selectivity correction techniques lead to two, conceptually different, wage gap estimates. Including the selectivity correction factors in the computation of the wage gap leads to a conditional estimate, whereas excluding them leads to a potential estimate. © 1986.

Title: Sticky prices and purchasing power parity deviations
Abstract: This note tests one implication of the hypothesis that purchasing power parity (PPP) deviations are partly caused by different pricing behavior in goods and asset markets. Cross-country regressions of the variance of PPP deviations on the variance of money supply innovations support the hypothesis. © 1986.

Title: Tax rate effects on interest rates
Abstract: This paper investigates empirically the effects of personal and corporate taxes on taxable interest rates. The results suggest that the effective tax rate of marginal investors in the Treasury bill market is that of households, as opposed to that of tax-exempt institutions or corporations. © 1986.

Title: Finite state markov-chain approximations to univariate and vector autoregressions
Abstract: The paper develops a procedure for finding a discrete-valued Markov chain whose sample paths approximate well those of a vector autoregression. The procedure has applications in those areas of economics, finance, and econometrics where approximate solutions to integral equations are required. © 1986.

Title: A minimax approach to the implicit programming problem
Abstract: Existence results in non-linear analysis and equilibrium models have been unified by the application of Ky Fan's inequality, which is a type of minimax theorem. This inequality is here used to answer the existence question for the implicit programming problem. © 1986.

Title: An aspect of the wald test for linear restrictions in the seemingly unrelated regressions model
Abstract: This paper shows that, in a SUR context, there is an exact relationship between the Wald statistic for testing linear restrictions and the 'F statistic' based upon an estimate of the covariance matrix that adjusts for degrees of freedom. © 1986.

Title: The jackknife and heteroskedasticity
Abstract: The weighted jackknife leads to a consistent estimator for the covariance matrix of the least squares estimators of the parameters in a regression model. In this note we show that this estimator has a simple relationship to the White estimator which is widely used in econometrics. © 1986.

Title: Monte Carlo tests of autocorrelation
Abstract: Barnard's Monte Carlo test procedure can be used to eliminate the problem of the inconclusive region of the Durbin-Watson statistic in an elegant way. In contrast to conventional tests, this procedure can be extended straightforwardly to systems of equations, which is illustrated here for a translog system. An extension to bootstraps, which avoids the normality assumption, is also discussed. © 1986.

Title: A note on the asymptotic lower bound for the covariance matrix of the GMM estimator of the parameters of agents' utility functions
Abstract: This paper derives under simplifying assumptions an explicit expression for the lower bound on the asymptotic variance of the GMM estimate of the curvature parameter of the CRR utility function.
