Category index
Author index
A nested test of the Barten model of equivalence scales
Abstract: The Barten model, as the principal equivalence scale model, has considerable policy importance. It has, however, never been subjected to a statistically satisfactory test. This note proposes a simple modelling artefact that allows the Barten model to be nested and tested in the conventional way. Illustrative estimation is, then, carried out on U.K. budget data. © 1985.

Title: Social welfare losses due to a monopoly
Abstract: We compare the R&D decision of a second best social surplus maximizer to that of a profit maximizing monopolist in a second best world, namely one in which a monopolist makes production decisions. We show that a monopolist underinvests in R&D relative to a second best social surplus maximizer. We show that the expected present value social surplus under a monopoly situation increases with the production technology except at the technology level where a monopolist stops doing R&D. © 1985.

Title: An empirical analysis of analysts' forecasts in the capital asset pricing model
Abstract: Previous theoretical work suggests that it is appropriate to adjust the CAPM for information contained in analysts' earnings forecasts. This paper uses non-parametric statistical methods to test the relation between estimation risk and security returns. The evidence supports the theory that neglected firms earn abnormally high risk adjusted returns. © 1985.

Title: Multinational firms and government policy
Abstract: Taxing MNC capital and subsidizing wages in a dual LDC economy increases national income if and only if MNC employment increases. Unemployment depends on the labour demand elasticity in the traditional sector and the percentage of labour in each sector. © 1985.

Title: Forward implications of a simple stochastic asset market model
Abstract: The behavior of forward rates in a simple stochastic asset market model is investigated theoretically; empirical estimates from the foreign exchanges show the model to be of relevance. © 1985.

Title: On the term structure of the foreign exchange rates and market efficiency
Abstract: The efficiency hypothesis of the foreign exchange market is examined by considering the term structure of foreign exchange rates jointly with that of interest rates in the context of interest rate parity principle. The Canadian-U.S. data are found to be consistent with the hypothesis of the market efficiency and a constant exchange risk premium. © 1985.

Title: ‘News’ and the 1920's experience with floating exchange rates
Abstract: In this paper the 'news' approach to modelling the exchange rate is implemented for the inter-war experience with floating exchange rates. The results are shown to be broadly supportive of similar tests conducted for the 1970's experience with floating. © 1985.

Title: Quotas and retaliation
Abstract: This paper reconsiders the quota retaliation process examined by Rodriquez and Tower. It is shown that their trade-elimination outcome is a consequence of their particularly strong assumption on the distribution of quota rents. Once this assumption is weakened, the tariff and quota retaliation processes become more alike, and the possibility of a non-zero trading equilibrium appears for the latter. © 1985.

Title: The equivalence of the burden of internal and external public debt
Abstract: Abba Lerner's thesis that internal public debt involves no burden to the national economy, but that external public debt does involve a genuine burden, is re-examined. Application of the Ricardian equivalence theorem implies that there is no such asymmetry. © 1985.

Title: A divisia system approach to modelling monetary aggregates
Abstract: A complete system of Divisia partial adjustment asset equations based on the augmented-price expectations Baumol-Tobin inventory and transactions postulates is used to study the dynamic behaviour of monetary aggregates and their components in Australia during 1969.III to 1983.IV. The system provides a new and useful approach to modelling demand-for-money functions for effective monetary policy controls and targetting. © 1985.

Title: Prospective monetary policy and the empirical relation between money and output
Authors: John F. Boschen, Leonard O. Mills
Abstract: This note clarifies the empirical implications of non-neutral, prospective monetary policy. The basic message is that prospective monetary policy, even if empirically important, is not an explanation for the positive correlations between observed money growth and output found in the data. © 1985.

Title: Exact maximum likelihood regression estimation with ARMA (n, n − 1) errors
Abstract: Pesaran (1973) discusses regression estimation with first order moving average MA (1) errors. This paper provides similar closed form expression for the likelihood function in the general ARMA (n, n - 1) case. © 1985.

Title: A note on the mixed instrumental variables estimator in a stochastic regressors model
Abstract: In this note, we examine small sample properties of the mixed instrumental variables estimator in a stochastic regressors model by Monte Carlo experiments. It is shown that the mixed instrumental variables estimator is superior to the instrumental variables estimator in terms of the mean square error when the sample size is small, while Giles (1982) showed that these two estimators have the same asymptotic distribution when the sample size is large. © 1985.

Title: A note on the inefficiency of non-linear estimators
Abstract: An upper bound on the inefficiency of non-optimally weighted method of moments estimators is reported, along with a necessary and sufficient condition for the equivalence of non-optimally and optimally weighted estimators. An example is considered in which a precise expression for the inefficiency bound is attainable. © 1985.

Title: Estimating the trans-log cost function with insufficient observations
Abstract: If the production technology is non-homothetic, efficient estimation of the trans-log approximation requires joint estimation of the cost and share equations. In this note we adopt the method of extraneous estimation to obtain a method of efficient joint estimation when there are insufficient observations on the cost equation. © 1985.

Title: Unbiased estimation of the inflationary effects of relative price disturbances
Abstract: Most recent versions of the expectations-augmented Phillips curve have incorporated terms to capture the effects of relative price disturbances. This paper demonstrates that the standard specification of these equations leads to biased estimates of the coefficients on the relative price terms and that this bias reduces seriously the out-of-sample fit of the price equation. A remedy is suggested that eliminates the source of the coefficient bias and improves the predictive accuracy of the model. © 1985.

Title: Wage indexation and the variability of inflation
Authors: Avia Spivak, J. Weinblatt, B.Z. Zilberfarb
Abstract: The effect of wage indexation on the variability of inflation is empirically tested. The empirical analysis, based on pooling annual data (1954-1976) for eleven countries, provides evidence that wage indexation increases the variability of inflation. © 1985.

Title: A general measure of inflation tax revenues
Abstract: A general measure of the revenues from the inflation tax and seignorage is presented, which is correct across models. Previous measures, seemingly dependent on specific policy assumptions, can be seen as special cases of this unified measure. © 1985.

Title: Time-varying hall consumption function
Abstract: According to the Hall consumption function the level of consumption itself follows a random walk with drift, which, however, recent econometric work fails to support compellingly. While there are many possible explanations for this failure, we pay attention to the neglected possibility that the labour market may not clear, and look at the question of whether labour supply rationing matters for consumption behaviour by using U.S. quarterly data over the period 1948.II-1980.IV. Estimation results both from linear and threshold models are compatible with the hypothesized effects of labour supply rationing on consumption autoregressions. © 1985.

Title: Perfect Nash equilibria in finite repeated game and uniqueness of Nash equilibrium in the constituent game
Abstract: It is shown that when the Nash equilibrium of a particular game is unique then in a perfect Nash equilibrium of the finite repetition of this game the set of actions in each of the successive plays of the game must be a Nash equilibrium of the constituent game. The uniqueness of the Nash equilibrium in the constituent game is crucial for this implication, except in the last play of the repetition. © 1985.

Title: A new formula for the Shapley value
Authors: Norman L. Kleinberg, Jeffrey H. Weiss
Abstract: In this letter we present a simple and straightforward proof of a new formula for the Shapley value. Unlike the usual weighted-average-of-marginal-contributions expression, our formula emphasizes the relative worths of players within each coalition size. © 1985.

Title: Expected utility and revelation of subjective probabilities
Abstract: The subjective probabilities of an expected utility maximizer cannot be inferred from his choices among lotteries. For lotteries with finitely many outcomes, the transformations of probabilities consistent with the given preferences (of an expected utility maximizer) are characterized. © 1985.

Title: Errata
A note on decentralizability in consumer demand models with quantity rationing
Abstract: It is shown that in a context of quantity rationing, it is not always possible to decentralize the consumer's intertemporal behavior in a sequence of atemporal, static optimization programs. Whether or not decentralizability holds crucially depends on the perceived rationing scheme. © 1985.

Title: Bargaining and shift length
Abstract: We examine the determination of shift length, employment and wages in a partial equilibrium bargaining framework. Using the Nash bargaining solution, a number of clearcut results are obtained, perhaps the most interesting of which concern the effects of changes in demand on shift length. In two of the cases examined hours worked are invariant with respect to an increase in demand, whilst in a third shift length actually falls. © 1985.

Title: A general model of customer-class pricing
Abstract: A theory of utility customer-class pricing is developed, and a firm's pricing incentives under various objectives are derived. Rate of return regulation is shown to motivate non-optimal prices in an output counterpart to the Averch-Johnson effect. © 1985.

Title: Retail margins during recession and growth
Abstract: The influence of consumer spending on retail price setting behaviour is investigated in the context of a theory developed in previous research. The results indicate that the effect is not the same for growth and decline of spending. © 1985.

Title: Brain drain, illegal migration and capital exports from less developed economies
Abstract: A model with sector-specific capital is employed to analyze the effects of brain drain on a small open LDC economy when there is limited international mobility of industrial capital and unskilled labor. Brain drain triggers emigration of unskilled labor and capital exports, skilled workers and agricultural capitalists gain, unskilled workers and industrial capitalists lose, and 'demodernization' of the economy results. © 1985.

Title: Terms of trade and national saving rates in Asia
Abstract: In recent theoretical work, Obstfeld, and Svensson and Razin re-examine the Harberger-Laursen-Metzler effect of terms-of-trade changes on the balance-of-payments' current account. Their models of intertemporal utility maximization indicate that individuals' saving responses to a change in the terms of trade are ambiguous in theory. From this they infer that the corresponding movements in the current account are also ambiguous. However, they ignore the positive rate-of-growth effect incorporated in the life-cycle theory on the aggregate saving rate. This paper presents an empirical analysis of the terms-of-trade effect on aggregate national saving rates in 14 Asian developing countries over the period 1961-1981. It turns out to be significantly positive, as the life-cycle model predicts. © 1985.

Title: The Rybczynski theorem in the three-factor, two-good model
Abstract: This paper proves that if each factor is normal in the three-factor, two-good model, the expansion of a factor endowment always increases, at constant commodity prices, the output of the commodity which uses the expending factor most intensively. © 1985.

Title: A problem with the negative income tax
Abstract: The goal of a negative income tax is to increase the work incentives of welfare recipients. This note points out that it may not do so, and empirical simulations show that this is a real-world possibility. © 1985.

Title: Population intervals and the true cost-of-living index with known price distributions
Abstract: This note provides a simple closed form expression for an aggregate cost-of-living index when prices paid differ across consumers. Properties of the lognormal distribution are used to construct a population interval around the index so that a given fraction of consumers have a true cost-of-living index in the interval. © 1985.

Title: A study of economic and financial flows
Abstract: A multi-sector and multi-activity duality-based allocation model is used to study the behaviour of economic and financial flows and their stability in Australia for the period 1959.III to 1983.IV. The findings indicate the existence of allocative instability and reject the unitary income elasticity hypothesis. Financial flows are, however, independent of growth of national disposable income. © 1985.

Title: A linear algebraic procedure for solving linear perfect foresight models
Abstract: This paper presents a failsafe method for analyzing any linear perfect foresight model. It describes a procedure which either computes the reduced-form solution or indicates why the model has no reduced form. © 1985.

Title: Are all asymptotic standard errors awful?
Authors: Walter S. McManus, Mercedes C. Rosalsky
Abstract: Skepticism concerning reliability of asymptotic standard errors in system-wide estimation led us to look at the non-linear single-equation model. © 1985.

Title: The Lagrange Multiplier test for autocorrelation in the presence of linear restrictions
Abstract: This note reports the correct form of the Lagrange Multiplier (LM) test for autocorrelation in a regression model subject to linear restrictions. A principal finding is that homogenous restrictions are imposed in the auxiliary regression of the LM test even if inhomogenous restrictions apply to the original regression model. © 1985.

Title: A clarifying note on the effects of linear approximation on hypothesis testing
Abstract: In this paper we demonstrate that most of the Bera and Byron (1983) results are valid utilising exact sampling distributions, but show how powers can be calculated easily to compare the two alternative tests. © 1985.

Title: Goodness-of-fit for allocation models
Abstract: It is shown that, when the same regressors appear in each equation of an allocation model, one of the feasible measures of goodness-of-fit is a function of a statistic proposed by Deaton (1972); this statistic was found by Bewley (1983) to have excellent small sample properties. It is also shown that the usual R2 is not invariant to the equation being deleted and an alternative measure is suggested. © 1985.

Title: Divisia moments of U.S. consumption, 1929–1982
Abstract: Using U.S. consumption data for 1929 to 1982, Divisia price and volume indexes are computed as well as Divisia variances and covariances. The quantity variances tend to be larger than the price variances, and the majority of the price-quantity covariances is negative. © 1985.

Title: A note on additive utility and bargaining
Abstract: Necessary and sufficient conditions are given under which a decision maker's von Neumann-Morgenstern utility function on the Cartesian product of two prospect spaces can be expressed as a sum of coordinate utility functions, assuming that all preferences are given. A main motivation for this result is an application in axiomatic bargaining theory. © 1985.

Title: Credibility, disinflation and gradualism
Abstract: The following conundrum is examined: Success or failure of a disinflation policy depends largely on expectations of maintained lower money growth. This suggests two equilibria: (a) A policy is expected to be maintained and succeeds; Policy makers are re-elected, maintaining the policy and validating initial expectations. (b) A policy is not expected to be maintained and fails; Policy makers are not re-elected. The policy is not maintained, validating initial expectations. © 1985.

Title: The consumption function and the precautionary demand for savings
Abstract: Under the assumptions of constant absolute risk aversion and serially correlated, normally distributed, income shocks, an explicit solution to the consumer's intertemporal optimization problem is derived which parameterizes the precautionary demand for savings. © 1985.

Title: On the interpretation of income variables in discrete-choice models
Abstract: In certain discrete-choice models, the unestimated function of income may be recovered. However, care must be taken lest inconsistency with choice theory result; the correct interpretation of income in such models affects the computation of quantities such as income elasticities. © 1985.

Title: Erratum
On the optimal resource rent tax
Abstract: This paper originally appeared in Economics Letters, Vol.13, Nos. 2-3 (1983) pp. 263-268. © 1985.

Title: Notes on a new functional form for the Lorenz curve
Abstract: A new functional form for the Lorenz curve was proposed by Kakwani and Podder (1976). n = aπα (√2-π)β. This letter applies this form of the Lorenz curve to Brazilian data and illustrates some problems with it. © 1985.

Title: Divisia moments of Indian consumption
Abstract: Divisia moments of the first and second order are presented for Indian annual price and quantity data separately for 23 and 8 commodity groups of consumption covering the period 1960-1979. Contrary to the results reported for other countries, in a majority of cases the price variances tend to exceed the quantity variancesin both data sets. © 1985.

Title: Human capital and the time-profile of human fertility
Abstract: This paper re-examines a recently proposed model of the intertemporal distribution of births [Cigno (1983)]. Contrary to the author's claims: (a) the optimal time-profile does NOT satisfy the Hotelling rule of natural resource depletion, (b) the implied optimal timing of births is for all women, regardless of their human capital, to concentrate births at the end of the fertile period. This prediction is inconsistent with available empirical evidence. © 1985.

Title: Conventional arbitration, final offer arbitration and the chilling effect
Abstract: The chilling effect of conventional arbitration is demonstrated in a formal model and shown also to apply to final offer arbitration. © 1985.

Title: A non-stationary hazard function of leaving unemployment for employment
Abstract: This paper introduces a non-stationary hazard of exiting unemployment for employment. The source of the non-stationarity is the duration dependent intensity of offer arrivals subject to a Poisson process. Based on these non-stationary offer arrivals and simplifying assumptions, a closed form non-stationary hazard of exiting unemployment is derived using a sequential search model. © 1985.

Title: Sticky wages and adjustment in the Australian labour market
Authors: Philip E.T. Lewis, Gerald H. Makepeace
Abstract: The Mussa price adjustment model is estimated for the Australian aggregate labour market and compared to both the 'full equilibrium' and the 'full disequilibrium' specifications. The evidence suggests that the 'full disequilibrium' model is an appropriate description of the market. © 1985.

Title: Aggregate consumption and allocation of time
Abstract: In contrast to previous studies, this paper includes an investigation of the effects of changing female labor force participation on a macroeconomic rather than microeconomic level. Specifically, it looks at the effects on aggregate consumption of changing family allocation of time between market work and non-market, home production. The composition of income, between labor and asset income, and between market and imputed income, is shown to be a significant determinant of aggregate consumption. Further, home production and market consumption are shown to be complements rather than substitutes and female labor force participation has an effect on consumption in addition to, and independent of, an income effect. © 1985.

Title: Wage prospects and the existence of job queues when the wage is a sorting device
Abstract: We consider a labor market where information is asymmetric. Previous research suggests that excess supply may result in this situation. We find no excess supply if labor suppliers respond to wage prospects - the wage times the probability of employment. © 1985.

Title: Public utility pricing under risk
Abstract: The existing literature on public utility pricing with stochastic demand has reached no consensus on the profitability of pricing and investment policies which maximize expected surplus. This note contributes a theorem which resolves the issue and contains previous results as special cases. © 1985.

Title: Active pegging, rational expectations, and autonomy of monetary policy
Abstract: A simple stochastic model of an open economy is used to analyze the effects of exchange rate policies and variability in the money supply process on monetary autonomy. With deterministic exchange rate policies (active pegging), and assuming serially uncorrelated expectations monetary autonomy can be increased although not without limit. © 1985.

Title: Excess burden and the marginal cost of public spending
Abstract: The relationship between excess burden of taxation and the shadow price of public expenditure is explored. An equality is established between compensated and uncompensated versions of the marginal social costs of taxation. © 1985.

Title: The rates of turnover of money goods under efficient monetary trade
Abstract: The relationship of money good stocks and their rates of circulation under efficient monetary trade is used to rationalize the money stock and velocity aggregates in the equation of exchange. An index number pair is exhibited which is useful for empirical measurement of these aggregates. © 1985.

Title: The positiveness and the uniqueness of a solution
Abstract: This paper presents a sufficient condition which assures the positiveness and uniqueness of a solution for various economic equations and inequality systems. © 1985.

Title: Maximal elements over non-compact subsets of linear topological spaces
Abstract: We provide an extension of Browder's fixed point theorem which is used to prove a very general existence of maximal elements result. This result generalizes previous theorems on the existence of maximal elements. It also corrects a recent claim of Mehta. © 1985.

Title: Estimation and testing in a regression model with spherically symmetric errors
Abstract: In this paper we show that both the restricted and the unrestricted likelihood estimators of the error variance, obtained under normality, are not in general robust against the spherical distribution of errors. Thus, care should be taken in interpreting the residual variances in the applied work. The robustness of Rao's score, Wald's and the likelihood ratio tests, are also analyzed. © 1985.

Title: Lp-norm estimation of non-linear systems
Authors: Henri Theil, Mercedes C. Rosalsky, Walter S. McManus
Abstract: Weighted least squares and L p -norm estimators of non-linear systems are compared in the context of fat-tailed mixtures of multinormal error distributions. © 1985.

Title: Least squares and maximum likelihood estimation of non-linear systems
Abstract: A simple weighted version of least squares appears to be about as good as the conventional maximum likelihood method for the estimation of systems that are non-linear in the parameters. the possible implications for robust estimation are indicated. © 1985.

Title: Positive definite maximum likelihood covariance estimators
Abstract: Covariance matrices are a priori positive definite. Imposing this restriction need not seriously complicate maximum likelihood estimation. The restriction can be incorporated directly into the likelihood function without significantly complicating estimation for a wide class of covariance structures. © 1985.

Title: Testing linear hypothesis on regression coefficients after a pre-test for disturbance variance
Abstract: In this note, we analyze the sampling performance of the two-stage test that tests the linear hypothesis on regression coefficients after a pre-test for disturbance variance. It is shown that the two-stage test has a serious upward bias in size when the degrees of freedom is small, but it gets smaller as the degrees of freedom gets larger and the power of the two-stage test is higher than that of the conventional F test for the linear hypothesis which does not conduct the pre-test. © 1985.

Title: A note on the use of a proxy variable in testing hypothesis
Abstract: In this note, we examine the effects of the use of a proxy variable on the test for an other observable variable. It is shown that using a proxy variable is better than omitting an unobservable variable in terms of the effects on the size of the test for the ohter observable variable. © 1985.

Title: The joint asymptotic distribution of multistep prediction errors of estimated vector autoregressions
Abstract: The joint asymptotic distribution of multistep prediction errors of an estimated stationary vector autoregressive process is given under the assumption that the order of the underlying process is unknown. This result can, for instance, be used to derive the asymptotic distribution of prediction errors of certain non-stationary processes. © 1985.

Title: On the distribution function of various model selection criteria with stochastic regressors
Abstract: It is shown that, at the same level of significance, the power functions of several alternative model selection criteria are identical. We derive the distribution function for the criterion with stochastic regressors and report some calcutions on the power function based on numerical integration. © 1985.

Title: An em algorithm for the heteroscedastic regression models with censored data
Abstract: This paper proposes an EM algorithm for the heteroscedastic regression models with censored data. The uniqueness of the EM algorithm is discussed. An iteratively reweighted least squares estimator is proposed. © 1985.

Title: Wald tests for the independence of stochastic variables and disturbance of a single linear stochastic simultaneous equation
Abstract: Wald test statistics are obtained for the independence of a subset of stochastic regressors and disturbance in a limited information simultaneous equations framework. Simple regressions for obtaining the statistics are presented. The statistics are briefly compared with Hausman and Taylor's (1981) specification test. © 1985.

Title: The equivalence of Hausman and Lagrange Multiplier tests of independence between disturbance and a subset of stochastic regressors
Abstract: This note shows that the Hausman test and Lagrange Multiplier tests of independence between the disturbance term and a subset of stochastic regressors in a regression equation are algebraically equivalent if they are evaluated at the 2SLS estimates of parameters. © 1985.

Title: Anticipated versus ‘surprise’ inflation in household consumption behaviour
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to look at the question of whether it is the anticipated or 'surprise' inflation (or both) that matter for household consumption and saving behaviour. We use a large data sample from 23 countries covering mostly the period 1960-1979. Evidence is overwhelming against the hypothesis that only the 'surprise' part of inflation matters for household consumption and saving behaviour, but is a bit mixed on the question of whether the anticipated and 'surprise' parts of inflation affect with equal force which would 'justify' the observed inflation as the appropriate inflation variable in household consumption and saving functions. © 1985.

Title: Aggregate economic activity and the variance of inflation
Abstract: The time series of forecast errors and forecast variances estimated from Engle's ARCH model are used to estimate the relationship between the volatility of inflation and key macroeconomic variables. This is done using both a Lucas supply framework and a Granger-causality framework; the results of the latter, in particular, are strikingly different from previous work. © 1985.

Title: How to eat a cake of unknown size
Authors: Murray C. Kemp, Ngo Van Long
Abstract: We formulate the problem of managing a renewable resource, the extent of which is known only in terms of a subjective probability distribution. It is shown that, as in the case of non-renewable resources, the optimal path of extraction may be non-monotone but that, in contrast to the case of non-renewable resources, there exists no stationary solution when the probability distribution is exponential. © 1985.

Title: Saving behavior in retirement when life horizon is uncertain
Abstract: We try to explain some recent empirical observations that retired people continue to save in retirement for several years, a behavior which seems to contradict the life-cycle hypothesis. We show that such a behavior is consistent if individuals become more 'optimistic' about their life probability distribution or if individuals become more risk-averse as they age. © 1985.

Title: A Bayesian perspective on biases in risk perception
Abstract: Psychological risk perception studies have shown that individuals overassess low frequency events and underassess high frequency events. This letter develops a new test that reconciles these findings with the Bayesian learning approach frequently used in economic analysis. © 1985.

Title: Competitive bidding with entry costs
Abstract: This paper presents a simple model of competitive procurement, in which potential bidders incur non-recoverable resource costs in preparing bids. The main findings are that equilibrium entry achieves a welfare optimum but that expected procurement cost need not decline with increases in the number of potential bidders. © 1985.

Title: Asymptotic stability of Bayesian updating for Spencian examples
Abstract: Under the assumption of a common prior over a signalling cost parameter, employers revising their beliefs in a Bayesian fashion are shown to converge to a separating equilibrium of Spence's (1974b) continuous ability model. Following him, specific functional forms are used. © 1985.

Title: Risk, discounts and the pricing of indivisible goods
Abstract: We analyze the effect that indivisibilities have on the pricing of goods under imperfect information. We show that risk bearing arguments alone can account for the lower prices per unit of consumption or service of larger indivisible goods or size discounts. This result holds whether or not there are economies of scale in the production of larger goods. © 1985.

Title: Self-insurance, self-protection and increased risk aversion
Abstract: In this paper we study the effect of increased risk aversion upon self-insurance and self-protection activities. We show that for self-protection, increased risk aversion does not always induce an increase in its level while a more intuitive result holds true for self-insurance. © 1985.

Title: Multi-period contracts between principal and agent with adverse selection
Abstract: Multi-period contracts with adverse selection at the time of contracting are studied. With risk-neutrality and independent private information, all inefficiency arises in the first period only. With positive serial correlation, inefficiency is more pervasive but declines over time. © 1985.

Title: Repeated principal-agent relationships with lending and borrowing
Abstract: It is shown optimal long-term contracts are strictly better than a series of unrelated short-term contracts for two reasons: long-term contracts allow risk to be spread over time and the agent's intertemporal choices provide information about the unobservable random variable. © 1985.

Title: Investigating the probability of a voting cycle when the electorate is large
Abstract: For the framework customarily employed to compute the probability of a voting cycle, in the limit as the number of voters approaches infinity the probability of a cycle is either 0 or 1, except in a subset of cases of measure 0. © 1985.

Title: A note on wage indexation in a model with staggered wage setting
Abstract: The purpose of this note is to show that, in the staggered wage setting à la Taylor, exogenous indexation of wages is destabilizing in terms of both prices and output. In a small open economy, the simultaneous application of an exchange rate policy aimed at maintaining purchasing power parity would help in eliminating output variability. © 1985.

Title: Consistent conjecture and free entry oligopoly
Abstract: This paper shows that, in an oligopoly model that allows free entry, only competitive conjecture is consistent for any demand and cost functions and for any conjectural variation function that depends on the firm's own output and the outputs of the other firms. © 1985.

Title: A cross-country time-series analysis of the volume and quality of consumption
Abstract: Using the cross-section results of Kravis et al. (1982) and Working's (1943) model, we provide time series of the volume of consumption per capita and of the quality index for eight OECD countries with base U.S. = 100 in 1975. © 1985.

Title: Income effects and the marginal utility of income
Abstract: It is shown in this note that the marginal utility of income corresponding to a money metric utility function can be computed from price/quantity data plus knowledge of income effects. Information about price derivatives of demand functions (or about the Hicks-Slutsky substitution matrix) is not required. © 1985.

Title: Perfect competition in strategic market games with interlinked preferences
Abstract: When the competitive system is viewed as a strategic market game with a continuum of agents, concern for others need not influence outcomes. The generalization of preference conditions is noted and discussed. © 1985.

Title: Publisher's note
Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Finite-sample power of tests for autocorrelation in models containing lagged dependent variables
The implicit valuation of risks to life
Abstract: This paper reports estimates of the implicit valuation of risk reductions for different sources of risk - on-the-job accidents and exposure to air pollutants. A hedonic wage model estimated using the May 1978 Current Population Survey for individuals in 44 SMSA's provides the basis for the estimates of implicit values of risk. The findings suggest quite different valuations of comparable risk changes. © 1984.

Title: Price and income elasticities of demand for hospital care free of quality bias
Abstract: Our estimates based on a cross-section of time-series for the individual states over 1965-1977 indicate that the elasticity of bed-day demand with respect to net price is -0.20 in the long run and the same with respect to income is 0.40. The variation in the quality of care has been modeled in terms of unobserved error components, correlated with a sub-set of regressors. © 1984.

Title: The hazard rate from unemployment when the search environment is characterised by a decreasing probability of offer
Abstract: When the search environment is stationary, the job search model predicts a monotone increasing hazard rate from unemployment. We show that when the searcher faces a decreasing probability of offer, the hazard may be monotone decreasing or non-monotone. The implications of these results for data analysis are discussed. © 1984.

Title: The importance of the measure of health in empirical estimates of the labor supply of older men
Authors: Kathryn H. Anderson, Richard V. Burkhauser
Abstract: When a more objective measure of health is used, economic variables previously masked by self-reported health measures are found to significantly affect work effort of older men. This may explain differences in results of previous studies even when the same empirical specifications are used. © 1984.

Title: Factor intensity rankings in U.S. production
Authors: John L. Solow, Deborah A. Johnson
Abstract: This paper examines whether we can in general characterize goods as having unambiguous relative factor intensity rankings. We calculate correlation statistics for relative factor intensities for a three-factor, thirty-one good disaggregation of U.S. production. We find that we can generally characterize goods as being either energy intensive or non-energy intensive, but that we can not characterize non-energy intensive goods as being either capital intensive or labor intensive. © 1984.

Title: The effect of ownership on market value and risk of R&D intensive firms
Abstract: This paper tests the effect of ownership on market value and risk for R&D intensive firms. It seems that ownership has a positive effect on firms' market value but not on sales. This is consistent with the view that owner controlled R&D intensive firms are less risky. © 1984.

Title: Input market surplus
Abstract: This note establishes the exact relationship among input and output market Marshallian surpluses and input-user industry profit when said industry is imperfectly competitive. The results are useful both for valuing an input price change and for estimating the degree of competition in the user industry. © 1984.

Title: Monopoly regulation, quality choice and welfare
Abstract: We extend the analysis of regulation to the case where a domestic monopolist produces goods of variable quality and is facing competition from foreign firms. In contrast with the closed economy case, we show that because of import competition, looser price regulation becomes more desirable. © 1984.

Title: The impact of concentration and elasticity on line of business profitability
Authors: William F. Long, David J. Ravenscraft
Abstract: This paper explores the roles played by concentration and elasticity in a model of line of business profitability. It concludes that the roles are conceptually distinguishable, that concentration has a seperate effect on profit (via the degree of collusion) which is not eliminated by its dependence on elasticity, and that assertions about a bias due to the exclusion of elasticity are based on incomplete theoretical foundations. © 1984.

Title: A closed loop analysis of competitive innovation
Abstract: Using dynamic programming, the symmetric, closed loop equilibrium of an oligopolistic market with competition in R&D is derived. Numerical analysis indicates that increasing the number of market firms improves economic performance. This differs from the result obtained by Spence (1982). © 1984.

Title: On the relationship between Macaulay's bond duration and the term to maturity
Abstract: This letter presents a mathematically tractable expression of Macaulay's bond duration which is then used to examine analytically the relationship between a bond's duration and its term to maturity. © 1984.

Title: Risk aversion and weekly money
Abstract: The risk premium hypothesis suggests that absolute changes in short-term interest rates will be larger if the unanticipated component of the Federal Reserve's weakly money supply announcement is positive. Statistical tests suggest, however, that the magnitude of interest rate changes is unrelated to the sign of monetary surprises. © 1984.

Title: Generalization of M(x)-matrices
Abstract: Square matrices with properties such as non-negativity, diagonal dominance and equal row sums frequently occur in mathematical economics. In this paper Sierksma's matrices of class M(x) are generalized to multisector models and are applied to the problem of pooling cross-section and time series data. © 1984.

Title: Predicting the change in the cost of living
Abstract: When the publication of quantity data lags behind that of price data, approximations are necessary for the computation of the cost of living. We evaluate the improvement of the approximation which results from the use of an estimated system of demand equations. © 1984.

Title: Significance tests in the presence of model uncertainty and specification search
Abstract: A simple method of testing the significance of a parameter in the linear model in the presence of uncertainty concerning the appropriate specification of the rest of the model is derived based on an Edgeworth expansion for the posterior distribution. © 1984.

Title: Coefficient values and the dynamic properties of econometric models
Abstract: As a tool to simplify an econometric model dynamically, this paper proposes to interpret sums of elasticities of eigenvalues. It is demonstrated that this approach unifies and generalizes some known related procedures. © 1984.

Title: A joint test for serial correlation and heteroscedasticity
Authors: Maxwell L. King, Merran A. Evans
Abstract: The problem of testing jointly for first-order autoregressive and heteroscedastic disturbances in the linear regression model is considered. A test which is most powerful invariant in a predetermined neighbourhood of the alternative hypothesis parameter space is proposed. © 1984.

Title: A class of almost unbiased and efficient estimators of regression coefficients
Abstract: In this paper we develop a family of approximately unbiased non-linear estimators and show that they are more efficient than OLS as well as improved biased estimators. © 1984.

Title: Estimation of the correlation coefficient in a bivariate probit model using the method of moments
Abstract: A consistent method of moments estimator is derived for the bivariate probit model when the regressors are multivariate normally distributed. In more familiar settings, the estimator is useful for exploratory work and provides a close starting point for the MLE. © 1984.

Title: Omitted variables in a weibull regression model
Abstract: Asymptotic biases of maximum likelihood and least squares estimators in a Weibull model, subject to omitted variables, are given. The results are contrasted to those of a small sample Monte Carlo experiment. © 1984.

Title: Recursive competitive equilibrium
Abstract: In this paper we demonstrate how the neoclassical model of stochastic growth can be decentralized in a recursive competitive framework. We provide a closed form parametric example to facilitate a conceptual understanding of the more abstract variations of this line of research. © 1984.

Title: Cross-country demand systems and centrally planned economies
Authors: Leon Podkaminer, Renate Finke, Henri Theil
Abstract: The cross-country data of Kravis et al. (1982) include data on four centrally planned economies. The question is addressed as to how such data fit cross-country demand systems. © 1984.

Title: Increasing risk and consumption-saving decisions
Abstract: In the two-period, consumption-savings model with uncertain returns on savings, increasing relative risk aversion in the sense of Ross and boundedness of the utility function will unambiguously sign the response of the optimal savings rate to a mean-preserving increase in risk. © 1984.

Title: Hedging and the competitive firm under price, output and quality uncertainties
Abstract: This paper presents a model of the risk-averse competitive firm choosing output and forward contracts under price, output and quality uncertainties and investigates conditions under which the firm's output choice becomes independent of both the firm's attitude towards risk and that towards uncertainty. © 1984.

Title: An example of a dominance approach to rational expectations
Abstract: Dominance and independence produce an alternative approach to rational expectations in a simple stationary overlapping-generations model. Dominance and independence delimit rational behaviour, but predict a range of rational choice rather than a single rational choice. In particular, a coherent interpretation of multiple rational expectations equilibria is provided. © 1984.

Title: The impossibility of a non-discriminating liberal
Abstract: This letter is concerned with establishing an incompatibility between, on the one hand, a principle of non-discrimination which bears a resemblance to Ronald Dworkin's notion of the 'right to equal treatment' and, on the other, a principle of liberty due to Amartya Sen. © 1984.

Title: Smooth versus discontinuous mechanisms
Abstract: This note provides an example of a social choice rule which can be implemented in Nash-equilibrium strategies by a discontinuous mechanism, while there does not exist a smooth implementing mechanism. © 1984.

Title: Urban unemployment and urban development
Abstract: A dynamic model of a dual economy has been developed with specialization in production in the urban and the rural sector and with the Harris-Todaro migration mechanism. It appears that there is no conflict between a programme of urban development and the solution to the urban unemployment problem. © 1984.

Title: Another look at symmetry testing
Abstract: This paper explores implementable alternatives for the F test of Slutsky symmetry when the contemporaneous covariance matrix of the error terms is unknown. The power of the test is also considered. © 1984.

Title: A direct proof that zero degree homogeneity, monotonicity, and quasiconvexity of the indirect utility function implies negative semidefiniteness of the slutsky substitution matrix
Abstract: In this paper, negative semidefiniteness of the Slutsky substitution matrix of a system of utility-maximizing consumer demand functions is proved directly from the properties of zero homogeneity, monotonicity and quasiconvexity of the indirect utility function and Roy's identity. © 1984.

Title: Maximum likelihood and minimum information estimation of allocation models with fat-tailed error distributions
Authors: Lennart R. Flood, Renate Finke, Henri Theil
Abstract: The ML and MI (minimum information) approaches to the estimation of allocation models, proposed by Theil et al. (1984), are extended to models whose error vectors are fat-tailed mixtures of multinormal distributions. © 1984.

Title: The existence of mixed-strategy equilibria in a price-setting oligopoly with convex costs
Abstract: This paper shows that a mixed-strategy equilibrium will exist in an industry producing a homogeneous product with perfectly informed consumers if firms are identical, and have weakly-convex costs. This generalises an earlier result by Dasgupta and Maskin. © 1984.

Title: The cost function given imperfectly flexible capital
Authors: Robert A. Becker, Daniel F. Spulber
Abstract: The properties of the firm's cost function are examined when investment is irreversible and there are costs of capital adjustment. The effects of the firm's initial capital stock on total, marginal and average costs are analysed. © 1984.

Title: Another perspective on changes in international inequality from 1950 to 1980
Abstract: Real income data derived from the third phase of the International Comparisons Project are used to compute Theil's population-weighted indices of intercountry inequality for several years between 1950 and 1980. Contrary to some recently reported results, a substantial increase in inequality is observed. Internationally comparable consumption data indicate consumption inequality increased more than income inequality. © 1984.

Title: Distributional effects of true economic indexes
Abstract: Generalized integrable Working system parameter estimates are used to construct the true differential indexes of (a) the cost of living, (b) the real income, and (c) the marginal prices to study distributional effects of inflation and real income in Australia over the period 1970.IV to 1983.II. The findings provide useful results for disaggregate household analysis and reveal the severe bias of aggregate indexes in sectoral studies of economic welfare. © 1984.

Title: Migration, unemployment and development
Abstract: A time-minimizing problem of attaining a full employment state is solved in a dual-economy model with Harris-Todaro migration mechanism and with a positive level of urban unemployment in the starting period. It appears that the optimum solution lies in the specialization of investment in the urban sector at least in the initial stage of development if the per-capita capital stock in the urban sector is very small in the starting period. © 1984.

Title: Estimates of the generalized working model
Authors: Murray D. Smith, Kenneth W. Clements
Abstract: This paper presents estimates of the one-parameter generalization of Working's (1943) model proposed by Laitinen et al. (1983). © 1984.

Title: Optimal R&D levels when firm j benefits from firm i's inventive activity
Abstract: We amend the static model of industry structure in Dasgupta and Stiglitz to include external benefits from a firm's R&D. Now 'the market' can be seen to underinvest in R&D relative to the social optimum. The work of Mansfield suggests that such external benefits are pervasive. © 1984.

Title: The over-capitalization effect with diversification and cross subsidization
Abstract: This paper examines diversification and cross subsidization in the context of an Averch-Johnson model. Even if the allowed rate of return is less than the cost of capital, the over-capitalization effect exists provided the firm is sufficiently diversified. © 1984.

Title: On the consistency of consistent conjectures
Abstract: A Consistent Conjectures Equilibrium, CCE, requires that firms be correct in their beliefs concerning rival behavior. This paper presents conditions which ensure equivalence of CCE's in price and quantity models of oligopoly. © 1984.

Title: On the effects of differentiated income taxation on portfolio selection
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to show within a simple two-asset portfolio selection model with one safe and one risky asset that, in contrast with the results of standard consumer theory, (i) the own substitution effects of changes in tax rates on the safe and risky asset are indeterminate and that (ii) the cross-substitution effects are asymmetric. Moreover, given the reasonable assumption of decreasing absolute risk aversion these results imply that the comparative statics of differentiated income taxation with full loss offsets yields ambiguous signs in all cases. © 1984.

Title: Term structure variance bounds and time varying liquidity premia
Abstract: Including a time varying liquidity premium in Shiller's variance bound does not reverse Shiller's conclusion that long-term interest rates are too volatile relative to short-term rates to be explained by the rational expectations model of the term structure. © 1984.

Title: On the valuation of currency options and exchange rate insurance programs
Abstract: This paper provides pricing formulae for European and American call and put currency options. It then uses these formulae to show that the current systems of exchange rate insurance programs give rise to multiple effective exchange rate systems. © 1984.

Title: Oil news and the petropound
Abstract: In the context of the 'news' approach, it is shown that shocks to expected UK oil revenues, as measured by the index of oil sector share prices, can help to explain the fluctuations in the UK pound/US dollar exchange-rate from the late seventies onward. © 1984.

Title: The identical country assumption and CPI inflation adjustment processes in a two-country world under flexible exchange rate regime
Abstract: In a world composed of a key country plus a home country, anticipated money stock disturbances in the key country produce adjustment in the home country CPI inflation rate which is decreasing in the parameter 'l' of the home country. © 1984.

Title: Social classes and state behavior
Authors: Ben van Velthoven, Frans van Winden
Abstract: Van Winden (1983) developed the interest function approach to the study of politico-economic phenomena. It starts from the familiar premise that economic agents have preferences with regard to the results of economic and political processes. This paper develops a behavioral model with four classes of participants in the system and attempts to estimate the behavioral influences of these groups on the state. © 1984.

Title: Measuring the opportunity cost of holding money
Abstract: This paper tests the statistical importance and forecasting performance of a term structure money demand equation relative to two competing specifications. The evidence indicates that the term structure specification is preferred to one using a long-term interest rate, but not a short-term rate. Forecasts for 1981-1982 reveal that the term structure model is preferable to both alternatives. © 1984.

Title: The policy evaluation problem and the demand for money
Abstract: This paper applies the Lucas policy evaluation proposition to the money demand function. We find some support for the hypothesis that the decrease in serial correlation of interest rates since the Fed policy change in 1979 has resulted in an increase in the estimated elasticity of money demand. © 1984.

Title: Duality in fixed point theory of multivalued mappings
Abstract: This paper gives some applications in economics of the duality in fixed point theory of multivalued mappings. The existence of maximal elements for preferences is proved under dual conditions on the preference correspondences. © 1984.

Title: A simple way of determining the supply side in macroeconomic models
Abstract: This paper suggests a simple way for determining the supply side in macroeconomic models based on a clay-clay type vintage production model. Shown is how production capacity and utilization rates can be quantified for Germany, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom and the United States. © 1984.

Title: Some simple but flexible differential consumer demand systems
Abstract: Three differential consumer demand systems are proposed, each of which has some particular advantages over the well-known Rotterdam model. In each demand equation only two explanatory variables are used: real income and the relative own-price. The features of the most preferred model are: PIGLOG/Working-Leser Engel curves, a limited number of parameters while no preference independence is assumed, and easy estimation by (iterated) OLS, taking into account all theoretical restrictions, even in case of a large number of commodities. © 1984.

Title: Modeling a competitive industry with entry
Abstract: This paper discusses the structure of econometric models of partial equilibrium analysis in industry in which entry and exit occur over time and are endogenous to the equilibration process. Specification and intertemporal structure of the suitable econometric model is discussed. © 1984.

Title: Testing for linear and log-linear regressions with heteroscedasticity
Abstract: This paper considers the problem of jointly testing for linear and log-linear regressions with heteroscedasticity. Lagrange multiplier tests are suggested; which do not require the heteroscedastic structures to be specified and are computationally easier than likelihood ratio tests. © 1984.

Title: How trustworthy are the standard errors of translog coefficients?
Authors: Lennart R. Flood, Mercedes C. Rosalsky
Abstract: A simulation study indicates that the conventionally computed asymptotic standard errors of the ML estimates of the parameters of the indirect translog model underestimate the true variability of these estimates. © 1984.

Title: Sequential search without reservation price
Abstract: For a consumer who searches sequentially from a known distribution, but subject to a budget constraint, the optimal search policy does not necessarily have a reservation price and may generate demand curves with positively sloped segments. However, absence of risk aversion and inferiority is sufficient to avoid these implications. © 1984.

Title: Moral hazard with a finite number of states
Abstract: Pure moral hazard situations with a finite number of underlying states and multidimensional actions are considered. Conditions are derived under which the first-best can be achieved. It is shown that the absence of resource constraints is important for this result. © 1984.

Title: On alternative methods of generating risk sensitive decision rules
Abstract: Certainty equivalent decisions are risk neutral with respect to uncertainty about outcomes. This note compares the characteristics of different risk sensitive rules for multiperiod decisions. Distinctions are drawn between the complete density function, the mean-variance, ant the generalised utility approaches. © 1984.

Title: Participation constraints in the vickrey auction
Abstract: Economic agents are characterized by two privately observable parameters: their willingness to pay for an item being auctioned, and their reservation utility level which must be exceeded, in expectation, to induce them to participate in this auction. This creates a situation in which the distribution of willingness to pay among the bidders is endogenous. For the case in which the parameters are jointly uniformly distributed, the existence of an equilibrium is proven and characterized. © 1984.

Title: On increasing risk in incomplete markets
Abstract: It is shown that, in the absence of insurance markets, an increase in risk may be beneficial to all consumers. Sufficient conditions to exclude this possibility appear as extremely restrictive. © 1984.

Title: A reformulation of Chichilnisky's impossibility theorem
Abstract: Continuity of social choice is reformulated in terms of the quotient topology on profiles of individual preferences induced by the equivalence class corresponding to anonymity. It is shown that Chichilnisky's impossibility continues to hold. © 1984.

Title: Generalizing the composite commodity theorem
Abstract: The composite commodity theorem is shown to hold for the case where the goods being aggregated face a convex choice set determined by the intersection of a collection of linear constraints. Non-convexities in the choice set generally invalidate the result. © 1984.

Title: Budget share transitions in the Netherlands, 1952–1977
Abstract: Budget share transitions and their components are displayed for 10 broad consumer goods. The decrease in the budget share of food is dramatic; the increase in the share of medical care is quite substantial. © 1984.

Title: Rotating credit collusion in repeated auctions with a single buyer and several sellers
Authors: Soo Hong Chew, Mei Hui Mao, Stanley S. Reynolds
Abstract: This note follows an earlier paper [Chew and Mao (1983)] which investigated the Nash equilibrium strategies in a repeated bidding institution called the rotating credit association. We study a parallel application of the rotating credit structure for tacit collusion among several sellers with a single agent buying an indivisible commodity from them at regular intervals via sealed-bid auctions. © 1984.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Corrigenda
On the capitalization of land improvement projects
Abstract: A model of two cities is presented to provide sufficient conditions for the value of a capital improvement to be underestimated by the change in land rents. © 1984.

Title: A measure of income inequality in the U.S. for the years 1952–1980 based on the beta distribution of the second kind
Abstract: This paper presents Gini measures of inequality for the U.S. size distribution of total income for the years 1952-1980. A beta distribution of the second kind is used as the hypothetical statistical distribution to approximate actual empirical income data; we then examine the fit of the distribution and conclude that the beta distribution provides a good approximation to the actual empirical income data. © 1984.

Title: A note on the calculation and interpretation of the Gini index
Abstract: We derive a convenient way to calculate the Gini coefficient, using the covariance. Our approach improves on accuracy since, unlike other approaches, it requires no aggregation. We also point out some intuitive ways of interpreting the Gini. © 1984.

Title: Demand aggregation and integrability of the HOGLEX demand function
Abstract: We find indirect utility and expenditure functions and the implications of Slutsky symmetry for the HOGLEX demand function X(p,y) = yα(p)B(p)+ yC(p). These implications restrict the usefulness of the HOGLEX function in the theory of preference aggregation unless α is constant. © 1984.

Title: Some microeconomic evidence concerning the determinants of saving through private pension funds in the U.S.
Authors: J. David Cummins, J. François Outreville
Abstract: This note presents some new evidence about determinants affecting the contributions to private pension plans. Through the bargaining process, employer decisions about pensions reflect employee preferences. According to our estimation results on a time series basis, there is a clear significant relationship between the firm variables, Social Security taxes and Saving through private pension plans. © 1984.

Title: Residential demand for liquid petroleum gas
Abstract: This is the first micro-based study of residential demand for liquid petroleum gas (LPG). The data are from DOE's Residential Energy Consumption Survey. Results are compared with elasticity estimates derived from the same data set for the three other main residential fuels. LPG has a price elasticity for space and water heating combined of -1.3. Income elasticity is 0.207. © 1984.

Title: Monetary policy and exchange rate stability in open economies
Abstract: The solution to a model of exchange rate, price, and wage dynamics is studied by considering the choice of monetary policy reaction function parameters which form part of the solution. Leaning against the wind (for example, choosing parameters to contract the money supply when the exchange rate depreciates above its equilibrium value) is a stabilizing policy reaction; analysis also shows that passive policy, end even a policy of leaning with the wind, can be undertaken on some occasions without generating a vicious circle of wage and price inflation and exchange rate depreciation. © 1984.

Title: Estimating invisible trade on aggregate time-series data in the presence of large measurement errors
Abstract: Swedish data on exports of invisibles comprise extremely large measurement errors due to underreporting. The exact nature of the error term is not known. A robust regression method was therefore employed in estimating a forecasting model for invisibles. Owing to the nature of aggregate time series, the differences between the robust and OLS estimates were smaller than one could expect. © 1984.

Title: Protection and the harmful effects of endogenous capital flows
Abstract: Assume a country has in place a binding tariff, and is a price taker on world markets in which capital is internationally mobile and unimpeded. Regardless of trade patterns, possible specificity of capital, or factor intensities, an increase in the tariff harms the country if capital is frozen, and harms the country even more when capital mobility brings rates of return into line among countries. © 1984.

Title: Theory and practice in optimal aggregation of linear models
Abstract: This paper gives a new presentation as well as extensions of results on optimal aggregation of linear prediction models. The extensions concern optimal disaggregation and a very simple heuristic for obtaining partitions of the set of exogenous variables. Criteria for the evaluation of partitions in the special case of input-output models are described. © 1984.

Title: A generalization of the ‘maximum theorem’
Abstract: This note generalizes the well-known 'Maximum Theorem' [Berge (1963)] to include cases with discontinuous objective functions without any loss in the structure of the derived choice correspondence. © 1984.

Title: A note on estimating and testing exogenous variable coefficient estimators in simultaneous equation models
Abstract: The exact distribution of 2SLS estimators of exogenous variable parameters is derived conditional on the endogenous parameter estimates. An approximate signific ance test is then developed for which lower bounds for the critical values are found from the F distribution. © 1984.

Title: On double k-class estimators of coefficients in linear regression
Abstract: In this article we provide a technique to obtain an unbiased estimator of the mean squared error of any double k-class estimator of coefficients in linear regression and illustrate its use to obtain conditions under which this estimator has smaller mean squared error than the least squares estimator. © 1984.

Title: Declining productivity revisited
Authors: Stuart D. Allen, Albert N. Link
Abstract: Dickens (1982) argued that the productivity slowdown since the mid 1960s is cyclical and not a long-term trend. This letter tests the robustness of Dickens' conclusion, specifically with respect to labor productivity. © 1984.

Title: A welfare analysis of convergence to rational expectations
Abstract: This paper investigates a model with intertemporally inconsistent preferences where individuals begin by making mistakes and converge to rational expectations. It is shown that the properties of rational expectations do not carry over to paths that monotonically converge to RE and that, if individuals begin by making mistakes, then everyone cannot benefit by convergence to rational expectations. © 1984.

Title: Moral hazard
Abstract: It is shown that the condition justifying the use of the agent's first-order condition to describe his optimal action in a principal-agent situation with pure moral hazard is related to, but not the same as, diminishing returns to effort. Examples are provided to illustrate the joint implications for the production function, the nature of the underlying uncertainty, and the disutility of effort. © 1984.

Title: A comment on two concepts of risk premia and certainty equivalents
Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to examine alternative univariate definitions of the risk premium which are applicable in cases of moral hazard where a decision variable affects the risk premium. An appealing definition is the maximum of the objective function under certainty minus the selling price of the risk. The welfare significance of this risk premium is examined. The competitive firm under price uncertainty serves to exemplify the results. © 1984.

Title: On the consistency of Kelly's principle of liberalism
Abstract: In establishing the 'impossibility of a just liberal', Kelly has made use of a notion of liberalism which, it is argued in this letter, is not internally consistent. © 1984.

Title: More on symmetry-constrained estimation
Abstract: This paper extends the Fiebig-Theil (1983) simulation experiment to other specifications of the error covariance matrix. Also, a promising method of testing Slutsky symmetry is suggested. © 1984.

Title: Minimum information estimation of allocation models
Authors: Henri Theil, Renate Finke, Lennart R. Flood
Abstract: A promising method of estimating the parameters of allocation models is that which minimizes the average information inaccuracy. Simulation experiments for two different models indicate that this method is superior to maximum likelihood when the contemporaneous covariance matrix of the error terms is unknown. © 1984.

Title: A time series analysis of a demand system based on cross-country coefficient estimates
Abstract: Annual Dutch consumption data (1952-1977) for 10 goods which exhaust the consumer's budget are analyzed by means of a complete demand system whose coefficients are obtained from the cross-country data collected by Kravis. (1982). © 1984.

Title: An observation on gross substitutability and the weak axiom of revealed preference
Abstract: It is shown that if there are three commodities or less, an excess demand function that fulfills the property of Gross Substitutability satisfies also the Weak Axiom of Revealed Preference. © 1984.

Title: Chaotic price behavior in a non-linear cobweb model
Abstract: The cobweb model for the evolution of prices is considered with backward bending supply curves and multi-valued demand curves. These deterministic, non-linear dynamical systems are shown to exhibit a broad spectrum of complex time behavior including stable periodic cycles of arbitrary order and chaos. © 1984.

Title: An extended version of minimum information estimation of allocation models
Abstract: The minimum information approach proposed by Theil et al. (1984) for the estimation of allocation models is extended to include Strobel measures for goodness of fit and bootstrap replications for standard errors. Also, a comparison is made with maximum likelihood results. © 1984.

Title: The behavior of the cost of living at different levels of real income
Abstract: The cost of living in the Netherlands from 1952 to 1977 is analyzed at three different levels of real income. The increase in the cost of living is larger for the more well-to-do. © 1984.

Title: Utility measurement
Abstract: A simple proof, making use of no prior results, is given of Oskar Lange's conjecture regarding the axiomization of cardinal utility. © 1984.

Title: Price setting supergame with different costs
Abstract: This paper applies supergame theory to a price setting duopoly where the two firms produce perfect substitutes with different costs. It is generally believed that technological progress increases welfare. It is shown that technological progress of the higher cost firm can lead to welfare loss in a price setting supergame. © 1984.

Title: On the frequency of the transfer paradox
Abstract: It is shown here that the transfer paradox (TP) might be very common in reality. Almost every world with m≥3 countries and two commodities possesses many initial states where TP occurs at a unique and stable equilibrium. © 1984.

Title: Household formation and the failure of intergenerational resource allocation
Abstract: The present paper introduces a (biological) reproduction process of households into Barro's simple overlapping generations model with bequests. This leads to a model in which capital will typically be underaccumulated relative to the socially optimal level because of the coordination problem regarding bequests. © 1984.

Title: On approximate cores of non-convex economies
Authors: Birgit Grodal, Walter Trockel, Shlomo Weber
Abstract: In this note we investigate, for non-convex finite economies, the relationship between the existence of approximate core allocations and the size of an economy. © 1984.

Title: Erratum
On the effects of minimum-lot-size zoning
Abstract: A simple model is presented of a small, open city which requires new residents' houses to occupy a minimum land area. It is shown that increasing the required land area must increase the value of new houses, and decrease the unit price of land. © 1984.

Title: Direct tests of the life-cycle hypothesis using systems of generalized integrable consumption functions
Abstract: The life-cycle hypothesis is tested by means of a system of generalized integrable consumption functions fitted to Australian expenditure and income survey data for different age groups. In this system, the distinction between consumption needs and work-related expenses is accentuated. Our findings reject the hypothesis in relation to aggregate expenditure but give it favourable support in the conditional consumption of necessities such as fuel, food, vice, clothing, and medical and health care. © 1984.

Title: Normative indices for measuring social mobility
Abstract: This paper introduces 'relative' and 'absolute' indices of social mobility. To each index there corresponds a different social welfare function. When the symmetric mean of order θ (<1) social welfare function is employed, the relative index becomes the King (1983) index of social mobility. © 1984.

Title: Total utility, overlapping generations and social security
Abstract: In Gigliotti (1983), necessary and sufficient conditions for an optimal path were found in an overlapping generations model that maximized the infinite discounted sum of total utility per generation. Here we show, as Samuelson (1975b) did in the per capita utility model, that, with an appropriate social security system, individuals, acting to maximize their own utility, will save enough to finance the optimal steady state growth of the economy in a total utility model. © 1984.

Title: Wage rigidities, unemployment compensations and Pareto optimality
Abstract: It is shown that wage rigidities may imply that in order to attain ex-ante and/or ex-post Pareto optimality transfers to the unemployed must be made. In a Pareto optimal equilibrium, the level of unemployment compensations is strictly positive but less than 100%. © 1984.

Title: Underemployment and normal leisure
Abstract: A combined worksharing-layoff-wage-severance pay contract is shown to imply, inter alia, that normal leisure and underemployment do coexist provided the elasticity of substitution between employment and hours is sufficiently low (as defined rigorously in the text). © 1984.

Title: Technical change, the rate of profit and joint production
Abstract: In indecomposable, single-product industries models, the introduction of a cost-reducing method of production causes an increase in the uniform rate of profit, if the real wage rate is fixed. I show that this result does not extend to pure joint-production models. © 1984.

Title: On measuring concentration and diversification
Abstract: This paper generalises some earlier results [Clarke and Davies (1983)] in the decomposition of aggregate concentration into market concentration and firm diversification components, and considers implications of weighting schemes implied in these decompositions. © 1984.

Title: Price–cost margins and imports in an oligopolistic market
Abstract: In a recent letter in this journal Urata (1979) found an unexpected, positive, and significant association between price-cost margins and import to domestic shipment ratio for the U.S. textile and apparel industries. In the present letter a theoretical explanation for this phenomenon is presented by extending a conjectural variation oligopoly model. © 1984.

Title: Consistent conjectures in utility-maximizing firms with constant marginal cost
Abstract: Bresnahan (1981) and Perry (1982) have shown that only competitive behavior is consistent when marginal costs are constant. This paper generalizes that result to show that competition is consistent when firms are utility-maximizers rather than simple profit-maximizers. © 1984.

Title: Market price and the stability of cartels
Abstract: We analyse a relationship between market price and the stability of cartels. The approach yields insight into the size of the stable cartel relative to the economy. © 1984.

Title: A peculiar example of temporal price discrimination
Abstract: A seemingly small change in a demand assumption reverses several standard conclusions about temporal price discrimination. © 1984.

Title: Official Japanese intervention in foreign exchange markets
Abstract: Several recent studies have suggested that official Japanese intervention in foreign exchange markets is limited to simple 'leaning against the wind'. This note provides evidence, however, that Bank of Japan intervention is systematically biased against yen appreciation. © 1984.

Title: The pound sterling/US dollar exchange rate and the ‘new’
Abstract: The theory that the exchange rate responds to the 'news' content of the fundamental variables is tested. The innovations in the monetary approach variables are proxied by ARIMA residuals and the reduced form equation for the exchange rate is fitted by 2SLS. © 1984.

Title: The monetary impact of universal reserve requirements under alternative operating targets
Abstract: This paper estimates the gain in short-run money stock control associated with the 1980 Monetary Control Act. The estimated improvement is small for a monetary base target but rises sharply for total and non-borrowed reserve operating targets. © 1984.

Title: Mobility and wages
Abstract: We show that even for the simplest job search model the effect of mobility on wages depends on the distribution of wage offers and the cost of job changes. The effect for symmetric wage distributions is derived. © 1984.

Title: Testing linear restrictions on non-linear models
Abstract: This note shows that the significance level and power of the F-test for a linear hypothesis is affected by non-linearity, but not systematically. © 1984.

Title: Second moments of consumption components and unexpected inflation
Authors: Ronald A. Ratti, Jang Hwan Park
Abstract: A rise in unexpected inflation is found to increase variability in the relative prices and quantities of components of personal consumption expenditures, and to reduce the covariance of these relative prices and quantities. © 1984.

Title: The real effects of price variability in the Federal Republic of Germany, 1953–1977
Abstract: Using a forty industry data set for the years 1953-1977 for the Federal Republic of Germany evidence is presented on the real effects of price variability. Measuring price variability as the expenditure share weighted sum of squared deviations about the rate of inflation, it is found that increased variability reduces real GDP, hours of work, and production employment, while increasing the unemployment rate. Further, it is found that unanticipated inflation has a positive influence on real variables for six different measures of unanticipated inflation. The six inflation series do not support the natural rate hypothesis in that the effect of the expected inflation rate is not always insignificant. © 1984.

Title: Risk and linear-quadratic stabilization
Abstract: The linear-quadratic theory of economic policy rules is extended to allow for risk. The use of the Arrow-Pratt measure of constant absolute risk-aversion still results in linear rules, although the multiperiod certainty equivalence principle no longer holds. © 1984.

Title: On the desirability of an income stabilisation scheme
Abstract: As a preliminary to further empirical work, this letter considers the desirability for producers of a scheme which stabilises incomes by introducing a negative covariance between price and production and which is to be funded by producers. It examine the way in which this desirability depends on the cost of the scheme, the risk aversion of producers, and the extent of their initial income instability. © 1984.

Title: Acceptable mean-variance indifference curves
