Abstract: A letter by Allen (1983) shows that not all convex upward sloping curves in mean-variance space are consistent with von Neumann-Morgenstern utility functions. This letter derives a second-order partial differential equation which provides a means of identifying those which are. © 1984.

Title: On the inconsistency of a non-pairwise version of the libertarian principle
Abstract: It is shown that the non-pairwise libertarian principle is inconsistent with most relaxations of the Pareto principle, given some rather mild choice-consistency properties. © 1984.

Title: Societal opposition on ethical grounds and the liberal paradox
Abstract: It has been shown that justice-constrained libertarian claims can resolve Sen's impossibility of a Paretian liberal. The underlying libertarian claims are extremely weak, however. Therefore, we propose to apply one of the 'standard' resolution schemes and add a justice constraint that is more appealing. © 1984.

Title: The Cagan schedule in an overlapping generations setting
Abstract: Cagan's portfolio balance schedule under rational expectations is generated by an overlapping generations model. Tenuousness of the equilibrium described by Cagan's schedule can be interpreted as following from a requirement that the old generation be risk neutral. © 1984.

Title: Stability of a discrete-time, macroeconomic disequilibrium model
Abstract: We investigate the stability of a macroeconomic monetary discrete-time model with a constraint on the market for bank-credit. A theorem is proved on asymptotic stability of a piecewise linear discrete-time system in R2. © 1984.

Title: Constant elasticity of substitution production functions with three or more inputs
Abstract: An approximation procedure is developed to allow arbitrary and constant elasticities of substitution between aggregate inputs in production functions with three or more factors. The procedure is necessary to overcome the serious constraints on structure imposed on CES schedules by the Uzawa-McFadden results. © 1984.

Title: An evaluation of alternative demand systems by means of implied income elasticities
Authors: Lennart R. Flood, Renate Finke, Henri Theil
Abstract: Working's model and the indirect translog model are compared and evaluated by means of the implied behavior of the income elasticities for two sets of data. The effect of deleting observations is also discussed. © 1984.

Title: Maximum likelihood and instrumental variable estimation of a consumer demand system for Japan and Sweden
Authors: Renate Finke, Lennart R. Flood, Henri Theil
Abstract: Working's model (with a substitution term added) is applied to annual per capita data of Japan and Sweden. The model is estimated by ML and IV methods, and the variability of the IV estimates is evaluated by means of bootstrap methods. © 1984.

Title: More on goodness of fit of allocation models
Authors: Denzil G. Fiebig, Renate Finke, Henri Theil
Abstract: Strobel (1982) provides a percentage decomposition of the information inaccuracy of an allocation model over individual goods. This notion is applied to the cross-country consumption data analyzed by Finke (1983). The entropy of the percentage decomposition is also considered; it measures the extent to which the inaccuracy of the model results from few equations that fit relatively poorly or from many equations which have approximately the same quality of fit. © 1984.

Title: Frich's conjecture and the own-price elasticity of the demand for food
Authors: Kenneth W. Clements, Renate Finke, Henri Theil
Abstract: Frich's (1959) conjecture on the behavior of the income elasticity of the marginal utility of income is tested by means of cross-country data, particularly in relation to the behavior of the Frisch own-price elasticity of the demand for food. © 1984.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Net liquid assets and net illiquid assets in the consumption function
Abstract: This note reports details of estimating consumption equations for the United Kingdom which separate net wealth into net liquid assets and net illiquid assets. The estimation framework is related to that in the influential article by Hendry and von Ungern-Sternberg (1981), but recognises the importance of defining income to allow not only for inflation induced losses but also for depreciation provisions. The empirical results provide some support for a role for both liquid and illiquid assets in determining consumption decisions. © 1984.

Title: Competitive, monopolistic and efficient utilization of an exhaustible resource in the presence of habit-formation effects and stock dependent costs
Abstract: The letter investigates the utilization of an exhaustible resource under perfect competition and monopoly, and compares monopolistic and competitive depletion patterns with those under social surplus maximization. Demand and costs are assumed to depend on current as well as accumulated output. © 1984.

Title: The statistical significance of a change in concentration
Abstract: This note examines statistical tests for the significance of a change in the logvariance measure of concentration between two points in time. The note points out flaws in two existing tests, proposes a correct test, and provides an empirical example. © 1984.

Title: Testing for ‘news’ in foreign exchange markets
Abstract: Traditional tests of the role of interest rate news on foreign exchange rates are analysed and found to be of little empirical value. © 1984.

Title: Price dynamics in an input-output model
Abstract: The suggested approach is developed, on the basis of firms' markup behaviour, in terms of current prices making value coefficients change as the effects of the initial price rise spread through the economy. © 1984.

Title: Iterative aggregation
Abstract: The two-level iterative aggregation procedure for solution of a large set of linear equations is shown in an example of its simplest implementation (where aggregation is into a single equation) to have a convergence rate slower than simple iteration. Some extensions of Schennikov's (1965) original structure are presented. The effect of a special choice of demand vector is investigated. © 1984.

Title: The properties of some covariance matrix estimators in linear models with AR(1) errors
Abstract: A Monte Carlo study is used to demonstrate how poor some traditional covariance matrix estimators can be in linear models with AR(1) errors. It is also shown that a second-order approximation suggested recently by Ullah et al. (1983) does not lead to a more accurate covariance matrix estimator. © 1984.

Title: Linear aggregation of vector autoregressive moving average processes
Abstract: A framework is developed in which to analyze both temporal and contemporaneous linear aggregation of vector autoregressive moving average processes. An aggregated finite order process is shown to be again a finite order process, and upper bounds for the autoregressive and moving average order are given. © 1984.

Title: Instrumental variables regressions involving seasonal data
Abstract: Various approaches to handling seasonal data are known to be equivalent in the context of least squares estimation of a fixed-regressor linear model. This note extends these results to models which have stochastic regressors and are estimated by the method of Instrumental Variables. © 1984.

Title: Testing linear and log-linear regressions with autocorrelated errors
Abstract: This paper considers the problem of testing linear and log-linear models with autocorrelated errors. Test of functional form as well as functional form and autocorrelation simultaneously are obtained using the Lagrange multiplier approach. © 1984.

Title: Testing for linear Engel curves
Abstract: The demand system, NLES, proposed recently by Blundell and Ray (1982), is shown to aggregate consistently across households. It is then used to analyse time series expenditure data of Korea, Greece, Israel and Puerto Rico. The empirical results reject linear Engel curves for each country. © 1984.

Title: Timing of decisions and the competitive firm under input price uncertainty
Abstract: This paper studies the behavior of a competitive firm faced with input price uncertainty when the ex ante decision variable is output, not the quantities of the inputs. Highly unconventional results are obtained about the effects of uncertainty and of marginal increases in risk. © 1984.

Title: Flight insurance pricing and the theory of choice
Abstract: The conclusion of Eisner and Strotz that the purchase of air-travel insurance is inconsistent with the von Neumann-Morgenstern theory of choice is shown to depend critically upon their specific pricing formula. An alternative pricing scheme eliminates this inconsistency. © 1984.

Title: Group incentive compatibility in a market with indivisible goods
Abstract: In a market where each trader has one unit of an indivisible good, there are procedures for exchanging goods which result in competitive allocations. One of these procedures, the top trading cycle, has the property that it is in each trader's best interest to report his true preferences over the set of goods. This note shows that no subset of traders can misrepresent their preferences and improve the allocation for all members of the subset. Additionally, if there are no indifferences in the preferences, then some traders in a subset that misrepresents preferences do worse. © 1984.

Title: Estimating compensating and equivalent income variations from hedonic price models
Abstract: Estimates of welfare changes obtained from hedonic price models usually consist of changes in Marshallian consumer's surplus. This note shows how compensating and equivalent income variations can be computed from the information available in hedonicprice models. © 1984.

Title: Bootstrapping for standard errors of instrumental variable estimates
Abstract: Theil and Finke (1983) used the distance from the equator as an instrumental variable (IV) in the estimation of a cross-country demand system. Here we obtain standard errors of the IV estimates using Efron's (1979) bootstrap technique. © 1984.

Title: Errata
Testing the stability of the hall consumption function specification
Abstract: This paper contains stability tests of Hall's consumption specification by using cross-country data from 11 OECD-countries. Taken as a whole results are in favour of Hall's hypothesis, even though there is some conflicting evidence. © 1984.

Title: On indices of relative deprivation
Abstract: In this paper we have suggested normative indices of relative deprivation. The Yitzhaki (1979) index of relative deprivation is a special case of one of our indices. © 1984.

Title: Unemployment insurance meets the classical labor supply model
Abstract: Through making average income dependent on the breakdown of non-employment into frequency and duration, the classical labor supply model with unemployment insurance has important implications for labor force participation, the duration of employment and unemployment, and modes of worker behavior that are by and large consistent with empirical knowledge. © 1984.

Title: A classification of second-order technical progress operators
Abstract: This paper demonstrates that any technical progress operator can always be classified as a member of either the hyperbolic, parabolic, or elliptic class of linear partial differential operators. This classification is useful for studies that estimate the contributions to economic growth of economies of scale and technological progress. © 1984.

Title: Assessing the profitability effects of airline deregulation
Abstract: This paper implements a methodology developed in Spiller (1982) to assess the differential profitability effects of the deregulation of the airline industry. It is found that the 'standard' residual analysis does not uncover the true impact of this regulatory change: large differential changes in profitability which are, in most instances, accompanied by large risk changes. This paper then shows the usefulness of the new methodology. © 1984.

Title: A note of the theory of international transfers
Abstract: If each of N trading countries supplies each of several international public consumption goods then sufficiently small international transfers have no effect on the consumption, production or welfare of any country. © 1984.

Title: Policy impacts on the open economy in different unemployment regimes
Abstract: The analysis examines the impact of selected policy instruments on output, employment and the trade balance of a less than fully employed, open economy subject to a fixed exchange rate. The following unemployment disequilibria are characterised: generalised excess supply, domestic recession and classical unemployment, and the diverse effects of selected instruments in different unemployment disequilibria are explained. © 1984.

Title: Public intermediate inputs, property values, and allocative efficiency
Authors: Jan K. Brueckner, Thomas L. Wingler
Abstract: This letter shows that when public goods are intermediate inputs as well as final consumption goods, stationary of aggregate property value under a marginal change in public spending implies satisfaction of a generalized Samuelson efficiency condition. This result shows that the empirical test for efficiency of Brueckner (1982) remains valid when public goods enter firm production functions. © 1984.

Title: Variability of the Japanese money stock
Abstract: McKinnon's currency substitution model predicts that variable U.S. money growth causes greater variability of foreign money growth. Contrary to this thesis. the variability of Japan's monetary targets is found to be inversely related to the variability of U.S. M1. © 1984.

Title: A dynamic generalisation of the almost ideal demand system
Abstract: This paper proposes and estimates on annual time series U.K. data (1900-1980) a dynamic generalisation of the 'Almost Ideal Demand System'. The results support the proposed generalisation and point to the dynamic AIDS as a potentially useful tool in future applications. © 1984.

Title: Autocorrelation and the sensitivity of reset
Authors: Richard D. Porter, Anil K. Kashyap
Abstract: This paper shows that the Thursby-Schmidt specification test (T-S RESET) in a linear regression model is not robust to autocorrelated error terms. © 1984.

Title: Testing hypotheses on the unidentifiable structural parameters in the classical ‘errors-in-variables’ model with application to Friedman's permanent income model
Abstract: Methods for hypothesis testing for the standard errors in variables model with normal disturbances are discussed. This is possible even though the parameters are unidentified. Confidence intervals are also constructed. © 1984.

Title: A note on likelihood ratio tests of functional form and structural change in demand systems
Abstract: We present some small-sample Monte Carlo results on Likelihood Ratio tests of particular functional form restrictions and structural change in non-linear demand systems. In all cases the standard Likelihood Ratio test statistic rejects the (true) null hypothesis too often. © 1984.

Title: The downward bias of asymptotic standard errors of maximum likelihood estimates of non-linear systems
Authors: Mercedes C. Rosalsky, Renate Finke, Henri Theil
Abstract: A simulation study indicates that the asymptotic standard errors understate the actual inaccuracy of ML system estimates even when the number of coefficients estimated is small. The understatement increases in size when the system is larger. © 1984.

Title: A method of moments interpretation of sequential estimators
Abstract: It is shown that sequential estimators can be interpreted as members of a class method of moments of estimators, and that this interpretation facilities derivation of asymptotic covariance matrices for two-step estimators. An example is given which deals with a two-step least squares estimator used to estimate rational expectations models. © 1984.

Title: The likelihood function and a test for serial correlation in a disequilibrium market model
Abstract: The likelihood function for an econometric disequilibrium market model of Fair and Jaffee with autocorrelated disturbances is derived. A statistic is introduced for the test of serial correlation in such a model. The statistic can be regarded as generalization of the Durbin-Watson statistic. © 1984.

Title: Regime classifications in the disequilibrium market models
Abstract: The classification of sample observations to periods of excess demand and excess supply is in the domain of discriminant analysis. The classification rule suggested by Kiefer (1980) and Gersovitz (1980) is shown to be optimal in the sense that it minimizes the total probability of misclassification. © 1984.

Title: Finite-sample power of tests for autocorrelation in models containing lagged dependent variables
Abstract: Monte Carlo evidence is presented to indicate that for a given size of the test, the Durbin-Watson test is more powerful than Durbin's h test in testing for autocorrelation in models with a lagged dependent variable. © 1984.

Title: Comparing stochastic price regimes
Abstract: Marshallian consumer's surplus can often be defended as a useful approximation to Hicksian compensating variation. Under price uncertainty, however, expected compensating variation is not a generally valid welfare measure, and expected consumer's surplus cannot be justified as an approximation to a rigorous construct. © 1984.

Title: Sufficient conditions for a sufficient statistic theorem
Abstract: A sufficient statistic theorem for principal-agent relations can be shown under specific integrability conditions. © 1984.

Title: Maximal elements for non-transitive binary relations
Abstract: Using a fixed-point theorem of Browder, we prove the existence of a maximal element for a non-transitive relation on a set X which is not assumed to be compact or convex. This theorem is a generalization of the results available in the existing literature. © 1984.

Title: Chaos, Naivete, and consistent conjectures
Abstract: Bresnahan's consistent conjectures equilibrium is discussed as a more general means of avoiding chaos than naive strategies. Also, contrasting examples establish that perfectly and imperfectly competitive markets may exhibit similar, chaotic dynamics, contrary to a long-held view of industrial organization. © 1984.

Title: On a market demand function satisfying the weak but not the strong axiom of revealed preference
Abstract: Hildenbrand (1983) states conditions under which the market demand function satisfies the Weak Axiom of Revealed Preference. An example is provided which shows that in general this market demand function does not satisfy the Strong Axiom of Revealed Preference. © 1984.

Title: On final choice functions
Abstract: A choice function h is said to be a final choice function if hh = h. We shall count the all final choice functions on a finite set X. We consider a semigroup of all fuzzy rational choice functions on X. © 1984.

Title: A cross-country tabulation of own-price elasticities of demand
Authors: Renate Finke, Wen-He Lu, Henri Theil
Abstract: This paper tabulates Frisch, Slutsky and Cournot own-price elasticities for each of 10 goods at the per capita real-income levels of 30 countries ranging from India to the United States. © 1984.

Title: On the existence of local nash equilibrium with price and quality competition
Abstract: This note demonstrates no local Nash equilibrium exists in a specific example of the market for a product which varies in quality. The 'local' restriction rules out the sort of undercutting which preludes existence of equilibrium in Hotelling-type models. © 1984.

Title: Non-causalities and time inconsistency in dynamic non-cooperative games
Authors: Andries S. Brandsma, A.J. Hughes Hallett
Abstract: Non-casuality arises whenever expected future decisions can influence current target outcomes. Transforming a behavioural model so that the non-casual multipliers become explicit as part of the optimisation procedure is necessary, but not sufficient, for constructing optimal and time consistent strategies. © 1984.

Title: A note on aggregation of Fechner-Thurstone direct utility functions
Authors: R.L. Basmann, D.J. Molina, D.J. Slottje
Abstract: This paper demonstrates that exact aggregation of individual to per capita demand functions is achieved when the Fechner-Thurstone functional form is the underlying direct utility function. The exact aggregation takes place without the restrictive assumptions that characterize systems of demand functions derived from other functional forms. © 1984.

Title: A limit theorem on the core with differential information
Abstract: In an economy with differential information, core allocations tend to favor those who have superior information. In this paper, we show that as the economy gets replicated, this informational advantage diminishes, and disappears in the limit. © 1984.

Title: Problems with average cost pricing in the presence of set-up costs
Abstract: Average cost pricing equilibria may not exist if average costs are unbounded as output goes to zero. This is the case with set-up costs. The equilibrium correspondence in these cases is not upper hemicontinuous. © 1984.

Title: A second note on the core of the overlapping generations model
Abstract: This note provides an example of an overlapping generations economy with a Pareto optimal Walrasian equilibrium and an empty core. Then, in the context of the economy examined by Balasko and Shell (1980) a sufficient condition is provided for a Pareto optimal Walrasian equilibrium to be contained in the core. © 1984.

Title: The permanent income hypothesis and the real interest rate
Abstract: A test of the permanent income hypothesis in panel data is formulated taking into account both the time-series and cross-section variation in the rate of return. The over-identifying restrictions of the theory rejected. © 1984.

Title: Downward bias in a new measure of wage discrimination
Abstract: Wage discrimination measured as a comparison of male and female characteristics within the same wage bracket is shown to differ from the conventional measure by excluding the wage regression constant term. Australian data confirm that this provokes downward bias. © 1984.

Title: Firm size and the incentive to differentiate
Abstract: The conjectural variation is treated as a choice variable capturing the behavioral impact of product differentiation. By this means it is shown that firms have a profit incentive to differentiate, large firms more than small ones, and a differentiating firm more than its rivals. © 1984.

Title: On the relationship between the New York closing spot U.S.$⧸$A exchange rate and the Reserve Bank of Australia's official rate
Abstract: The paper considers: (i) the hypothesis that the Reserve Bank's official U.S.${plus 45 degree rule}$A spot rate may be predicted from overnight movements in the closing New York rate, and (ii) the informational content of the official rate in explaining movements in the New York rate. © 1984.

Title: Dynamic stability in a model of dual exchange rates
Abstract: The dynamic stability of a small open economy operating under a regime of dual exchange rates is shown to depend on residents' net foreign asset position. This result is in contrast to the economy's dynamic behavior under unified fixed-rate and flexible-rate regimes where stability is unrelated to net foreign asset position. © 1984.

Title: Club optimality
Abstract: This article clarifies the bounds of a recent theorem on club optimality. In so doing, the Pareto-optimal conditions for both homogeneous and heterogeneous-member clubs are set forth for a variable-use, fixed number of clubs. © 1984.

Title: Non-linearities in applied general equilibrium models
Abstract: In this paper we discuss some extensions of the general equilibrium model Keller (1980) used to analyze tax-incidence. We compute the comparative static results of Keller on tax-incidence, now taking into account non-linearities. This is done by employing a method of iterative linearization. It turns out that the error made by linearization is small. © 1984.

Title: Distribution of a generalized t ratio for biased estimators
Abstract: For certain biased estimators the standard error can be small (even zero) and Student's t ratio over-estimates their statistical significance. This paper studies the distribution of a generalized t ratio where the denominator has the square root of an unbiased estimate of the mean squared error. © 1984.

Title: Bank credit and debt, income, and causality
Abstract: By employing the Sims test this study examines the exogeneity, or casual ordering, of bank credit and two measures of debt from the US Federal Reserve Flow of Funds Accounts. Evidence presented here suggests that Bank Credit and Funds Raised by Private Domestic Nonfinancial Sectors are not appropriate targets. The Sims test of causality clearly indicates undirectional causality running from Total Funds Raised by Private Domestic Nonfinancial Sectors to spending. © 1984.

Title: A note on the Wald, LR and LM tests and misspecification
Abstract: In this note, we investigate sensitivity of the Wald, LR and LM tests to specification error. It is shown that these three tests are very sensitive to specification error, but the LM test is relatively superior to other two tests under certain situations. © 1984.

Title: On the consequences of trend for simultaneous equation estimation
Abstract: It is shown that the presence of trend in the exogenous variables violates some standard assumptions that govern large sample asymptotics in simultaneous equations, and that contrary to the standard analysis Ordinary Least Squares may be consistent with trended data. Necessary and sufficient conditions are derived for this to happen, and in case of consistency the asymptotic distributions for a wide class of k-class estimators are shown to be identical. © 1984.

Title: Interest rates and the fisher effect in India
Abstract: This study throws light on the importance of adjustment lags, variability of inflation, changes in real income, etc. in the empirical estimation of Fisher hypothesis. Variability of inflation has a significant negative impact on both short- and long-term interest rates in a developing economy like India. The 'Philips Curve Effect' has not been operative in a developing country. © 1984.

Title: Unidimensional median voter results in probabilistic voting models
Abstract: This paper studies the policy outcomes that can be expected to occur when candidates are uncertain about voter behavior. Its analysis begins with an example that illustrates how the 'Comaner-Hinich effect' (i.e., the possibility of non-median outcomes) can occur under such circumstances. This example is then modified in ways which restore a median outcome. After this is done, the method of restoration is generalized to obtain a unidimensional median voter result for probabilistic voting models. © 1984.

Title: The neutrality of systematic monetary policy in models with a disequilibrium price level
Abstract: A condition is offered which is necessary and sufficient for the neutrality of aggregate output and the real rate of interest with respect to systematic monetary policy in a general class of stochastic macroeconomic models with rational expectations, additive disturbances, lagged information and a disequilibrium price sequence. © 1984.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Errors in variables and reverse regression in the measurement of wage discrimination
Abstract: Several recent articles have proposed 'reverse regression' as a solution to errors-in-variables problems in wage discrimination regressions. This note demonstrates that the reverse regression approach is biased against finding evidence of discrimination. © 1983.

Title: Human capital and the time-profile of human fertility
Abstract: This is a first attempt at an explicitly intertemporal, microeconomic theory of the distribution of births over a woman's fertile period. The main results are (a) that the optimal time-profile will satisfy the Hotelling rule for the depletion of a natural resource (in the present case of the woman's stock of human capital at marriage), and (b) that, under certain simplifying assumptions, women with 'high' initial endowments of human capital will have all their children in the first part of married life and then return to full-time employment, while women with 'low' initial endowments will spread childbearing more evenly over the fertile period. © 1983.

Title: Determinants of R&D in an LDC
Abstract: R&D behaviour of LDC industrial firms is an unexplored subject. Data on the largest engineering firms in India are analysed to test the hypothesis that technological effort in LDCs is primarily directed at assimilating and adapting foreign technologies. © 1983.

Title: Exports as a signal of quality
Abstract: Dumping, namely selling abroad at a price below the marginal cost of production, is the result of the monopolist's profit maximizing behavior. This result is obtained when the firm takes into account the informative role played by exports in the domestic market. The level of exports serves as a signal of the quality of the new product. © 1983.

Title: The formation of expectations
Abstract: This paper investigates the expectations formation process of weekly money supply forecasts derived from survey data. The evidence indicates that forecaster's expectations are modelled best as regressive. Moreover, the results are unaffected by the October 1979 change in monetary operating procedures. © 1983.

Title: A note on the underestimation and overestimation in stochastic input-output models
Abstract: Here we show that (i) the Leontief inverse (I - A)-1 is underestimated when the elements of A, the fixed coefficient input-output matrix, are biproportionally stochastic, and (ii) the output vector in a non-linear input-output system is overestimated when the final demand vector is stochastic. © 1983.

Title: The distance from the equator as an instrumental variable
Abstract: To attack the problem of measurement errors in independent variables, the distance from the equator is used as an instrumental variable for per capita income. Application of this idea to the estimation of a demand system from the cross-country data of Kravis et al. (1982) yields promising results. © 1983.

Title: Reserve requirements and control of a broad monetary aggregate
Authors: Richard T. Froyen, Kenneth J. Kopecky
Abstract: When at least one component of a broad monetary aggregate pays a market-determined interest rate, this paper shows that monetary control does not necessarily improve if all reserve ratios are set at feasible maximums and equalized across all components. © 1983.

Title: Estimation in censored samples when there is heteroskedasticity
Abstract: Heteroskedasticity generally leads to inconsistency of the simple estimators that correct for sample selection bias. A correction for heteroskedasticity is derived for the sample selection estimator proposed by Gronau. The correction can be applied to censored samples where the selection variable is unobserved. © 1983.

Title: A note on the econometric use of constant dollar inventory series
Abstract: One dollar of finished goods inventories does not represent the same amount of physical goods as one dollar of sales, when Department of Commerce constant dollar series are used. This can cause seriously biased regression estimates. © 1983.

Title: Capital accumulation with a finite decision horizon
Abstract: The possibility that capital will be over-accumulated when agents have finite decision horizons is examined. This possibility can generally be ruled out if agents are free to choose their labour supply optimally. © 1983.

Title: Multi-agent control in perfectly correlated environments
Abstract: The basic Principal-Agent model is extended to a case in which there are two agents. The agents are risk-averse and their stochastic environments are perfectly correlated. Two cases are described in which the principal can extract all the rents from the agents while ensuring the optimal action from his point of view. © 1983.

Title: The incentive implications of incomplete insurance
Abstract: When states of nature are not completely verifiable and payments in a Pareto efficient insurance scheme contribute multiplicatively to wealth, the insured may be better off in the insured against event, depending upon the behavior of relative risk aversion. © 1983.

Title: The effect of size on prices
Authors: J. Luis Guasch, Robert C. Marshall
Abstract: We present here an analysis of the effects that the firm's size, in the sense of the quantity of its assets, has on the price charged per asset. We show that the larger the firm is, the higher the price it charges. Our argument is not based on the traditional monopoly power associated with size but rather on the ability to bear risk. © 1983.

Title: Goodness of fit and outliers in cross-country demand systems
Abstract: For a 10-good consumer demand system, the fit for 30 countries in the sample is compared with that for five countries outside the sample. © 1983.

Title: The rate of return regulated version of Shephard's lemma
Abstract: In this paper, the rate of return regulated version of Shephard's lemma is proved. © 1983.

Title: Estimating dynamic demand systems
Abstract: This paper estimates dynamic extensions of recent LES generalisations on rural India's budget data. The results provide evidence of dynamic demand behaviour and point to the Generalised Translog as the preferred model. © 1983.

Title: A conditional logit model for executive incentives
Abstract: In this paper, firm and executive characteristics are directly related to the probability of termination of the contract of the chief executive of a firm. A conditional logit model is specified from which implications concerning profit maximization can be inferred. © 1983.

Title: Estimating the intertemporal elasticity of labor supply in a contractual market
Abstract: If labor services are exchanged in contractual markets, existing micro estimates of the intertemporal substitution elasticity contain a negative bias. Hedonic wage regressions of compensating differentials for layoffs provide unbiased estimates in contractual markets. © 1983.

Title: Energy consumption in LDCs
Abstract: This paper constructs estimates of the price elasticity of energy consumption in LDCs. It also studies the effect of omitting the price variable from energy consumption equations on the estimates of the income elasticities and updates estimates of this income elasticity to test the stability of the energy-GDP relationship during the period 1970-1978. © 1983.

Title: On the optimal resource rent tax
Abstract: Total payments to government by a mineral exploration firm which follows Bayesian procedures when deciding on exploration plans are shown to vary with the rate of resource rent tax in a two part tax scheme which also includes a competitive auction of the right to explore and mine. If the explorer is risk neutral, then a zero tax rate maximises government revenue. © 1983.

Title: The welfare effects of complexity and variability in regulations
Abstract: The model posits type-A firms who need to comply with regulations and type-B firms who supply compliance services. Compliance costs are increasing in regulatory complexity (C) and variability (V). Type-A firms can either purchase the service or provide it for themselves. An equilibrium is defined and aggregate welfare is seen to diminish with additional C and V. If regulators have welfare functions that are concave, C and V will be set at socially excessive levels. © 1983.

Title: Choosing duopoly solutions by consistent conjectures and by uncertainty
Abstract: Breshnahan's consistent conjectures criterion and Robson's linear supply function equilibrium under uncertainty are equivalent in the sense that they single out the same Bowley conjectural variations as the unique conjectural variations satisfying the given consistency requirements. © 1983.

Title: Successive cournot-nash industries
Abstract: Successive Cournot-Nash industries yield a higher final price the more concentrated at each stage and the less completely vertically integrated, they are but will not remain incompletely vertically integrated if mergers are costless. © 1983.

Title: The structure-performance relationship at the firm level
Abstract: This letter provides an explanation for recent empirical results that suggest that market concentration has a negative effect on profitability at the firm level. It also casts doubts on traditional interpretations of high market shares as evidence of market power. © 1983.

Title: An all-encompassing consumption function
Abstract: The paper reports some empirical findings of the Davidson, Hendry, Srba and Yeo (1978) consumption function fitted to Australian quarterly data for the period 1969.3 to 1982.2. The evidence rejects, in terms of the maximum likelihood ratio test, the unitary differencing and price homogeneity restrictions and supports a simple dynamic forecasting model with unconstrained parameters. © 1983.

Title: Non-traded goods and the general equilibrium effects of tariffs in the short run
Authors: Francisco L. Rivera-Batiz, Aquiles A. Almansi
Abstract: A short-run general equilibrium model with non-traded goods is developed and the response of the output of importables to an import tariff is examined. It is found that, under standard assumptions, the tariff always increases the output of importables. © 1983.

Title: Analysts' forecasts in the capital asset pricing model
Abstract: The abnormally high returns on small, neglected firms are explained by a respecified CAPM, which incorporates the information contained in analysts' forecasts by allowing for uncertainty in the mean ex ante return. © 1983.

Title: The monetary multiplier when money is measured as a Divisia quantity index
Abstract: The traditional algebraic derivation of the monetary multiplier for conventional simple sum monetary aggregates is extended to cover the case of money defined as a Divisia monetary quantity index. Thus, the procedures developed by Johannes and Rasche for assessing the controllability of money can be applied to the issue of controllability of the Divisia aggregates. © 1983.

Title: Government capital and the production function for U.S. private output
Abstract: Theoretical and policy discussions make unsupported assumptions about the productivity of capital which governments own. Estimates of an aggregate production function for U.S. private business, 1949-1973, show government capital to be significant, statistically and in economic terms. © 1983.

Title: The private provision of a public good is independent of the distribution of income
Abstract: When a single public good is provided at positive levels by private individuals, its provision is unaffected by a redistribution of income. This holds regardless of differences in individual preferences and despite differences in marginal propensities to contribute to the public good. © 1983.

Title: Asymptotic tests on moving average representation coefficients with an application to innovations on spot and forward exchange rates
Abstract: The asymptotic distribution is derived for moving average representation coefficients from a vector autoregressive process. The results are computationally feasible and allow asymptotic tests of restrictions on the coefficients to be carried out. The technique is illustrated with a two equation model. © 1983.

Title: A note on algebraic equivalence of White's test and a variation of the Godfrey/Breusch-Pagan test for heteroscedasticity
Abstract: Two, recently proposed tests for heteroscedasticity are examined. Under certain conditions and a modification of one of the tests already proposed in the literature, they are found to be algebraically equivalent. © 1983.

Title: Non-linear least squares estimation under non-linear equality constraints
Abstract: Asymptotic properties of the non-linear least squares estimator are derived for the case where non-sample information in the form of equality constraints is taken into account. Provided the conditions for consistency and asymptotic normality of the unconstrained least squares estimator are satisfied, the restricted least squares estimator is also consistent and asymptotically normally distributed under rather general assumptions for the constraints. © 1983.

Title: A note on testing for structural change in a single equation belonging to a simultaneous system
Abstract: A simple-to-implement, finite sample test for structural change in an equation belonging to a simultaneous system and estimated by Two-Stage Least Squares, is presented. © 1983.

Title: Methods of estimation for models of markets with bounded price variation under rational expectations
Abstract: The present paper extends the analysis in an earlier paper by Maddala on estimation of disequilibrium market models with controlled prices to the case where the supply function depends on expected prices and expectations are formed rationally as suggested by Muth. © 1983.

Title: Does there exist a relation between inflation and relative price-change variability?
Abstract: The actual magnitude of relative price-change variability is dependent on the level of aggregation. This note demonstrates the effect of this dependence when we try to estimate a relation between inflation and relative price change variability and when we perform a decomposition analysis of this variability. © 1983.

Title: A reconsideration of Sims' evidence concerning monetarism
Abstract: In VAR systems such as those of Sims (1980), monetary policy surprises may be more accurately represented by interest rate than money stock innovations, especially if the monetary authority uses an interest rate instrument. © 1983.

Title: Adaptive expectations and the variance hypothesis
Abstract: It is shown that Lucas' 'variance' hypothesis on output-inflation tradeoff is consistent even with adaptive price expectations. Hence empirical evidence of the model need not support the rational expectations-natural rate hypothesis. © 1983.

Title: A test for structural instability in the secular growth rate of productivity
Authors: Arthur E. Blakemore, Don E. Schlagenhauf
Abstract: In this paper we challenge the orthodox notion that long-run productivity in the U.S. has suffered two distinct structural breaks. Instead, we find that the slowdown in the secular growth rate can be more appropriately characterized as a continuous, non-linear decline since the early 1950's. © 1983.

Title: Sustainable solutions for dynamic bargaining problems
Abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic bargaining problem in which players have to agree on a time path of actions. The axiomatic approach for such problems may yield a solution which is not sustainable. For every given partition of the time interval however, we can construct a sustainable solution. © 1983.

Title: Optimal hedging in the futures market under price uncertainty
Authors: Simon Benninga, Rafael Eldor, Itzhak Zilcha
Abstract: We show that there exists a simple optimal hedging rule in the futures markets, for all risk averse decision makers, given that (a) futures price today is an unbiased predictor of the futures price next period, (b) basis is independent of the spot price. © 1983.

Title: The number of weak orders
Abstract: We derive a closed form formula for the number F(n) of weak orders on a set containing n alternatives starting from a recursive formula due to Kelly (1981). In addition a generating function for F(n) is given as well as an asymptotic formula. Finally we discuss the accuracy of this approximation. © 1983.

Title: Marginal welfare measures for discrete choice models
Abstract: This letter deals with the use of discrete choice models for applied welfare analysis. An approximate formula is presented for the marginal willingness to pay for a change in the attributes of any of the discrete alternatives which is simple to calculate and has an intuitive interpretation. © 1983.

Title: Relative vs. absolute price rigidity
Abstract: It is shown that to explain some nominal price rigidity it is sufficient to assume changes in costs to be imperfect signals on nominal changes, and not necessary to assume nominal costs to respond less than proportionally to nominal changes. © 1983.

Title: A note on the interaction between buyers and sellers
Abstract: This note demonstrates that common results are sensitive to the form of the buyer-seller interaction, whose important role is ignored by most market models. This is presented by an example of a market in which a buyer does not consider a seller's price quotation as final and can demand a lower price threatening to leave if his offer is not met. © 1983.

Title: Rational choice and gain functions derived from a fuzzy relation
Authors: Jin Bai Kim, Kern O. Kymn
Abstract: No theory of choice and gain based on a set-theoretic approach developed from new relational concepts termed 'fuzzy relations' in mathematics [Kim (1979,1980)] has been advanced. As evidenced in the literature [Kim (1979, 1980)], advances have occurred in set theory involving the concept of fuzzy relations that appear to be suitable for application in constructing a new and rigorous theory of choice and gain. The purpose of this paper is to derive rational choice and gain functions using the concept of fuzzy relations. © 1983.

Title: The two perils of symmetry-constrained estimation of demand systems
Abstract: When the error covariance matrix Σ of a demand system is unknown and is estimated, (1) symmetry-constrained estimates based on such a Σ estimate may have large mean squared errors, and (2) the conventionally computed standard errors may seriously underestimate the variability of these estimates. Several procedures are compared; the conventional one (which uses a Σ estimate consisting of mean squares and products of LS residuals) performs worst. © 1983.

Title: The integrability of generalized working models
Abstract: This paper demonstrates the integrability of the generalized Working (1943) model as proposed by Laitinen, Theil and Raparla (1983). © 1983.

Title: A generalization of working's model
Authors: Kenneth Laitinen, Henri Theil, Tejaswi Raparla
Abstract: Working's (1943) model states that budget shares are linear functions of the logarithm of income; it implies constant differences between corresponding marginal and budget shares. A one-parameter generalization is proposed which allows each marginal share to be a linear function of the corresponding budget share. This model can be further extended (with one extra parameter) so that all goods are either specific substitutes or specific complements. © 1983.

Title: Cobweb versus rational expectations models
Abstract: A cobweb model of occupational choice is found to fit the data almost as well as a rational expectations model, even though there are large forecastable changes in demand. Striking differences, however, are revealed when we simulate the two models. © 1983.

Title: Estimates of the option values for water quality improvements
Authors: V.Kerry Smith, William H. Desvousges, Ann Fisher
Abstract: This paper presents estimates of the option values associated with increased oppurtunities for outdoor recreation resulting from improved water quality. The estimates are based on a 1981 survey of 301 households in the Pennsylvania Monongahela River Basin. © 1983.

Title: Market power and output stability
Abstract: The conjectural variation elasticity is used in a comparative statics analysis to show that, contrary to a long-standing tenet of industrial organization, market power may destabilize output when cost and demand are stochastic, under other assumptions similar to those of recent empirical studies. © 1983.

Title: Increasing returns to scale and the reverse flexible accelerator
Abstract: We show that the flexible accelerator principle characterizes optimal investment behavior only when the firm's technology exhibits decreasing returns to scale throughout. When there are increasing returns we show that there is a range in which investment increases as the capital stock increases towards its long-run equilibrium level. © 1983.

Title: Constancy of equilibrium interest rates for power utility functions and stochastic constant returns to scale technologies
Abstract: Metron (1969, 1971) examined, inter alia the consumption and portfolio rules in a partial equilibrium context wherein the preferences are represented by a time additive power utility function. In these papers he exogenously assumed a constant instantaneously risk free rate of interest. In this paper we naturally embellish the results of Merton in a closed production economy where there are a number of stochastic constant returns to scale technologies with correlated outputs and show that the endogenously determined interest rate is a constant. While this result is recognized by researchers, explicit analytical characterization of equilibrium interest rate obtained in this paper is a new result. This paper establishes the internal consistency of the assumptions found in Metron (1969, 1971). © 1983.

Title: Are exchange rate movements a random walk?
Abstract: This note reports some evidence which shows that while month-to-month changes in exchange rates are difficult to explain in 1970's, year-to-year variations in exchange rates can be explained by standard variables such as money supplied, interest rates, and incomes. © 1983.

Title: Trade taxes and the current account
Abstract: We show that, under some conditions, a temporary import tariff improves the current account, whereas a temporary export tax deteriorates it. Permanent import tariffs and export taxes have an identical, although ambiguous, effect on the current account. © 1983.

Title: The multi-country transfer problem
Abstract: A general formula is derived for the welfare effects of a set of transfers among several countries in a two-good model with production and substitution, and compatible with Walrasian stability. The relation to recent work on transfer paradoxes is sketched. © 1983.

Title: The information matrix test
Abstract: In Chesher (1982) I show that the Information Matrix test introduced by White (1982) is a score test for parameter constancy. In this letter I show that this result leads to a simple computational procedure for calculating the Information Matrix test. The procedure involves computing, for a sample of n observations, n times the R2 from the least squares regression of a column of ones on a matrix whose elements are functions of 1st and 2nd derivatives of the log density function. © 1983.

Title: Multi-valued decision rules and coalitional non-manipulability
Abstract: In this paper we show that under the restriction that the individual's sincere preference orderings are linear (strict), there exists a fairly wide class of coalitionally non-manipulable democratic decision rules. These positive results are established without any restriction on the pairwise choice. It is also shown that the possibility of manipulation even by a single individual arises once he adopts a pessimistic approach in comparing two different sets of outcomes which reflect his attitude to risk. © 1983.

Title: A new characterization of simple majority
Abstract: Three axiomatic characterizations of two-alternative simple majority choice are presented. The first, by Kenneth May, uses anonymity and neutrality along with a positive responsiveness condition. The third characterizes simple majority solely in terms of local dynamics and a Pareto-optimality condition. The second, noted previously by the author, provides a connecting link between the others. © 1983.

Title: Price level determinacy and the choice of policy targets under rational expectations
Abstract: We show that in a conventional macro model with rational expectations, the government can use monetary policy to peg real interest rates, and still attain a determinate price level provided it also pegs some nominal policy variable, e.g., nominal expenditures. © 1983.

Title: Some notes on the stability of a simple Cournot economy with a leontief technology
Abstract: The stability analysis of a simple linear Cournot model is extended by including two branches producing inputs to each other and for consumption. Equilibrium turns out as stable under continuous adjustment. © 1983.

Title: Verifying a demand system by simulation
Authors: Henri Theil, Renate Finke, Mercedes C. Rosalsky
Abstract: An intriguingly small value of the asymptotic standard error of the estimate of the income flexibility inspired us to simulate the demand system. The procedure used should have more general applicability. © 1983.

Title: A new cross-country tabulation of the quality index of consumption
Abstract: Cross-country data are used to tabulate a quality index of consumption for each of 30 countries ranging in affluence from the U.S. to India as well as the real-income, relative-price and residual components of the quality index. © 1983.

Title: Blockmodeling complex statutes
Authors: Scott A. Boorman, Paul R. Levitt
Abstract: Blockmodeling, a combinatorial technique for relational data analysis, is applied to studying texts of complex economic legislation. By making this area a subject for mathematical modeling, using methods related to combinatorics, logic, and discrete optimization, we describe a new type of frontier between law and economics. © 1983.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
A new cross-country tabulation of income elasticities of demand
Authors: Renate Finke, Mercedes C. Rosalsky, Henri Theil
Abstract: Cross-country data are used to tabulate income elasticities of demand for ten commodity groups at the per capita real-income levels of 30 countries varying from India to the U.S. © 1983.

Title: Energy consumption in Australia
Authors: Tran Van Hoa, D.S. Ironmonger, I. Manning
Abstract: The paper reports an application of the generalized Working model, as proposed by Laitinen-Theil-Raparla (1981) to Australian household expenditure data, to obtain estimates of income elasticities for four types of energy: electricity, gas, other fuels and petrol. The evidence indicates some gain in the Laitinen-Theil-Raparla model but this gain is insufficient, in terms of the Atkinson (1973) test, to significantly discriminate it from the linear expenditure system. © 1983.

Title: Industrial sector interfuel substitution following the first major oil shock
Abstract: Strict conditions for a two-stage translog expenditure shares model are violated. A single- stage homothetic symmetry/equality model is rejected in favour of a non-homothetic equality model. International own-price elasticities derived from the latter for oil, gas, coal and electricity are -0.26, -0.81, -0.97 and -0.02, little changed from -0.24, -0.71, -1.35 and -0.09 for the former. © 1983.

Title: The value of large resource deposits or, how precious are the sea-bed nodules?
Abstract: It is shown that under a wide class of cases the social rent attributable to a large resource deposit is negligible. © 1983.

Title: A welfare analysis of monopolistic R & D
Abstract: Welfare analysis of monopolistic R&D is considered in this paper. The concept of reservation technology level as introduced in the economic literature is used. A reservation technology level is defined as that technology level, such that an R&D decision maker is just indifferent between doing R&D or not. It is demonstrated that a monopolist is less persistent in R&D search than a social welfare maximizer in the sense that a monopolist has a lower reservation technology level than a social welfare maximizer. © 1983.

Title: Profit cost margin, monopoly power and R & D intensity for industrial firms
Abstract: This paper analyzes the return to R & D and shows that R & D expenditures are correlated with firm monopoly power measured by the price cost margin. This may explain the above normal returns to R & D found in earlier empirical work. © 1983.

Title: Non-structural measures of competition
Abstract: Procedures for detecting or measuring market power have been suggested in recent years by Iwata, Rosse and Panzar, and Bresnahan. This paper integrates elements from all three approaches to provide a single, more unified alternative to the structure-conduct-performance paradigm. © 1983.

Title: A geometric note on some propositions in spatial pricing policy
Abstract: This note uses a simple geometric device to derive rules for identifying the shape of delivered price schedules. It is shown that the predatory pricing is not compatible with profit maximisation in situations where consumers are characterised by identical local demand functions. Only if demand functions vary over space in particular ways is it likely that predatory pricing can be justified as a profit maximising response. © 1983.

Title: Risk-aversion and the term structure of real interest rates correction
Inflation ‘news’ and exchange rates
Abstract: This paper presents a new test of the purchasing parity theory by investigating the announcement effect of unexpected inflation on the exchange rate of the US dollar against three European currencies. The evidence presented does not support the theory, at least in the very short run. © 1983.

Title: The service sector, monopolistic competition and the impact of emigration
Abstract: A framework is developed in which the service sector is characterized by the production of slightly-differentiated commodities under conditions of monopolistic competition. The impact of labor emigration is then examined and found to be welfare-worsening for the non-migrants. © 1983.

Title: Tax progression in Lindahl equilibrium
Abstract: This paper demonstrates that the incidence of benefit taxation depends on the ratio of income and price elasticities of demand for public goods. Several previously stated special cases of this formula are derived and some conflicting empirical evidence is discussed. © 1983.

Title: Competitive banks and the inflation tax
Authors: Guillermo A. Calvo, Roque B. Fernandez
Abstract: The purpose of this note is to show that the presence of a competitive banking sector has important quantitative implications for the revenue-maximizing rate of inflation. © 1983.

Title: The information loss through aggregation of the UK monetary components
Abstract: This paper calculates the information content of the UK monetary components in terms of their ability to predict movements in nominal income and assesses how much of this information is lost through restricting attention to subsets of these components and by sum aggregation. © 1983.

Title: Currency by denomination
Abstract: The distribution of the Dutch currency circulation by denomination is related to the requirements of efficient payment, i.e., payment involving a minimum number of coins or banknotes for any amount. © 1983.

Title: A note on the equivalence between two cones generated by a correspondence
A generalized recoverability theorem
Abstract: This paper investigates the feasibility of recovering intermediate production functions from observable market data. Specifically, n-factor multi-stage production processes are considered. It is proven that the total differential equation for production technology, estimated from basic factor input data, can always be reduced to a canonical form that is a function of intermediate products. © 1983.

Title: The independence of tests for structural change in regression models
Abstract: It is shown that the common tests for stability of regression coefficients and of the disturbance variance in linear regression models are independent. This enables the size of the joint test procedure to be controlled exactly. © 1983.

Title: The J-test as a Hausman specification test
Abstract: The purpose of this note is to show that the J-test of non-nested regression models proposed by Davidson and MacKinnon (1981), can also be viewed as a test of misspecification along the lines put forward by Hausman (1978). We give a proof for the case of single-equation linear models. © 1983.

Title: Small sample properties of alternative forms of the Lagrange Multiplier test
Abstract: We argue that alternative forms of the LM test may perform very differently in small samples. One common variant often yields misleading inferences, while an alternative variant, which we have recently proposed, performs much better. © 1983.

Title: The unimodal maximum entropy density
Abstract: In this paper we show how to obtain a fully unimodal maximum entropy density estimate. We use a characterization of unimodality due to Khinchine together with some derived moment equalities to formulate the problem as a constrained maximum entropy problem for an auxiliary variable. The technique and solution are new and do not involve smoothing an empirical histogram. © 1983.

Title: Interpreting the effects of binary variables in transformed models
Authors: James R. Blaylock, David M. Smallwood
Abstract: A mathematical formula is derived for use in interpreting the effects of binary explanatory variables in equations which have been transformed using the Box-Cox method. The formula expresses the proportionate change in the original dependent variable associated with a unit change in a dummy variable. © 1983.

Title: A note on the effects of linear approximation on hypothesis testing
Abstract: In this note we demonstrate that the use of a linear approximation model may effect the usual F-test for linear hypothesis when the true model is non-linear. © 1983.

Title: A note on the variability of inflation and the dispersion of relative price changes
Abstract: The relationship between the variance of inflation and the variability of relative price changes is analyzed empirically. A strong positive association is found for 1948-1969 and 1948-1975. Application of Chow's test indicates structural instability, and Granger's test suggests a feedback effect between these variables. © 1983.

Title: Inventories, rational expectations and economic activities
Authors: Kenneth S. Chan, Yannis M. Ioannides
Abstract: This paper examines the role of inventories, when adjustments in output involve fixed employment costs (such as hiring and training costs). These costs force the firm to use inventories to stabilize output fluctuations. Contrary to the Blinder-Fisher model, unanticipated aggregate disturbances in the present model may have no subsequent impacts on the economy. The exchange between McCallum and Blinder-Frydman are also discussed in this context. © 1983.

Title: Efficiency of sophisticated choice
Abstract: In the literature on changing tastes the fact that sophisticated choice is inefficient is well known. This paper explores the possibility that other equilibrium outcomes can Pareto dominate sophisticated choice. The paper contains necessary and sufficient conditions for this to be feasible. © 1983.

Title: A simple implementation of efficient allocations
Abstract: A simple constrained game form implementing Pareto-optimal allocations in any neoclassical environment is constructed. The mechanism treats group members symmetrically, it is feasible and finite dimensional. This general scheme is then applied to a problem of income redistribution in a society in which members exhibit social conscienceness. © 1983.

Title: On the cost-minimizing number of firms
Abstract: This note revises the Baumol-Fischer analysis of the cost-minimizing industry structure to the effect that all necessary information is limited to scale assumptions and that bounds on the cost-minimizing number of firms are guaranteed to exist. © 1983.

Title: Tests of a heterogeneous bidders theory of first price auctions
Authors: James C. Cox, Vernon L. Smith, James M. Walker
Abstract: This paper reports the results of eight first price sealed bid auction market experiments using cash motivated subjects to test a constant relative risk averse model (CRRAM) of equilibrium bidding behavior of heterogeneous bidders. © 1983.

Title: The complete breakdown of gross-substitutability in a Cobb-Douglas world
Abstract: We consider a simple Cobb-Douglas exchange economy with 2 traders. Taking effective demand as the relevant concept of demand, gross substitutability is shown to be generally ill-defined in a neighborhood of equilibrium prices. © 1983.

Title: To graduate or not
Abstract: A representative Dutch sample of about 1500 workers is analyzed for the effect of graduation on allocation (job level attained) and on earnings. Results differ between allocation and earnings and among types of education. For some types of education, there is clearly no evidence of screening. For some secondary types of education, a sequential information model is supported. As for higher vocational and university education, the evidence supports the gradual skill-augmenting view. © 1983.

Title: In search of a test of investor capital gain realization behavior to capital gain tax rates
Abstract: Existing empirical work on the effects of taxation on the realization of capital gains does not closely conform to recent theoretical work on the same question. Methodology is proposed to provide weak tests of the theory. © 1983.

Title: The sampling performance of pre-test estimators of the scale parameter under squared error loss
Authors: T.A. Yancey, G.G. Judge, D.M. Mandy
Abstract: This paper evaluates the sampling properties of the conventional, inequality and minimum mean square pre-test estimators of the scale parameter under a squared error loss. © 1983.

Title: Estimating models of expectations
Abstract: This paper outlines a simple method for continuous updating of parameters that requires direct estimation only in the initial period. The basic technique, which is fairly well-known in the statistics literature, is useful for estimating models of expectations where period by period updating is typically necessary. © 1983.

Title: Extension of the ridge regression technique to non-linear models with additive errors
Abstract: An extension of the ridge regression technique is proposed for non-linear models, when ill-conditioned data lead to imprecise non-linear least squares estimates. A large sample Bayesian interpretation of the approach is also provided. © 1983.

Title: The effects of inflation uncertainty and supply shocks on real interest rates
Abstract: Increased inflation uncertainty and negative supply shocks have been suggested separately as causes of the 1970s decline in real interest rates. When both factors appear in empirical interest rate models, supply forces exert a statistically significant impact on real rates while the effect of inflation uncertainty is insignificant. © 1983.

Title: Additional evidence on inflation variability
Abstract: The relationship between inflation and its variability has been examined by using time series data for eight Asian Countries. It is found that this relationship also holds for countries which have enjoyed a period of long price stability. Furthermore, this relationship also holds for highly industrialized countries. © 1983.

Title: An empirical note on money, government debt and inflation
Abstract: This paper uses U.S. post-war data and band spectral regression to test two polar hypotheses regarding the fundamental determinant of the price level. © 1983.

Title: Learning to agree
Abstract: An explicit model of communication and informational equilibrium is constructed and some results generalizing Aumann's theorem on the impossibility of agreeing to disagree are obtained, together with an example showing that full rationality may be sub-optimal. © 1983.

Title: Market demand is a continuous function of prices
Abstract: A natural class of probabilities on the space of consumers' preferences is presented for which market (i.e., mean) demand is a (continuous) function of prices although individual preferences may be non-convex. © 1983.

Title: Differentiability of the cost functions is equivalent to strict quasiconcavity of the production functions
Abstract: The assumption that cost functions are differentiable with respect to input prices is equivalent to the assumption that production functions are strictly quasiconcave. © 1983.

Title: The cournot oligopoly and competitive equilibria as solutions to non-linear complementarity problems
Abstract: The Cournot oligopoly and competitive equilibria are identified with solutions to non-linear complementarity problems, which leads to integration of the existence and stability proofs of these equilibria. © 1983.

Title: Shephard's lemma and rate of return regulation
Abstract: By counter example this paper shows that in general, Shephard's lemma cannot be used for the usual formulation of the rate of return regulated cost function. A solution to the problem is supplied. © 1983.

Title: From intertemporal strong quasi-concavity to temporary one
Abstract: One proves here that intertemporal strong quasi-concavity implies temporary strong quasi-concavity, without utilizing any separability assumption. © 1983.

Title: Keynesian unemployment as a nash equilibrium with endogenous wage/price setting
Abstract: A simple 3 good, 1 consumer, 1 firm model of fixed price, quantity constrained equilibrium is developed. A game is then defined on the set of (globally unique) equilibria. The consumer sets the money wage, the firm sets the money price of output (money is numeraire). Nash solutions of the game exist and may involve Keynesian unemployment but never involve Classical unemployment or Repressed inflation. © 1983.

Title: Communication in markets
Abstract: This paper draws attention to the problem of the communication of information between individuals. It suggests a mathematical tool, the theory of stochastic graphs which should prove particularly useful when modelling situations in which such communication is imperfect. Examples of the sort of result which may be obtained using this tool are given. © 1983.

Title: Family income and participation in schooling and higher education
Abstract: This note distinguishes between the participation rates of school-age students and those eligible to undertake higher education. That is, participation in higher education is only measured relative to those who have successfully completed their schooling, not to the whole population of young people in the relevant age group. © 1983.

Title: Trade union growth in Ireland, 1943–1977
Abstract: This paper reports some results which were obtained when the Bain and Elsheikh model of union growth was employed in an analysis of the Irish experience during the period 1943 to 1977. © 1983.

Title: A note on overemployment/underemployment in labor contracts under asymmetric information
Abstract: Models of labor contracts under asymmetric information may predict either overemployment or underemployment. This paper shows that this result depends crucially on whether or not leisure is a normal good if firms are risk neutral. © 1983.

Title: Suboptimal plant capacity in U.S. manufacturing
Abstract: Here, a new statistical proxy, called suboptimal plant capacity, is developed and empirically analyzed for a large sample of census industries. Suboptimal plant capacity is closely related with previous indices of suboptimal capacity, and has a clear relationship to the ratio of actual to optimal plant sizes. © 1983.

Title: Complete sterilization and perfect capital mobility
Abstract: It is shown that the received incompatibility of complete sterilization of foreign reserve movements with perfect capital mobility is not valid when the government adjusts purchases as interest payments alter, within a given total public expenditure. © 1983.

Title: Are developed country multilateral tariff reductions necessarily beneficial for the U.S.?
Abstract: Since the formation of the GATT in 1947, the belief underlying U.S. participation in GATT multilateral tariff reductions has been that they are beneficial to the U.S. This paper reports general equilibrium computations of the welfare effects of a 50% multilateral tariff reduction among developed countries using a seven region world trade model due to Whalley (1982). © 1983.

Title: Factor movements with three factors and two goods in the U.S. economy
Abstract: Ruffin's (1981) theoretical finding that extreme factors must be enemies and the middle factor must be a friend of both extreme factors, with constant product prices, in a three-factor, two-good general equilibrium model, is confirmed empirically for the United States. Results are used to explain the positions factor owners take on issues of factor movement policies. © 1983.

Title: Order-separable spaces
Abstract: This paper gives applications in utility theory of the fact that a second countable space can be embedded in an order-separable space. It is shown that Peleg's theorem is a generalization of both the classic Debreu theorems on the existence of continuous utility functions. © 1983.

Title: Use of the principal component method in the maximum likelihood estimation procedure of the logit model
Abstract: The maximum likelihood estimates of a qualitative response market are solved by an iterative procedure. When severe multicollinearity exists among the explanatory variables, this procedure may fail to converge. In this note, using a bank-failure model, we demonstrate how the principle component method can make the iterative procedure converge when it fails to do so in the untransformed model. © 1983.

Title: On calculating the edgeworth approximate distribution of an econometric estimator or test statistic
Abstract: This note outlines a practical algorithm for calculating the Edgeworth approximation of a general class of econometric estimators and test statistics. © 1983.

Title: Definitions of ‘second order approximation’ and of ‘flexible functional form’
Abstract: Second order approximations are widely used in demand modeling, although Diewert and Lau have provided different definitions of 'second order approximations'. We identify the relationship of each of those definitions to existing definitions in the mathematics of local approximation orders. © 1983.

Title: An alternative approach to simulating var models
Abstract: This paper proposes a simple approach to the problem of handling contemporaneous correlation of the error terms when simulating VAR models. The approach is illustrated with an example using an estimated VAR model of the New Zealand economy. © 1983.

Title: Regret theory and measurable utility
Abstract: This paper examines the relationship between regret theory and a novel set of axioms for choice under uncertainty, discusses the extent of complementarity and points to certain important distinctions between the two approaches. © 1983.

Title: Admissible mean standard deviation indifference curves
Abstract: This note considers the question of which indifference curves in mean standard deviation space can be derived from expected utility preferences. It is shown that the well known requirement that the slope of indifference curves be zero when standard deviation is zero is not the only restriction: many families of curves satisfying this requirement which are also nicely behaved and convex downwards can be ruled out because they imply behavior inconsistent with expected utility preferences. It is therefore not possible to draw arbitrary indifference curves and assume there exist underlying expected utility preferences which correspond to these. © 1983.

Title: Equilibrium points of non-atomic games
Abstract: An elementary proof, as well as an asymptotic version of David Schmeidler's theorem on the equilibrium points of non-atomic games is presented. © 1983.

Title: The signs of compensated price effects in quantity/quality models
Abstract: A disturbing feature of models embodying a quantity/quality trade-off is that income-compensated price effects on quantity and quality are permitted to be positive. It is shown in this note that it is nevertheless possible to place strong and useful restrictions on such price effects. It is shown that the signs of such effects will as a rule be negative if quantity and quality are net substitutes with respect to the composite of all other goods. © 1983.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Disparities in income elasticities by ethnic origin
Authors: Kenneth W. Clements, Lester W. Johnson
Abstract: This paper uses expenditure survey data to analyse disparities in income elasticities of demand by ethnic origin. Engel curve estimates indicate that the food elasticity varies with ethnic origin, while the others are quite similar. With data on five food commodities, the income elasticities display considerable disparities. © 1983.

Title: On the rationality of buying from a price predator
Abstract: By means of a simple example, I demonstrate that it may be rational for consumers to purchase at predatory prices, even though the exit of the intended victim and the consequent price increase are correctly anticipated. © 1983.

Title: On variable capital utilization and international trade theory
Abstract: If variable capital utilization results from within-period technological productivity variations, no modification of standard trade theory is required. If it results from within-period factor price variations, the modifications required are those of many factors in variable supply, i.e., non-traded goods. © 1983.

Title: An asymptotic property of equilibrium on futures markets arising from speculation
Abstract: This paper presents an asymptotic property of a joint spot-futures market equilibrium established in Cheng-Magill (1982). As speculators diversity over a large number of markets, the equilibrium risk premium converges to an asymptotic premium, the behaviour of which depends solely on the stochastic dependence between the spot price and an index of average returns on other markets. Risk arising from the variability of the spot price itself is diversified away. The results are related to the arbitrage pricing theory of Ross (1976). © 1983.

Title: A remark on a generalized specification test
Abstract: In testing orthogonality of a set of regressors when there exist other regressors known to be endogenous or exogenous, the appropriate test should be based on the difference between two estimators of the coefficients of regressors whose orthogonality is being tested. © 1983.

Title: On the classical nature of the Wu-Hausman statistics for the independence of stochastic regressors and disturbance
Abstract: Algebraic equivalences are shown between Lagrange Multiplier and Wald statistics and the various Wu (1973) and Hausman (1978) statistics for testing of independence of the full set of stochastic regressors and disturbance term in a single linear regression equation. © 1983.

Title: Conflict among testing procedures?
Abstract: This paper demonstrates that under certain conditions the Lagrange Multiplier test provides a better approximation to the asymptotic X2 distribution than the more familiar Wald and Likelihood Ratio tests. © 1983.

Title: Pre-test estimation under squared error loss
Authors: G.G. Judge, T.A. Yancey, M.E. Bock
