Abstract: A Divisia version of the country-product-dummy method of Kravis et al. is obtained and extended to include income as an explanatory variable. Income elasticities of relative prices for eight goods across 15 countries are obtained and compared with the income elasticities of the demand for these goods. © 1980.

Title: The maximal degree of dependence among inputs, outputs, and consumer goods
Abstract: The maximal degree of dependence among consumer goods, inputs, or outputs is determined by the ratio of the arithmetic mean to the geometric mean of the latent roots of the independence transformation. These roots are the income elasticities of the transformed consumer goods or the Divisia elasticities of the transformed inputs or outputs. The maximum is attained when all observed goods have the same own-price elasticity. © 1980.

Title: Variable output elasticities and technique-specific technical progress
Abstract: The possibility of accounting for technique specific technical progress in an econometric production function is raised. In addition the validity of the assumption of constant output elasticities over input combinations is questionned and tested using aggregate U.S. industrial data. There appears to be considerable variation in output elasticities over different techniques of production. © 1980.

Title: Monopoly and product selection
Abstract: It is shown by example that, even if there are fixed costs, a monopolist may provide more than the socially optimal number of products. © 1980.

Title: Country-specific and time-specific factors in the demand for international reserves
Authors: Jacob A. Frenkel, Craig S. Hakkio
Abstract: This paper allows for country-specific and time-specific factors in the demand for international reserves by applying the error-components model. Forecasts based on the GLS parameter estimates are shown to be superior to those based on the OLS estimates. © 1980.

Title: A note on the dynamic adjustment of the demand for international reserves by LDC's
Abstract: The dynamics of the adjustment of the demand for international reserves by LDC's is analyzed. Using a GLS procedure on pooled cross section-time series data it is showed that, contrary to previous results, the speed at which actual reserves adjust to desired reserves is very fast: in one year 95 percent of this adjustment is completed. © 1980.

Title: An empirical note on bond-yield uncertainty and the demand for money
Abstract: This paper empirically tests the effect of bond-yield uncertainty on the demand for money, as implied by the capital theory approach to the demand for money, suggested by Friedman and Tobin. It is expected that the demand for money is affected not only by the yield on bonds (which are a substitute asset), but it also in increasing function of their risk. The empirical tests, which employ two alternative measures of uncertainty (mean of squared deviations from the average, and the mean of squared deviation from a predictor obtained by exponential smoothing) seem to support the Friedman-Tobin hypothesis. © 1980.

Title: The precision gain from additional predictions
Abstract: The gain in precision from an additional prediction is analyzed by regressing the error of this prediction on those of the predictions already available. The result is simple and illuminating; it is extended to the case of m additional predictions. © 1980.

Title: A simple form of the maximum entropy moment matrix and its inverse
Abstract: The maximum entropy (ME) moment matrix is always non-singular due to a ridge above the diagonal. This paper gives an explicit expression for this ridge and for the inverse of the ME moment matrix. © 1980.

Title: Disequilibrium econometrics and non-linear budget constraints
Abstract: In ordinary estimation situations a linear, additive error term captures some unknown combinations of population hetereogeneity and disequilibrium error. If the budget constraint is non-linear, these two sources can be separately identified. © 1980.

Title: On a simple procedure for testing non-nested regression models
Abstract: In this note we discuss some aspects of a procedure which we recently proposed for testing non-nested regression models. It is argued that, although the procedure is arbitrary to some degree, this arbitrariness is inconsequential. © 1980.

Title: Testing the permanent income hypothesis using a general rational lag formulation
Authors: Richard T. Baillie, Patrick C. McMahon, David J. Smyth
Abstract: This paper estimates a permanent income model of consumption with a constrained moving average error process. Our results do not support the permanent income theory. © 1980.

Title: A golden rule for uncertain monopolists
Abstract: It is shown that monopolists who are uncertain of the level of output at which they will maximise profits can use a simple decision rule, based on the 'golden section', for choosing an efficient sequence of experiments. © 1980.

Title: On equity and efficiency
Abstract: We investigate the following problem within the context of a simple exchange economy: Will a sequence of fair net trades (wherein each agent prefers his or her trade to that of any other), starting from the equal division allocation, result in a final allocation which is itself fair? The answer is generally negative. © 1980.

Title: The ‘flexible accelerator’ and optimization with a finite horizon
Abstract: So-called 'flexible accelerator' or partial adjustment models can be derived from dynamic optimization under convex adjustment costs. However, even with time-invariant adjustment costs and constant discount rate, constancy of the speed of adjustment requires infinite horizon planning. Using a simple production model, it is shown here that for finite horizons, the adjustment may nevertheless be approximately constant for much of the time if the discount rate is high enough and if the marginal adjustment cost is sufficiently small. © 1980.

Title: Multiple variable factors, demand uncertainty, and the cooperative firm
Abstract: It has been shown that the risk averse, cooperative firm producing its output with labor as the only variable input and selling this output in a competitive market will produce more than the cooperative firm operating under condition of certainty. This letter proves that this result may not apply to the case of the cooperative firm facing a stochastic demand and/or employing more than one variable input. © 1980.

Title: On the recoverability of intertemporal preferences
Abstract: In the absence of futures markets, a consumer's complete set of intertemporal demand functions may not be revealed. Under mild regularity conditions, the multiperiod utility function that generates the observable demand functions is shown to be unique in the class of additively separable and stationary functions. © 1980.

Title: An alternative to steady-state comparisons
Abstract: For derivative changes in parameters, this note derives a simple expression for the present discounted value of the change in an economic variable along the convergent path from one steady state to another. This expression is not more complicated than the comparison of steady states ignoring the convergence. © 1980.

Title: A factor price and public input equalization theorem
Abstract: We elaborate on the remark that free international trade equalizes factor returns as well as the quantities of public inputs. © 1980.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Erratum
The measurement and trend of inequality
Abstract: A variety of revisions and adjustments to our standard measures of inequality have been proposed in recent years. This note corrects a serious error in that work which could reverse conclusions in instances of great inequality. © 1979.

Title: Freedom, affluence, growth and inequality
Abstract: Following Gastil's classification of countries into 'free', 'partly free' and 'not free', and considering the developing world, there appears to be a mild negative correlation between freedom and per capita income. However, no clear pattern emerges in the relationship between freedom and income growth, or between freedom and intra-country inequality. © 1979.

Title: The cost minimizing number of firms and the discipline of competition
Abstract: Starting from the premise that costs of production are partly a function of the level of competition, we proceed to analyse the implications of the trade-off between cost decreases due to rivalry and cost increases due to fragmentation of production. © 1979.

Title: Revenue and cost constraints in efficient multi-division firms
Abstract: If revenue and cost of a division are monotonically related for any state of the world and the firm's centre chose between constraining revenue and cost prior to that state being revealed, then behavioural and welfare implications of the choice may be significant and are the subject of this letter. © 1979.

Title: Effects of exogenous changes in foreign exchange rates and income growth rates on the geographic pattern of exports: The case of Israel
Abstract: The movement to a universal system of flexible exchange rates has meant that countries are continually facing fluctuations in the price of their currency relative to that of their major trading partners. The stronger a currency becomes the more exports it will attract, and if imports are a normal good then exports will also increase as income rises. These hypotheses are tested for Israel vis à vis its three main trading partners, the United States, Germany and the U.K. © 1979.

Title: Hypothesis tests and confidence intervals for mean elasticities calculated from linear regression equations
Abstract: This paper outlines and evaluates two techniques for testing hypotheses about mean elasticities obtained from linear regression equations. These tests are often necessary so that the implications of the estimates can be fully appreciated. For example, we are often interested in whether a given elasticity is greater or smaller than unity. © 1979.

Title: A note on the Tobit likelihood function
Abstract: The likelihood functions for several econometric models are unbounded over certain sequences in parameter space. Examples are the disequilibrium model, the conditional logit model and a certain type of switching regression model. We show how a similar difficulty may arise in the Tobit model but that the presence of this anomaly becomes less likely as sample size increases. © 1979.

Title: Rebased and revised data — their effects on econometric estimates
Abstract: A constant-price macroeconomic model for 1956 to 1976 is estimated using three different sets of data: at 1970 prices published in 1977, at 1975 prices published in 1978 and at 1975 prices published in 1979. The differing estimates are compared. © 1979.

Title: A Filippov solution of a system of differential equations with discontinuous right-hand sides
Abstract: This note advocates a Filippov solution for a system of differential equations with discontinuous right-hand sides. The Filippov solution is applied to a dynamic disequilibrium macroeconomic model, showing a unique solution is determined despite discontinuities at the boundaries of different regimes. © 1979.

Title: Estimation in multimarket disequilibrium models
Authors: Stephen M. Goldfeld, Richard E. Quandt
Abstract: A two-market disequilibrium model with spillovers is formulated. The parameters are estimated in sampling experiments by (1) ignoring spillovers, (2) treating them as if they were exogenous, (3) maximizing the likelihood function that is appropriate in the presence of spillovers. It is found that the cost in terms of root mean square error of using the incorrect estimator is serious. However, the computational time needed to maximize the likelihood function with spillovers rises sharply with the number of markets in the model due to the multiple integrals involved in evaluating the likelihood function. © 1979.

Title: Measurement error and the demand for money in Australia
Authors: Kenneth W. Clements, James F. Meisner
Abstract: Theil's (1979a) measurement error interpretation of the constant terms in differential demand equations is shown to be consistent with the Australian data used by Meisner and Clements (1979). © 1979.

Title: A simulation study of the maximum entropy moment matrix
Abstract: Whereas the sample moment matrix may not yield an estimate of the inverse of the population moment matrix because of singularity, the maximum entropy (ME) moment matrix is always positive definite. An experiment indicates superiority of the ME moment matrix over the sample moment matrix even when the latter is not singular. © 1979.

Title: Misspecified polynomial detrending
Abstract: This letter shows that substantial errors result in linear detrending of the data when a linear trend is inappropriate. These errors increase without bound with increasing sample size! Also, the reliability of the linear trend is overstated. © 1979.

Title: Antithetic variates to estimate the simulation bias in non-linear models
Abstract: This paper describes a Monte Carlo experiment, which makes use of antithetic variate sampling, to get an accurate estimate of the deterministic simulation bias in the non-linear Klein-Goldberger model. The computational efficiency is more than 500 times greater than in case of simple random sampling. © 1979.

Title: Computation of search duration probabilities and the integral of the normal distribution function
Abstract: The constraction of likelihood functions for data on individuals assumed to be sampling from a price distribution and operating a reservation price policy involves calculation of the probability that their duration of search exceeds, say, t periods, P( T > t). In this note we show how this calculation can be simply done by (a) working in continuous time, and (b) using a result on the integral of the Normal distribution function. We then use the result to study some properties of the model. © 1979.

Title: A note on monetary policy effectiveness, the correspondence principle, and the positively sloped is curve
Abstract: This note considers the implications of a positively sloped IS curve subject to Samuelson's correspondence principle. Explicit derivation of the stability conditions leads to the conclusion that the less interest elastic is the demand for money, the faster is the speed with which monetary and fiscal policies operate. © 1979.

Title: Club participation under uncertainty
Abstract: Exclusion from clubs entails uncertainty about participation. Implications of this uncertainty for optimal club size and the club's choices are derived. © 1979.

Title: Consumption externalities and stability
Abstract: This paper analyses the stability properties of simple general equilibrium models involving reciprocal consumption externalities and explores the relationship between stability and the anomalous behaviour noted by Diamond and Mirrlees (1973) and others. © 1979.

Title: Errata
Temporal risks and the tenure decision in housing markets
Abstract: A model of housing quality hierarchy is used to analyze the tenure decision in housing markets under uncertainty. © 1979.

Title: The effect of the shape of the income distribution on two inequality measures
Abstract: This letter describes the effect of skewness and kurtosis of the log-income distribution on two measures of income inequality. Positive skewness and leptokurtosis affect inequality positively. © 1979.

Title: The response of fertility to the expectation of death
Authors: Stephen Haynes, Llad Phillips, Harold L. Votey
Abstract: Demographic transitions are often characterized by a period of declining death rates and high or even rising birth rates. This note summarizes an economic explanation for the period which is based on (1) the response of fertility to the expectation of the death of children, and (2) the distinction between actual and desired family size. © 1979.

Title: Price-cost margins and foreign trade in U.S. textile and apparel industries: An analysis of pooled cross-section and time-series data
Abstract: This study finds an unexpected, positive and significant association between price-cost margins and import-domestic shipment ratio for the U.S. textile and apparel industries, using pooled cross-section and time-series data. Distortions created by import quotas account for this anomalous finding. © 1979.

Title: The cost of adjustment and inventory accumulation studies
Abstract: Because so called flexible accelerator model (FAM) representations of inventory accumulation are misspecified, and because the two hypotheses are not properly nested, the superiority of Feldstein-Auerbach's (1976) target-adjustment model in fitting the data, cannot be taken as an indication that FAM are inappropriate. The misspecification involves omission of a cost of adjustment variable, omission of user cost of inventory variables, and a linear specification. © 1979.

Title: The effect of forward markets on exporting firms
Abstract: This note suggests that exchange rate uncertainty does not affect exports if firms can insure their revenue in forward markets. © 1979.

Title: International reserves: Adjustment dynamics
Authors: John F.O. Bilson, Jacob A. Frenkel
Abstract: This paper presents evidence suggesting that central banks have a target level of international reserves, and that the dynamics of adjustment is rapid. The estimated speed of adjustment is faster than suggested by previous estimates. © 1979.

Title: A note on the use of elasticity identities as empirical devices
Abstract: This note investigates the empirical properties of identities commonly used by empiricists in international trade. The analysis suggests that traditional applications of the identities to empirical problems are invalid, but that a modified procedure may be useful. © 1979.

Title: The precision gain from adding an equation in joint linear estimation
Abstract: What is the gain in precision when we extend joint estimation of L equations by adding another equation? The answer is formulated in terms of (1) the degree of linear independence of the explanatory variables of each of the L equations of those of the added equation and (2) the degree of linear dependence of the disturbances of the added equation on those of all others jointly. © 1979.

Title: A simple lagrange multiplier test for lognormal regression
Authors: Dale J. Poirier, Paul A. Ruud
Abstract: In the spirit of diagnostic testing, this study proposes a simple Lagrange multiplier test for the appropriateness of the lognormal regression model. The alternative hypothesis covers the class of Box-Cox truncated regression models considered by Poirier (1978). The simplicity of the test arises from the absence of any truncation under the null hypothesis. © 1979.

Title: On the generalized Berkson's estimator in the general qualitative response model
Abstract: Estimation of the general qualitative response model, P k = F k (xβ 1 ,..., x H β), k = 1,..., K, where H ≤ K, is considered. We show under general conditions that asymptotically efficient generalized Berkson's estimators can be derived even if H < K. Two bivariate polychotomous probit models are analyzed. © 1979.

Title: Divisia moments of U.S. industry, 1947–1978
Abstract: Divisia moments of the first and second order are presented for annual price and quantity data on 56 two-digit U.S. industries in 1947-1978. Quantity variances tend to exceed price variances, while price-quantity covariances are almost all negative. © 1979.

Title: Education as a signal
Abstract: It is shown that education can work as a signal, even if its costs are not correlated with the desired characteristic. A positive correlation between the benifits of holding a degree and ability will do the trick equally well. The set of signals owing their existance to this second criterion may be of considerable practical relevance. © 1979.

Title: The classical supply hypothesis and the observational equivalence of Classical and Keynesian models
Abstract: The possibility of distinguishing between Keynesian and Classical macroeconomic structures from reduced form estimates is examined under alternative versions of the aggregate supply hypothesis. It is shown that the intertemporal substitution of labour under rational expectations includes the Sargent-Wallace hypothesis and the Lucas supply function. It is more general than the restriction introduced by McCallum that only current innovations influence output. In general, one cannot distinguish between the two macroeconomic models in the absence of McCallum's restriction. © 1979.

Title: Non-cooperative equilibrium with price discriminating firms
Abstract: There exists a unique, non-cooperative equilibrium in output levels for a group of firms which sell differentiated products and are able to practice first degree price discrimination. The equilibrium does not maximize joint profits. © 1979.

Title: Signalling: Efficiency and equilibrium
Authors: Keith Leffler, John B. Long, Thomas Russell
Abstract: This paper explores the differences with respect to the existence of equilibrium in continuous versus discrete signalling models. Contrary to prior claims, we show that there is no qualitative difference; in either case efficient and/or inefficient equilibria can exist. © 1979.

Title: Willingness to pay and the compensation threshold
Abstract: Willingness to pay is formally defined as the maximum price a consumer will pay for one of a set of alternatives. This concept and a related concept, the compensation threshold, are shown to be useful in the context of discrete choice theory. © 1979.

Title: Private markets and production decisions
Abstract: The creation of personalized markets for artificial commodities can be used to analyze the choice of profit maximization as a firm's objective function and the choice of product 'characteristics'. A re-interpretation of Lindahl-type equilibria in these models provides useful insights into the structure of these models. © 1979.

Title: Forecasts of construction activity for states
Abstract: This note presents a description of a computerized information system (including an econometric model) that will provide analyses of construction labor demand in local areas. In addition, preliminary results from the housing sector of the model are presented. © 1979.

Title: Components of the change in regional inequality
Abstract: The change in regional inequality can be decomposed in terms of per capita income changes and population changes. Application to U.S. data for states and larger regions shows that the regional inequality decline from 1970 to 1977 is wholly due to per capita income changes. © 1979.

Title: International income inequality: 1970 and 1978
Abstract: Cross-country income inequality increased by 10% to 15% between 1970 and 1978. Use of ordinary, rather than 'real', exchange rates overstates cross-country inequality by 60% to 75%. Fairly detailed data suggest average within-country inequality is about one-half of inter-country inequality. © 1979.

Title: On the weak versus the strong version of the screening hypothesis
Abstract: The paper draws a theoretical distinction between the weak and the strong version of the screening hypothesis, depending on wether employers pay irrational wages at the initial hiring point (weak) or continuously thereafter (strong). This theoretical distinction is empirically tested using micro data from the United Kingdom. The results of the tests do not support the strong screening version. © 1979.

Title: A general asset pricing model
Abstract: With only minimal assumptions, a general version of the security market line is obtained. In addition, it is suggested that instead of concentrating on the relationship between risk and return, the testable theories of capital market equilibrium should contain specific hypotheses about the true aggregate demands and supplies of risky assets. © 1979.

Title: A note on the neutrality of the cash flow corporation tax
Abstract: The cash flow tax has been widely recommended as a form of taxing corporate income which is neutral with respect to investment decisions. This note points out that the claim is valid only under the assumption that the tax rate is constant over time. By contrast, an 'ideal' profits tax is neutral whatever the time shape of the tax rate. © 1979.

Title: A many-good Corlett-Hague tax rule
Abstract: The paper proves the Corlett-Hague tax rule for the many-good economy. © 1979.

Title: Portfolio and wealth effects of bond finance and the stability of the monetarist policy rule
Abstract: It is shown that the potential instability of the monetarist policy rule does not disappear if government bonds are not net wealth; on the contrary, portfolio balance effects make instability very likely for this case. © 1979.

Title: Exact aggregation and estimation
Abstract: In this paper we provide sufficient conditions, which, when combined with recent developments in the theory of exact aggregation, permit estimation of group specific demand systems when micro-level information is unavailable. We illustrate the approach by estimating group specific cost of living indices using only readily available census information and aggregate expenditure data. © 1979.

Title: On comparisons of normal and logistic models in the bivariate dichotomous analysis
Abstract: In discriminating between normal and logistic models in the analysis of bivariate dichotomous dependent variables, Cox-type statistics have been proposed; however we point out that there are cases in which the two models are either statistically equivalent or nested and Cox-type statistics are not suitable for use. © 1979.

Title: On the interpretation of the cox test in econometrics
Abstract: This note is concerned with discrimination and significance testing in respect of non-nested hypotheses in econometrics. It is argued that logic requires a test of discrimination to be one-tailed and a significance test for a non-nested hypothesis to be two-tailed. It is also argued that the significance test of a pair of non-nested hypotheses sensibly involves consideration of another. This is introduced so that the cause of deviation from the tested hypothesis away from the alternative may be attributed to it. © 1979.

Title: Biological capital theory: a question and a conjecture
Authors: Murray C. Kemp, Elvin J. Moore
Abstract: A community possesses an empty tract of land, good only for growing trees of a particular type. What is the optimal pattern of planting and harvesting? If utility is convex in consumption it is optimal to plant and harvest periodically. If the utility function is strictly concave our numerical analyses suggest that the forest approaches a balanced state in which the rate of timber production is uniform. © 1979.

Title: Capital accumulation and welfare: a note
Abstract: Diamond's neoclassical growth model with National Debt is reconsidered with respect to dynamic welfare considerations. Conditions under which capital deepening implies increasing welfare are dependent upon the stability of the steady state, the interest elasticity of savings, and the relationship between the marginal propensity to save and the elasticity of substitution in production. © 1979.

Title: A direct characterization of Black's first borda count
Abstract: This note shows that a characterization of Black's first Borda score can be derived directly from this score itself (which Black neglected because 'it is clumsier and needs much more labour') by using two characteristic functions. The note closes by obtaining Black's original characterization of his second Borda score as a corollary and giving an alternative 'closeness to unanimity' interpretation. © 1979.

Title: On aversion to positive risks and preference for negative risks
Abstract: An intertemporal Von Neumann-Morgenstern utility function may account for aversion to risks when only gains are at stake and preference for risks when only losses are at stake. It may therefore be used to account for the findings of Markowitz and Kahneman and Tversky. © 1979.

Title: Utilitarian versus egalitarian redistributions
Abstract: If preferences admit an inferior good, then non-exceptional cases are shown to arise, where the sum of two consumers' concave utilities will be increased by transfers of any goods, themselves inferior or not, from the worse-off consumer to the better-off. © 1979.

Title: Terminal conditions as a means of ensuring unique solutions for rational expectations models with forward expectations
Authors: Patrick Minford, Kent Matthews, Satwant Marwaha
Abstract: Terminal conditions are imposed on rational expectations models as a means of finding a unique solution among a continuum of potential solutions. It is argued that using terminal conditions is superior to invoking stability. The method can be applied to non-linear as well as linear systems. © 1979.

Title: Equilibrium business cycle theory with centralized trading in some assets
Abstract: This paper studies the consequences of information produced by economy-wide trading in assets for the equilibrium theory of the business cycle. The effects of unanticipated monetary disturbances are shown to depend on the nature of the other aggregate disturbances. © 1979.

Title: Competitive price adjustment
Abstract: A study is made of a competitive trading process in which a price-maker calls prices periodically under the obligation of trading for his own account to satisfy excess demand. Characteristics of the price-maker's optimal behavior are derived. The price-maker system is evaluated with respect to an alternative market clearing system. © 1979.

Title: The demand function with quality
Abstract: This letter provides a possible derivation of a demand function which involves quality as an argument on a basis of a simple consumer's behaviour model. Using the model one can analyse the cross elasticity sign. © 1979.

Title: Uniqueness of general economic equilibrium
Abstract: For a well-known economic model involving n commodities that are offered for sale, it is proved that there is at most one normalized equilibrium if the values of a certain matrix-valued function of order (n - 1) are Hicksian (i.e., have positive principal minors) throughout its domain of definition. The condition has a nice interpretation, and the result differs from an earlier (and very differently proved) uniqueness result of Arrow and Hahn primarily in that the class of excess-demand functions considered here is considerably less restricted in an important sense. © 1979.

Title: A note on the global stability in dynamical economic systems
Abstract: A simple set of sufficient conditions is given for utility functions to satisfy the Q-matrix condition of Brock and Scheinkman. Utility functions must be sufficiently concave but not excessively concave compared with the discount rate. © 1979.

Title: Acknowledgement
Determinants of cross-country consumption differences other than the real income difference
Abstract: The variance of the equivalent income changes measures the degree to which real income fails to account for observed consumption changes. Such variances are applied and discussed in a cross-country context, together with their substitution and residual components, for data on 15 countries. © 1979.

Title: A cross-cross-section analysis of consumption patterns
Authors: Haji Y. Izan, Kenneth W. Clements
Abstract: Houthakker's (1957) cross-section data are pooled across surveys to estimate one Engel curve system. Using the Working (1943) - Leser (1963) model, the estimated income elasticities are for food 0.78, clothing 1.07, housing 1.08 and miscellaneous 1.28. © 1979.

Title: Short-run employment functions for public utilities in the United States
Abstract: The well-known short-run employment function model is found to perform well for the U.S. Telephone and Telegraph and Electric utilities, but to be inapplicable to the Gas industry. © 1979.

Title: Agricultural research and biological productivity: Some Australian results
Abstract: Data on scientific publication is used as a proxy for the intensity of research activity in a study of the influence of research on agricultural productivity. Publications are separated according to the commodity to which they are related. © 1979.

Title: A note on exchange rate dynamics
Abstract: A solution to a model designed to study how exchange rates respond to policy changes is obtained. The solution may be used to predict the effect of an anticipated increase in the money supply. © 1979.

Title: Measuring the rate of protection with index numbers
Authors: Ernest H. Oksanen, James R. Williams
Abstract: Two approaches to measuring the rate of protection in binary comparisons, involving use of Fisher's Ideal Index, are proposed. One is relevant to measuring 'discrimination' in tariffs and the other is relevant to measuring a 'composition effect'. © 1979.

Title: Public good provision with optimal and non-optimal commodity taxation
Abstract: The criterion for welfare-enhancing changes in the level of public good provision is studied in a model with optimal, and more general, commodity tax structures. The welfare rule is sensitive to the precise nature of interactions between public spending and (ordinary or compensated) demands for taxed goods. © 1979.

Title: The velocity behavior and information content of Divisia monetary aggregates
Authors: William A. Barnett, Paul A. Spindt
Abstract: Monetary aggregates are commonly sums, although summation quantity aggregation is disreputable. We compare summation versus Divisia aggregation of monetary assets. The velocity behavior and the information content of the Divisia index are superior to those of the summation index. © 1979.

Title: Data revisions in the U.S. international transactions statistics
Abstract: This note will examine data revisions in a subset of the U.S. international transaction statistics to determine whether the earliest and final data show similar patterns. © 1979.

Title: A new estimation procedure under rational expectations
Abstract: A new procedure for the estimation of behavioral equations that involve the present discounted value of rationally expected future income stream is proposed. The procedure is then applied to the estimation of the permanent income consumption function. © 1979.

Title: Variations across households in the rate of inflation
Abstract: The variance of inflation across households is expressed in terms of (1) the inequality of the income distribution and (2) price changes of luxuries relative to those of necessitates. © 1979.

Title: On the stability of the Klein-I model
Authors: Carlo Bianchi, Giorgio Calzolari, Paolo Corsi
Abstract: This paper presents a revision of the numerical results by Theil and Boot (1962) on the asymptotic standard errors of characteristic roots in the Klein-I model. © 1979.

Title: Fair rights
Abstract: This note argues that analysis of constraints on rights assignments per se is important for social choice theory. By way of illustration, the equity concept of 'fairness', when applied to rights, is shown to admit the existence of libertarian social decision functions. © 1979.

Title: Monetary non-neutrality with anticipatory price setting and rational expectations
Abstract: It is proved that the neutrality proposition for anticipated monetary policy fails, when markets do not continuously clear and prices partly adjust in accordance with rationally anticipated disequilibrium. The model exhibits non-uniqueness, but all solutions are non-neutral. © 1979.

Title: The consistent application of boundary conditions in rational expectations models
Abstract: When boundary conditions are applied consistently, real variables are invariant to the unit of account in both backward looking and forward looking solutions to monetary models of inflation with rational expectations. © 1979.

Title: Substitution and scale effects with and without homotheticity
Abstract: This paper derives a simple functional relation between substitution and scale concepts applicable to the theories of consumption and production. Its usefulness is illustrated by pulling together various results about the relation between savings and the interest rate. © 1979.

Title: A note on the duty of disclosure
Abstract: This letter studies the possibility of voluntary breach of contract in the presence of new information. If the information had to be disclosed prior to the agreement, it is shown by example that all individuals may be worse off than if the act of disclosure is itself voluntary. © 1979.

Title: Demand estimation, risk-aversion and sticky prices
Abstract: Uncertainty about the price elasticity of demand has an effect comparable to that of a kink in the demand curve, for a risk-averse firm; the kink being located at the prevailing price and quantity. © 1979.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Cross-country variation in the quality of consumption
Abstract: The quality of consumption, formulated in terms of the luxary/necessity composition of the consumer's basket, is measured by means of an index for each of 15 countries ranging in affluence from the U.S. to India. The discussion includes the real-income, relative-price, and residual components of this index. © 1979.

Title: Speculative bubbles, crashes and rational expectations
Abstract: Self ending speculative bubbles, i.e., speculative bubbles followed by market crashes, are consistent with the assumption of rational expectations. More generally, speculative bubbles may take all kinds of shapes. Detecting their presence or rejecting their existence is likely to prove very hard. © 1979.

Title: A differential approach to input-output analysis
Abstract: The differential production theory approach is applied to input-output analysis under the assumption that each industrial sector behaves as a homothetic cost-minimizing firm. This yields substitution terms which take a simple form under input independence. © 1979.

Title: Income tax progressivity and revenue growth
Authors: John P. Hutton, Peter J. Lambert
Abstract: Musgrave and Musgrave's average rate progression is shown to be a measure of the progressivity of an income tax schedule from which useful propositions about the built-in flexibility and elasticity of total revenue can be obtained. © 1979.

Title: The effect of measurement errors on the estimation of demand systems
Abstract: Statistical inference in complete demand systems is usually based on imperfect data. This letter explores some of the implications of these imperfections, in particular for the estimates of income elasticities. © 1979.

Title: Some consequences of viewing LIML as an iterated Aitken estimator
Abstract: This note demonstrates that LIML can be formulated as Zellner's SUR estimator. The result provides an analytic formula for LIML and its derived reduced form estimator, expresses LIML as the sum of 2SLS and a correction factor and facilities exogeneity testing. © 1979.

Title: Mixed logit and fully recursive logit models
Abstract: Mixed logit model has been proposed for modelling simultaneous effects of qualitative and continuous response in the econometrics literatures. However, we point out that the concept of simultaneity does not apply in that model. It is an equivalent representation of a fully recursive logit model. © 1979.

Title: The direct estimation of the equilibrium response in a linear dynamic model
Abstract: It is shown that any linear dynamic model can be written in a form which enables the equilibrium multipliers to be estimated directly. Furthermore, these estimates are directly equivalent to those derived from the unrestricted reduced form. © 1979.

Title: On market imperfections and labor management
Abstract: It is shown that, in an imperfect setting, the labor-managed firm must stop producing in the long-run. © 1979.

Title: On fixed point theorems and social choice paradoxes
Abstract: This note explores the relationship of social choice paradoxes to fixed point theorems. A special case of the paradox proven in Chichilnsky (forthcoming), the non-existence of a continuous anonymous rule that respects anonymity with two voters and two dimensional choice spaces, is proven here to be equivalent to a fixed point problem. We indicate also how the results can be extended to higher dimensional choice spaces and any finite number of agents. © 1979.

Title: The effectiveness of monetary reform under rational expectations
Abstract: Automatic monetary stabilizers based on interest rate information are analyzed in a rational expectations framework. Their impact on price level variability is studied, and their effectiveness is compared to optimal decentralized monetary instruments. © 1979.

Title: A note on modelling downturns
Abstract: This note presents empirical/simulations results which compare a simple Kaldor-type non-linear model and comparable linear autoregressive schemes as models of sharp movements often observed in macroeconomic time series that exhibit persistent fluctuations. © 1979.

Title: Price dispersion in atomistic competition
Abstract: This note presents necessary conditions for non-degenerate price dispersion in a continuous atomistic market where buyers with price-elastic demand search sequentially for the lowest price, and firms maximize profit subject to a variable average cost function. © 1979.

Title: On the stability of the stackelberg oligopoly equilibrium
Abstract: The stability of the equilibrium in the Stackelberg undifferentiated oligopoly model where each oligopolist strives for leadership is analyzed for general demand and cost functions and for a discrete system with non-instantaneous adjustment. © 1979.

Title: Optimality: where competition fails and monopoly succeeds
Abstract: Where, initially, the demand curve is a marginal curve and the supply curve is an average curve, 'exploitation' only of the supply curve, transforming it into a marginal curve, is required. If, initially, the reverse is true, optimality requires that the demand curve alone be 'exploited'. © 1979.

Title: Temporal convergence and factor intensities
Authors: Ronald W. Jones, J. Peter Neary
Abstract: In the two-sector neoclassical production model with no factor-market distortions, the value and physical factor-intensity rankings of the two sectors may differ when the economy is out of long-run equilibrium, but such a difference does not imply any failure of convergence to long-run equilibrium. © 1979.

Title: A refinement of the core equivalence theorem
Abstract: It is known that if blocking coalitions are restricted to be small relative to the size of the economy then the approximation of core allocations by competitive allocations can still be assured. This paper proves that the same type of approximation result is valid if the absolute size of the blocking coalition is bounded. The methods of Anderson (1978) are applied. © 1979.

Title: On economic games which are not necessarily superadditive
Abstract: Core-like solution concepts based on stable coalition structures are studied in the context of games which are not necessarily superadditive. It is shown that a simple economic model involving local public goods financed by wealth taxes has this characteristic. © 1979.

Title: Erratum
A cross-country analysis of divisia variances of quantities and budget shares
Abstract: Divisia variances of quantities consumed and budget shares for 105 pairs of countries are analyzed in terms of real-income, relative-price, and residual effects. One result is that luxuries tend to be more expensive relative to necessities in richer countries. The relatively low price of food in rich countries is an important factor for this result. © 1979.

Title: A cross-country analysis of Divisia covariances of prices and quantities consumed
Abstract: Divisia price-quantity covariances obtained from consumption data for 15 countries are analyzed in terms of real-income and relative price differences of these countries. More than 70 percent of the observed cross-country variation in the covariances is accounted for by these differences. © 1979.

Title: An application of the Theil-Stambaugh model of intergenerational mobility to American data
Abstract: Theil and Stambaugh (1977) applied a one-parameter model for intergenerational occupational mobility to British and Danish data. This letter describes an application of the model to American data published by Brittain (1977). © 1979.

Title: The Lerner index and measures of concentration
Abstract: The paper investigates the relationship between price-cost margins (the Lerner index) and measures of seller concentration. It shows that previous disparate conclusions on the appropriate concentration measure are special cases that can be reconciled in a more general formulation. © 1979.

Title: Empirical evidence for trends in capital markets
Abstract: The random walk hypothesis of price formation in capital markets is tested against a price-trend hypothesis, using a new test statistic. Empirical results prove that commodity and currency prices are not random but exhibit price-trend behaviour. © 1979.

Title: Some evidence in defense of the vehicle currency hypothesis
Abstract: The role of the dollar as a vehicle currency has been questioned by reference to patterns of trade invoicing. Here it is shown that a cross-section of country dollar holdings can be explained by reference to trade patterns. © 1979.

Title: Interindustry and intra-industry specialization do occur in world trade
Authors: H. Glejser, K. Goossens, M. Vanden Eede
Abstract: The existence of interindustry and intra-industry specialization of various groups of countries is detected by a procedure different from those used by B. Balassa and his followers. Whether high or low wage countries are considered seems to have an important influence. © 1979.

Title: Inflation, investment and the neutrality of money
Abstract: One argument made against inflation is that it discourages new investment because calculating depreciation allowances and inventories on the basis or original costs overstates profits and taxes and results in a lack of finance for new investment. This note shows that, in addition, inflation lowers the rate of return on prospective investment independently of the question availability of finance. © 1979.

Title: A note on the specification of the fisher equation under inflation uncertainty
Abstract: The effect of uncertainty on the relationship between the nominal interest rate and the expected rate of inflation, the Fisher equation, is examined both theoretically and empirically. It is found that the coefficient of the expected rate of inflation is significantly below unity. Variable rates of inflation tend to effect the nominal rate of interest positively, but real yields are apparently effected only by expected inflation, but not its variance. © 1979.

Title: The information criterion in model selection
Abstract: This note argues that the recent emphasis on model size (e.g., dimensionality) for choosing among economic models is misleading. With a reasonable formulation of prior information, it is important to take into account the a priori theoretical economic rationale for an economic model. © 1979.

Title: The rationality of savers with respect to expected inflation
Abstract: The impact of unanticipated inflation on savings is investigated using Belgian data from 1955-1977. Individuals are shown to save little of the proceeds of unexpected inflation. They would have to save all of it if their real wealth were to remain constant. © 1979.

Title: A simple test of the theory of the short-run Phillips curve
Abstract: The theory of the Phillips curve is reexamined taking into account the relationship between workers and firms. Emphasis is given to the firm's role in determining employment and hours over the business cycle. Empirical relations between real wages, employment and unemployment using distributed lag estimation are examined. © 1979.

Title: On methods for avoiding the a priori numerical specification of preferences in policy selection
Abstract: Generalised inverses, repeated simulations, and regression analogies are all ways of avoiding the explicit specification of a policy optimization objective. They are contrasted here with a numerical search procedure which avoids specifying, a priori, approximations to such objectives. © 1979.

Title: A note on the maximand of a fixed-membership labour-managed firm
Abstract: If technology has unrestricted domain it is shown that necessary and sufficient conditions for a fixed-membership labour-managed firm to have the conventional maximand exist and are very restrictive. © 1979.

Title: Asymptotic search behavior based on the Weibull distribution
Abstract: Fixed sample size search rules are examined for the case of a small marginal cost of search. The asymptotic Weibull distribution of minimum price is used to derive the optimal number of searches for a large class of parent price distributions. It is shown that the asymptotic price elasticity of the demand for search is a negative rational number less than 1 in absolute value. © 1979.

Title: Specific complements and the demand for money in Australia
Authors: James F. Meisner, Kenneth W. Clements
Abstract: Clements and Nguyen, using Australian data, found that money, durables, and other consumption are specific complements. This letter applies a Nasse-type model to the same data and describes the associated preference independence transformation in order to interpret the results. © 1979.

Title: Distortion of preferences and the Nash theory of bargaining
Authors: Vincent P. Crawford, Hal R. Varian
Abstract: It is shown that in Nash bargaining over division of a single good, when agents are allowed to distort their von Neumann-Morgenstern utility functions into any (weakly) concave form, reporting linear utility functions constitutes a unique dominant-strategy Nash equilibrium. © 1979.

Title: A cross-country tabulation of income elasticities of demand
Authors: Kenneth W. Clements, Frederick E. Suhm, Henri Theil
Abstract: International cross-sectional Engel curve estimates are used to compute income elasticities of demand for eight commodity groups and 15 countries. © 1979.

Title: On the physical quality of life index and evaluating economic welfare between nations
Authors: David A. Larson, Walton T. Wilford
Abstract: This paper tests for the statistical relationship between the Physical Quality of Life Index and an index of per capita gross national product for 150 nations and concludes that both provide essentially similar welfare rankings. We utilize principal components methodology to estimate PQLIs for 150 countries and find that, due to intercorrelation between the variables in the PQLI, the first principal component explains about 95% of the generalized variance. © 1979.

Title: The estimation of Gini coefficients from grouped data
Abstract: The conventional method of estimating the Gini coefficient (e.g., for an income distribution) from grouped data on a continuous variable is known to be an underestimate. This note provides a distribution free upper bound, using information about class boundaries. © 1979.

Title: International capital movements: A synthesis of alternative models
Abstract: The several alternative approches to international capital movements have not been compared theoretically. By showing that each represents a special case from a general simultaneous equation model, this note clarifies the theoretical relationships among the approaches, thus providing a convenient framework for their evaluation. © 1979.

Title: Estimating the price deflator for nominal cash balances
Abstract: A differential money demand equation is used to estimate the weight given to each commodity group in the price index which transforms nominal into real cash balances. The results indicate that food receives the largest weight and that the CPI is a good proxy for the true deflator. © 1979.

Title: The econometrics of labor supply on convex budget sets
Abstract: A method to account for a convex tax system arising from progressive taxation is given for econometric estimation of labor supply models. © 1979.

Title: On the first and second moments of the truncated multi-normal distribution and a simple estimator
Abstract: The relations between the first two moments of multivariate normal random variables with some components truncated are found. Simple instrumental variable estimators are available. The analysis extends results of Amemiya, and Sickles and Schmidt. © 1979.

Title: A ‘conservative’ ridge estimator
Abstract: In this paper an alternative to the Ordinary Ridge Estimator (ORE) introduced by Hoerl and Kennard (1970) is proposed. This estimator is called a 'Conservative' Ridge Estimator (CRE), because it puts a heavier weight on the unbiasedness and a smaller weight on the statistical stability of the 'unstable' estimation components than the ORE does. Nevertheless, the CRE often performs better in terms of the Mean Square Error of estimation. © 1979.

Title: The Antonelli matrix and the reciprocal Slutsky matrix
Abstract: Inverted demand models which describe deflated price changes in terms of quantity changes can be formulated by means of the Antonelli matrix or the reciprocal Slutsky matrix. The two approaches differ with respect to the price deflator and the role of the Divisia volume index. © 1979.

Title: Examples of Von Neumann-Morgenstern utility functions not recoverable from asset demands
Abstract: Counterexamples are given which show that preference orderings on portfolios need not uniquely determine the von Neumann-Morgenstern utility of income function. These counterexamples may not be robust, but robust examples exist if high and low incomes cannot be observed. © 1979.

Title: The value of changes in individual risk in a large mixed economy
Abstract: Changes in an individual's risk will affect all other individuals in the economy because of the interdependence created by the government's budget constraint. If government policy is optimal, these spillover benefits are measured by the change in the expected government budget surplus. © 1979.

Title: The dynamic behaviour of a simple macroeconomic model with a tax based incomes policy
Abstract: Tax based incomes policies are studied in a mark-up pricing framework with adaptive expectations. Stability may be endangered by such polities. Implications of these stability effects for policy decisions are drawn. © 1979.

Title: Equilibria of price-setting and quantity-setting duopolies
Authors: Neville J. Hathaway, John A. Rickard
Abstract: The relation between equilibria of output-setting and price-setting duopolies is investigated using the Inverse Function Theorem. The region that equilibria of the former occupy in relation to equilibria of the latter is found. A minimum of assumptions about the market functions are made. © 1979.

Title: Income effects in quality-quantity models
Abstract: The theorems on quality-quantity interactions well known in the fertility literature generally hold even when all goods in the utility function have a quality component. Although the results in this paper are presented in terms of the quality-quantity framework, it is clear that they can be applied to any problem in which the constraint is multiplicative in the variables. © 1979.

Title: A note on the allocation of time
Abstract: A multi-commodity model in which time as well as nominal income is necessary in the process of consumption is analyzed. Duality theory is used to provide a counter example to the 'Linder Theorem' that a rise in real wages will decrease consumption of some good if it is more time intensive than the weighted average of the time intensity of all other commodities. © 1979.

Title: A solution to a class of sequential decision problems
Abstract: This paper presents an extension to standard results on optimal stopping rules for a class of search problems in which some attributes of interest to the searcher are not revealed during the search process. The suggested solution takes the form of a two-stage decision process. © 1979.

Title: Supply and marginal firms in general equilibrium
Abstract: For economies with a large number of small firms, price induced changes in supply are decomposed into substitution and entry effects. Marginal firms (those earning zero profit) play a significant role in the determination of the slope of aggregate supply. © 1979.

Title: Exploitation in neoclassical general equilibrium
Abstract: Amongst other results, it is shown that in exploiting its ability to drive down the price of its intensive factor a constant returns monopoly operating in a two-sector economy may produce more than would a competitive industry. © 1979.

Title: Intracommunity fiscal surplus and an efficient system of land-rent
Abstract: Hamilton's claim that housing plus public service bundles can be efficiently supplied if each community maintains a system of differential land-rent within itself, reflecting fiscal surplus is analyzed in a general model of residential assignment. © 1979.

Title: A cross-country consumption comparison based on divisia variances and covariances
Abstract: A preliminary analysis of price and quantity data of the consumption in 16 countries, based on Divisia variances and covariances, indicates that poor countries are pairwise much more different than affluent countries are. © 1979.

Title: Cross-country prediction of changes in consumption patterns
Abstract: Changes in consumption patterns in 16 countries from 1970 to 1973 are predicted in a cross-sectional context. The method is successful (in the sense that it beats no-change extrapolation of budget shares) for the U.S. and six Western European countries, but it is not successful for most countries outside the North-Atlantic region. © 1979.

Title: Equicorrelated substitutes and Nasse's extension of the linear expenditure system
Abstract: Nasse's (1970) model can be used to provide an easily implementable approximation of the equicorrelated-substitutes model. The preference independence transformation based on this approximation is also considered. © 1979.

Title: Alternative demand models for close substitutes
Abstract: Three specifications of demand systems are compared and applied to U.S. data on beef, pork, chicken, and lamb in 1950-1972. © 1979.

Title: Empirical comparison of the shape of welfare functions
Authors: Floor G. Van Herwaarden, Arie Kapteyn
Abstract: This study compares the fit of the lognormal welfare function proposed by Van Praag (1968) with the fit of 12 other functions. The comparison uses a sample of about 14;000 respondents. The lognormal function outperforms 11 alternatives in terms of the residual variance criterion, while the logarithm performs slightly better. © 1979.

Title: Migration and marital status
Abstract: This study uses the National Longitudinal Survey of Young Women to document for the first time that single women have substantial earnings gains associated with migration. Married women who migrate lose relative to their non-migrant counterparts. © 1979.

Title: Bonding and the enforcement of labor contracts
Abstract: Bonded contracts are a perfect substitute for legally enforceable contracts, if capital markets are perfect. This idea is applied to labor market contracts involving specific training. © 1979.

Title: Technical progress, population growth and intergenerational equity in a model with many exhaustible and renewable resources
Abstract: A condition ensuring intergenerational equity is derived using a neoclassical model of many exhaustible and renewable resources involving technical progress and population growth. © 1979.

Title: Tax evasion and labour supply
Abstract: The total effect of a change in the probability of detection, or other parameters, on the level of tax evasion can be divided into three separate effects, only one of which is determinate. © 1979.

Title: A brief note on a non-existent theorem about the optimality of uniform taxation
Abstract: This note attempts to clarify the relationship between the separability of utility into goods and leisure and the question of whether uniform commodity taxes are optimal. The failure of several authors to recognize subtle differences in assumptions has caused confusion. © 1979.

Title: On the constancy of real interest rates
Abstract: In the context of a small structural model, we show that the autocorrelation and the variance of the ex ante real rate of interest can be uniquely estimated; the random forecasting errors need not confound the problem of identifying variations in the real rate. © 1979.

Title: Convenient singularities and maximum likelihood estimation
Abstract: In this note we point out that certain inequality restrictions correspond to singularities of likelihood functions, which makes it very easy to impose these restrictions on maximum likelihood estimates. This argument is illustrated by considering two specific examples. © 1979.

Title: An invariance property of the Slutsky symmetry test statistic
Abstract: The test statistic for Slutsky symmetry of a demand system is usually computed after one equation of the system is deleted. A simple direct proof is given of the proposition that the value of the statistic is not affected when a different equation is deleted. © 1979.

Title: On the determination of maximum accuracy for regression processes with endogenous variable constraints
Abstract: Optimal regression design is studied for a sequential problem in which the experimenter wishes to constrain the probable value of a dependent variable to the vicinity of a given target. In the context suggesting the problem, the dependent variable is an effluent, and the target arises from anti-pollution regulation. © 1979.

Title: On permanent effects of transitory phenomena in a simple growth model
Abstract: It is demonstrated that, because of learning-by-doing in the production process, transitory phenomena, such as market disequilibrium, can permanently affect long-run production techniques and the steady-state path of capital accumulation. © 1979.

Title: On duality theory in intertemporal choice with uncertainty
Abstract: We discuss here the implications that arise for the fundamental duality relationships given by Roy's Identity (1943) and Shephard's Lemma (1953) when the underlying consumer choice problem is dynamic and involves uncertainty. © 1979.

Title: Remarks on an investor's ‘paradox’
Abstract: A decreasing absolute risk averse investor invests λW in a safe asset with return s, and (1-λ)W in a risky asset with fixed distribution. An explicit example shows that λ and sλ can decrease as s increases over part of its domain. The existence of such examples has been suggested in earlier articles. © 1979.

Title: Insurance and protection of irreplaceable commodities
Abstract: This paper deals with the effect of life insurance upon the individual's 'value of life'. In a single period framework we analyse the factors which determine whether life insurance and safety will be treated as substitutes or complements. © 1979.

Title: The cost of search and rational random behavior
Abstract: Sequential search for the lowest price is shown to be directly related to Theil's (1979) rational random behavior approach. An explicit relationship between the optimal number of searches and the optimal decision distribution is derived for the exponential family of price distributions. © 1979.

Title: A monetary policy ineffectiveness result in a model with a predetermined price level
Abstract: This paper demonstrates that the rational expectations 'neutrality' proposition may hold in a macroeconomic model in which the price level is fully predetermined - i.e., entirely insensitive to current-period market conditions. © 1979.

Title: Editorial Board
Category index
Author index
Equilibrium in a system of communities with local public goods
Abstract: Equilibrium community configurations are analysed using a simple model where a community's public good output is chosen by majority voting and financed by a head tax. Examples which contradict the Tiebout hypothesis are presented. © 1979.

Title: The optimal parole period
Abstract: A probabilistic, theoretical model is developed for determining the optimal length of parole. Optimal parole periods are then calculated for alternative parameter estimates based on empirical data. The model, primarily designed for property crimes, can be extended to other offences. © 1979.

Title: The measurement of inter-industrial specialization in international trade
Abstract: Several authors including Hirsch and Lev (1971), O'Brien (1972), Soutar (1977), and Theil (1967) proposed informational measures for the analysis of international trade. The measurement of inter-industrial specialization (also of intra-industry trade) is another candidate. © 1979.

Title: A multisectoral model of a small, open economy with non-shiftable capital and imperfect labor mobility
Abstract: We report a model designed for the study of a less-developed economy whose labor force is composed of distinct ethnic or regional groups. The model is useful for the study of both positive and normative questions and offers a synthesis of some recent work in development and trade theory. © 1979.

Title: Shadow prices, market prices and project losses
Abstract: Provided that non-optimal taxes and subsidies are the only distortions affecting market prices, a project that is viable at the optimal set of shadow prices automatically generates enough tax revenue indirectly to finance any losses it incurs at market prices. © 1979.

Title: Optimally uniform commodity taxes
Abstract: In a many-person economy with an optimal linear income tax, weak separability between goods and leisure together with linear Engel curves for goods render discriminatory commodity taxes unnecessary. The result extends to uniform taxation for separable groups of goods. © 1979.

Title: Alternative transactions variables and the empirical evidence of economies of scale in money holdings
Abstract: Empirical results often seem to contradict the prediction of economies of scale in money holdings of the Baumol-Tobin model. The difference between theory and results might, however, be caused by an under-estimation of transactions by the usual proxy GNP. An illustration is given by estimates of Swedish demand for money equations involving an alternative proxy. © 1979.

Title: A pre-topological analysis of the input-output model
Authors: Jean-Paul Auray, Gérard Duru, Michel Mougeot
Abstract: The letter proposes a new method for analyzing the industrial structures. This method is founded on the pre-topological properties of the set of activities. © 1979.

Title: Inflation variability in Latin America
Abstract: Time series evidence is used to examine the relationship between the level of inflation and its variability in Latin American countries. © 1979.

Title: Inventory investment in United States manufacturing
Abstract: An inventory function for the U.S. manufacturing sector is estimated using quarterly data. The adjustment of inventories to optimum level in response to sales changes is sufficiently speedy that net unintended inventory changes do not occur and about two-thirds of the adjustment is complete within a year. © 1979.

Title: On the political theory of the business cycle
Abstract: The Nordhaus model of political business cycles is extended to allow for an endogenous length of the inter-election period. Vote-maximizing economic policies are analyzed. Alternative specifications of the vote function are explored. © 1979.

Title: Money, inflation and maximizing behaviour
Authors: Murray C. Kemp, Ngo Van Long
Abstract: It is shown that a simple economy with just one asset (money) which grows at a constant proportional rate with a population of farsighted overlapping generations is unstable in the sense that, away from the steady state, either the real value of the stock of money goes to zero or the monetary system breaks down altogether. © 1979.

Title: Stochastic dominance without risk aversion
Abstract: The time at which uncertainty is being resolved, rather than risk aversion, is used to show that if there exists a market for fair gambles then consumers will, in general, prefer less variability in their future income. © 1979.

Title: A progress report on Kelly's majority conjectures
Authors: Peter C. Fishburn, William V. Gehrlein, Eric Maskin
Abstract: LetC(m, n) be the proportion of n-voter profiles on m alternatives that have a majority winner. Jerry Kelly conjectured that C(m, n) > C(m + 1, n) for m ≥ 3 and n = 3 and n ≥ 5, and C(m, n) > C(m, n + 2) for m ≥ 3 and n ≥ 3. We prove these for special cases. © 1979.

Title: The cost structure of a simple general equilibrium system
Abstract: A two-sector, two-factor general equilibrium model is used in which one sector is subject to distortions. Cost functions are used to give a graphical analysis of the equilibrium and its comparison to the distortion-free, competition situation. © 1979.

Title: Unanticipated money, ‘disequilibrium’ modelling and rational expectations
Authors: Kenneth W. Clements, Peter D. Jonson
Abstract: This paper provides a synthesis of two recent approaches to macroeconomics, rational expectations and disequilibrium macromodelling. The unifying theme of the two approaches is the emphasis on the effects of the difference between actual and anticipated (or equilibrium) values of important variables such as the money supply. © 1979.

Title: The independence transformation of specific substitutes and specific complements
Abstract: When all n observed goods are specific substitutes (complements) in Houthakker's (1960) sense, the independence transformation yields one transformed good in which all observed goods are positively represented, viz., the transformed good with the smallest (largest) income elasticity. The n - 1 other transformed goods are all contrasts between observed goods. © 1979.

Title: The positive correlation of affluence and freedom
Abstract: Non-communist countries rated 'free' have on average a much higher per capita income than those rated 'partly free' or 'not free'. The latter two groups differ primarily in terms of the dispersion of their per capita incomes, those rated 'not free' being much more dispersed than those rated 'partly free'. © 1979.

Title: The impact of motivation and socioeconomic background on earnings
Abstract: In an effort to examine the effect of achievement motivation and socioeconomic background on the earnings of young men, a path model has been specified and estimated using OLS. Using a richer data set than others have had available, we find that motivation and socioeconomic differences are significant in explaining earnings differences. © 1979.

Title: On temporary layoffs and job search theory
Abstract: This note explores some properties of job search models in which layoff status to a particular job may be considered as a job offer which is conditional on having been employed at that job. © 1979.

Title: Depreciation and the conservation of energy
Abstract: It is argued that accelerating the rate at which firms can depreciate existing capital can move forward the date at which they will switch to more energy efficient processes. The price effect of inelastic industrial demand for energy might thereby be muted. © 1979.

Title: Managerial incentives in the financial sector
Authors: Mark John Hirschey, Gregory J. Werden
Abstract: Despite significant academic and policy interest the nature of managerial incentives in the non- industrial sector has escaped close scrutiny. Contrary to some earlier suggestions, this note finds traditional incentives to maximize profits or market value prevalent in the financial sector. © 1979.

Title: Spectral analysis as a tool for model discrimination
Abstract: Empirical discrimination between 'stock' and 'flow' formulations of international investment based on regression tests has consistently proved unsuccessful. By applying the new technique of model discrimination in the frequency domain, this note provides unequivocal empirical support for the stock model. © 1979.

Title: Flows of direct investment and their effects on investment in Canada
Abstract: An accelerator-flow of funds model of investment is used to estimate the effects of direct investment abroad by Canadian firms and direct investment by foreign firms on domestic investment in Canada for the period 1957.I-1971.IV. The results show that direct investment abroad has a negative effect, whereas foreign direct investment has a positive effect on domestic investment. The latter results confirm earlier findings by Caves and Reuber (1971). © 1979.

Title: Quotas and equilibrium relative prices in the trade restricting country
Authors: Werner A. De Haan, Patrice E. Visser
Abstract: This paper is concerned with the effects of international trade restriction through quotas. It is shown that a casual relationship exists between the fraction of licences distributed domestically, the terms of trade, and the domestic relative price of the importable. © 1979.

Title: Estimating changes in real size of the public sector
Abstract: A new deflator for total government expenditure can now be derived from major components of the total. Applied to government spending in the US over the past quarter-century, results show near-stability in real size of the public sector. © 1979.

Title: Maximum likelihood estimation of the Rotterdam model under two different conditions
Abstract: This letter describes maximum likelihood (ML) procedures for the Rotterdam model (1) when the model is formulated in relative prices and (2) under the constraints of the theory of rational random behavior. © 1979.

Title: The time–covariance function
Abstract: This note establishes the relationship between the time interval over which changes in two random variables are measured and the covariances between these changes for various intervals. It then shows that the properties of this relationship can be used to detect the presence of intertemporal cross serial correlations between time series data. © 1979.

Title: The sad fate of the asymptotic Slutsky symmetry test for large systems
Abstract: The standard test statistic for Slutsky symmetry is biased toward rejection of the null hypothesis, particularly for large demand equation systems. © 1979.

Title: Heteroscedasticity and the use of Box–Cox transformations
Authors: Marc J.I. Gaudry, Marcel G. Dagenais
Abstract: Direct and inverse power Box-Cox transformations are used to characterize the form of heteroscedasticity in models where the variables themselves are subjected to direct Box-Cox transformations. Resulting formulations are extended to take serial correlation simultaneousy into account. © 1979.

Title: A distributed lag estimator derived from Shiller's smoothness priors
Abstract: In this paper we consider a polynomial distributed model with varying coefficients and Shiller's smoothness priors. It has been shown that the Bayes estimator under this specification produces a less smooth lag pattern than the Almon and Shiller estimators for the fixed coefficients case. © 1979.

Title: Attitudes to risk
Authors: Peter J. Lambert, John D. Hey
Abstract: Diamond and Stiglitz' approach to defining increased risk is developed, and partial orderings emerge which are closely connected with the risk orderings of Meyer. The new orderings are related to behaviour at the extremes of risk aversion and risk loving. © 1979.

Title: Dynamic Stackelberg stability
Authors: Neville J. Hathaway, John A. Rickard, Terence D. Howroyd
Abstract: A model of competition in a single-product market is given. The dynamics are studied using Gersgorin's Theorem under the assumptions of Cournot and Stackelberg behavior. Stability is enhanced by smaller adjustment speeds in the former, but not necessarily in the latter case. © 1979.

Title: A model of profits and market adjustment
Abstract: A market adjustment process is analyzed, where the prevailing rate of profit affects the rates of change of quantity produced and unit cost of production. Only under special conditions does the process lead to a steady-state where the rate of profit is zero. © 1979.

Title: New results on rational random behavior
Authors: John P. Bowman, Kenneth Laitinen, Henri Theil
Abstract: This letter deals with conditions under which it is preferable to buy a zero amount of information; with a proportionality of the information and loss variances associated with two different decision distributions; and with a limiting chi-square distribution of the decision maker's loss when the marginal cost of information is small. © 1979.

Title: The measurement of inequality by components of income
Abstract: Cowell (1977) considered the inequality by components of income (wages, property income, welfare, etc.). This note shows that this measurement problem can be elegantly handled in terms of informational inequality measures. © 1979.

Title: The upper tail of the earnings distribution
Abstract: The functional description of the upper tail of the earnings distribution is re-examined using British data disaggregated by occupational group. The superiority of the Pareto distribution, over the lognormal is shown to be much less well-supported than at the aggregate level. © 1979.

Title: The time to adoption
Authors: R. Lindner, A. Fischer, P. Pardey
Abstract: A decision-theoretic model of the decision to adopt a process innovation is developed, and used to derive a simple result for the time lag from a decision maker's first knowledge of the innovation to his first use of it. © 1979.

Title: Stagflation and expansionary economic policies under flexible exchange rates
Abstract: For a small Keynesian open economy with imported inputs and rational price expectations of workers it is shown that under flexible exchange rates expansionary domestic monetary or fiscal policy may cause stagflation. Simple conditions for such an outcome are given. © 1979.

Title: Equilibrium in capital markets
Abstract: The Capital Asset Pricing Model depends on assumptions which have undesirable implications. The letter presents an alternative model based on exponential utility functions, which in some respects can be considered as a generalization. © 1979.

Title: Quantitative versus qualitative measures of price expectations: The evidence from Australian consumer surveys
Abstract: This letter analyses price expectations data derived from the quarterly Australian Survey of Consumers. The survey asks both qualitative and quantitative price expectations questions. The information loss arising from using the more readily available qualitative based series as approximations to the quantitative series is assessed. Qualitatively based series are found to greatly exaggerate changes in consumer price expectations in times of high inflation. © 1979.

Title: International comparisons of GDP and data revisions
Abstract: This note illustrates the substantial data revisions which may occur in National Accounts data for developing countries. © 1979.

Title: A Monte Carlo approach to compute the asymptotic standard errors of dynamic multipliers
Authors: Carlo Bianchi, Giorgio Calzolari, Paolo Corsi
Abstract: A Monte Carlo method to compute asymptotic standard errors of dynamic multipliers is proposed. It is applied to Hein's Model I to find standard error of interim multipliers of taxes on nominal income. © 1979.
